ddGetUpdatedLib.desc: Returns the path to the cds.lib file that was last used by ddUpdateLibList. This is the same as ddGetForcedLib if a forced library was in effect.

ddIsId.name: ddIsId
ddIsId.desc: Returns t if b_objId is an opaque ID known to the PI, and nil otherwise. Some dd functions will accept nil as the ID parameter, but this function returns nil if the argument is nil.

ddIsHiddenCell.name: ddIsHiddenCell
ddIsHiddenCell.desc: Determines whether the specified cell is hidden. A cell is hidden if it is a member of the Hidden category or a member of a subcategory of the Hidden category.

ddIsObjLibMarked.name: ddIsObjLibMarked
ddIsObjLibMarked.desc: Returns t if the library that owns b_objId is marked to be deleted or its path is changed.

ddIsObjReadable.name: ddIsObjReadable
ddIsObjReadable.desc: Returns t if the object specified by b_objId can be read by the current process.

ddIsObjReadableEx.name: ddIsObjReadableEx
ddIsObjReadableEx.desc: Returns t if the object specified by b_objId can be read by the current process. This function is similar to ddIsObjReadable except that you can specify whether to look for the object in the temporary directory or the master directory, or both, with the x_pathType argument.

ddIsObjWritable.name: ddIsObjWritable
ddIsObjWritable.desc: Returns t if the object specified by b_objId can be modified by the current process.

ddIsObjWritableEx.name: ddIsObjWritableEx
ddIsObjWritableEx.desc: Returns t if the object specified by b_objId can be modified by the current process. This function is similar to ddIsObjWritable except that you can specify whether to look for the object in the temporary directory or the master directory, or both, with the x_pathType argument.

ddIsPathManageable.name: ddIsPathManageable
ddIsPathManageable.desc: Returns t if the supplied path is manageable (is in a location that is supported by a design management system).

ddIsPathManaged.name: ddIsPathManaged
ddIsPathManaged.desc: Returns t if the specified path is currently managed by a design management system. A path is managed if the file associated with the path is checked in. You can use ddIsPathManaged to implement a check against creating a file when another user has already created it but the local user work area is not updated to reflect the creation.

ddLibIs5X.name: ddLibIs5X
ddLibIs5X.desc: Determines if the library was created with the 5.X library structure.

ddLibHasTmpDir.name: ddLibHasTmpDir
ddLibHasTmpDir.desc: Checks if the library has a temporary directory. A temporary directory for a library is defined by putting a TMP attribute on the library with an ASSIGN statement in a cds.lib file.

ddLockDescribe.name: ddLockDescribe
ddLockDescribe.desc: Fills a static string with a message.

ddLockFree.name: ddLockFree
ddLockFree.desc: Releases any existing lock on the file specified by b_lockId.

ddLockGetStatus.name: ddLockGetStatus
ddLockGetStatus.syntax:
ddLockGetStatus( 
b_lockId 
) 
=> x_sysId t_type x_value t_userName t_userHost t_fileHost t_filePath
ddLockGetStatus.desc: Retrieves frequently needed information from the lock table: The lock-system ID, type, and value and the holder's user name and hostid.

ddLockPath.name: ddLockPath
ddLockPath.desc: Creates a handle that allows you to lock the file and returns a lock ID for the file. Once you call ddLockFree, all references to that lock ID become invalid.

ddLockSet.name: ddLockSet
ddLockSet.syntax:
ddLockSet( 
b_lockId 
t_mode 
[ t_block ] 
[ t_message ] 
) 
=> t / nil
ddLockSet.desc: Gets the type of lock in t_mode for the file ID. If you have already locked the file, this function changes the lock type.

ddLockSetEx.name: ddLockSetEx
ddLockSetEx.syntax:
ddLockSetEx(
b_lockId 
t_mode 
[ g_block ] 
[ t_message ] 
[ g_doErrMsgs] 
[ g_timeout ] 
) 
=> t / nil
ddLockSetEx.desc: An extension of ddLockSet with two additional arguments.

ddMapGetDataTypeFileName.name: ddMapGetDataTypeFileName
ddMapGetDataTypeFileName.desc: Returns the pattern registered in the registry for t_dataType.

ddMapGetDataTypeList.name: ddMapGetDataTypeList
ddMapGetDataTypeList.desc: Returns a list of names of the data types specified in the registry.

ddMapGetFileDataType.name: ddMapGetFileDataType
ddMapGetFileDataType.desc: Returns the name of the data type associated with b_fileObjId.

ddMapGetFileTool.name: ddMapGetFileTool
ddMapGetFileTool.desc: Looks up the data format registered in the registry for b_fileObjId's file name, and returns the tool name of the preferred editor (if there is one) or the default editor which is registered for that data format.

ddMapGetFileViewType.name: ddMapGetFileViewType
ddMapGetFileViewType.desc: Returns the name of the view type associated with b_fileObjId.

ddMapGetToolNameDataType.name: ddMapGetToolNameDataType
ddMapGetToolNameDataType.desc: Returns the name of the first data type in the registry which is associated with t_toolName.

ddMapGetToolNameList.name: ddMapGetToolNameList
ddMapGetToolNameList.desc: Retrieves a list of the names of the tools specified in the registry, in alphabetical order.

ddMapGetToolNameViewType.name: ddMapGetToolNameViewType
ddMapGetToolNameViewType.desc: Returns the name of the first view type in the registry which is associated with t_toolName.

ddMapGetViewTypeFileName.name: ddMapGetViewTypeFileName
ddMapGetViewTypeFileName.desc: Returns the pattern registered in the registry for a view alias or data type named t_viewType.

ddMapGetViewTypeList.name: ddMapGetViewTypeList
ddMapGetViewTypeList.desc: Returns a list of names of view types defined in the registry, in alphabetical order. If a data type in the registry has a dfII_viewType property defined, the value of that property will be in the list. Otherwise, the data type name will be in the list.

ddMapIsFileNameKnown.name: ddMapIsFileNameKnown
ddMapIsFileNameKnown.desc: Returns t if the file name is registered as the pattern for some data format in the registry.

ddMapIsToolLegal.name: ddMapIsToolLegal
ddMapIsToolLegal.desc: Returns t if t_toolName is either the preferred editor or the default editor for b_fileObjId.

ddMapIsToolNameKnown.name: ddMapIsToolNameKnown
ddMapIsToolNameKnown.desc: Returns t if t_toolName is defined in the registry.

ddMarkObjMaster.name: ddMarkObjMaster
ddMarkObjMaster.desc: Changes the master.tag file to designate the object as the new master. The master.tag file must be located with the file it designates, so you must be able to write a file to mark it master. The master.tag file is checked out of the Design Management system, if necessary.

ddNeedCheckout.name: ddNeedCheckout
ddNeedCheckout.desc: Enables the tools that need to provide automatic checkout behavior to determine if these tools need to call the ddCheckout and ddCheckin functions.

ddObjHasNamedObj.name: ddObjHasNamedObj
ddObjHasNamedObj.desc: Returns t if b_objId has a child object named t_fileName.

ddObjHasNamedObjEx.name: ddObjHasNamedObjEx
ddObjHasNamedObjEx.syntax:
ddObjHasNamedObjEx(
b_objId
t_fileName 
x_pathType
)
=> t / nil
ddObjHasNamedObjEx.desc: Returns t if b_objId has a child object named t_fileName. This function is similar to ddObjHasNamedObj except that you can specify whether to look for the object in the temporary directory or the master directory, or both, with the x_pathType argument.

ddObjIsInMaster.name: ddObjIsInMaster
ddObjIsInMaster.desc: Checks if the object exists in the master directory.

ddObjIsInTmp.name: ddObjIsInTmp
ddObjIsInTmp.desc: Checks if the object exists in the temporary directory. A temporary directory for a library is defined by putting a TMP attribute on the library with an ASSIGN statement in a cds.lib file. The library itself is considered the master directory.

ddProduceObjRelNames.name: ddProduceObjRelNames
ddProduceObjRelNames.syntax:
ddProduceObjRelNames( 
b_objId 
g_consumer 
g_clientData 
) 
=> t / nil
ddProduceObjRelNames.desc: Produces the names of all the objects that belong to a library, cell, or view and calls the given function with each name and any provided data structure.

ddProduceObjRelNamesEx.name: ddProduceObjRelNamesEx
ddProduceObjRelNamesEx.syntax:
ddProduceObjRelNamesEx(
b_objId 
g_consumer 
g_clientData 
x_pathType
) 
=> t / nil
ddProduceObjRelNamesEx.desc: Produces the names of all the objects that belong to a library, cell, or view and calls the given function with each name and any provided data structure. This function is similar to ddProduceObjRelNames except that you can specify whether to look for the objects in the temporary directory or the master directory, or both, with the x_pathType argument.

ddRegHiddenCellsFunc.name: ddRegHiddenCellsFunc
ddRegHiddenCellsFunc.desc: Registers a user-defined SKILL function that will be called to obtain a list of hidden cell names. Note that additionally the Virtuoso environment considers a cell to be hidden if it is a member of the Hidden category or its subcategories.

ddRegTrigger.name: ddRegTrigger
ddRegTrigger.syntax:
ddRegTrigger( 
t_triggerName 
s_triggerFunc 
[ x_priority ] 
) 
=> t / nil
ddRegTrigger.desc: Registers a function to be called when the triggering event occurs. Adds callbacks (triggers) to PI functions that change things. Each of these PI functions has a pre-trigger and an post-trigger.

ddReleaseObj.name: ddReleaseObj
ddReleaseObj.desc: When you find an object using write (w) or append (a) mode, and the object and its parents do not yet exist, ddGetObj creates the object and its parents in the file system. The effect of this action is to make them visible in the browser and to permit us to designate file as a Master. After you close the file, you should call ddReleaseObj, which then deletes the file if you did not save it yet.

ddSetForcedLib.name: ddSetForcedLib
ddSetForcedLib.desc: If the given path is a valid path, the forcedLib is used for all future library updates/creates/deletes and t is returned. If the path is an empty string, the default cds.lib file is used for all future library updates/creates/deletes and t is returned. If a path is given that is not valid, nil is returned with no error message and the forcedLib will be unchanged.

ddSetForcedLibEx.name: ddSetForcedLibEx
ddSetForcedLibEx.desc: Sets the cds.lib file to be used instead of searching for them in the default locations. If no cds.lib is specified but a lib.defs file is specified, the function will use the specified lib.defs as a forced cds.lib file. Cadence recommends you to use the ddSetForcedLib function instead.

ddSetLibUnmanaged.name: ddSetLibUnmanaged
ddSetLibUnmanaged.desc: Sets the DMTYPE entry of the cdsinfo.tag file in the library directory to none. This will guarantee that regardless of the default value for DMTYPE, this library will not be DM managed. If the library has a temporary directory, it will also not be managed.

ddSetLibDmType.name: ddSetLibDmType
ddSetLibDmType.desc: Sets the DMTYPE entry of the cdsinfo.tag file in the library.

ddSetTmpdirWarn.name: ddSetTmpdirWarn
ddSetTmpdirWarn.desc:
Enables or disables printing of a warning message for an ASSIGN statement with attribute TMP which appears in cds.lib files. The TMP attribute defines a temporary storage directory for a read-only or reference library. If you set the DD_TMPDIR_ON environment variable to NO, the temporary directory functionality is turned off and DDPI skips ASSIGN and UNASSIGN statements when parsing cds.lib files. In that case, DDPI prints the following warning by default:
WARNING `<PATH_TO_CDSLIB_FILE>/cds.lib', Line 3: skipping: 'ASSIGN' lib1 TMP /tmp 
If you do not want the warning message to be printed, specify nil for the g_doWarn argument.

ddUnregHiddenCellsFunc.name: ddUnregHiddenCellsFunc
ddUnregHiddenCellsFunc.desc: Unregisters a hidden cells function that was registered using ddRegHiddenCellsFunc.

ddUnregTrigger.name: ddUnregTrigger
ddUnregTrigger.desc: Removes a callback (trigger function) from a named list of trigger functions.

ddUpdateLibList.name: ddUpdateLibList
ddUpdateLibList.desc: Establishes and re-establishes a list of libraries in virtual memory to be used by ddGetObj.

ciwAddTranslatorItem.name: ciwAddTranslatorItem
ciwAddTranslatorItem.syntax:
ciwAddTranslatorItem(
s_tag
t_itemText
t_callback
)
=> t / nil
ciwAddTranslatorItem.desc: Adds an entry for the Import or Export commands.

ciwCreateMenu.name: ciwCreateMenu
ciwCreateMenu.desc: Creates a menu from the given menu definition. The menu created can be used as a pop-up menu. This function exists primarily for application support.

ciwCreatePulldown.name: ciwCreatePulldown
ciwCreatePulldown.desc: Creates a pulldown menu from the given menu definition. The ls_menuDef argument can either be a list defining the contents of a pulldown menu or the SKILL symbol that represents the list. This function exists primarily for application support.

ciwMenuInit.name: ciwMenuInit
ciwMenuInit.desc:
Initializes and installs the CIW pulldown menus based on the menu files found in the hierarchy. This function will be called instead of hiInstallCIWMenus. It can also be called from the CIW to debug the menu file contents.

If g_reset is specified as t, the CIW menus are reset. Calling ciwMenuInit without any arguments will initialize the CIW menus only if it has not already been done.

ciwMenuInstall.name: ciwMenuInstall
ciwMenuInstall.desc: Creates and installs into r_window a menu banner based on ls_bannerDef. Useful for applications that create and manage their own windows. This function exists primarily for application support.

ciwMenuLoadFile.name: ciwMenuLoadFile
ciwMenuLoadFile.desc: Reads menu files found in the DFII hierarchy using t_appName.

ciwRemoveTranslatorItem.name: ciwRemoveTranslatorItem
ciwRemoveTranslatorItem.syntax:
ciwRemoveTranslatorItem(
s_tag
t_itemText
t_callback
)
=> t / nil
ciwRemoveTranslatorItem.desc: Removes an entry from the Import or Export commands.

ddsAboutDFII.name: ddsAboutDFII
ddsAboutDFII.desc: Opens the product information dialog box, which indicates the product, the release number, and copyright information. This dialog box is used for the custom IC design tools.

ddsBrowserAction.name: ddsBrowserAction
ddsBrowserAction.desc: Returns the Boolean value of the requested Library Browser option. This function explains how applications use the Library Browser preferences and the actions specified in the ddsSyncWithForm function. If you are integrating your own Library Browser, you must decide whether to support such actions; if so, you can use this function. This functionality provides applications the ability to support the user's need to see the Library Browser when a particular command is executed.

ddsCheckinPreferences.name: ddsCheckinPreferences
ddsCheckinPreferences.desc: Sets the prompt behavior you choose for the current DFII design session for checking in design data. This function displays a form to set the auto checkin prompt preferences for properties, files, and cellviews. This process controls access to the design data files that design and team members store in a project data repository.

ddsCheckoutPreferences.name: ddsCheckoutPreferences
ddsCheckoutPreferences.desc: Sets the prompt behaviors you select for the current DFII design session for checking out design data. This function displays a form to set the auto checkout prompt preferences for properties, files, and cellviews. This process controls access to the design data files that design and team members store in a project data repository.

ddsCheckSessionName.name: ddsCheckSessionName
ddsCheckSessionName.desc: Checks to see if the current MPS session is also the default session for the user. If the given session name is the same as the effective user ID's name or if there is no session name, builds a unique session name using the process ID. This implies that the current process checks the session and returns the session name to use - either the given name if it is checked or a new unique name to use to perform the checking.

ddsEditProp.name: ddsEditProp
ddsEditProp.desc: Invokes the property editor on the named object. Calls peEditProp after getting the ID for the named object.

ddsEndSyncWithForm.name: ddsEndSyncWithForm
ddsEndSyncWithForm.desc: Terminates an application's form synchronization with the Library Browser and closes the Library Browser.

ddsFileBrowseCB.name: ddsFileBrowseCB
ddsFileBrowseCB.syntax:
ddsFileBrowseCB( 
g_form
s_targetName
[ t_filter ] 
[ s_mode ] 
[ t_caption ] 
)
=> t / nil
ddsFileBrowseCB.desc: Creates a file browser dialog for specifying file names through browsing.

ddsGetCurrentLib.name: ddsGetCurrentLib
ddsGetCurrentLib.desc: Accesses the currently selected library in the Library Browser.

ddsGetCustomLibSelect.name: ddsGetCustomLibSelect
ddsGetCustomLibSelect.desc: Returns the name string passed to ddsRegCustomLibSelect if a custom Library Browser is registered to the system. If a custom Library Browser is not registered, nil is returned.

ddsGetServiceName.name: ddsGetServiceName
ddsGetServiceName.desc: Returns a string that can be used as an MPS service name. The string is the name of the invoked program plus the process ID number.

ddsHiCloseData.name: ddsHiCloseData
ddsHiCloseData.desc: Displays the Close and Purge Data form that prompts you to select one or more objects to close and purge form virtual memory.

ddsHiCreateLibrary.name: ddsHiCreateLibrary
ddsHiCreateLibrary.desc: Create new libraries from within DFII.

ddsHiMakeReadOnly.name: ddsHiMakeReadOnly
ddsHiMakeReadOnly.desc: Displays a form that prompts you to select cellviews currently open in edit mode and change them to read only mode.

ddsHiOpenCdsLibEditor.name: ddsHiOpenCdsLibEditor
ddsHiOpenCdsLibEditor.desc: Brings up the Library Path Editor.

ddsHiPreferences.name: ddsHiPreferences
ddsHiPreferences.desc: Invokes the Browser and CIW Preferences form.

ddsHiRefresh.name: ddsHiRefresh
ddsHiRefresh.desc: Opens a form listing the open technology files, properties, and cellviews that are not current with their corresponding files on disk.

ddsLEWhatsNewAtStartup.name: ddsLEWhatsNewAtStartup
ddsLEWhatsNewAtStartup.desc: Brings up the What's New window for Virtuoso Layout Editor.

ddsOnLineHelp.name: ddsOnLineHelp
ddsOnLineHelp.desc: Brings up online Help documentation for DFII tools.

ddsOpenConvertToolBox.name: ddsOpenConvertToolBox
ddsOpenConvertToolBox.desc: Displays the Conversion Tool Box user interface.

ddsOpenLibManager.name: ddsOpenLibManager
ddsOpenLibManager.desc: Starts the library manager. The separate process, library manager, is invoked and connected to using mps.

ddsProgramName.name: ddsProgramName
ddsProgramName.desc: Returns the name of the program minus any .exe extension.

ddsRefresh.name: ddsRefresh
ddsRefresh.syntax:
ddsRefresh(
[ ?cellview { t | nil } ]
[ ?cdf { t | nil } ]
[ ?property { t | nil } ]
[ ?techfile { t | nil } ]
)
=> t / nil
ddsRefresh.desc: Refreshes open cellviews, CDFs, property bags, and technology files that are not current with their corresponding files on disk.

ddsRegPreRefreshTrigger.name: ddsRegPreRefreshTrigger
ddsRegPreRefreshTrigger.desc: Registers a user-defined SKILL function that is called before executing the Refresh command using CIW - File - Refresh or the ddsRefresh SKILL function.

ddsRegPostRefreshTrigger.name: ddsRegPostRefreshTrigger
ddsRegPostRefreshTrigger.desc: Registers a user-defined SKILL function that is called after completion of the Refresh command using CIW - File - Refresh or the ddsRefresh  SKILL function.

ddsRegCustomLibSelect.name: ddsRegCustomLibSelect
ddsRegCustomLibSelect.syntax:
ddsRegCustomLibSelect( 
t_name 
s_sync 
s_update 
s_endSync 
s_curlLib
)
=> t / nil
ddsRegCustomLibSelect.desc: ddserv only supports one customization at a given time. If you call this function more than once, the latest set of functions are registered. The ddsRegCustomSelect function performs an isCallable Check on each of its arguments to insure that the functions have been loaded into the system. If not, a message is generated.

ddsHiSaveData.name: ddsHiSaveData
ddsHiSaveData.desc: Displays the Save Modified Data form that prompts you to select one or more objects to save from virtual memory.

ddsServSelect.name: ddsServSelect
ddsServSelect.desc: Processes a select request from the browser process if and only if a form is synchronized to it. It is the call logged in the cds.log file. The function sets the appropriate form field with the library, cell, and view values.

ddsSetLibManLCV.name: ddsSetLibManLCV
ddsSetLibManLCV.syntax:
ddsSetLibManLCV(
t_lib
[ t_cell ]
[ t_view ]
)
=> t / nil
ddsSetLibManLCV.desc: Allows the application to set the library name, cell name, or view name entries in the library manager from a DFII session.

ddsGetLibManLCV.name: ddsGetLibManLCV
ddsGetLibManLCV.desc: Returns the library, cell, and view name entries currently selected in the library manager

ddsSyncWithForm.name: ddsSyncWithForm
ddsSyncWithForm.syntax:
ddsSyncWithForm( 
g_form 
s_action 
s_libField 
[ s_cellField [ s_viewField [ l_viewTypes ] ] ] 
)
=> t / nil
ddsSyncWithForm.desc: Registers the given form and fields of that form for synchronization with the Library Browser. The Library Browser is seeded with the current values of the library, cell, and view names from the fields in the form if they are not blank. The field value is not updated by ddsSyncWithForm when its enabled or editable attribute is set to nil. From this point until ddsEndSyncWithForm, selections in the Library Browser seed the given form fields.

ddsUnregCustomLibSelect.name: ddsUnregCustomLibSelect
ddsUnregCustomLibSelect.desc: Un-registers the custom Library Browser interface during a session.

ddsUpdateSyncWithForm.name: ddsUpdateSyncWithForm
ddsUpdateSyncWithForm.desc: If an application has registered a form with the Library Browser by calling ddsSyncWithForm or dmbSyncWithForm, this function updates the Library Browser with the values currently in the respective form fields.

ddsViewDDProp.name: ddsViewDDProp
ddsViewDDProp.desc: Finds information about the specified object and any properties found in its property bag.

ddsWhatsNew.name: ddsWhatsNew
ddsWhatsNew.desc: Brings up the What's New window.

dmbGetCurrentLib.name: dmbGetCurrentLib
dmbGetCurrentLib.desc: Returns the ddId of the library currently selected in the Library Browser if a form is registered to it (otherwise, the Library Browser is hidden).

dmbLibBrowserFormDone.name: dmbLibBrowserFormDone
dmbLibBrowserFormDone.desc:
Terminates the synchronization between the last form registered and the Library Browser. Applications should ALWAYS call this function when they know their Library Browser/form interaction has terminated (using Cancel or OK). Leaving it hanging could result in unpredictable behavior which would degrade the usability of the system. 

Supplied for compatibility. Replace with ddsEndSyncWithForm.

dmbOpenLibBrowser.name: dmbOpenLibBrowser
dmbOpenLibBrowser.desc:
Invokes the library manager. The separate process, library manager, is invoked and connected to using mps. 

Supplied for compatibility. Replace with ddsOpenLibManager.

dmbSetBrowserInteractions.name: dmbSetBrowserInteractions
dmbSetBrowserInteractions.syntax:
dmbSetBrowserInteractions(
[ ?openDesignOption { t | nil } ]
[ ?openPlaceInstanceOption {t | nil} ]
[ ?openOthersOption { t | nil } ]
)
=> t / nil
dmbSetBrowserInteractions.desc: Specifies whether the Library Browser is automatically opened when certain types of forms appear. This function is provided for backward compatibility with only the 4.3.4 version.

dmbSyncWithForm.name: dmbSyncWithForm
dmbSyncWithForm.syntax:
dmbSyncWithForm( 
s_form s_synctype 
s_libraryName 
s_cellName	
s_viewName 
[ s_versionNumber ] 
) 
=> t / nil
dmbSyncWithForm.desc: Establishes synchronization between a given form and the Library Browser. The given library, cell, and view fields are filled in as you select items in the Library Browser.

dmbSyncWithCellForm.name: dmbSyncWithCellForm
dmbSyncWithCellForm.syntax:
dmbSyncWithCellForm( 
s_form 
s_synctype 
s_libraryName 
s_cellName 
[ s_viewName ] 
[ s_versionNumber ] 
)
=> t / nil
dmbSyncWithCellForm.desc: Establishes synchronization between a given form and the Library Browser. The given library, cell, and view fields are filled in as you select items in the Library Browser.

dmbUpdateBrowser.name: dmbUpdateBrowser
dmbUpdateBrowser.desc: Updates the library browser with the values currently in the registered form formFields. This function lets applications update the Library Browser based on what users type into a form.

ddCatOpen.name: ddCatOpen
ddCatOpen.syntax:
ddCatOpen( 
b_ddId 
t_categoryName 
t_mode 
) 
=> b_objId / nil
ddCatOpen.desc: Opens a category with the given name and uses the mode to get the object ID.

ddCatOpenEx.name: ddCatOpenEx
ddCatOpenEx.syntax:
ddCatOpenEx( 
b_ddId 
t_categoryName 
t_mode 
x_keepEmpty 
)
=> b_objId / nil
ddCatOpenEx.desc: Opens a category with the given name using the mode to get the object ID.

ddCatAddItem.name: ddCatAddItem
ddCatAddItem.syntax:
ddCatAddItem( 
b_ddId 
t_name 
t_type 
) 
=> t / nil
ddCatAddItem.desc: Adds the specified name to the given category.

ddCatSubItem.name: ddCatSubItem
ddCatSubItem.desc:
Removes the named item from the given category.

If the name is the name of a category (that is, removing a subcategory from another category), the  checks if it is referenced in any other category. If not, the category is moved to the library category list. This action ensures that the caller must do a ddCatRemove to remove category entries from a library. Changes are not written to disk until a ddCatSave is done.

ddCatSave.name: ddCatSave
ddCatSave.desc: Writes the category information to disk. This writes out any changes made to the category to disk.

ddCatRemove.name: ddCatRemove
ddCatRemove.desc: Removes the category and its contents from disk. All references to the category are removed from the library.

ddCatClose.name: ddCatClose
ddCatClose.desc: Closes the category and purges its information from virtual memory. Any edits since the last ddCatSave are lost.

ddCatGetCatName.name: ddCatGetCatName
ddCatGetCatName.desc: Returns the category name of the given category ID.

ddCatGetCatMembers.name: ddCatGetCatMembers
ddCatGetCatMembers.desc: Returns the list of members of the given category. The function does not return the members (cells) that do not exist in the library.

ddCatGetLibCats.name: ddCatGetLibCats
ddCatGetLibCats.desc: Returns the list of library-level categories.

ddCatFindCat.name: ddCatFindCat
ddCatFindCat.syntax:
ddCatFindCat( 
b_ddId 
t_name 
t_mode 
) 
=> b_objId / nil
ddCatFindCat.desc:
Returns the ID of a category with the given name in the given mode. Traverses category hierarchies. 

This function calls ddCatOpen to get the category ID to be returned. The caller must call ddCatClose to properly flush the information from virtual memory when done. The category is opened in the given mode.

ddCatGetCellsNotInCat.name: ddCatGetCellsNotInCat
ddCatGetCellsNotInCat.desc: Returns the names of cells that are not in any category. This information is derived from an existing library.

ddCatIsObjInCat.name: ddCatIsObjInCat
ddCatIsObjInCat.desc: Searches for the named object in the given category.

dmAddCellToCategory.name: dmAddCellToCategory
dmAddCellToCategory.desc: Adds the specified cells to the category.

dmCreateCellCategory.name: dmCreateCellCategory
dmCreateCellCategory.syntax:
dmCreateCellCategory( 
g_libOrCatId 
t_categoryName 
l_cellList 
) 
=> t / nil
dmCreateCellCategory.desc: Creates a cell category and adds all specified cells to the category.

dmRemoveCellCategory.name: dmRemoveCellCategory
dmRemoveCellCategory.desc: Removes a cell category from a library or from a parent cell category.

dmRemoveCellFromCategory.name: dmRemoveCellFromCategory
dmRemoveCellFromCategory.desc: Removes one or more cells from a cell category.

deAddAppCapabilities.name: deAddAppCapabilities
deAddAppCapabilities.syntax:
deAddAppCapabilities(
t_viewType
[ ?newFile g_newFile ]
[ ?openFile g_openFile ]
)
=> t / nil
deAddAppCapabilities.desc: Adds the required application capabilities to the specified view type.

deRegApp.name: deRegApp
deRegApp.syntax:
deRegApp(
[ ?viewType t_viewType ]
[ ?parentType t_parentType ]
[ ?appName t_appName ]
[ ?help t_help ]
[ ?dataTrigger s_dataTrigger ]
[ ?appTrigger s_appTrigger ]
[ ?enableTrigger s_enableTrigger ]
[ ?menuTrigger s_menuTrigger ]
[ ?postInstallTrigger s_postInstallTrigger ]
[ ?viewNameSwitchTrigger s_viewNameSwitchTrigger ]
[ ?widgetType t_widgetType ]
[ ?noCadenceMenu g_noCadenceMenu ]
[ ?windowBBoxProc s_function ]
[ ?appTitle t_appTitle ]
[ ?exclusive g_exclusive ]
) 
=> t / nil
deRegApp.desc: Registers the characteristics and entry points of applications so that they can be called in the appropriate situations.

deRemoveAppCapabilities.name: deRemoveAppCapabilities
deRemoveAppCapabilities.syntax:
deRemoveAppCapabilities(
t_viewType
[ ?newFile g_newFile ]
[ ?openFile g_openFile ]
)
=> t / nil
deRemoveAppCapabilities.desc: Removes the required application capabilities from the specified view type.

deUnRegApp.name: deUnRegApp
deUnRegApp.desc:
Un-registers the view type.

Only one application can currently be registered for each view type. If a second registration is attempted, an error results. To re-register a view type with different procedures, the view type must first be unregistered with this routine.

deRegUserTriggers.name: deRegUserTriggers
deRegUserTriggers.syntax:
deRegUserTriggers( 
t_viewType 
[ s_appTrigger [ s_menuTrigger [ s_postInstallTrigger ] ] ] 
) 
=> t / nil
deRegUserTriggers.desc: Registers user application, user menu, and user post install triggers.

deUnRegUserTriggers.name: deUnRegUserTriggers
deUnRegUserTriggers.desc: Removes any user triggers associated with t_viewType.

deInheritEnabling.name: deInheritEnabling
deInheritEnabling.desc: Enables t_viewType to depend on the enabling of its parent type. Thus, the user must have the parent application licensed in order to use the application. t_viewType must be a subclass of some other view type.

deUnInheritEnabling.name: deUnInheritEnabling
deUnInheritEnabling.desc: Removes the inheritance of enabling for t_viewType.

deInheritMenus.name: deInheritMenus
deInheritMenus.desc: Causes t_viewType to inherit the menus defined by its parent class.

deUnInheritMenus.name: deUnInheritMenus
deUnInheritMenus.desc: Removes the inheritance of menus for t_viewType.

deRegProbeTrigger.name: deRegProbeTrigger
deRegProbeTrigger.desc: Registers a probe trigger, s_probeTrigger, to be called after creating a new window or installing a new design in an existing window.

deGetAppInfo.name: deGetAppInfo
deGetAppInfo.desc: Returns the application registration information associated with t_viewType and its sub-view types.

deHiSetDefaultApplication.name: deHiSetDefaultApplication
deHiSetDefaultApplication.desc: Opens the Set Default Application form for the current cellview.

deSetWorkspace.name: deSetWorkspace
deSetWorkspace.desc: Sets a workspace name to a given window (as long as the workspace name is valid for that window).

deRegPlugin.name: deRegPlugin
deRegPlugin.syntax:
deRegPlugin(
t_appName
s_className
s_superClass
[ ?appTitle t_appTitle ]
[ ?bindkeys l_bindkeys ]
[ ?group t_group ]
[ ?help t_help ]
[ ?pluggableMainApps g_pluggableMainApps ]
[ ?pluggableViewTypes l_pluggableViewTypes ]
[ ?shortDescription t_shortDescription ]
[ ?excludeViewTypes l_excludeViewTypes ]
)
=> l_appClassInfo

deInstallPlugin.name: deInstallPlugin
deInstallPlugin.desc: Installs (or activates) the specified plugin in an application window associated with the given ID. For each session window, DE makes only one instance of a plugin. deInstallPlugin function installs a plugin in an application window. A session window can host multiple application windows. This means that if an instance of the plugin already exists in the specified window, the instance is returned. And, if there exists an instance in another tab of the same session window, the instance is shared.

deRemovePlugin.name: deRemovePlugin
deRemovePlugin.desc: Removes (or deactivates) the named plugin from the specified application window-session or tab window. If the ID is of a session window, the plugin is removed from all tab windows associated with the session window.

deFindPlugin.name: deFindPlugin
deFindPlugin.desc: Searches for and returns an instance of the specified plugin installed in the given application window

deBeginConfigurePlugins.name: deBeginConfigurePlugins
deBeginConfigurePlugins.desc: Lets applications issue a series of deInstallPlugin and deRemovePlugin calls to add or remove plugins in the specified application window. Using deBeginConfigurePlugins before adding or removing plugins helps in reducing calls to the hiApplyWinConfig SKILL function.

deEndConfigurePlugins.name: deEndConfigurePlugins
deEndConfigurePlugins.desc: Indicates an end to a series of calls for deInstallPlugin and deRemovePlugin marked by the deBeginConfigurePlugins in the same application window.

deFindAssistant.name: deFindAssistant
deFindAssistant.syntax:
deFindAssistant(
t_assistant
w_sessionWindow
[ ?search_object_name { t | nil } ]
[ ?search_window_name { t | nil } ]
[ ?in_active_tab { t | nil } ]
)
=> w_dwindow / nil
deFindAssistant.desc: Returns the dock window ID associated with the specified assistant name in the specified session window. By default, the function returns the assistant whose window name matches t_assistant in the currently active tab of w_sessionWindow. You can optionally widen the search to include object names in all tabs of the specified session window.

deGetPlugins.name: deGetPlugins
deGetPlugins.desc: Returns a list of all plugin instances installed in the given application window

deGetAppClassInfo.name: deGetAppClassInfo
deGetAppClassInfo.desc: Returns a copy of the registration information (DPL) associated with the given application

deoEnableTrigger.name: deoEnableTrigger
deoEnableTrigger.desc: Determines if the application is enabled for use by the current user. The enable trigger will normally do any appropriate security checks necessary to make this determination. Design Editor calls the enable trigger before installing a plugin and then installs the plugin only if this trigger returns a non-nil value. The default deoEnableTrigger permits a plugin to be installed on top of an application as long as it is pluggable to the application.

deoExitTrigger.name: deoExitTrigger
deoExitTrigger.desc: When a plugin is being removed from a window, Design Editor calls the exit trigger before disabling all GUI components of the plugin and removes the plugin only if this trigger returns a non-nil value. The return value of the exit trigger is ignored if the window on which the plugin is installed is being closed. The default implementation is a no-op, and always returns t.

deoGetAssistantList.name: deoGetAssistantList
deoGetAssistantList.desc: Returns a list of t_assistant_name and s_placement pairs (called an association list and contains a list of key and value pairs). The default implementation returns all assistants defined by this plugin and super-plugins.

deoGetBindkeys.name: deoGetBindkeys
deoGetBindkeys.desc: Returns a copy of bindkeys defined for the plugin in the format that is acceptable by hiSetBindKeys(). When installing a plugin, DE calls hiSetBindKeys using the value of deoGetBindkeys method. A default implementation of deoGetBindkeys is provided by DE, which returns a list of bindkeys collectively defined by a plugin and its super-plugin(s) through deRegPlugin ?bindkeys argument. The bindkeys returned are ordered from generic to specific.

deoMenuTrigger.name: deoMenuTrigger
deoMenuTrigger.desc: Returns a list of menus to be installed in the banner of a window. The menu trigger is called when the Design Editor installs and removes the plugin. Whenever there's an application switching event, deoMenuTrigger is called again for plugins that are pluggable to the application being switched into. For example, given a plugin whose pluggableViewTypes equals schematic, the plugin is pluggable to all schematic-based applications. So, if the plugin is currently installed in a VSE window then, if you launch VSE XL in the same window the menu trigger will be called again. Also push down, or return back into another schematic cell-view, the deoMenuTrigger is called again. The default deoMenuTrigger is a no-op. It returns args->bannerMenus as is.

deoOnTabSwitch.name: deoOnTabSwitch
deoOnTabSwitch.syntax:
deoOnTabSwitch(
g_application
w_sessionWin
w_intoWin
g_outofWin
)
=> g_value
deoOnTabSwitch.desc: An event notification function called during HI calling post tab switch procedures. The order in which calls are made to all deoOnTabSwitch functions is not defined.

deoOnApplicationChange.name: deoOnApplicationChange
deoOnApplicationChange.desc: An event notification function called when data or application changes in a window, such as when a user opens new data or installs a new application in a window, traverses down or up a design hierarchy, or opens another cellview. This function is called for all active plugins at the same time the DE change-application-trigger is called. The order in which calls are made to all deoOnApplicationChange functions is not defined.

deoPostInstallTrigger.name: deoPostInstallTrigger
deoPostInstallTrigger.desc: The post-install trigger is called after all other processing is done, including installation of banner menu, toolbar, assistant, bindkeys. This is provided for those applications that need to finish up any initialization that must occur after GUI is installed.

deoRequireToolbars.name: deoRequireToolbars
deoRequireToolbars.desc: Returns a list of toolbar names (string) that are to be customized by the plugin. A plugin can customize toolbars of a main application, or those of another plugin. For a plugin to declare which toolbars need customization, re-define method deoRequireToolbars.

deoUpdateToolbar.name: deoUpdateToolbar
deoUpdateToolbar.syntax:
deoUpdateToolbar(
g_plugin
t_name
o_toolbar
l_args
)
=> g_value
deoUpdateToolbar.desc: Customizes a toolbar that is requested by deoRequireToolbars. DE calls this method during installing and removing a plugin.

deoOnEvent.name: deoOnEvent
deoOnEvent.desc: This event handler can be reimplemented in a subclass to receive various events.

deFileNew.name: deFileNew
deFileNew.desc: Opens the Create New File form.

deOpen.name: deOpen
deOpen.syntax:
deOpen( 
[ l_fileSpec [ g_winSpec [ t_accessMode [ t_appName g_sessionWindow g_saveSessionHistory] ] ] ] 
) 
=> w_window / nil
deOpen.desc: Takes a design specification and a window specification and attempts to install the design in the specified window.

args.name: l_fileSpec [ g_winSpec [ t_accessMode [ t_appName g_sessionWindow g_saveSessionHistory] ] ]

deFileOpen.name: deFileOpen
deFileOpen.desc: Similar to deOpen(). Radio buttons on the Open form are displayed that allow selection between opening the cellview in a new tab, current tab, or a new window.

deNew.name: deNew
deNew.syntax:
deNew( 
[ l_fileSpec ] 
[ g_winSpec ] 
[ t_accessMode ] 
[ t_appName ] 
) 
=> w_windowId / nil
deNew.desc: Creates a new cellview and opens it in a window.

deNewCellView.name: deNewCellView
deNewCellView.syntax:
deNewCellView( 
t_libName 
t_cellName 
t_viewName 
t_viewType 
g_winSpec 
)
=> w_windowId / nil
deNewCellView.desc: Creates a new cellview and opens it in a window.

deOpenCellView.name: deOpenCellView
deOpenCellView.syntax:
deOpenCellView( 
t_libName 
t_cellName 
t_viewName 
t_viewType 
g_winSpec 
t_accessMode 
)
=> w_windowId / nil
deOpenCellView.desc: Opens an existing cellview in a window.

deBack.name: deBack
deBack.desc: This API allows you to go back to a particular window event. It takes two optional integer arguments, w_window and numSteps. If deBack is called without any arguments it will open and display the cellview that was displayed prior to the current cellview in the current window.

deForward.name: deForward
deForward.desc: Allows you to go forward to a particular window event. It takes two optional integer argument; w_window and numSteps. If the command is called without any arguments it will open and display the cellview that was displayed prior to the use of the last deBack command in the current window.

dePush.name: dePush
dePush.syntax:
dePush( 
[ l_fileSpec [ g_winSpec [ t_accessMode [ t_appName ] ] ] ] 
) 
=> w_window / nil
dePush.desc: The same as deOpen, except that if the window already exists, the current contents are not removed. Instead the new design is pushed on top of the existing one.

deSetHistoryOpenMode.name: deSetHistoryOpenMode
deSetHistoryOpenMode.desc: Controls whether designs are opened from history in a new tab or a new window. The setting applies equally to opening a design from the CIW as well as from a session window.

deSwap.name: deSwap
deSwap.syntax:
deSwap( 
[ l_fileSpec [ g_winSpec [ t_accessMode [ t_appName] ] ] ] 
) 
=> w_window / nil
deSwap.desc: This function is same as deOpen, except that if the window already exists, the current contents are not removed. Instead the current stack item is replaced with the new design.

deToggleAssistants.name: deToggleAssistants
deToggleAssistants.desc: Toggles the visibility of the current assistants off or on to maximize the size of the design window.

deToggleAssistantVisibility.name: deToggleAssistantVisibility
deToggleAssistantVisibility.desc: Toggles the visibility of the given assistant in the given session window.

deToggleToolbars.name: deToggleToolbars
deToggleToolbars.desc: Toggles the currently visible toolbars off. If no visible toolbars are found, toggles the previously hidden toolbars on.

deFindToolbar.name: deFindToolbar
deFindToolbar.desc: Searches for and returns an instance of the specified toolbar installed in the given session window. This function also supports the Virtuoso design editor toolbars, such as Workspaces, Go, and Bookmarks.

deManageToolbar.name: deManageToolbar
deManageToolbar.syntax:
deManageToolbar( 
w_sessionWindow
o_toolbar
[ g_appName ]
)
=> t / nil
deManageToolbar.desc: Puts the toolbar handle on the given session window (under DE management) for the specified application. A managed toolbar is displayed as a menu item in Window-Toolbars and in the context menu of the session window.

deCustomizeToolbars.name: deCustomizeToolbars
deCustomizeToolbars.syntax:
deCustomizeToolbars( 
[ ?app t_appName ]
[ ?toolbar t_toolbar ]
[ ?toolbarItem t_toolbarItem ]
)
=> t / nil
deCustomizeToolbars.desc: Invokes the Toolbar Manager graphical user interface for customizing toolbars in the Virtuoso environment.

deUnmanageToolbar.name: deUnmanageToolbar
deUnmanageToolbar.syntax:
deUnmanageToolbar( 
w_sessionWindow
s_toolbar
[ g_appName ]
)
=> t / nil
deUnmanageToolbar.desc: Removes the toolbar from the given session window (under DE management) for the specified application. A toolbar should be removed using the deUnmanageToolbar function before it can be deleted.

deEditInPlace.name: deEditInPlace
deEditInPlace.syntax:
deEditInPlace( 
w_window 
[ l_fileSpec [ t_accessMode [ t_appName ] ] ] 
) 
=> w_window / nil
deEditInPlace.desc: Requires that w_window exists and has at least one stack element.

deReturn.name: deReturn
deReturn.desc: Pops the window stack one or more levels.

deCopy.name: deCopy
deCopy.desc: Makes a complete copy of the given window, including its stack and the context data stored on it.

dataTrigger.name: dataTrigger
dataTrigger.desc: The data trigger is called after the DE has collected and verified all of the trigger arguments, checked for the proper application registration, and opened or validated a window for the design.

appTrigger.name: appTrigger
appTrigger.desc: The application trigger is responsible for any necessary banner setup (except for menus), installing the window popup menu, and other application-specific initialization. It is also responsible for managing the application context.

userAppTrigger.name: userAppTrigger
userAppTrigger.desc: After the application trigger is called, the user application trigger is called with the same argument list. The user application trigger allows clients to subclass existing application triggers, and thus add additional context to that already managed by the application. The user application trigger's return value is ignored, but should indicate t for success and nil for failure.

enableTrigger.name: enableTrigger
enableTrigger.desc: The enable trigger is a special routine loaded separately from the application context, normally by an autoload file.

menuTrigger.name: menuTrigger
menuTrigger.desc: The menu trigger is called when an application is about to be installed as the current application in a window. At the time the menu trigger is called, all other triggers have already been called, and the window is about to be displayed (or if the window was a previously existing window, about to be refreshed).

userMenuTrigger.name: userMenuTrigger
userMenuTrigger.desc: The user menu trigger is called just before the application menu trigger is called and performs the same function. This trigger allows the user to attach menus to an application. Although it is called prior to the application menu trigger, the menu list it returns is appended after the application menus.

postInstallTrigger.name: postInstallTrigger
postInstallTrigger.desc: Enables application to do processing, such as adding menu items to an existing menu, that cannot be done before all other processing is complete, including installation of banner menus and the display of the window.

userPostInstallTriggers.name: userPostInstallTriggers
userPostInstallTriggers.desc: Called immediately after the post-install trigger. It serves the same function but is intended for use only by the customer.

probeTrigger.name: probeTrigger
probeTrigger.syntax:
probeTrigger( 
w_window 
s_action 
[ w_source ] 
) 
=> t / nil
probeTrigger.desc: The probe trigger is called when the Design Editor has installed a new design in a window, whether an existing one or a new one. It is also called when the window is closed. This trigger allows the probing mechanism to keep its data structures consistent without requiring each application to call it separately.

lbuiGetCheckedOutLicenses.name: lbuiGetCheckedOutLicenses
lbuiGetCheckedOutLicenses.desc: Returns a list of the licenses consisting of each license feature name and the number of licenses (tokens) checked out.

lbuiPrintLicenseUseReport.name: lbuiPrintLicenseUseReport
lbuiPrintLicenseUseReport.desc: Displays the license usage report (for example: user logins, host names, display time, number of licenses, and license version) in the CIW or the specified output log file.

iclicCheckOutAndLock.name: iclicCheckOutAndLock
iclicCheckOutAndLock.desc: Checks out the specified layout license, layout option license, or an appropriate higher-tier license and locks it after successful checkout.

eliCheckOutAndLock.name: eliCheckOutAndLock
eliCheckOutAndLock.desc: Checks out and locks the specified license feature. After the specified license feature is locked, it cannot be checked in until the session ends. Use this function in a scripted batch process to reduce runtime due to licensing.

deGetCellView.name: deGetCellView
deGetCellView.desc: Returns the cellview for the item on the window stack corresponding to x_level. A value of nil is returned if the stack is empty, x_level is not a valid stack level in w_window, or x_level is -1. If x_level is defaulted or nil then the current item on the stack is used.

deGetEditCellView.name: deGetEditCellView
deGetEditCellView.desc: Returns the cellview for the item on the window stack corresponding to the current edit level. nil is returned if the stack is empty.

deSetCellView.name: deSetCellView
deSetCellView.syntax:
deSetCellView( 
[ w_window [ d_cellview [ x_level ] ] ] 
) 
=> t / nil
deSetCellView.desc: Replaces the cellview for the current item on the window stack. nil is returned if the stack is empty. This routine is intended for use by data triggers executing the 'swap operation. It should never be called by an application outside of a data trigger.

deGetViewType.name: deGetViewType
deGetViewType.desc: Returns the view type of the item at x_level in w_window. nil is returned if the stack is empty. If x_level is not specified, the current level is assumed.

deGetEditViewType.name: deGetEditViewType
deGetEditViewType.desc: Returns the t_viewType of the item at the current edit level in w_window.

deGetRootType.name: deGetRootType
deGetRootType.desc: Returns the root class t_viewType of the item at x_level in w_window. nil is returned if the stack is empty. If x_level is not specified, the current level is assumed.

deGetEditRootType.name: deGetEditRootType
deGetEditRootType.desc: Returns the root class view type of the item at the current edit level in w_window.

deGetContext.name: deGetContext
deGetContext.desc: Returns the context for the item on the window stack corresponding to x_level. A value of nil is returned if the stack is empty or x_level is -1. If x_level is not specified or is nil, the current item on the stack is used.

deGetEditContext.name: deGetEditContext
deGetEditContext.desc: Returns the context for the item on the window stack corresponding to the current edit level.

deIsEditInContext.name: deIsEditInContext
deIsEditInContext.desc: Tells whether the current edit cellview in the window is in the context of a Hierarchy Manager configuration.

deSetContext.name: deSetContext
deSetContext.syntax:
deSetContext( 
[ w_window [ g_context [ x_level ] ] ] 
) 
=> t / nil
deSetContext.desc: Replaces the context for the item at the specified level on the window stack. nil is returned if the stack is empty. This routine is intended for use by data triggers executing the 'swap operation. It should never be called by application code outside of a data trigger.

deGetMaxInContextLevel.name: deGetMaxInContextLevel
deGetMaxInContextLevel.desc: Gets the maximum level of the given window that is being edited in the context of the Hierarchy Manager configuration ID associated with the window. If the window has no configuration ID, 0 is returned.

deGetConfigId.name: deGetConfigId
deGetConfigId.desc: Gets the Hierarchy Manager configuration ID associated with the given window.

deSetConfigId.name: deSetConfigId
deSetConfigId.desc: Sets the Hierarchy Manager configuration ID associated with the given window. Also creates a path vector and sets the window path vector. If g_hdbConfigId is nil, the window path vector is destroyed, and the window configuration ID is set to nil.

deGetVector.name: deGetVector
deGetVector.desc: Gets the Hierarchy Manager path vector associated with the given window.

deGetEIP.name: deGetEIP
deGetEIP.desc: Returns the edit-in-place state for the item on the window stack corresponding to x_level. The edit-in-place state is t if that stack level was created by the deEditInPlace function and nil otherwise. f nil is returned if the stack is empty or x_level is -1. If x_level is not specified or is nil then the current item on the stack is used.

deGetPushed.name: deGetPushed
deGetPushed.desc: Returns the pushed state for the item on the window stack corresponding to x_level. The pushed state is t if that x_level is any level other than the current edit level and nil otherwise. nil is returned if the stack is empty or x_level is -1. If x_level is defaulted or is nil then the current item on the stack is used.

deGetProbeContext.name: deGetProbeContext
deGetProbeContext.desc: Returns the probe context for the window.

deSetProbeContext.name: deSetProbeContext
deSetProbeContext.desc: Sets the probe context for the window. This is normally executed only by the probing implementation in the probe trigger.

deGetEditLevel.name: deGetEditLevel
deGetEditLevel.desc: Returns the current edit level of w_window. If the stack is empty, the routine returns -1. The current edit level is the level of the stack which is currently being displayed. This is normally the maximum edit level, unless deGoToLevel was executed.

deGetMaxEditLevel.name: deGetMaxEditLevel
deGetMaxEditLevel.desc: Returns the highest edit level of w_window. If the stack is empty, returns -1.

deEnableApp.name: deEnableApp
deEnableApp.desc: Enables the application registered with t_appName in w_window. It affects only the customizer menu in w_window. It is available to allow certain applications to be enabled depending on run-time state associated with a particular design.

deDisableApp.name: deDisableApp
deDisableApp.desc: Enables the application registered with t_appName in w_window. It affects only the customizer menu in w_window. It is available to allow certain applications to be disabled depending on run-time state associated with a particular design.

deInstallApp.name: deInstallApp
deInstallApp.desc: Switches the current application in w_window to t_appName. The enable trigger is called before switching, and if it returns nil, the switch is aborted. Otherwise, the application menus and bindkeys are installed as if the user had executed the corresponding customizer item.

deGetAllApplicationNames.name: deGetAllApplicationNames
deGetAllApplicationNames.desc: Returns a list of all applications that can be associated with the given root view type.

deGetAllRootTypes.name: deGetAllRootTypes
deGetAllRootTypes.desc: Returns a list of all currently registered root view types.

deGetAllViewTypes.name: deGetAllViewTypes
deGetAllViewTypes.desc: Returns a list of all fully registered view types and view sub types. Any view sub type for which some parent has not been registered will not appear in this list.

deGetRootViewTypeList.name: deGetRootViewTypeList
deGetRootViewTypeList.desc: Returns a list of root view types, which have an associated tool as specified in the tool registry.

deMapUserTypeToViewType.name: deMapUserTypeToViewType
deMapUserTypeToViewType.desc: Maps a user type to the dfII_viewType.

deMapViewTypeToUserType.name: deMapViewTypeToUserType
deMapViewTypeToUserType.desc: Maps the dfII_viewType to the user type.

deViewTypeIsRegistered.name: deViewTypeIsRegistered
deViewTypeIsRegistered.desc: Returns a non-nil value if t_viewType is fully registered; that is, all ancestors up to and including the root type are currently registered.

deGetLowerTierApp.name: deGetLowerTierApp
deGetLowerTierApp.desc: Returns a list of application names, which are x_lowerBy levels lower in tier in the same family of given t_appName. The default value for x_lowerBy is one.

dplp.name: dplp
dplp.desc: Checks whether the specified argument is a disembodied property list, a list of symbol or value pairs that is not attached to a specific object or symbol.

hiAddExtraRepeatCommand.name: hiAddExtraRepeatCommand
hiAddExtraRepeatCommand.desc: Adds the specified SKILL command to the extra repeat command list so that the command becomes repeatable next time the hiRepeat function is called. Additionally, you can add the specified commands to the extra repeat command list that are not repeated automatically after there first run.

hiAddNonRepeatPrefix.name: hiAddNonRepeatPrefix
hiAddNonRepeatPrefix.desc: Adds a string to the list of repeat filter strings. All strings is compared on every command run.

hiBoxCenter.name: hiBoxCenter
hiBoxCenter.desc: Returns the center point of a bounding box.

hiDisplaySaveForRestoreDialog.name: hiDisplaySaveForRestoreDialog
hiDisplaySaveForRestoreDialog.desc: Displays the Save Session Form, which lets you specify the file in which to save your session information. This function is the programmatic equivalent of selecting Options - Save Session in the CIW.

hiEditfile.name: hiEditfile
hiEditfile.desc: Brings up the Specify a File to Edit form in which you can specify the file you want to edit and then calls the edit function on the file.

hiEnqueueCmd.name: hiEnqueueCmd
hiEnqueueCmd.desc: Adds t_command, which is to be run after returning from the current function and re-entering the event loop, to the command queue.

hiFlush.name: hiFlush
hiFlush.desc: Synchronizes event queues and processes all exposure events. This ensures that newly exposed or updated windows and forms are drawn. This function is used primarily for quicktests.

hiFlushCIW.name: hiFlushCIW
hiFlushCIW.desc: Flushes any buffered output to the CIW (Command Interpreter Window). The function also processes the input and timer events. To avoid any additional event processing use the hiFlushInfo function.

hiFlushInfo.name: hiFlushInfo
hiFlushInfo.desc: Processes exposure events to allow the output of the previous program to be displayed in the CIW during SKILL code processing.

hiFlushLogFile.name: hiFlushLogFile
hiFlushLogFile.desc: Flushes the contents of the main file and any open secondary log files.

hiFocusToCIW.name: hiFocusToCIW
hiFocusToCIW.desc: Temporarily refocuses the input window to the CIW until a return is entered.

hiGetAttention.name: hiGetAttention
hiGetAttention.desc: Rings the bell in the keyboard or terminal.

hiGetMouseMoveSampleRate.name: hiGetMouseMoveSampleRate
hiGetMouseMoveSampleRate.desc: Gets the current mouse sample rate.

hiGetMouseStopDetectTime.name: hiGetMouseStopDetectTime
hiGetMouseStopDetectTime.desc: Checks if the mouse is working using the current setting (in milliseconds).

hiGetMultiClickTime.name: hiGetMultiClickTime
hiGetMultiClickTime.desc: Returns the number of milliseconds that must elapse before a mouse click is recognized as a single click rather than the second click of a double click.

hiGetNonRepeatPrefixes.name: hiGetNonRepeatPrefixes
hiGetNonRepeatPrefixes.desc: Returns list of hiRepeat filter strings.

hiGetScreenSize.name: hiGetScreenSize
hiGetScreenSize.desc: Returns the size of the current display screen as a list of two lists, the first being the width and height in pixels, the second being the width and height in millimeters.

hiGetBannerPoint.name: hiGetBannerPoint
hiGetBannerPoint.desc: Retrieves the X:Y location value stored in the banner of the specified window. If the window ID is not specified, Virtuoso returns the location of the current window.

hiGetBeepVolume.name: hiGetBeepVolume
hiGetBeepVolume.desc: Retrieves the loudness of the beep.

hiGetCommandPoint.name: hiGetCommandPoint
hiGetCommandPoint.desc: Gets the location where the cursor was the last time a mouse button or keyboard key was pressed, but only until the cursor leaves that window.

hiGetCIWindow.name: hiGetCIWindow
hiGetCIWindow.desc: Retrieves the window identity of the CIW.

hiGetExtraRepeatCommands.name: hiGetExtraRepeatCommands
hiGetExtraRepeatCommands.desc: Retrieves all commands added by the hiAddExtraRepeatCommand SKILL function in the extra repeat command list.

hiGetPoint.name: hiGetPoint
hiGetPoint.desc: Retrieves the xy position for the current location of the cursor within the boundaries of the window. It returns the xy position even if the cursor is in another window or form that is covering the specified window, as long as the cursor is within the boundaries of the specified window.

hiGetRepeatCommand.name: hiGetRepeatCommand
hiGetRepeatCommand.desc: Returns the command that would be run by hiRepeat, which the command that was last run in the CIW.

hiGraphicMode.name: hiGraphicMode
hiGraphicMode.desc: Checks if the Virtuoso environment is currently running in graphical mode. Returns nil if it is running in -nograph mode.

hiInsertBlankCIWOutputPage.name: hiInsertBlankCIWOutputPage
hiInsertBlankCIWOutputPage.desc: Inserts a blank page in the CIW output area.

hiIsExtraRepeatCommand.name: hiIsExtraRepeatCommand
hiIsExtraRepeatCommand.desc: Checks whether the specified SKILL command is in the extra repeat command list.

hiQuit.name: hiQuit
hiQuit.desc: Quits the Virtuoso session. It displays a dialog box to confirm if you wish to quit and then calls exit if you click Yes.

hiRegTimer.name: hiRegTimer
hiRegTimer.desc: Registers a SKILL function string that is initialized after the specified time.

hiRemoveExtraRepeatCommand.name: hiRemoveExtraRepeatCommand
hiRemoveExtraRepeatCommand.desc: Removes the specified SKILL command from the extra repeat command list. The commands in this list are added using hiAddExtraRepeatCommand. When the command is removed it becomes unrepeatable.

hiRemoveNonRepeatPrefix.name: hiRemoveNonRepeatPrefix
hiRemoveNonRepeatPrefix.desc: Removes a repeat filter prefix that has been previously added using hiAddNonRepeatPrefix.

hiRepeat.name: hiRepeat
hiRepeat.desc: Re-runs the last command run in the CIW.

hiSaveForRestore.name: hiSaveForRestore
hiSaveForRestore.desc: Saves your session information in the file you specify. This function is the programmatic equivalent of selecting the Options - Save Sessions command in the CIW and saving a file in the Save Sessions form that appears.

hiScaleBox.name: hiScaleBox
hiScaleBox.desc: Returns a bounding box that has the same center point as the bounding box passed, but whose sides are scaled by 1/n_scale.

hiSetBeepVolume.name: hiSetBeepVolume
hiSetBeepVolume.desc: Sets the loudness of the beep when a default in the system is detected.

hiSetMouseMoveSampleRate.name: hiSetMouseMoveSampleRate
hiSetMouseMoveSampleRate.desc: Sets the number of mouse motion events to be processed.

hiSetMouseStopDetectTime.name: hiSetMouseStopDetectTime
hiSetMouseStopDetectTime.desc: Sets the stop detection time to detect if a mouse has stopped moving.

hiSetMultiClickTime.name: hiSetMultiClickTime
hiSetMultiClickTime.desc: Sets the number of milliseconds that must elapse before a mouse click is recognized as a separate single click rather than the second click of a double click.

hiSetUserPreferences.name: hiSetUserPreferences
hiSetUserPreferences.desc: Displays the User Preferences form with the latest values.

hiSetWindowDefaultPrompt.name: hiSetWindowDefaultPrompt
hiSetWindowDefaultPrompt.desc: Sets the prompt for the window associated with the given window ID instead of the default SKILL prompt. The function returns either the value of the previously set prompt or nil. If you specify an empty string for t_prompt, the function resets the prompt to the default value, which is the SKILL prompt.

hiSetWindowFocus.name: hiSetWindowFocus
hiSetWindowFocus.desc: Sets the focus to the window associated with the given window ID.

hiSynchronize.name: hiSynchronize
hiSynchronize.desc: Flushes the event queue by calling QApplication::flush().

hiSync.name: hiSync
hiSync.desc: For programs with several GUI-related creation and deletion operations running in a loop, Qt objects deferred to be deleted later may accumulate and affect performance. This function solves this issue by forcing Qt to immediately delete these objects.

hiCheckAbort.name: hiCheckAbort
hiCheckAbort.desc: Returns the value of the global abort flag.

hiGetUserAbort.name: hiGetUserAbort
hiGetUserAbort.desc: Aborts a procedure when Ctrl+C is pressed.

hiResetAbort.name: hiResetAbort
hiResetAbort.desc: Sets the global abort flag to nil. This flag can be set to t by calling hiSetAbort.

hiSetAbort.name: hiSetAbort
hiSetAbort.desc: Sets the global abort flag to t. This flag can be set to nil by calling hiResetAbort.

hiEndLog.name: hiEndLog
hiEndLog.desc: Stops writing the transaction log to the file specified by hiStartLog.

hiGetLogFileName.name: hiGetLogFileName
hiGetLogFileName.desc: Returns the rooted file name of the Virtuoso session log file.

hiIsInReplay.name: hiIsInReplay
hiIsInReplay.desc: Indicates whether your Virtuoso session is in replay mode, that is, if commands are being executed from a replay file, which is typically a log file. Your session is in replay mode if you are running a Virtuoso workbench with the -replay logfile or -test option or if you are replaying a file with the hiReplayFile SKILL function.

hiLogDragEvents.name: hiLogDragEvents
hiLogDragEvents.desc: Starts logging drag events (mouse movements in a graphics window while an enter function is active) in the log file so that they can be replayed later.

hiPrintToLogFile.name: hiPrintToLogFile
hiPrintToLogFile.desc: Prints the specified string to the CDS.log file and to any secondary log files that might have been opened with hiStartLog, without displaying it in the CIW output area.

hiReplayFile.name: hiReplayFile
hiReplayFile.desc: Replays a log file. Use this function only for testing or debugging. In general, use the functions load or loading instead of hiReplayFile. hiReplayFile is intended to be run only from a Command Interpreter Window.

hiSetFilter.name: hiSetFilter
hiSetFilter.desc: Sets the output message filter for the CIW with the option specified by t_filter. The output area of the CIW is refreshed immediately. If no option is specified, the Set Log File Display Filter form appears allowing you to specify the display options you want.

hiSetFilterOptions.name: hiSetFilterOptions
hiSetFilterOptions.syntax:
hiSetFilterOptions(
g_accelInput
g_prompt
g_output
g_returnAccel
g_typedReturn
g_errorOutput
g_warnOutput
) 
=> t / nil
hiSetFilterOptions.desc: Sets the output message filter for the CIW with the specified options. This function corresponds to the Set Log File Display Filter form (displayed by choosing Options - Log Filter in the CIW). Standard message output, return values from typed-in commands, errors and warning messages are displayed by default.

hiStartLog.name: hiStartLog
hiStartLog.desc: Writes a transaction log to a file.

hiGetBBoxResource.name: hiGetBBoxResource
hiGetBBoxResource.desc: Returns the bounding box specification defined in the .Xdefaults file for the specified resource.

hiGetGeometryResource.name: hiGetGeometryResource
hiGetGeometryResource.desc: Gets geometry resources from the X resource database.

hiGetStringResource.name: hiGetStringResource
hiGetStringResource.desc: Gets resources from the resource database of the X Window System.

hiGetFont.name: hiGetFont
hiGetFont.desc: Returns the font type (if valid), or a list of valid font types if t_fontType is all. This function is being provided for compatibility with previous releases and should no longer be used.

hiGetFontInfo.name: hiGetFontInfo
hiGetFontInfo.desc: Returns the Disembodied Property List (DPL), which contains the name, size, weight, and italic style along with the description of the font.

hiGetXFontName.name: hiGetXFontName
hiGetXFontName.desc: Returns the default font name for the specified font type that was used prior to TrueType fonts.

hiGetTextWidth.name: hiGetTextWidth
hiGetTextWidth.desc: Returns the width, in pixels, of a string of characters that has a specified font.

hiQueryFont.name: hiQueryFont
hiQueryFont.desc: Returns the values of the attributes of S_fontType.

hiSetFont.name: hiSetFont
hiSetFont.syntax:
hiSetFont(
[ S_fontType 
?name t_fontName 
?size x_fontSize 
?bold g_useBold 
?italic g_useItalics 
?fontInfo l_fontInfoDpl ] 
) 
=> t / nil
hiSetFont.desc: Sets the required font attributes, such as font name, font size, or font weight for label, text, or ciw. If no argument is specified, then the Set Fonts window is displayed. In this window, you can set any of the valid fonts and click the Apply button to save the changes. If any of the key arguments is specified in this function, then it is mandatory to specify S_fontType.

args.name:
S_fontType 
?name t_fontName 
?size x_fontSize 
?bold g_useBold 
?italic g_useItalics 
?fontInfo l_fontInfoDpl

hiTextWidth.name: hiTextWidth
hiTextWidth.desc: Determines the width, in pixels, of a string of characters that has a specified font. Returns nil if the font type is not valid.

envCyclicStringToIndex.name: envCyclicStringToIndex
envCyclicStringToIndex.desc: Returns the index of the string for the given cyclic variable. This order is determined by the order of choices specified in the tool's registration file. The index is 0-based. -1 is returned for an invalid choice.

envCyclicIndexToString.name: envCyclicIndexToString
envCyclicIndexToString.desc: Returns the string choice associated with a particular index. This order is determined by the order of choices specified in the tool's registration file. The index is 0-based. -1 is returned for an invalid choice.

envGetAvailableTools.name: envGetAvailableTools
envGetAvailableTools.desc: Allows users to know which tools are available to be loaded.

envGetDefVal.name: envGetDefVal
envGetDefVal.desc: Retrieves the registered default value for a variable. The tool is faulted in if it is not already faulted in, where faulting in is the process of reading the .cdsenv file and initializing the variables.

envGetLoadedTools.name: envGetLoadedTools
envGetLoadedTools.desc: Allows users to know which tools have currently been loaded.

envGetModifiedTools.name: envGetModifiedTools
envGetModifiedTools.desc: Returns a list of all tools with modified variables.

envGetVal.name: envGetVal
envGetVal.desc: Retrieves the value of an environment variable. The tool is faulted in if it is not already faulted in, where faulting in is the process of reading the .cdsenv file and initializing the variables.

envGetVarType.name: envGetVarType
envGetVarType.desc: Returns the type of the variable specified. This query loads the tool, if it has not already been loaded.

envIsToolModified.name: envIsToolModified
envIsToolModified.desc: Checks if any of the variables for a specified tool have been modified.

envIsVal.name: envIsVal
envIsVal.syntax:
envIsVal(
t_tool[.Partition]
t_varName
[ g_faultIn ]
)
=> t / nil
envIsVal.desc: Indicates whether a particular variable has been loaded and whether it exists for the given tool[.partition].

envLoadFile.name: envLoadFile
envLoadFile.desc: Specifies that a set of environment variables is to be loaded from a specified file. This function is equivalent to calling envLoadVals( ) with the ?tool argument set to ALL. All values loaded is marked as modified.

envLoadVals.name: envLoadVals
envLoadVals.desc: Specifies that a set of environment variables is to be loaded from a specified file.

envRegLoadDumpTrigger.name: envRegLoadDumpTrigger
envRegLoadDumpTrigger.syntax:
envRegLoadDumpTrigger(
?tool t_toolName 
?loadFunc s_loadFunc 
?dumpFunc s_dumpFunc
?preDumpFunc s_preDumpFunc
)
=> t / nil
envRegLoadDumpTrigger.desc: Registers the trigger function to be called when a tool's environment variables are loaded or saved to a file. Both the load and dump trigger functions are called after the load or dump of the environment variables, respectively. The preDump trigger is called just before the dump occurs. The dump trigger can be used to update the defValues of forms when a saving of defaults is performed.

envRegSetTrigger.name: envRegSetTrigger
envRegSetTrigger.desc: Registers a set trigger function for a tool. This trigger is called after an environment variable is set. You can set only one trigger for a tool. Subsequent calls to envRegSetTrigger for the same t_tool returns nil, indicating that the trigger was not set.

envSetToolCurrValToDefault.name: envSetToolCurrValToDefault
envSetToolCurrValToDefault.desc: Sets the current value of all the environment variables to the default values.

envSetToolDefaultToCurrVal.name: envSetToolDefaultToCurrVal
envSetToolDefaultToCurrVal.desc: Sets the default value of all the environment variables to the current value of the variables.

envSetVal.name: envSetVal
envSetVal.syntax:
envSetVal(
t_tool[.Partition]
t_varName
s_varType
g_newVal
) 
=> t / nil
envSetVal.desc: Sets an environment variable value in the setup database. The tool is faulted in if it is not already faulted in, where faulting in is the process of reading the .cdsenv file and initializing the variables. If a set trigger function is registered for this variable (see the  envRegSetTrigger function), it gets called after the value is set.

envSetVarCurrValToDefault.name: envSetVarCurrValToDefault
envSetVarCurrValToDefault.desc: Sets the current value of the environment variable you specify to the default value.

envSetVarDefaultToCurrVal.name: envSetVarDefaultToCurrVal
envSetVarDefaultToCurrVal.desc: Sets the default value of the environment variable you specify to the current value of the variable.

envStoreEnv.name: envStoreEnv
envStoreEnv.syntax:
envStoreEnv(
[ ?envFile t_fileName ] 
[ ?tool t_tool[.partition] ] 
[ ?toolStatus t_toolStatus ]
[ ?varStatus s_varStatus ]
[ ?fileStatus t_fileStatus ]
)
=> t / nil
envStoreEnv.desc: Stores environment variables associated with tools to a specific file. You can choose to save variables for a specific tool, all loaded tools, or all possible tools. You can also specify whether you want to save all the variables for a tool, the variables that have been modified, or only the variables that have been modified and that are different from the default value.

envUnregLoadDumpTrigger.name: envUnregLoadDumpTrigger
envUnregLoadDumpTrigger.syntax:
envUnregLoadDumpTrigger(
?tool t_toolName 
?loadFunc s_loadFunc 
?dumpFunc s_dumpFunc
?preDumpFunc s_preDumpFunc
)
=> t / nil
envUnregLoadDumpTrigger.desc: Deregisters the specified trigger functions for the specified tool. The specified functions are deleted from the corresponding list of the trigger functions for the tool.

envUnregSetTrigger.name: envUnregSetTrigger
envUnregSetTrigger.desc: Deregisters the specified set trigger function for the specified tool. The specified function is deleted from the list of the set trigger functions for the tool.

hiAddMenuItem.name: hiAddMenuItem
hiAddMenuItem.desc: Adds the menu item or action to the end of all instances of the specified hiMenu.

hiCreate2DMenu.name: hiCreate2DMenu
hiCreate2DMenu.desc: Creates a two-dimensional popup menu. Once this menu is created, you can display it with hiDisplayMenu or associate it with a window using hiSetWindowMenu.

hiCreateHorizontalFixedMenu.name: hiCreateHorizontalFixedMenu
hiCreateHorizontalFixedMenu.syntax:
hiCreateHorizontalFixedMenu(
s_menuHandle 
l_menuItems 
x_rows 
x_cols 
[ S_doneCallback ]
[ s_showTextWithIcon ]
) 
=> r_hiMenu
hiCreateHorizontalFixedMenu.desc: Creates a horizontal fixed menu that is a free-floating menu unattached to any application window. The fixed menu is created as a grid of row x column dimensions, and contains menu item objects created by hiCreateMenuItem. An additional Done item is added as the last item. Selecting Done removes the fixed menu from the screen.

hiCreateMenu.name: hiCreateMenu
hiCreateMenu.desc: Returns the SKILL representation of a popup menu. Once this menu is created, you can display it with hiDisplayMenu or associate it with a window using hiSetWindowMenu.

hiCreateMenuItem.name: hiCreateMenuItem
hiCreateMenuItem.syntax:
hiCreateMenuItem(
?name s_itemHandle 
?itemText t_menuItemText 
[ ?itemIcon g_menuIcon ] 
[ ?callback t_itemCallback ]
[ ?disable g_disabled ] 
[ ?statusTip t_statusTip ]
[ ?font t_font ]
) 
=> r_hiMenuItem
hiCreateMenuItem.desc: Creates a menu item that can be used in any type of menu, except two-dimensional menus and simple menus.

hiCreatePulldownMenu.name: hiCreatePulldownMenu
hiCreatePulldownMenu.desc: Creates a pulldown menu that contains text, icon, or slider menu items. s_menuHandle is the SKILL symbol set to the created menu.

hiCreateSimpleMenu.name: hiCreateSimpleMenu
hiCreateSimpleMenu.syntax:
hiCreateSimpleMenu(
s_menuHandle 
t_menuTitle 
l_menuItems 
l_menuItemCallbacks 
) 
=> r_hiMenu
hiCreateSimpleMenu.desc: Returns the SKILL description of a simple menu, which is a single level menu containing only text menu items, none of which invoke a submenu. Once this menu is created, you can display it with hiDisplayMenu or associate it with a window using hiSetWindowMenu.

hiCreateSeparatorMenuItem.name: hiCreateSeparatorMenuItem
hiCreateSeparatorMenuItem.desc: Creates a menu separator-a horizontal line that separates menu items. This menu item is used in the l_menuItems argument of the hiCreateMenu and hiCreatePulldownMenu functions. You can use the separator menu item in more than one menu or in multiple locations in the same menu.

hiCreateSliderMenuItem.name: hiCreateSliderMenuItem
hiCreateSliderMenuItem.syntax:
hiCreateSliderMenuItem(
?name s_itemHandle 
?itemText t_menuItemText 
?subMenu r_pulldownMenu 
[ ?itemIcon l_menuIcon ]
[ ?disable g_disabled ]
[ ?statusTip t_statusTip ]
[ ?font t_font ]
) 
=> r_hiSliderItem
hiCreateSliderMenuItem.desc: Creates a slider menu item that is used in functions that create a menu, all menus except simple or 2D menus. Slider menu items bring up submenus when selected. They can contain text (t_menuItemText) or icon (l_menuIcon) information.

hiCreateTypeinMenuItem.name: hiCreateTypeinMenuItem
hiCreateTypeinMenuItem.syntax:
hiCreateTypeinMenuItem(
?name s_name 
[ ?itemIcon g_icon ] 
[ ?itemText t_text ] 
[ ?callback S_funcname ] 
[ ?disable g_disable ] 
[ ?statusTip t_statusTip ] 
[ ?toolTip t_toolTip ] 
[ ?completerType s_type ] 
[ ?completerList l_list ]
) 
=> r_menuItem / nil
hiCreateTypeinMenuItem.desc: Creates a type-in menu item that can receive user inputs. When a user types text in the type-in menu item created using this function and presses Enter, the specified callback function S_funcname is run.

hiSetTypeinMenuItemCompleterList.name: hiSetTypeinMenuItemCompleterList
hiSetTypeinMenuItemCompleterList.syntax:
hiSetTypeinMenuItemCompleterList(
r_menu 
s_menuItem 
l_completerList 
) 
=> t / nil
hiSetTypeinMenuItemCompleterList.desc: Replaces the list of strings that store the history of user inputs for the specified type-in menu item. This list is used to assist user inputs in the type-in menu item.

hiCreateVerticalFixedMenu.name: hiCreateVerticalFixedMenu
hiCreateVerticalFixedMenu.syntax:
hiCreateVerticalFixedMenu(
s_menuHandle 
l_menuItems 
x_rows 
x_cols 
[ S_doneCallback ]
[ s_showTextWithIcon ]
) 
=> r_hiMenu
hiCreateVerticalFixedMenu.desc: Creates a vertical fixed menu that can be displayed in the root window. Fixed menus can no longer be displayed in application windows; use the new toolbar functions to create toolbars for windows instead.

hiDeleteMenu.name: hiDeleteMenu
hiDeleteMenu.desc: Destroys the menu given by hiMenu, which must be a valid data structure. Individual menu items contained in this menu are also destroyed.

hiDeleteMenuItem.name: hiDeleteMenuItem
hiDeleteMenuItem.desc: Deletes a menu item or action from all instances of the specified r_hiMenu.

hiDisableMenuItem.name: hiDisableMenuItem
hiDisableMenuItem.syntax:
hiDisableMenuItem(
r_hiMenu 
s_itemHandle
[ w_windowId ] 
) 
=> t / nil
hiDisableMenuItem.desc: Grays out a menu item on pull-down, pop-up, or fixed menus, making it unselectable.

hiDisplayFixedMenu.name: hiDisplayFixedMenu
hiDisplayFixedMenu.syntax:
hiDisplayFixedMenu(
r_hiMenu 
g_menuLocation
[ x_width ]
[ x_height ] 
[ g_staysOnTop }
) 
=> t / nil
hiDisplayFixedMenu.desc: Displays the specified fixed menu in the default root window (screen). The menu appears on a side of the screen, to be shared among Cadence application windows contained within the screen. The x_width and y_height arguments are ignored and currently exist only for compatability reasons. x_width and y_height of the menu are automatically determined by the size of the menu items and the number of columns and rows.

hiDisplayMenu.name: hiDisplayMenu
hiDisplayMenu.desc: Displays a menu created by hiCreateMenu, hiCreateSimpleMenu, or hiCreate2DMenu. For non-2D menus, the menu is always displayed at the current cursor's position at the time hiDisplayMenu is called.

hiDisplayWindowMenu.name: hiDisplayWindowMenu
hiDisplayWindowMenu.desc: Displays the popup menu associated with the given w_windowId, which must be a valid data structure returned by a call to hiOpenWindow or hiCreateWindow.

hiEnableMenuItem.name: hiEnableMenuItem
hiEnableMenuItem.syntax:
hiEnableMenuItem(
r_hiMenu 
s_itemHandle
[ w_windowId ] 
) 
=> t / nil
