simOutWithArgs(
l_fileList
t_runDirName
t_libName
t_cellName
t_viewName
) 
=> t / nil
simOutWithArgs.desc: Translates the netlister-assigned names for nets and instances in the input files specified in fileList to the corresponding user-assigned names, and produces the output files specified in fileList.

simPostNameConvert.name: simPostNameConvert
simPostNameConvert.desc: Clears all allocated storage and marks the map structure as invalid. Since this function can be called using SKILL, the parameter has to be maintained as a list.

simPostNetlistTriggerList.name: simPostNetlistTriggerList
simPostNetlistTriggerList.desc: Returns the list of functions registered through simRegPostNetlistTrigger when this function is specified in the .simrc file or the CIW. For backward compatibility, hnlPostNetlistTriggerList can be used as an alias for simPostNetlistTriggerList.

simPreNameConvert.name: simPreNameConvert
simPreNameConvert.desc: Sets up the variables needed for name conversion routines. If no arguments are passed, it does the setup by doing a lookup of the simulator environment settings.

simPreNetlistTriggerList.name: simPreNetlistTriggerList
simPreNetlistTriggerList.desc: Returns the list of functions registered through simRegPreNetlistTrigger when this function is specified in the .simrc file or the CIW. For backward compatibility, hnlPreNetlistTriggerList can be used as an alias for simPreNetlistTriggerList.

simPrintEnvironment.name: simPrintEnvironment
simPrintEnvironment.desc: Writes the primary simulation control variables and their values to the si.env file in the simulation run directory.

simPrintError.name: simPrintError
simPrintError.desc: Prints the text argument to the stderr port if executed in the Cadence nongraphic environment. If the function is called from within the Cadence graphics environment, the output is written to the CIW window.

simPrintErrorLine.name: simPrintErrorLine
simPrintErrorLine.desc: Prints the errors for a cell and writes them out to a file.

simPrintMessage.name: simPrintMessage
simPrintMessage.desc: Prints the text argument to the stdout port if executed in the Cadence non-graphic environment. If the function is called from within the Cadence graphics environment, the output is written to the CIW window.

simPrintTermList.name: simPrintTermList
simPrintTermList.syntax:
simPrintTermList(
t_libName
t_cellName
t_viewName
t_fileName
) 
=> t
simPrintTermList.desc: Lists the terminals for a cell and writes them out to a file.

simReadNetCapFile.name: simReadNetCapFile
simReadNetCapFile.desc: Reads in the net capacitance file and initializes the simAllNets global variable. This contains the list of all nets in the design and their associated capacitance values, which are present in the capacitance file.

simRegPostNetlistTrigger.name: simRegPostNetlistTrigger
simRegPostNetlistTrigger.desc: Registers a function to be called after the netlist has been generated. This is applicable for both hierarchical and flat netlisting. For backward compatibility, hnlRegPostNetlistTrigger can be used as an alias for simRegPostNetlistTrigger.

simRegPreNetlistTrigger.name: simRegPreNetlistTrigger
simRegPreNetlistTrigger.desc: Registers a function to be called before the netlisting begins. This is applicable for both hierarchical and flat netlisting. For backward compatibility, hnlRegPreNetlistTrigger can be used as an alias for simRegPreNetlistTrigger.

simRunDirInfile.name: simRunDirInfile
simRunDirInfile.desc: Opens the file specified using the fileName argument in the simulation run directory for reading. It creates a full file system path name to the file in the simulation run directory and then passes the file as an argument to the SKILL infile function. The function returns a SKILL port.

simRunDirLoad.name: simRunDirLoad
simRunDirLoad.desc: Loads the file specified using the t_fileName argument in the simulation run directory. It creates a full file system path to the file in the simulation run directory and then passes the file as an argument to the SKILL load function.

simRunDirOutfile.name: simRunDirOutfile
simRunDirOutfile.desc: Opens the file specified using the fileName argument in the simulation run directory for writing. It creates a full file system path name to the file in the simulation run directory and then passes the file as an argument to the SKILL outfile function. The function returns a SKILL port.

simRunNetAndSim.name: simRunNetAndSim
simRunNetAndSim.desc: Starts an analysis job in either foreground or background mode.

simRunNetAndSimWithArgs.name: simRunNetAndSimWithArgs
simRunNetAndSimWithArgs.syntax:
simRunNetAndSimWithArgs( 
t_libName | nil
t_cellName | nil
t_viewName | nil
t_simulatorName | nil
g_doNetlist
g_doSimulation
g_runBackground
x_jobPriority
) 
=> t / nil
simRunNetAndSimWithArgs.desc: Starts an analysis job in either foreground or background mode.

simRunNetAndSimWithCmd.name: simRunNetAndSimWithCmd
simRunNetAndSimWithCmd.syntax:
simRunNetAndSimWithCmd( 
t_libName | nil
t_cellName | nil
t_viewName | nil
t_simulatorName | nil
t_cmdToBeExecuted
g_runBackground
x_jobPriority
) 
=> t / nil
simRunNetAndSimWithCmd.desc: Runs a command that you specify in either foreground or background mode. The simulation environment must be initialized before simRunNetAndSimWithCmd is called. The simRunDir global variable specifies the current run directory. It is set when the simulation environment is initialized.

simSetDef.name: simSetDef
simSetDef.desc: Sets the g_variableName variable to g_value only if the variable is not yet set or if the symbol variableName evaluates to nil. If the variable was set prior to calling this function, and the simGenWarnings variable is not nil, a warning message is printed to stdout that the value of the variableName variable is overridden.

simSetDefWithNoWarn.name: simSetDefWithNoWarn
simSetDefWithNoWarn.desc: Sets the g_variableName variable to g_value, same as the simSetDef function, except that no warning is generated if variableName is already set.

simStringsToList.name: simStringsToList
simStringsToList.desc: Accepts a string of names separated by blanks and tab characters as an argument and returns a list of strings.

simSubProbeCapByScreen.name: simSubProbeCapByScreen
simSubProbeCapByScreen.desc: Displays all the net capacitance on the current screen.

simVertToHoriz.name: simVertToHoriz
simVertToHoriz.desc: Reads in the inputFileName file, converts names in vertical table headers to horizontal, and copies the rest of the file.

simViewFileWithArgs.name: simViewFileWithArgs
simViewFileWithArgs.syntax:
simViewFileWithArgs( 
t_fileName
l_windowSize
[ t_windowTitle ]
) 
=> winID / nil
simViewFileWithArgs.desc: Calls the view function with the file name as the first argument and the window size as the second argument. The view function creates a viewFile window where the file text is displayed with the banner as the value supplied through the optional windowTitle argument.

simWaveOpen.name: simWaveOpen
simWaveOpen.desc: Invokes a form displaying the current simulation run directory name, and prompts you for the name of the waveform file to display. The default waveform file is raw/waves in the simulation run directory. When the file name is specified, a new window is opened, displaying the waveform information.

vhdlHiImport.name: vhdlHiImport
vhdlHiImport.desc: Builds and displays the VHDL Import form.

vhdlImport.name: vhdlImport
vhdlImport.syntax:
vhdlImport(
t_libName
l_srcFiles
t_logName
l_params
[ g_runInBackground ]
[ g_displayResults ]
)
=> t / nil
vhdlImport.desc: Runs vhdlin to import a list of VHDL source files into the specified library with the given parameters. The parameters are the names of the vhdlin parameters, passed in as a disembodied property list. Optionally, it can run vhdlin as a background process and display the results interactively.

vhdlPinListToVHDL.name: vhdlPinListToVHDL
vhdlPinListToVHDL.syntax:
vhdlPinListToVHDL(
t_libName
t_cellName
t_viewName
l_pinList
)
=> t / nil
vhdlPinListToVHDL.desc: Allows the generation of VHDL views from an intermediate pin list format.

vhdlRegisterSimulator.name: vhdlRegisterSimulator
vhdlRegisterSimulator.syntax:
vhdlRegisterSimulator(
[ t_parserCallBack ]
[ t_analyzerCallBack ]
[ t_analyzerFileExt ]
[ t_elaboratorCallBack ] 
[ t_simulatorCallBack ]
[ t_dataDirCallBack ]
[ t_dataFileCallBack ]
[ t_workLibCallBack ]
)
=> t / nil
vhdlRegisterSimulator.desc: Lets you  use non-Cadence VHDL tools by defining your own SKILL procedures and registering this information with the toolbox..

vhdlToPinList.name: vhdlToPinList
vhdlToPinList.syntax:
vhdlToPinList(
t_libName
t_cellName
t_viewName
) 
=> list / nil
vhdlToPinList.desc: Translates a VHDL cellview into an intermediate pin list format.

vhmsCompilationFailure.name: vhmsCompilationFailure
vhmsCompilationFailure.syntax:
vhmsCompilationFailure(
t_libName
t_cellName
t_viewName
t_fileName
)
=> l_list / nil
vhmsCompilationFailure.desc: Informs about the compilation failures of the file specified with the fileName parameter. A compilation error message is displayed and you can open the file for editing by clicking 'Yes'.

vhmsDefaultEdit.name: vhmsDefaultEdit
vhmsDefaultEdit.syntax:
vhmsDefaultEdit(
t_libName
t_cellName
t_viewName
t_fileObj
t_mode
[ t_errFile ]
)
=> t / nil
vhmsDefaultEdit.desc: Opens an existing file or creates a template and opens it in an editor. If the mode is set to r, which indicates read-only then it tries to open an existing file.

vhmsGetCellParameters.name: vhmsGetCellParameters
vhmsGetCellParameters.desc: Returns the CDF parameters of the vhdl generics. The sub-list returned contains the name of the generic, the default value, and the type.

vhmsPinListToVHDLAMS.name: vhmsPinListToVHDLAMS
vhmsPinListToVHDLAMS.syntax:
vhmsPinListToVHDLAMS(
t_libName
t_cellName
t_viewName
l_pinList
)
=> t / nil
vhmsPinListToVHDLAMS.desc: Creates a vhdlams entity, package, body, configuration, or architecture depending on the view name. Specify the view name as entity, package, body, or configuration for creating an entity, package, body, or configuration respectively. If nothing is specified, an architecture view is created. The view is created in ./libName/cellName/viewName.

vhmsSaveFile.name: vhmsSaveFile
vhmsSaveFile.syntax:
vhmsSaveFile(
t_libName
t_cellName
t_viewName
t_fileName
)
=> l_list / nil
vhmsSaveFile.desc: Compiles the vhms file. If the symbol does not exist, it displays a prompt to create the symbol. If the compilation fails, it calls the vhmsCompilationFailure function.

vhmsSymbolToPinListGen.name: vhmsSymbolToPinListGen
vhmsSymbolToPinListGen.syntax:
vhmsSymbolToPinListGen(
t_libName
t_cellName
[ t_viewName ]
)
=> l_pinList / nil
vhmsSymbolToPinListGen.desc: Generates a pin list from the symbol.

vhmsToPinList.name: vhmsToPinList
vhmsToPinList.syntax:
vhmsToPinList(
t_libName
t_cellName
t_viewName
)
=> l_list / nil
vhmsToPinList.desc: Translates a VHDLAMS cellview into an intermediate pin list format. The pin list represents all the ports to the VHDLAMS description and their directions, such as input, output, and inout.

vhmsUpdateCellCDFParams.name: vhmsUpdateCellCDFParams
vhmsUpdateCellCDFParams.desc: Updates the CDF parameters by reading all the parameters from the pin list. The CDF is updated if a given parameter does not exist in the CDF.

vosHiDisplayNetlist.name: vosHiDisplayNetlist
vosHiDisplayNetlist.desc: Displays the generated VHDL netlist. This function can be used only when a single netlist is generated for the complete design.

vosLaunchIrunSimulation.name: vosLaunchIrunSimulation
vosLaunchIrunSimulation.desc: Launches the xrun simulator from the command line. If the vhdlSimNetlistandSimulate variable is set to t, the function netlists the design before launching the xrun simulator. Otherwise, it launches the simulator without netlisting the design.

tfEditTechfile.name: tfEditTechfile
tfEditTechfile.desc: Starts the Techfile IDE in a standalone mode.

vxfiLoadNets.name: vxfiLoadNets
vxfiLoadNets.desc: Specifies to load the nets in the Voltus-XFi Result Browser. This function should be called after the vxfiOpenLayout and vxfiLoadEMIRResults functions.

vxfiLoadEMIRResults.name: vxfiLoadEMIRResults
vxfiLoadEMIRResults.desc: Specifies to load the EMIR results database file (.wdb) in the Voltus-XFi Result Browser. This function should be called after the vxfiOpenLayout function.

vxfiOpenLayout.name: vxfiOpenLayout
vxfiOpenLayout.syntax:
vxfiOpenLayout(
libname
cellname
viewname
[ mode ]
)
=> w_windowId
vxfiOpenLayout.desc: Opens the design in the Virtuoso layout and launches Voltus-XFi Results Browser.

vxfiSaveNetSummaryInfoToCSV.name: vxfiSaveNetSummaryInfoToCSV
vxfiSaveNetSummaryInfoToCSV.desc: Specifies to write the net summary given in the Voltus-XFi Results Browser interface to a text file in the current working directory.

vxfiSessionConnect.name: vxfiSessionConnect
vxfiSessionConnect.syntax:
vxfiSessionConnect(
t_sessionName
t_signalName
s_callbackFunction
)
=> t / nil
vxfiSessionConnect.desc: Registers a SKILL callback to be connected to a known signal or trigger emitted from a Voltus-XFi session. This function supports event-based trigger callbacks for pre-extraction, post-extraction, and pre-simulation. The function can be used to run LVS before running extraction, after running extraction, and before running simulation by registering the LVS run callback for these three events.

vxfiSessionRegisterCreationCallback.name: vxfiSessionRegisterCreationCallback
vxfiSessionRegisterCreationCallback.desc: Registers a SKILL function as callback to be called whenever the event for which it is registered is occurred.

vxfiSetLVSQueryOutputDirectory.name: vxfiSetLVSQueryOutputDirectory
vxfiSetLVSQueryOutputDirectory.desc: Specifies the path to the LVS output directory in which the input data is stored for extraction.

vxfiSetLVSRunName.name: vxfiSetLVSRunName
vxfiSetLVSRunName.desc: Specifies the LVS run name to be used for extraction.

vsaOpenSchematic.name: vsaOpenSchematic
vsaOpenSchematic.desc: Opens the design on the Virtuoso layout for running Voltus-Fi-L.

vsaDescendView.name: vsaDescendView
vsaDescendView.desc: Descends in the hierarchy and opens the child view of the design in Virtuoso for running Voltus-Fi-L.

appendPath.name: appendPath
appendPath.desc: Appends a new path to the end of the search path list. You can append as many paths as you want with this command.

path.name: path
path.desc: Sets the search path for included files.

prependPath.name: prependPath
prependPath.desc: Adds a new path to the beginning of the search path list. You can add as many paths as you want with this command.

setup.name: setup
setup.syntax:
setup(
[ ?numberNotation s_numberNotation ]
[ ?precision x_precision ]
[ ?reportStyle s_reportStyle ]
[ ?charsPerLine x_charsPerLine ] 
[ ?messageOn g_messageOn ] 
) 
=> t / nil

history.name: history
history.desc: Displays the command history. By default, it the last twenty commands are listed from the current session and the most recently terminated session. More commands can be printed by giving a number as an argument.

ocnSetSilentMode.name: ocnSetSilentMode
ocnSetSilentMode.desc: Filters out OCEAN warning and information messages and allows only error messages to be written. This functionality is useful while running the OCEAN scripts when you might want to skip all OCEAN messages except errors.

ac.name: ac
ac.syntax:
ac(
g_fromValue
g_toValue
g_ptsPerDec
) 
=> undefined / nil

analysis.name: analysis
analysis.syntax:
analysis(
s_analysisType 
[ ?analysisOption1 g_analysisOptionValue1 ]... [ ?analysisOptionN g_analysisOptionValueN ]
) 
=> undefined / nil
analysis.desc: Specifies the analysis to be simulated.

converge.name: converge
converge.syntax:
converge( 
s_convName
t_netName1
f_value1 ... [ t_netNameN f_valueN ]
) 
=> undefined / nil

connectRules.name: connectRules
connectRules.syntax:
connectRules(
t_ruleName
[ ?lib t_libName ] 
[ ?view t_viewName ] 
[ ?baseRule t_baseRule ]
[ ?moduleInfo l_moduleInfo ] 
[ ?resolutionInfo l_resolutionInfo ] 
[ ?commonParam l_commonParam ]
[ ?userDefined s_userDefined ]
)
=> t / nil
connectRules.desc: Sets connect rules for a given AMS OCEAN session required by the elaborator. To specify multiple connect rules, use this command multiple times. To add a connect rule to an OCEAN session, you can either choose a built-in rule from the connectLib library (by specifying t_ruleName, t_libName and t_viewName) or one of your own compiled built-in connect rules (by specifying t_ruleName, t_libName and t_viewName). To add a user defined connect rule to an OCEAN session specify s_userDefined. To modify an existing built-in rule, you need to specify t_baseRule (the name of the built-in rule that needs be modified), specify a new name (by specifying t_ruleName, t_libName and t_viewName) and also specify one or more of the optional arguments.

createFinalNetlist.name: createFinalNetlist
createFinalNetlist.desc: Creates the final netlist for viewing purposes. The netlist also can be saved but is not required to run the simulator.

dc.name: dc
dc.syntax:
dc( 
t_compName 
[ t_compParam ] 
g_fromValue
g_toValue
g_byValue 
) 
=> undefined / nil
dc.desc: Specifies a DC sweep analysis with limited options. If other analysis options are needed, use the analysis command.

definitionFile.name: definitionFile
definitionFile.syntax:
definitionFile( 
t_fileName [ t_fileName2 ... t_fileNameN ]
) 
=> l_fileNames / nil
definitionFile.desc: Specifies definitions files to be included in the simulator input file.

delete.name: delete
delete.syntax:
delete( 
s_command 
[ g_commandArg1 ] [ g_commandArg2 ] ... 
) 
=> t / nil

deleteOpPoint.name: deleteOpPoint
deleteOpPoint.desc: Deletes the specified operating point instance.

design.name: design
design.syntax:
design( 
t_cktFile | t_lib t_cell t_view [ t_mode ] 
) 
=> t_cktFile / nil | (t_lib t_cell t_view) / nil
design.desc: Specifies the directory path to the netlist of a design or the name of a design to be simulated.

desVar.name: desVar
desVar.syntax:
desVar( 
t_desVar1 f_value1 ... [ t_desVarN f_valueN ]
) 
=> undefined / nil
desVar.desc: Sets the values of design variables used in your design. You can set the values for as many design variables as you want.

discipline.name: discipline
discipline.desc: Adds discrete disciplines to the existing set of disciplines for a given 'ams' OCEAN session. You can use delete('discipline) to delete one or more specified disciplines. You can use ocnDisplay('discipline) to view the currently active disciplines in an OCEAN session.

displayNetlist.name: displayNetlist
displayNetlist.desc: Displays the concatenated AMS complete design info file used in a given AMS OCEAN session. The concatenated file displays the netlisting of the cellviews used in the configuration along with the analog control file and the TCL file generated by AMS-ADE. This command is applicable for Spectre.

envOption.name: envOption
envOption.syntax:
envOption( 
s_envOption1 g_value1 ... [ s_envOptionN g_valueN ] 
) 
=> undefined / nil

evcdFile.name: evcdFile
evcdFile.desc: Sets an EVCD file for a given UltraSim OCEAN session. You also need to specify an EVCD info file while using this command. You can specify only one EVCD file for a session. You may use ocnDisplay('evcdFile) to view the currently active EVCD file.

evcdInfoFile.name: evcdInfoFile
evcdInfoFile.desc: Sets a EVCD info file for a given UltraSim OCEAN session. You also need to specify an EVCD file while using this command. You can specify only one EVCD info file for a session. You may use ocnDisplay('evcdInfoFile) to view the currently active EVCD info file.

forcenode.name: forcenode
forcenode.syntax:
forcenode( 
t_netName1 f_value1 ... [ t_netNameN f_valueN ] 
) 
=> undefined / nil
forcenode.desc: Holds a node at a specified value.

globalSigAlias.name: globalSigAlias
globalSigAlias.desc: Removes all the previous signal aliases and creates the specified aliases. The signal names in each of the signal lists are marked as aliases of each other. Each of the signal lists is a set of signal names that are to be aliased. The signal names should match the names that were specified using the globalSignal command. To unalias all signal, pecify nil instead of signal lists.

globalSignal.name: globalSignal
globalSignal.syntax:
globalSignal( 
[ ?name t_signalName ] 
[ ?lang t_langName ] 
[ ?wireType t_wireType ] 
[ ?discipline t_discipline ]
[ ?ground t_ground ]
@Rest args
) 
=> t / nil
globalSignal.desc: Adds or modifies a global signal for a given AMS OCEAN session needed by the elaborator. If the global signal already exists in the session, the values are updated. If it does not exist, a global signal with the specified name is added. In case of a vector signal, the range information can be appended with the name of the signal.

ic.name: ic
ic.syntax:
ic( 
t_netName1 f_value1 ... [ t_netNameN f_valueN ] 
) 
=> undefined / nil
ic.desc: Sets initial conditions on nets in a transient analysis.

includeFile.name: includeFile
includeFile.desc: Includes the specified file in the final netlist of the simulator for the current session.

modelFile.name: modelFile
modelFile.desc: Specifies model files to be included in the simulator input file.

nodeset.name: nodeset
nodeset.syntax:
nodeset( 
t_netName1 f_value1 ... [ t_netNameN f_valueN ]
) 
=> undefined / nil
nodeset.desc: Sets the initial estimate for nets in a DC analysis, or sets the initial condition calculation for a transient analysis.

ocnCloseSession.name: ocnCloseSession
ocnCloseSession.desc: Closes the current OCEAN session without saving any settings made during the session. The command has no effect if no session is currently active.

ocnDisplay.name: ocnDisplay
ocnDisplay.syntax:
ocnDisplay(
[ ?output t_filename | p_port ] 
s_command
[ g_commandArg1 ] [ g_commandArg2 ] ... 
) 
=> t / nil

ocnDspfFile.name: ocnDspfFile
ocnDspfFile.syntax:
ocnDspfFile( 
t_dspfFile [ t_dspfFile1 ... t_dspfFileN ] 
) 
=> t_dspfFile(s) / nil
ocnDspfFile.desc: Sets the parasitic (dspf, spf) files to be used in a Spectre OCEAN session. You can use this command to specify a list of parasitic files to be included in the control file. You can use ocnDisplay('dspfFile) to view the currently active parasitic (dspf, spf) files in an OCEAN session.

ocnSpefFile.name: ocnSpefFile
ocnSpefFile.syntax:
ocnSpefFile( 
t_SpefFile [ t_SpefFile1 ... t_SpefFileN ]
) 
=> t_SpecFile(s) / nil
ocnSpefFile.desc: Sets the parasitic (spef) files to be used in a Spectre OCEAN session. You can use this command to specify a list of parasitic files to be included in the control file. You can use ocnDisplay('SpefFile) to view the currently active parasitic (spef) files in an OCEAN session.

ocnPspiceFile.name: ocnPspiceFile
ocnPspiceFile.syntax:
ocnPspiceFile( 
t_PSpiceFile
[ t_PSpiceFile1 ... t_PSpiceFileN ]
) 
=> t_PSpiceFile(s) / nil
ocnPspiceFile.desc: Sets the PSpice files to be used in  a Spectre OCEAN session. Use this command to specify a list of PSpice files to be included in the control file.

ocnGetAdjustedPath.name: ocnGetAdjustedPath
ocnGetAdjustedPath.syntax:
ocnGetAdjustedPath( 
t_libName
t_cellName 
t_viewName 
t_netName ) 
=> t_adjustedPath / nil
ocnGetAdjustedPath.desc: Reduces the given hierarchical net path to the shortest hierarchical name that is equivalent to this net.

ocnGetInstancesModelName.name: ocnGetInstancesModelName
ocnGetInstancesModelName.desc: This function returns the model name used by the instance in opened simulation results.

off.name: off
off.syntax:
off( 
s_command
[ g_commandArg1 ] [ g_commandArg2 ]
) 
=> t / nil

option.name: option
option.syntax:
option( 
[ ?categ s_categ ]
s_option1 g_value1 [ s_option2 g_value2 ] ... ) 
=> undefined / nil
option.desc: Specifies the values for built-in simulator options. You can specify values for as many options as you want.

restore.name: restore
restore.desc: Tells the simulator to restore the state previously saved to a file with a store command.

resultsDir.name: resultsDir
resultsDir.desc: Specifies the directory where the PSF files (results) are stored.

run.name: run
run.desc: Starts the simulation or specifies a time after which an analysis should start. If distributed processing is not available on the system or is not enabled, the arguments specific to distributed processing (see Arguments section below for list of arguments specific to distributed processing) are ignored and the simulation runs locally. If distributed processing is available and is enabled, the environment default values are used if not specified in the run command arguments. The environmental default values are stored in the .cdsenv file.

save.name: save
save.syntax:
save(
[ ?categ s_categ ] s_saveType 
[ t_saveName1 ] ... [ t_saveNameN ] 
) 
=> undefined / nil
save.desc: Specifies the outputs to be saved and printed during simulation.

saveOpPoint.name: saveOpPoint
saveOpPoint.desc: Specifies the operating point parameters to be saved for a given instance.

saveOption.name: saveOption
saveOption.syntax:
saveOption(
[ s_option1 g_optionValue1 ]...[ s_optionN g_optionValueN ]
)
=> undefined / nil
saveOption.desc: Specifies save options to be used by the simulator.

simulator.name: simulator
simulator.desc: Starts an OCEAN session and sets the simulator name for that session. The previous session (if any) is closed and all session information is cleared.

solver.name: solver
solver.desc: Sets a solver for a given AMS OCEAN session. The valid values for solver are Spectre and UltraSim. You select Spectre if you want to use an accurate AMS-Spectre analog engine. You select UltraSim if you want to use the AMS-Ultrasim or FastSPICE(UltraSim) solver for a given AMS simulation.

stimulusFile.name: stimulusFile
stimulusFile.syntax:
stimulusFile(
t_fileName [ t_fileName2 ... t_fileNameN ]
[ ?xlate g_xlate ]
) 
=> l_fileNames / nil
stimulusFile.desc: Specifies stimulus files to be used by the simulator.

store.name: store
store.desc: Requests that the simulator store its node voltages to a file.

tran.name: tran
tran.syntax:
tran( 
g_fromValue
g_toValue
g_byValue
) 
=> g_byValue / nil
tran.desc: Specifies a transient analysis with limited options. If other analysis options are needed, use the analysis command.

vcdFile.name: vcdFile
vcdFile.desc: Sets a VCD file for a given AMS or UltraSim OCEAN session. You also need to specify a VCD info file while using this command. You can specify only one VCD file for a session. You may use ocnDisplay('vcdFile) to view the currently active VCD file.

vcdInfoFile.name: vcdInfoFile
vcdInfoFile.desc: Sets a VCD info file for a given AMS or UltraSim OCEAN session when you have set UltraSim as the solver. You also need to specify a VCD file while using this command. You can specify only one VCD info file for a session. You may use ocnDisplay('vcdInfoFile) to view the currently active VCD info file.

vecFile.name: vecFile
vecFile.syntax:
vecFile( 
t_vecFile [ t_vecFile1 ... t_vecFileN ]
) 
=> t_vecFile(s) / nil
vecFile.desc: Sets the vector files to be used in an AMS or UltraSim OCEAN session. You use the vecFile command to specify a list of vector files which go to control file. You may use ocnDisplay('vecFile) to view the currently active vector files in an OCEAN session.

hlcheck.name: hlcheck
hlcheck.desc: Sets or gets the value of the hlcheck option used in the vec_include statement in a netlist. You may use the ocnDisplay('hlcheck) command to view the current value of hlcheck in an OCEAN session associated with vector files.

ocnAmsSetUNLNetlister.name: ocnAmsSetUNLNetlister
ocnAmsSetUNLNetlister.desc: Sets the netlister mode to AMS Unified Netlister for a given ams OCEAN session.

dataTypes.name: dataTypes
dataTypes.desc: Returns the list of data types that are used in an analysis previously specified with selectResult.

deleteSubckt.name: deleteSubckt
deleteSubckt.desc: Deletes the specified subcircuit instance saved using the saveSubckt command.

displaySubckt.name: displaySubckt
displaySubckt.desc: Prints the subcircuit information to the output file.

getData.name: getData
getData.syntax:
getData(
t_name 
[ ?result s_resultName [ ?resultsDir t_resultsDir ] ] )
=> x_number / o_waveform / nil
getData.desc: Returns the number or waveform for the signal name specified.

getResult.name: getResult
getResult.desc: Gets the data object for a specified analysis without overriding the status of any previously executed selectResult() or openResults() commands.

i.name: i
i.syntax:
i( 
t_component
[ ?result s_resultName [ ?resultsDir t_resultsDir ] ] 
) 
=> o_waveform / nil
i.desc: Returns the current through the specified component.

ocnHelp.name: ocnHelp
ocnHelp.syntax:
ocnHelp( 
[ ?output t_filename | p_port ]
[ s_command ]
) 
=> t / nil
ocnHelp.desc: Provides online help for the specified command.

ocnResetResults.name: ocnResetResults
ocnResetResults.desc: Unsets the results opened by the openResults command. Use this command to return to the state that existed prior to using the openResults command.

openResults.name: openResults
openResults.syntax:
openResults( 
s_jobName | t_dirName 
[ g_enableCalcExpressions ] 
) 
=> t_dirName / nil
openResults.desc: Opens simulation results stored in PSF files or opens the results from a specified job, depending on which parameter is called.

outputParams.name: outputParams
outputParams.syntax:
outputParams(
t_compType 
[ ?result s_resultName [ ?resultsDir t_resultsDir ] ] 
)
=> l_outputParams / nil
outputParams.desc: Returns the list of output parameters for the specified component.

outputs.name: outputs
outputs.syntax:
outputs(
[ ?result s_resultName [ ?resultsDir t_resultsDir ] ] 
[ ?type t_signalType ]
) 
=> l_outputs / nil
outputs.desc: Returns the names of the outputs whose results are stored for an analysis. You can plot these outputs or use them in calculations.

phaseNoise.name: phaseNoise
phaseNoise.syntax:
phaseNoise(
g_harmonic S_signalResultName 
[ ?result s_noiseResultName [ ?resultsDir t_resultsDir ] ]
) 
=> o_waveform / nil
phaseNoise.desc: Returns the phase noise waveform which is calculated using information from two PSF data files.

pv.name: pv
pv.syntax:
pv( 
t_name
t_param 
[ ?result s_resultName [ ?resultsDir t_resultsDir ] ] 
) 
=> g_value / nil
pv.desc: Returns the value of the specified component parameter. You can use the outputParams command to get the list of parameters for a particular component.

resultParam.name: resultParam
resultParam.syntax:
resultParam( 
S_propertyName 
[ ?result s_resultName [ ?resultsDir t_resultsDir ] ] 
) 
=> L_value / nil
resultParam.desc: Returns the value of a header property from the selected result data.

results.name: results
results.desc: Returns a list of the type of results that can be selected.

saveSubckt.name: saveSubckt
saveSubckt.syntax:
saveSubckt(
t_name
[ ?voltage g_voltage ]
[ ?current g_current ]
[ ?power g_power ] 
[ ?vDepth s_vDepth ]
[ ?iDepth s_iDepth ]
[ ?pwrDepth s_pwrDepth ]
[ ?compress g_compress ]
[ ?filterRC g_filterRC ]
[ ?ports g_ports ]
[ ?userOptions g_userOptions ]
)
=> t / nil
saveSubckt.desc: Saves and modifies the specified subcircuit instances and signals.

selectResult.name: selectResult
selectResult.desc: Selects the results from a particular analysis whose data you want to examine.

sp.name: sp
sp.syntax:
sp( 
x_iIndex 
x_jIndex 
[ ?result s_resultName [ ?resultsDir t_resultsDir ] ]
) 
=> o_waveform / nil
sp.desc: Returns S-parameters for N port networks.

sprobeData.name: sprobeData
sprobeData.syntax:
sprobeData( 
t_ana 
t_sprobeInst 
[ ?type t_type ] 
[ ?dataDir t_dataDir ] 
) 
=> o_waveform / nil
sprobeData.desc: Returns the waveform for the specified analysis and parameter type of the given sprobe instance.

sweepNames.name: sweepNames
sweepNames.syntax:
sweepNames( 
[ o_waveForm ] 
[ ?result s_resultName [ ?resultsDir t_resultsDir ] ] ) 
=> l_sweepName / nil
sweepNames.desc: Returns the names of all the sweep variables for either a supplied waveform, a currently selected result (via selectResult()) or a specified result.

sweepValues.name: sweepValues
sweepValues.desc: Returns the list of sweep values of the outermost sweep variable of either the selected results or the supplied waveform. This command is particularly useful for parametric analyses.

sweepVarValues.name: sweepVarValues
sweepVarValues.syntax:
sweepVarValues(
[ t_varName ]
[ ?result s_resultName [ ?resultsDir t_resultsDir ] ]
)
=> l_sweepName / nil
sweepVarValues.desc: Returns the list of sweep values for a particular swept variable name. This command is particularly useful for parametric analyses.

v.name: v
v.syntax:
v( 
t_net

vm.name: vm

vp.name: vp
vp.desc: Aliased to phase(v()). Gets the phase of the voltage of a net.

vr.name: vr
vr.desc: Aliased to real(v()). Gets the real part of a complex number representing the voltage of a net.

vim.name: vim
vim.desc: Aliased to imag(v()). Gets the imaginary part of a complex number representing the voltage of a net.

im.name: im
im.desc: Aliased to mag(i()). Gets the magnitude of the AC current through a component.

ip.name: ip
ip.desc: Aliased to phase(i()). Gets the phase of the AC current through a component.

ir.name: ir
ir.desc: Aliased to real(i()). Gets the real part of a complex number representing the AC current through a component.

iim.name: iim
iim.desc: Aliased to imag(i()). Gets the imaginary part of a complex number representing the AC current through a component.

abs.name: abs
abs.desc: Returns the absolute value of a floating-point number or integer.

acos.name: acos

add1.name: add1
add1.desc: Adds 1 to a floating-point number or integer.

asin.desc: Returns the arc sine of a floating-point number or integer.

cos.name: cos

int.name: int

logRg.name: logRg

max.name: max
max.desc: Returns the maximum of the values passed in. Requires a minimum of two arguments.

min.name: min
min.desc: Returns the minimum of the values passed in. Requires a minimum of two arguments.

mod.name: mod
mod.desc: Returns the integer remainder of dividing two integers. The remainder is either zero or has the sign of the dividend.

random.name: random
random.desc: Returns a random integer between 0 and x_number minus 1.

round.name: round
round.desc: Rounds a floating-point number to its closest integer value.

sin.name: sin
sin.desc: Returns the sine of a floating-point number or integer.

sqrt.name: sqrt
sqrt.desc: Returns the square root of a floating-point number or integer.

srandom.name: srandom
srandom.desc: Sets the seed of the random number generator to a given number.

sub1.name: sub1
sub1.desc: Subtracts 1 from a floating-point number or integer.

tan.name: tan
tan.desc: Returns the tangent of a floating-point number or integer.

xor.name: xor

g_normalize 
[ ?percent d_percent ]
) 
=> o_waveform / nil
evmQAM.desc: Processes the I and Q waveform outputs from the transient simulation run to calculate the Error Vector Magnitude (EVM) for multi-mode modulations. The function plots the I versus Q scatterplot. EVM is a useful measurement to describe the overall signal amplitude and phase modulated signal quality. It is based on a statistical error distribution normalized from an ideal digital modulation. Quadrature Amplitude Modulation (QAM) is a typical modulation scheme where EVM is useful. The EVM is calculated by detecting the I and Q signal levels corresponding to the four possible I and Q symbol combinations and calculating the difference between the actual signal level and the ideal signal level.

)

EVM is a useful measurement to describe the overall signal amplitude and phase modulated signal quality. It is based on a statistical error distribution normalized from an ideal digital modulation. Quadrature Phase Shift Keying (QPSK) is a typical modulation scheme where EVM is useful. The EVM is calculated by detecting the I and Q signal levels corresponding to the four possible I and Q symbol combinations and calculating the difference between the actual signal level and the ideal signal level.

pvi.desc: Returns the spectral power from voltage and current for a specified harmonic list or for all harmonics.

pvr.desc: Returns the spectral power at a specified harmonic list or at all harmonics with resistor and voltage on the positive and negative nodes.

totalNoise.desc: Returns the total noise in a specified frequency limit.

)

vfreq.desc: Returns the voltage of a net at a specified frequency or at all frequencies in the frequency domain.

deleteJob.desc: Removes a job or series of jobs from the text-based job monitor.

digitalHostMode.name: digitalHostMode
digitalHostMode.desc: For mixed-signal simulation, specifies whether the digital simulator will run locally or on a remote host.

digitalHostName.name: digitalHostName
digitalHostName.desc: For mixed-signal simulation, specifies the name of the remote host for the digital simulator.

hostName.name: hostName
hostName.desc: Specifies the name of the remote host.

killJob.name: killJob
killJob.syntax:
killJob( 
t_jobName [ t_jobName2 t_jobName3 ... t_jobNameN ]
) 
=> t / nil
killJob.desc: Stops processing of a job or a series of jobs.

monitor.name: monitor
monitor.desc: Monitors the jobs submitted to the distributed system.

remoteDir.name: remoteDir
remoteDir.desc: Specifies the project directory on the remote host to be used for remote simulation.

resumeJob.name: resumeJob
resumeJob.syntax:
resumeJob(
t_jobName [ t_jobName2 t_jobName3 ... t_jobNameN ]
) 
=> t / nil
resumeJob.desc: Resumes the processing of a previously suspended job or series of jobs. The resumeJob command applies only to jobs that are suspended.

suspendJob.name: suspendJob
suspendJob.syntax:
suspendJob(
t_jobName [ t_jobName2 t_jobName3 ... t_jobNameN ]
) 
=> t / nil
suspendJob.desc: Suspends the processing of a job or series of jobs. The suspendJob command applies only to jobs that are pending or running.

wait.name: wait
wait.syntax:
wait(
[ ?queue t_queueName ] 
jobName [ jobName2 jobName3 ... jobNameN ]
) 
=> t / nil
wait.desc: Postpones processing of a script until the specified jobs complete. This command is ignored if distributed processing is not available.

if.name: if
if.desc: Evaluates g_condition, typically a relational expression, and runs g_thenExpression if the condition is true (that is, its value is non-nil); otherwise, runs g_elseExpression.

unless.name: unless
unless.desc: Evaluates a condition. If the result is true (non-nil), it returns nil; otherwise it evaluates the body expressions in sequence and returns the value of the last expression.

for.name: for
for.syntax:
for(
s_loopVar 
x_initialValue 
x_finalValue 
g_expr1 
[ g_expr2 ... ] 
) 
=> t
for.desc: Evaluates the sequence g_expr1 g_expr2 ... for each loop variable value, beginning with x_initialValue and ending with x_finalValue.

foreach.name: foreach
foreach.syntax:
foreach( 
s_formalVar 
g_exprList 
g_expr1 [ g_expr2 ... ]
) 
=> l_valueList
foreach.desc: Evaluates one or more expressions for each element of a list of values.

while.name: while
while.desc:
Repeatedly evaluates g_condition and the sequence of expressions 
g_expr1 ... if the condition is true.

case.name: case
case.syntax:
case( 
g_selectionExpr
l_clause1 [ l_clause2 ... ]
) 
=> g_result / nil
case.desc: Evaluates the selection expression, matches the resulting selector values sequentially against comparators defined in clauses, and runs the expressions in the matching clause.

cond.name: cond
cond.desc: Examines conditional clauses from left to right until either a clause is satisfied or there are no more clauses remaining.

close.name: close
close.desc: Drains, closes, and frees a port.

fscanf.name: fscanf
fscanf.syntax:
fscanf( 
p_inputPort
t_formatString 
[ s_var1 ... ]  
) 
=> x_items / nil
fscanf.desc: Reads input from a port according to format specifications and returns the number of items read in.

gets.name: gets
gets.desc: Reads a line from the input port and stores the line as a string in the variable. This is a macro.

infile.name: infile
infile.desc: Opens an input port ready to read a file.

load.name: load
load.desc: Opens a file and repeatedly calls lineread to read in the file, immediately evaluating each form after it is read in.

newline.name: newline
newline.desc: Prints a newline (backslash n) character and then flushes the output port.

outfile.name: outfile
outfile.desc: Opens an output port ready to write to a file.

pfile.name: pfile
pfile.desc: Opens an output port ready to write to a file or returns the name of an existing port indicating that it is available.

printf.name: printf
printf.desc: Writes formatted output to poport, which is the standard output port.

println.name: println
println.desc: Prints a SKILL object using the default format for the data type of the value, and then prints a newline character.

impHdlDisplay.name: impHdlDisplay
impHdlDisplay.desc: Displays the Verilog In form. Alternatively, in the CIW, choose File - Import - Verilog to open the Verilog In form.

conn2Sch.name: conn2Sch

t_srcLibName

t_srcViewName

[ ?block t_block ]
[ ?paramFile t_paramFile ]
[ ?cdslib t_cdslib ]
)
=> t / nil
conn2Sch.desc: Generates a schematic view from an imported netlist view.

conn2SchImpHdlDisplay.name: conn2SchImpHdlDisplay
conn2SchImpHdlDisplay.desc: Accepts the user interface name of Connectivity-to-Schematic tool as an argument and displays the GUI for the tool.

conn2SchStartUp.name: conn2SchStartUp
conn2SchStartUp.desc: Invokes the graphical user interface of the Connectivity-to-Schematic tool. This is a CIW menu callback function.

ivCallProc.name: ivCallProc
ivCallProc.desc: You can place this command anywhere in the rules file. Placing this command in a DRC rule deck will only provide access to the layout view. Any marker generating rules which execute before the ivCallProc will result in the markers being present in the layout view. It is recommended that markers not be modified though use of the ivCallProc command. Markers stored in the ivEDB error database are not accessable from within an ivCallProc. Depending on where you place this command in an Extract rule deck, it has the following results:

ivGetCellView.name: ivGetCellView
ivGetCellView.desc: From the rules file, this procedure gets the database ID of the layout cellview being processed, from which the cell, library, and techfile can be accessed. Properties associated with these are available for use in the rules.

ivCompilingFor.name: ivCompilingFor
ivCompilingFor.desc: From the rules file, this procedure returns t if any of the strings passed as arguments contain the constant diva. It is expected that the results of calling the procedure will be used in a SKILL if statement. You can use the SKILL statement to select the Diva rules in a rule deck containing both Diva and Assura rules.

avSwitch.name: avSwitch
avSwitch.desc: From the rules file, this procedure returns t if the string passed as an argument is a switch name set by the user through the use of the -set option in the ivVerify or LVS commands. Otherwise, avSwitch() returns nil. You can use this procedure to select rules in the rules deck.

ivConcICe.name: ivConcICe
ivConcICe.desc: Starts the ConcICe RC network reduction section of the layout verification program. Each of the arguments is a keyword preceded by a question mark (?). You must give each keyword a value, as indicated below. The ?cell, ?resModelData, and ?capModelData keywords are required, the other keywords are optional.

ivCreatePCells.name: ivCreatePCells
ivCreatePCells.desc: This command creates parameterized versions of existing cells for the display of devices created by the device extraction commands.

ivDRC.name: ivDRC
ivDRC.desc: Starts the DRC section of the layout verification program. Each of the arguments is a keyword preceded by a question mark (?). You must give each keyword a value or a symbolic name set to the value.The ?cell argument is required; the other arguments are optional.

ivERC.name: ivERC
ivERC.syntax:
ivERC( 
runDir
libName
cellName
viewName
netlist
jobPriority
rulesFromUnix
rulesLibName
rulesFilePath
machine
) => t / nil
ivERC.desc: Starts the ERC program of the layout verification system. All arguments are required.

ivExtract.name: ivExtract
ivExtract.desc: Invokes the Extraction section of the layout verification program. The ?cell argument is required; the other arguments are optional.

ivLVS.name: ivLVS
ivLVS.syntax:
ivLVS( 
runDir
layoutLibName
layoutCellName
layoutViewName
netlistLayout 
schematicLibName
schematicCellName 
schematicViewName 
netlistSchematic 
deviceFixing 
noRewire 
termCorr 
useFileCorr 
corrFile 
xref 
jobPriority
rulesFromUnix
rulesLibName
rulesFilePath
machine
switches
runInBg
) => t / nil
ivLVS.desc: Invokes the Layout Versus Schematic (LVS) Comparison program of the layout verification system. All arguments are required.

ivVerify.syntax:

ivVerify.desc: Runs DRC and extraction from the UNIX environment.

aelCheckRange.name: aelCheckRange
aelCheckRange.desc: Determines if a number falls within a particular range of numbers.

aelEngNotation.name: aelEngNotation
aelEngNotation.desc: Reformats a given number into engineering notation.

aelGetSignifDigits.name: aelGetSignifDigits
aelGetSignifDigits.desc: Returns the current number of significant digits used by the aelEngNotation function.

aelNumber.name: aelNumber
aelNumber.desc: Takes an integer, a double, a complex, or a strnum (including complex strnums) and returns an integer, double, a complex, or a strnum.

aelPopSignifDigits.name: aelPopSignifDigits
aelPopSignifDigits.desc: Discards (pops) the top value of the stack built by the aelPushSignifDigits function and returns a new top value.

aelPushSignifDigits.name: aelPushSignifDigits
aelPushSignifDigits.desc: Places (pushes) a given value onto the stack of values for the number of significant digits the aelEngNotation function uses to create engineering notation strnums.

aelSignum.name: aelSignum
aelSignum.desc: Analyzes an integer, a double, or a strnum (not including complex strnums) and returns -1 if the value is negative, 0 if it is zero, or 1 if it is positive.

aelStrDblNotation.name: aelStrDblNotation
aelStrDblNotation.desc: Calls the aelEngNotation function and, if the result is an integer, appends a decimal point and zero (.0).

aelSuffixNotation.name: aelSuffixNotation
aelSuffixNotation.desc: Calls the aelEngNotation function and replaces the e and exponent (if any) with the appropriate AEL suffix character. If the value is too small or too large for the AEL set of suffixes, the e and exponent are unchanged.

aelSuffixWithUnits.name: aelSuffixWithUnits
aelSuffixWithUnits.desc: Used to display values on forms.

aelEnvCompile.name: aelEnvCompile
aelEnvCompile.desc:
Compiles a given expression according to the evaluation mode set with aelEnvCreate and the state of globals for the given environment.
Compiled expressions are references to dynamically allocated memory. There is no facility for extending their lifetime or visibility beyond the process in which they are created. Do not attempt to store them in a design database. Compiled expressions are invalidated and yield undefined results if you apply the aelEnvFreeCompExpr function to them, or if you destroy their associated environment with the env = nil expression.

aelEnvCreate.name: aelEnvCreate
aelEnvCreate.desc: Creates and initializes an AEL environment.

aelEnvExecute.name: aelEnvExecute
aelEnvExecute.desc: Executes the previously compiled AEL expression with the current global values of the environment in which it was compiled.

aelEnvFreeCompExpr.name: aelEnvFreeCompExpr
aelEnvFreeCompExpr.desc: Frees the dynamically allocated memory used to store the compiled AEL expression.

aelEnvGetErrStr.name: aelEnvGetErrStr
aelEnvGetErrStr.desc: Converts the error code currently stored in the all-AEL-wide error flag into an appropriate message.

aelEnvGetGlobal.name: aelEnvGetGlobal
aelEnvGetGlobal.desc: Returns the current value of the named global, previously defined or deferred, in the given environment.

aelEnvInterpret.name: aelEnvInterpret
aelEnvInterpret.desc: Compiles and executes the specified expression in a single step.

aelEnvListDeferredFuncs.name: aelEnvListDeferredFuncs
aelEnvListDeferredFuncs.desc: Returns a list of all functions found in the compiled or interpreted expressions in the given environment that are undefined in AEL.

aelEnvListDeferredGlobals.name: aelEnvListDeferredGlobals
aelEnvListDeferredGlobals.desc: Returns a list of all globals found in the compiled or interpreted expressions in the given environment that have not been defined in a call to the aelEnvSetGlobals function.

aelEnvListExprFuncs.name: aelEnvListExprFuncs
aelEnvListExprFuncs.desc: Returns a list of all the functions found in the given expression.

aelEnvListExprGlobals.name: aelEnvListExprGlobals
aelEnvListExprGlobals.desc: Returns a list of all the globals found in a given expression.

aelEnvListFuncs.name: aelEnvListFuncs
aelEnvListFuncs.desc: Returns a list of all the functions defined for all AEL environments.

aelEnvListGlobals.name: aelEnvListGlobals
aelEnvListGlobals.desc: Returns a list of all the globals in a given AEL environment. The list does not include AEL predefined constant globals or deferred globals.

aelEnvListGlobalsValues.name: aelEnvListGlobalsValues
aelEnvListGlobalsValues.desc: Returns a list of all global names and their values in a given AEL environment. The list does not include AEL predefined constant globals or deferred globals.

aelEnvName.name: aelEnvName
aelEnvName.desc: Accepts text or a symbol and returns a legal AEL name stripped of any leading or trailing white space that might have been in the argument.

aelEnvSetGlobals.name: aelEnvSetGlobals
aelEnvSetGlobals.desc: Sets the values of the named globals in a given environment, creating them if necessary.

aelEnvSetGlobalList.name: aelEnvSetGlobalList
aelEnvSetGlobalList.desc: Using a disembodied property list as input sets the values of the named globals in a given environment.

aelSetLineage.name: aelSetLineage
aelSetLineage.desc: The aelSetLineage function sets reference to a lineage for hierarchical expression evaluation. The lineage can either be a list or an aelLineage (SKILL user-defined) object. In either case, an aelLineage object is returned. The list is an ordered list of cell views whose car is the current instance, whose cadr is its parent, and so on. The last element of this list should be the top cell view.

vpmDefinePowerSwitchInstance.name: vpmDefinePowerSwitchInstance
vpmDefinePowerSwitchInstance.syntax:
vpmDefinePowerSwitchInstance(
t_cellName
t_instName
g_type 
g_stage1Enable

vpmExportDotLib.name: vpmExportDotLib
vpmExportDotLib.desc: Exports the extracted power intent in the .lib file format.

vpmExportPowerIntent.name: vpmExportPowerIntent
vpmExportPowerIntent.desc: Exports the 1801 Design Model for a design. Ensure that the design has been extracted by using vpmExtractPowerIntent or the GUI options in Virtuoso Schematic Editor. This function requires a session ID, which is generated upon successful power intent extraction for the design.

vpmExportPowerModel.name: vpmExportPowerModel
vpmExportPowerModel.desc: Exports the 1801 power model for a design. Ensure that the design has been extracted by using vpmExtractPowerIntent, or using the GUI options in Virtuoso Schematic Editor. This function requires a session ID, which is generated upon successful power intent extraction for the design.

vpmExportPowerIntentSetup.name: vpmExportPowerIntentSetup
vpmExportPowerIntentSetup.syntax:
vpmExportPowerIntentSetup(
t_setup_file_name
[ ?overwriteExisting g_overwriteExisting ]
[ ?filter g_filter ]
[ ?lpDBLibName g_lpDBLibName ]
[ ?lpDBCellName g_lpDBCellName ]
[ ?lpDBViewName g_lpDBViewName ]
)
=> t / nil
vpmExportPowerIntentSetup.desc: Exports the loaded setup to a specified file. This file can be verified for the setup options that the Power Manager has used during import/export of power intent.

vpmExtractPowerIntent.name: vpmExtractPowerIntent
vpmExtractPowerIntent.syntax:
vpmExtractPowerIntent(
t_lib
t_cellName
t_viewName
)
=> session_id / nil
vpmExtractPowerIntent.desc: Extracts the power intent from the given design. It also identifies sub-hierarchical blocks in the top-level design, which need macro model extraction or are associated with a 1801 file.

vpmGenerateSigInfo.name: vpmGenerateSigInfo
vpmGenerateSigInfo.syntax:
vpmGenerateSigInfo(
t_libName
t_cellName
t_viewName
t_sigInfoFilePath
)
=> session_id / nil
vpmGenerateSigInfo.desc: Adds the signal type and voltage values for all the canonical nets in the design. If a design net spans across multiple levels in the hierarchy, the net at the highest level of the hierarchy is considered as canonical.

vpmImportPowerIntent.name: vpmImportPowerIntent
vpmImportPowerIntent.syntax:
vpmImportPowerIntent(
t_libname
t_cellname 
t_viewname
t_viewlist
t_file1801Path
[ ?resolveTopNets g_resolveTopNets ]
)
=> t / nil
vpmImportPowerIntent.desc: Imports the power intent for any cellview. It also creates the netSet properties and resolves tie connections in the design hierarchy and creates supply pins corresponding to the power domain nets and global nets.

vpmImportPowerIntentSetup.name: vpmImportPowerIntentSetup
vpmImportPowerIntentSetup.syntax:
vpmImportPowerIntentSetup(
t_libname
t_cellname 
t_viewname
t_setup_file_name
[ ?lpDBLibName g_lpDBLibName ]
[ ?lpDBCellName g_lpDBCellName ]
[ ?lpDBViewName g_lpDBViewName ]
)
=> t / nil
vpmImportPowerIntentSetup.desc: Imports a SKILL file that contains the user-defined setup. This has the attributes required to extract the desired information from the design cellview for importing or exporting the power intent.

vpmLoadInDesignViolations.name: vpmLoadInDesignViolations
vpmLoadInDesignViolations.syntax:
vpmLoadInDesignViolations(
t_libname
t_cellname 
t_viewname
t_vdbFilePath
)
=> t / nil
vpmLoadInDesignViolations.desc: Loads the specified violation database file that contains the violation details for a previous check on a design. As the SKILL function processes each violation from the violations file, it creates markers on relevant design objects.

vpmRemoveImportedPowerIntent.name: vpmRemoveImportedPowerIntent
vpmRemoveImportedPowerIntent.syntax:
vpmRemoveImportedPowerIntent(
t_libName
t_cellName
t_viewName
)
=> t_viewlist/ nil
vpmRemoveImportedPowerIntent.desc: Removes the entire power intent information that was imported for a cellview. This function also removes the netSet properties, tie connections, supply pins, and so on.

vpmRemovePowerSwitchInstance.name: vpmRemovePowerSwitchInstance
vpmRemovePowerSwitchInstance.desc: Removes registered transistor instances as power or ground switches.

hdlPkgCreateEnvSetupFile.syntax:
hdlPkgCreateEnvSetupFile( 
t_fileName 
[ ?formatLList { t | nil }]
)
=> t / nil
hdlPkgCreateEnvSetupFile.desc: Saves the environment variables used by the HDL Package Setup from the current Virtuoso setup database into a specified file. Each name-value pair for a variable is printed in the following format:

hdlPkgExportXrunArgs.name: hdlPkgExportXrunArgs
hdlPkgExportXrunArgs.syntax:
hdlPkgExportXrunArgs( 
t_fileName 
[ ?format { t | nil } ]
[ ?isExpandPath { t | nil } ]
[ ?userSpecOnly { t | nil } ]
)
=> t / nil
hdlPkgExportXrunArgs.desc: Exports the xrun arguments corresponding to environment variables used by the HDL Package Setup from the current Virtuoso setup database into the specified file.

teDiscardEdits.name: teDiscardEdits
teDiscardEdits.desc: Rolls back the recent updates being done in all the opened editors displaying the specified cellview to the last saved changes.

teGetCursorPosition.name: teGetCursorPosition
teGetCursorPosition.desc: Returns the character position of the cursor in the current or specified Virtuoso Text Editor window.

teIsModified.name: teIsModified
teIsModified.desc: Checks if a given text cellview been modified since last save.

teSave.name: teSave
teSave.desc: Saves the edits done in the text editor cellview.

teSaveWithDerivedData.name: teSaveWithDerivedData
teSaveWithDerivedData.desc: Saves the in-memory content of the text editor open for the given cellview and generates the derived data (typically, creates a shadow database).

teSetCursor.name: teSetCursor
teSetCursor.desc: Places the cursor on the specified character position in the current or specified Virtuoso Text Editor window.

teSetEditMode.name: teSetEditMode
teSetEditMode.desc: Sets the editing mode for the specifed cellview to read-only(r)or editable(a) based on the value of the mode argument.

teRegPostExtractTrigger.name: teRegPostExtractTrigger
teRegPostExtractTrigger.desc: Registers a user-defined function that is triggered after the text editor extraction completes.

teRegPreExtractTrigger.name: teRegPreExtractTrigger
teRegPreExtractTrigger.desc: Registers a user-defined function that is triggered before the text editor extraction starts.

teUnRegPostExtractTrigger.name: teUnRegPostExtractTrigger
teUnRegPostExtractTrigger.desc: Unregisters functions previously registered by you so that they are no longer triggered after the text editor functionality is being run.

teUnRegPreExtractTrigger.name: teUnRegPreExtractTrigger
teUnRegPreExtractTrigger.desc: Unregisters functions previously registered by you so that they are no longer triggered prior to running the text editor functionality.

hdlGenerateTextDatabase.name: hdlGenerateTextDatabase
hdlGenerateTextDatabase.syntax:
hdlGenerateTextDatabase( 
t_libName
t_cellName
t_viewName
) 
=> t / nil
hdlGenerateTextDatabase.desc: Generates the text database for analog and digital languages without requiring the Text Editor.

leEnvLoad.name: leEnvLoad
leEnvLoad.desc: Loads the Virtuoso Layout Suite environment variables from the .cdsenv files. This file must be in your home directory. The variables are read into memory, but the windows are not updated with the new values. When new windows are created, they assume the new values.

leGetEnv.name: leGetEnv
leGetEnv.desc: Returns the value currently assigned to the layout environment properties with the variable t_name.

leSetEnv.name: leSetEnv
leSetEnv.desc: Sets the layout environment properties with the variable t_name to the value g_value.

leIsLayoutViewerAppEnabled.name: leIsLayoutViewerAppEnabled
leIsLayoutViewerAppEnabled.desc: Checks whether the layout viewer application is available.

leIsLayoutViewerWindow.name: leIsLayoutViewerWindow
leIsLayoutViewerWindow.desc: Checks whether the given window has layout viewer application installed on it.

leCreateAutoPin.name: leCreateAutoPin
leCreateAutoPin.syntax:
leCreateAutoPin(
d_cellViewId 
l_point 
t_termName
t_termDir
[ l_lpp ]
[ g_pinSnapToWireEnd ]
[ x_depth ]
[ g_truncateWire ]
)
=> d_pinShapeId / nil
leCreateAutoPin.desc: Creates a pin shape in cellview d_cellViewId.

leCreatePath.name: leCreatePath
leCreatePath.syntax:
leCreatePath(
d_cellViewId 
l_layerPurposePair
l_points 
n_width 
[ t_pathStyle ]
[ n_offset ] 
[ t_justification ]
) 
=> d_pathId / nil
leCreatePath.desc: Creates a path in cellview d_cellViewId on the specified layer with point list l_points and width n_width.

leCreatePin.name: leCreatePin
leCreatePin.syntax:
leCreatePin(
d_cellViewId 
l_layerPurposePair
t_shape 
l_points 
t_termName 
t_termDir 
l_accessDir
)
=> d_pinShapeId / nil
leCreatePin.desc: Creates a pin shape in cellview d_cellViewId on the specified layer.

leDefineMPPTemplate.name: leDefineMPPTemplate
leDefineMPPTemplate.syntax:
leDefineMPPTemplate(
	?techId              d_techId
	?name                S_name
	?layer               list(layerName layerPurpose)
	[ ?width             n_width ]
	[ ?justification     S_justification ]
	[ ?offset            n_offset ]
	[ ?endType           S_endType ]
	[ ?beginExt          n_beginExt ]
	[ ?endExt            n_endExt ]
	[ ?choppable         g_choppable ]

	[ ROD Connectivity Arguments ]
	[ ?offsetSubPath     l_offsetSubpathArgs... ]
	[ ?encSubPath        l_encSubpathArgs... ]
	[ ?subRect           l_subrectArgs... ]

) ; end leDefineMPPTemplate
=> t / nil

	; ROD Connectivity Arguments
	[ ?termIOType             S_termIOType ]
	[ ?pin                     g_pin ]
	[ ?pinAccessDir           tl_pinAccessDir ]
	[ ?pinLabel               g_pinLabel ]
	[ ?pinLabelHeight         n_pinLabelHeight ]
	[ ?pinLabelLayer          txl_pinLabelLayer ]
	[ ?pinLabelFont           S_pinLabelFont ]
	[ ?pinLabelDrafting        g_pinLabelDrafting ]
	[ ?pinLabelOrient         S_pinLabelOrient ]
	[ ?pinLabelOffsetPoint     l_pinLabelOffsetPoint ]
	[ ?pinLabelJust           S_pinLabelJust ]
	[ ?pinLabelRefHandle      S_pinLabelRefHandle ]
	; end of ROD Connectivity Arguments

	;l_offsetSubpathArgs 
	list(
		list(
			?layer             list(layerName layerPurpose)
			[ ?width           n_width ]
			[ ?sep             n_sep ]
			[ ?justification   S_justification ]
			[ ?beginOffset     n_beginOffset ]
			[ ?endOffset       n_endOffset ]
			[ ?choppable       g_choppable ]
			[ Repeat ROD Connectivity Arguments here ]
			) ;End of first offset subpath list
			...		
		) ;End of offset subpath lists
	;End of l_offsetSubpathArgs

	;l_encSubpathArgs 
	list(
		list(
			?layer             list(layerName layerPurpose)
			[ ?enclosure       n_enclosure ]
			[ ?beginOffset     n_beginOffset ]
			[ ?endOffset       n_endOffset ]
			[ ?choppable       g_choppable ]	
			[ Repeat ROD Connectivity Arguments here ]
			) ;End of first enclosure subpath list
			...		
		) ;End of enclosure subpath lists
	;End of l_encSubpathArgs

	;l_subrectArgs 
	list(
		list(
			?layer              list(layerName layerPurpose)
			[ ?width            n_width ]
			[ ?length           n_length ]
			[ ?gap              S_gap ]
			[ ?sep              n_sep ]
			[ ?justification    S_justification ]
			[ ?beginOffset      n_beginOffset ]
			[ ?endOffset        n_endOffset ]
			[ ?beginSegOffset   n_beginSegmentOffset
			[ ?endSegOffset     n_endSegmentOffset
			[ ?space            n_space ]
			[ ?choppable        g_choppable ]
			[ Repeat ROD Connectivity Arguments here ]
			[?diagonal g_diagonalSubRect]
			) ;End of first subrectangle list
			...		
		) ;End of subrectangle lists
	;End of l_subrectArgs
leDefineMPPTemplate.desc: Provides the structure for defining the field names and default values for one multipart path (MPP) in an ASCII file. This information is referred to as an MPP template. A multipart path is a single relative object design (ROD) object consisting of one or more parts at level zero in the hierarchy on the same or on different layers. The purpose of an MPP template is to create MPPs in layout cellviews using predefined values. You can define any number of MPP templates in a single ASCII file by specifying leDefineMPPTemplate once for each MPP template; each template must be identified by a template name (t_name) that is unique within the ASCII file.

leHiCreateSlot.name: leHiCreateSlot
leHiCreateSlot.desc: Runs the Create Slot command in the specified window. You are prompted to select a rectangle or path to which you want to add slots. Press F3 to open the Create Slot form and specify the settings for creating slots. If w_windowId is not specified, the current window is used.

lePlot.name: lePlot
lePlot.desc: Generates the plot defined in the t_fileName plot template file. Plot options are stored in a disembodied property list called lePlotOptions. When lePlot() loads the plot template file, it reads the plot options from the lePlotOptions property list. There are two ways to create the plot template file: use vi, or save the options in the Submit Plot form to a file. The plot template file is used by lePlot() and by the Load command in the Submit Plot form. However, the following options are ignored by the Load command: library, cell, view, and plotSize.

leAlign.name: leAlign
leAlign.desc: Aligns the objects in the selection set. The objects are aligned to the left, right, top, or bottom edge of the selection box or along the center of the selection box in the vertical or horizontal direction.

leAttachFig.name: leAttachFig
leAttachFig.desc: Attaches d_figId1 to d_figId2 by making d_figId1 a child of d_figId2. If d_figId1 is already attached to another object, it is detached from it. If d_figId2 is not specified, d_figId1 is detached from any object it is currently attached to without attaching it to anything else.

leChopShape.name: leChopShape
leChopShape.syntax:
leChopShape(
d_shapeId 
l_points 
g_closed 
[ g_remove ] 
[ x_sides ]
) 
=> l_newShapes / nil
leChopShape.desc: Cuts the shape d_shapeId using the chop shape l_points.

leComputeAreaDensity.name: leComputeAreaDensity
leComputeAreaDensity.syntax:
leComputeAreaDensity(
w_windowId
l_lppSpec
[ ?depth x_depth ]
[ ?region l_region ]
) 
=> l_result / nil
leComputeAreaDensity.desc: Computes the total area and the density of shapes with specified layers within a region. If part of the shape is inside the region, only the area of the part that is inside the region is calculated.

leComputeFigArea.name: leComputeFigArea
leComputeFigArea.desc: Computes the area of an object. The following objects are supported: rectangle, label, text display, polygon, ellipse, dot, marker, donut, path, figGroup, row, pathSeg, transmission line (trl), bend, taper, area or layer blockage, and area, snap, cluster, or place and route (PR) boundary.

leConvertInstToMosaic.name: leConvertInstToMosaic
leConvertInstToMosaic.syntax:
leConvertInstToMosaic(
d_instId | ld_instId
[ mode { t | nil } ]
) 
=> ld_mosaicId / nil
leConvertInstToMosaic.desc: Converts one or more selected instances into one or more mosaics.

leConvertMosaicToModgen.name: leConvertMosaicToModgen
leConvertMosaicToModgen.syntax:
leConvertMosaicToModgen(
d_mosaicId | ld_mosaicId
) 
=> d_modgenId | ld_modgenId / nil
leConvertMosaicToModgen.desc: Converts one or more selected mosaics into one or more modgens.

leConvertPolygonToPath.name: leConvertPolygonToPath
leConvertPolygonToPath.desc: Converts the polygon d_polygonId to a path. If the conversion is successful, the polygon is replaced by a path with the same boundary as the polygon.

leConvertSelectedDynamicShapes.name: leConvertSelectedDynamicShapes
leConvertSelectedDynamicShapes.desc: (Virtuoso RF Option) Converts the selected dynamic shapes to static shapes.

leConvertShapeToPathSeg.name: leConvertShapeToPathSeg
leConvertShapeToPathSeg.desc: Converts a shape to an equivalent pathSeg. The function follows the routing direction defined for the corresponding layer in the technology file.

leConvertShapeToPolygon.name: leConvertShapeToPolygon
leConvertShapeToPolygon.desc: Converts shape d_shapeId to an equivalent polygon. If it is a conic, the polygon has the specified number of sides.

leConvertTrimmedShapesToPRStyle.name: leConvertTrimmedShapesToPRStyle
leConvertTrimmedShapesToPRStyle.syntax:
leConvertTrimmedShapesToPRStyle(
d_cvId
[ ?layerName t_layerName ]
[ ?depth x_depth ]
[ ?library l_library ]
) 
=> x_count / nil
leConvertTrimmedShapesToPRStyle.desc: Converts pathSegs that are trimmed by trim shapes in custom style to PR style so that they are readable in Innovus. Only pathSegs trimmed by trim shapes in the same cellview are converted. PathSegs that are trimmed by trim shapes in a different clone or in a different cellview are not converted. The function searches all trimmed pathSegs on the specified layer in the hierarchy up to the specified depth and converts them to PR style only in the cellviews of the libraries specified. The function also adds the relevant patch type to pathSegs abutted to trim shapes.

leCopyTemplatesToCellView.name: leCopyTemplatesToCellView
leCopyTemplatesToCellView.desc: Copies the row region templates and WSPDefs from the source cellview specified with the environment variable autoCopyTemplateCellViewList to the cellview specified in this function. If the cellview has existing templates, the new templates from the source cellview are not copied.

leCreateLayerField.name: leCreateLayerField
leCreateLayerField.syntax:
leCreateLayerField(
s_name
?callback t_callback
?appendChoices l_appendChoices
?prependChoices l_prependChoices
?maxVisibleItems x_maxVisibleItems
?syncedPaletteWindow w_syncedPaletteWindow
?techFile d_techFile
?value t_value
?enabled g_enabled
?invisible g_invisible
?layerFunction t_layerFunction
?maxWidth x_maxWidth
) 
=> t_layerfield
leCreateLayerField.desc: Creates a cyclic field for to display layer-purpose pair (LPP) names with swatches. The combo box created allows you to type and search for a layer purpose pair within the list of values. The list of layers is displayed only if a layout window is open.

leCreateNetField.name: leCreateNetField
leCreateNetField.syntax:
leCreateNetField 
name
?value t_value
?callback t_callback
x_maxVisibleItems
) 
=> netfield
leCreateNetField.desc: Creates cyclic field for showing net names of the current cellview. The combo box created allows you to type in and search for the net names within the list of values.

leCycleSnapModes.name: leCycleSnapModes
leCycleSnapModes.desc: Changes both the edit and create snap modes, in the order of diagonal, anyAngle, and orthogonal. If the edit and create mode values are different (unsynchronized), the first value for Create/Edit snap mode will be diagonal.

leDecrementStopLevelByOne.name: leDecrementStopLevelByOne
leDecrementStopLevelByOne.desc: Decrements the stop level value of the specified window by one when it is greater than zero.

leDefineExternalPins.name: leDefineExternalPins
leDefineExternalPins.desc: Starts the Define External Pins enter function in the current window. The Define External Pins enter function provides a user interface for defining one or more pins on a net as being externally connected outside of a device.

leDefineInternalPins.name: leDefineInternalPins
leDefineInternalPins.desc: Starts the Define Internal Pins enter function in the current window. The Define Internal Pins enter function provides a user interface for defining one or more pins on a net as being internally connected within a device.

leDefinePPPins.name: leDefinePPPins
leDefinePPPins.desc: Starts the Define Pseudo Parallel Connected Net enter function in the current window. Corresponds to the Connectivity - Pins - Pseudo Parallel Connect command. The Define Pseudo Parallel Connected Net form provides a user interface for defining one or more pins on a net as being pseudo parallel connected. If you do not specify w_windowId, the current window is used.

leDefineWeaklyConnectedPins.name: leDefineWeaklyConnectedPins
leDefineWeaklyConnectedPins.desc: Starts the Define Weak Pins enter function in the current window. The Define Weak Pins enter function provides a user interface for defining one or more pins on a net as being weakly connected within a device.

leEnableInstPropEditFields.name: leEnableInstPropEditFields
leEnableInstPropEditFields.syntax:
leEnableInstPropEditFields( 
t_libName
[ ?libField g_libField ]
[ ?cellField g_cellField ]
=> t / nil
leEnableInstPropEditFields.desc: Enables or disables the Library or Cell fields for an instance in the Property Editor form.

leFlattenInst.name: leFlattenInst
leFlattenInst.syntax:
leFlattenInst(
d_instId 
x_levels 
[ g_flattenPCells ]
[ g_preservePins ]
[ g_preserveRODobjs ]
[ g_delDetachedBlockages ]
[ g_preservePinFigs ]
[ g_flattenVias ]
[ g_preserveTermName ]
[ t_excludePcellListFileName ]
) 
=> t / nil
leFlattenInst.desc: Flattens instance d_instId up through x_levels of hierarchy. The optional arguments are positional: you must specify nil for optional arguments prior to an optional argument you want to specify. For example, if you do not want to specify g_flattenPCells, but want to set g_preservePins to t, you need to specify both (nil t).

leFreezeInst.name: leFreezeInst
leFreezeInst.syntax:
leFreezeInst(
d_instId 
t_libName
t_cellName
t_viewName
[ g_overwrite ]
[ g_reuse ]
) 
=> t / nil
leFreezeInst.desc: Converts a Pcell instance to a non-Pcell instance of a new master created on the disk for the specified library, cell, and view. This function is supported for mosaics.

leHiAreaDensity.name: leHiAreaDensity
leHiAreaDensity.desc: Opens the Area and Density Calculator form in the specified window. This form lets you compute area and density of shapes. You can choose options to specify region, LPP, and hierarchical depth for the shapes to be considered for area and density calculations. If w_windowId is not specified, the current window is used.

leHiAssignNet.name: leHiAssignNet
leHiAssignNet.desc: Starts the Assign Net enter function that provides the user interface for assigning new and existing nets to shapes, instance pins, vias, and pathSegs.

leHiConvertMosaicToModgen.name: leHiConvertMosaicToModgen
leHiConvertMosaicToModgen.desc: Converts one or more selected mosaics to an equivalent number of modgens. If w_windowId is not specified, the current window is used. You are prompted to select one or more mosaics to convert into modgens.

leHiEditSlot.name: leHiEditSlot
leHiEditSlot.desc: Opens the Edit Slot form in the specified window. You are prompted to select a rectangle or path containing slots, the settings of which are used to populate the Edit Slot form. If w_windowId is not specified, the current window is used.

leHiUnassignNet.name: leHiUnassignNet
leHiUnassignNet.desc: Unassigns nets to shapes, instance pins, and routed objects like vias and pathSegs.

leIncrementStopLevelByOne.name: leIncrementStopLevelByOne
leIncrementStopLevelByOne.desc: Increments the stop level value of the specified window by one.

leIOZoomToFigGroupTopLevelContext.name: leIOZoomToFigGroupTopLevelContext
leIOZoomToFigGroupTopLevelContext.desc: Zooms to the location of the selected figGroup occurrence in the main window.

leLmbCtrlOption.name: leLmbCtrlOption
leLmbCtrlOption.desc: Allows some Virtuoso Layout Suite creating and editing commands to override the Ctrl + Left mouse click. The command options are embedded in the Virtuoso Layout Suite software and cannot be changed.

leLmbShiftOption.name: leLmbShiftOption
leLmbShiftOption.desc: Allows some Virtuoso Layout Suite creating and editing commands to override the Shift + Left mouse click. The command options are embedded in the Virtuoso Layout Suite software and cannot be changed.

leMakeCell.name: leMakeCell
leMakeCell.syntax:
leMakeCell(
l_figs 
t_libName 
t_cellName 
t_viewName 
g_replace 
[ ?preserveConn g_preserveConn ]
[ ?createPins g_createPins ]
[ ?transInst g_transInst ]
[ ?pinsBelowBoundary g_pinsBelowBoundary ]
[ l_point ] 
[ t_cellType ] 
)
=> d_cellViewId / nil
leMakeCell.desc: Creates the cellview specified by t_libName, t_cellName, and t_viewName. If the cellview already exists, it is overwritten. The arguments ?preserveConn, ?createPins, ?transInst, and ?pinsBelowBoundary are only supported only in Layout XL and higher tiers.

leMakeHierReadonlyOrEditableMC.name: leMakeHierReadonlyOrEditableMC
leMakeHierReadonlyOrEditableMC.desc: Makes a cellview either read-only or editable. When one or more instances are selected before invoking this function, only the selected instance(s) are shown in the browser. When no instances are selected before invoking this function, all instances in the cellview are shown in the browser. If you do not specify w_windowId, the current window is used.

leMergeShapes.name: leMergeShapes
leMergeShapes.desc: Merges the list of shapes l_shapes. The input shapes can be on multiple layers. Merges only shapes on the same layer. Returns the list of shapes resulting from the operation.

leMicroEdit.name: leMicroEdit
leMicroEdit.desc: Allows using bindkeys instead of the mouse to move, copy, or stretch any shape. When no command is active, the selected shape is either moved or stretched, depending on whether the shape is fully or partially selected, respectively. When the copy, move, or stretch command is active, the selected shape is copied, moved, or stretched, respectively.

leModifyCorner.name: leModifyCorner
leModifyCorner.syntax:
leModifyCorner( 
d_figId
l_selArray
g_chamfer
x_distance
[ x_sides ]
) 
=> t / nil
leModifyCorner.desc: Rounds or cuts off selected corners of the rectangle or polygon specified by d_figID.

leMoveCellViewOrigin.name: leMoveCellViewOrigin
leMoveCellViewOrigin.desc: Moves the contents of cellview d_cellViewId so that the origin is at l_point.

lePasteFigs.name: lePasteFigs
lePasteFigs.syntax:
lePasteFigs(
d_cellViewId 
l_destPt 
[ t_rotation ]
[ t_referenceParameter ]
) 
=> t / nil
lePasteFigs.desc: Places the contents of the yank buffer in cellview d_cellViewId at the destination point l_destPt.

lePlGetApplyPrevData.name: lePlGetApplyPrevData
lePlGetApplyPrevData.desc: Prints the previously applied data from the property editor cache of the current session.

lePlGetEditorName.name: lePlGetEditorName
lePlGetEditorName.desc: Returns the editor name of the Edit Properties form if the form is open in the specified window.

leQuickAlignToggleMode.name: leQuickAlignToggleMode
leQuickAlignToggleMode.desc: Allows you to toggle between quick align modes - move or stretch, and copy.

leReturn.name: leReturn
leReturn.desc: Applies to instances, nested instances, groups, and nested groups for which you are editing-in-place. When editing instances or nested instances in Edit-in-Place mode, returns one level; when there is only one level, exits Edit-in-Place mode. When editing a un-nested group, exits Edit-in-Place Mode; when editing a nested group, returns to the group of which the edited group is a member. If you do not specify w_windowId, the current window is used.

leReturnToLevel.name: leReturnToLevel
leReturnToLevel.desc: Applies to instances, nested instances, groups, and nested groups for which you are editing-in-place. For instances, returns one or more levels up the hierarchy from the current level in the instance you last edited-in-place. When there is only one level, exits Edit-in-Place mode. When you have descended more than one level, this function displays the Return To Level form, showing the levels to which you can return. You select (highlight) the desired level and click OK. For example, if you are using leHiEditInPlace to edit a cellview two levels deep in your hierarchy, you can use leReturnToLevel to move up one or two levels in the hierarchy. For groups, returns from the group, and if the group is nested, from all groups in the nesting, and exits Edit-in-Place mode. If you do not specify w_windowId, the current window is used.

leReturnToTop.name: leReturnToTop
leReturnToTop.desc: Applies to instances, nested instances, groups, and nested groups for which you are editing-in-place. When editing instances or nested instances in Edit-in-Place mode, returns to top level, exits Edit-in-Place mode. For groups, returns from the group, and if the group is nested, from all groups in the nesting, and exits Edit-in-Place mode. If you do not specify w_windowId, the current window is used.

leSetStopLevelToEditLevel.name: leSetStopLevelToEditLevel
leSetStopLevelToEditLevel.desc: Sets the display stop level to the current editing level.

leSizeShape.name: leSizeShape
leSizeShape.desc: Resizes a shape by the specified amount. A shape can be resized uniformly in all directions or differently in different directions.

leSlice.name: leSlice
leSlice.desc: Performs the vertical slicing of a shape.

leSplitShape.name: leSplitShape
leSplitShape.syntax:
leSplitShape(
d_shapeId 
l_delta 
l_splitLine 
g_leftOrRight 
[ g_lockAngles ]
) 
=> t / nil
leSplitShape.desc: Splits a shape and moves one portion of it. Uses a multi-segment split line to divide the shape.

leStretchFig.name: leStretchFig
leStretchFig.syntax:
leStretchFig(
d_shapeId 
l_delta 
l_freePoints 
[ g_lockAngles ]
) 
=> t / nil
