leStretchFig.desc: Stretches shape d_shapeId by the delta l_delta. Donuts cannot be stretched.

leStretchShape.name: leStretchShape
leStretchShape.syntax:
leStretchShape(
d_shapeId 
l_delta 
l_freePoints 
[ g_lockAngles ]
) 
=> t / nil
leStretchShape.desc: Stretches shape d_shapeId by the delta l_delta. Donuts cannot be stretched.

leUnfreezeInst.name: leUnfreezeInst
leUnfreezeInst.desc: Unfreezes or converts the non-Pcell instance, d_instId, to its original Pcell instance. When an instance is unfreezed the leUnfreezeInst() function only re-evaluates the Pcell instance but does not explicitly call the CDF callbacks.

leUpdateInstanceCDFParameterValues.name: leUpdateInstanceCDFParameterValues
leUpdateInstanceCDFParameterValues.syntax:
leUpdateInstanceCDFParameterValues( 
d_cellViewId 
d_instId
l_paramNameList
) 
=> t / nil
leUpdateInstanceCDFParameterValues.desc: Updates the list of CDF parameters name-value pairs for the specified cellview and instance.

leYankFigs.name: leYankFigs
leYankFigs.syntax:
leYankFigs(
d_cellViewId 
l_ptArray 
x_nLevels
[ l_refPt ] 
[ x_nSides ]
) 
=> t / nil
leYankFigs.desc: Copies specified objects into a yank buffer for later pasting. Copies objects in cellview d_cellViewId that fall within the shape defined by the points in l_ptArray and that are in the levels of hierarchy specified by x_nLevels. Optionally uses l_refPt as the reference point for the yank and x_nSides as the number of polygon sides to use when converting objects intersected by the yank shape.

leApplyAreaFunction.name: leApplyAreaFunction
leApplyAreaFunction.syntax:
leApplyAreaFunction( 
s_funcs_funcSymbol
d_databaseId
l_paramList
) 
=> f_result / nil
leApplyAreaFunction.desc: Runs the area estimation function (provided as a function symbol) with provided parameters and database Id. This function is added as a part of Area Estimation consolidation.

leApplyLastCopyTransform.name: leApplyLastCopyTransform
leApplyLastCopyTransform.desc: Copies the selected objects and applies the same transform as done in the last copy command and selects the newly created objects.

leFullSelectFigOfSelSet.name: leFullSelectFigOfSelSet
leFullSelectFigOfSelSet.desc: Fully selects all the partially selected figures. If w_windowId is not specified, the current window is used.

leGetAreaEstimationDisplayNames.name: leGetAreaEstimationDisplayNames
leGetAreaEstimationDisplayNames.desc: Retrieves area estimation function alias name list defined for the specified object types. The object types supported are 'cellView, 'inst, cluster, 'group. This function is added as a part of Area Estimation consolidation.

leGetAreaEstimatorFunction.name: leGetAreaEstimatorFunction
leGetAreaEstimatorFunction.desc: Retrieves the function symbol of the area estimation function registered for alias name and object type. This function is added for Area Estimation Consolidation.

leGetAreaEstimatorParamList.name: leGetAreaEstimatorParamList
leGetAreaEstimatorParamList.desc: Retrieves the parameter list of the area estimation function registered for alias name and object type. This function is added as a part of area estimation consolidation.

leGetAreaEstimatorRunMode.name: leGetAreaEstimatorRunMode
leGetAreaEstimatorRunMode.desc: Retrieve the Run Mode list of the area estimation function registered for alias name and object types. This function is added as a part of area estimation consolidation.

leGetEditFigGroup.name: leGetEditFigGroup
leGetEditFigGroup.desc: Returns the database ID of the currently active figure group for Edit-In-Group mode editing, in the specified window or the current window.

leGetEntryLayer.name: leGetEntryLayer
leGetEntryLayer.desc: Returns the entry layer for technology file d_techFileId as a list containing the layer name and layer purpose. If d_techFileId is not specified, the current technology file is used.

leGetObjectSelectable.name: leGetObjectSelectable
leGetObjectSelectable.desc: Checks whether or not objects are set to selectable in the LSW.

leGetObjectVisible.name: leGetObjectVisible
leGetObjectVisible.desc: Checks whether or not objects are set to visible in the LSW.

leGetSnapOptions.name: leGetSnapOptions
leGetSnapOptions.desc: Generates the default snap options in the form of DPLs (Disembodied Property Lists). If a valid window ID is specified in the input list and it is a layout window, the options are listed considering window variables. If a window ID is not specified, the default values of environment variables are listed.

leGetSnapTransform.name: leGetSnapTransform
leGetSnapTransform.syntax:
leGetSnapTransform 
d_figToSnap 
d_targetRow | nil
l_projectionTransform 
l_ignoreFigs
l_options
g_detailedResults
) 
=> l_result / nil
leGetSnapTransform.desc: Returns snap transform for the figure. The cellview of the figure is the one where the snapping is taking place. This function does not modify figure or cellview so it works for read only cellview as well. The cellview and the specified options are used to determine the licenses needed for the function to run. If the licenses can be checked out, the function runs. If not, the return value signifies failure because of licensing.

leGetTechFormList.name: leGetTechFormList
leGetTechFormList.desc: Returns a disembodied property list (DPL) that stores the dynamic form Ids associated with a technology library opened in a Virtuoso session. If the forms have not been opened yet, the SKILL function creates the forms and returns the form ID list.

leGetValidLayerList.name: leGetValidLayerList
leGetValidLayerList.desc: Returns a list of the valid entry layers for technology file d_techFileId. A layout view must be open for leGetValidLayerList to return the list of valid entry layers.

leGetValidPurposeList.name: leGetValidPurposeList
leGetValidPurposeList.desc: Returns a list of all valid purposes for the specified technology file.

leIsFigSelectable.name: leIsFigSelectable
leIsFigSelectable.desc: Checks whether the figure d_figId is selectable.

leIsInstSelectable.name: leIsInstSelectable
leIsInstSelectable.desc: Checks whether the instances in d_techFileId are selectable. If d_techFileId is not specified, the current technology file is used.

leIsLayerSelectable.name: leIsLayerSelectable
leIsLayerSelectable.desc: Checks whether the layer l_layerPurposePair is selectable.

leIsLayerValid.name: leIsLayerValid
leIsLayerValid.desc: Checks whether layer l_layerPurposePair is a valid layer. If d_techFileId is not specified, the current technology file is used.

leIsLayerVisible.name: leIsLayerVisible
leIsLayerVisible.desc: Checks whether the layer specified by l_layerPurposePair is visible. If d_techFileId is not specified, the current technology file is used.

leIsNewODCInfraEnabled.name: leIsNewODCInfraEnabled
leIsNewODCInfraEnabled.desc: Checks if the new odcInfra is enabled or not in the current Virtuoso session.

leIsPinSelectable.name: leIsPinSelectable
leIsPinSelectable.desc: Checks whether the pins in d_techFileId are selectable. If d_techFileId is not specified, the current technology file is used.

leIsPointInsideFig.name: leIsPointInsideFig
leIsPointInsideFig.desc: Checks if the specified point is inside the figure.

leLSWGetBlockageSelectable.name: leLSWGetBlockageSelectable
leLSWGetBlockageSelectable.desc: Indicates whether a layer blockage is selectable.

leLSWGetBlockageVisible.name: leLSWGetBlockageVisible
leLSWGetBlockageVisible.desc: Sets whether a layer blockage is visible or not. If the blockage is successfully set to visible the function returns t. If it is not set to visible the function returns nil.

leLSWGetRoutingGridVisible.name: leLSWGetRoutingGridVisible
leLSWGetRoutingGridVisible.desc: Returns the visibility of the specified routing grid layer. For the layer specified, the following must be defined in the technology file: in the layerRules section, for routingDirections, the direction for the layer; in the constraintGroups section, for routingGrids, values for the horizontalPitch and verticalPitch. In the LSW, you can check this visibility by clicking on the Grid button, then on the Routing Grid button.

leLSWSetBlockageSelectable.name: leLSWSetBlockageSelectable
leLSWSetBlockageSelectable.syntax:
leLSWSetBlockageSelectable( 
t_blockageTypeName 
t_layerName 
g_status 
) 
=> t / nil
leLSWSetBlockageSelectable.desc: Sets whether a layer blockage is selectable or not. If the blockage is successfully set to selectable the function returns t. If it is not set to selectable the function returns nil.

leLSWSetBlockageVisible.name: leLSWSetBlockageVisible
leLSWSetBlockageVisible.syntax:
leLSWSetBlockageVisible( 
t_blockageTypeName 
t_layerName 
g_status 
) 
=> t / nil
leLSWSetBlockageVisible.desc: Sets whether a layer blockage is visible or not. If the blockage is successfully set to visible the function returns t. If it is not set to visible the function returns nil.

leLSWSetRoutingGridVisible.name: leLSWSetRoutingGridVisible
leLSWSetRoutingGridVisible.desc: Sets whether a specific routing layer grid is visible. For the layer specified, the following must be defined in the technology file: for routingDirections in the layerRules section, the direction for the layer; for routingGrids in the constraintGroups section, values for the horizontalPitch and verticalPitch. In the LSW, you set this visibility by clicking on the Grid button.

leLSWSetTrackPatternVisible.name: leLSWSetTrackPatternVisible
leLSWSetTrackPatternVisible.desc: Sets the status of the visibility of track patterns and the Track grid visibility button in the LSW. This function does not affect the visibility of individual track layer-purpose pairs; use the leSetObjectVisible function to control LLP visibility. To turn track grid visibility on or off using the graphical user interface, in the LSW window, click Grid, then check the Vis box next to Track.

lePrintHierarchyTree.name: lePrintHierarchyTree
lePrintHierarchyTree.desc: Opens a form to choose library, cell, and view and then generates the hierarchy information.

leRaiseLSW.name: leRaiseLSW
leRaiseLSW.desc: Raises the Layer Selection Window (LSW) to the top of the window stack. It can be used if the LSW has been iconified. If the LSW is already at the top of the window stack, this function has no effect.

leRegAreaEstimator.name: leRegAreaEstimator
leRegAreaEstimator.syntax:
leRegAreaEstimator( 
s_functionSymbol
t_functionAlias 
l_legalObjectTypes
[ l_parameterNameValuePairs ]
[ t_runMode ]
) 
=> t / nil
leRegAreaEstimator.desc: Registers a particular area estimation function. This function is part of area estimation consolidation. The name of the estimator that will appear in the cyclic Area Estimator field in the Create Cluster Boundary form, and the function the software will invoke when you click the Estimate button on the form. While searching for available area estimators, the applications/UI code should know the requirements for object types; the application provides database IDs and executes the area estimator in direct or deferred mode.

leRegClusterBdyEstimator.name: leRegClusterBdyEstimator
leRegClusterBdyEstimator.desc: Registers the name of the estimator which will appear in the cyclic field of the Area Estimator field in the Create Cluster Boundary form in the Floorplanning tool, and the function the software will invoke when you click the Estimate button on the form.

leRegisterPPNetNameFn.name: leRegisterPPNetNameFn
leRegisterPPNetNameFn.desc: Registers a SKILL function that specifies the names of pseudo-parallel subnets when called by the layout generation commands Generate All From Source and Update Components and Nets.

leRegisterUseGravity.name: leRegisterUseGravity
leRegisterUseGravity.desc: Enables a user-defined SKILL enter function to use the gravity feature. Gravity follows the options specified in the Layout Editor Options form.

leRegUserLayerSelectionFilter.name: leRegUserLayerSelectionFilter
leRegUserLayerSelectionFilter.desc: Registers a user-defined layer selection filter to prevent you from selecting shapes on the layers.

leRegUserObjectSelectionFilter.name: leRegUserObjectSelectionFilter
leRegUserObjectSelectionFilter.desc: Registers a user defined object selection filter to prevent you from selecting objects individually or as part of a selected set.

leRepeatCopyMoveStretch.name: leRepeatCopyMoveStretch
leRepeatCopyMoveStretch.desc: Copies, moves, or stretches the selected objects and applies the same transform as done in the last copy, move, or stretch command and selects the newly created objects. This function applies to all the options specified in the last copy, move, or stretch commands, including the Create Synchronous Copy option available only in Layout XL and higher tiers.

leReportTrimmedShapesInCustomStyle.name: leReportTrimmedShapesInCustomStyle
leReportTrimmedShapesInCustomStyle.syntax:
leReportTrimmedShapesInCustomStyle(
d_cvId
[ ?layerName t_layerName ]
[ ?depth x_depth ]
[ ?createMarker g_createMarker ]
[ ?printReport g_printReport ]
[ ?showReportWindow g_showReportWindow ]
[ ?saveReport t_saveReport ]
[ ?markerSeverity t_markerSeverity ]
) 
=> l_lists / nil
leReportTrimmedShapesInCustomStyle.desc: Reports pathsegs on the specified layer that have overlapping trim shapes and pathsegs that are abutted to trim shapes but do not have a relevant patch type. The function also reports the following: polygons, rectangles, and paths abutting or overlapping trim shapes, trim shapes that are abutted to pathsegs but do not have a bridge metal, and the trim shapes that are not abutted to pathsegs, polygons, rectangles, or paths in the same cellview. The function searches for trim shapes and metal shapes in the hierarchy up to the depth specified.

leResizeLSW.name: leResizeLSW
leResizeLSW.desc: Sets the Layer Selection Window's (LSW) bounding box to l_bBox. The bounding box specifies the lower left and upper right corners of the LSW window.

leSetAllGridObjectsVisible.name: leSetAllGridObjectsVisible
leSetAllGridObjectsVisible.desc: Sets all LSW grid pane objects to visible if g_isVisible is t, or invisible if g_isVisible is nil.

leSetAllLayerSelectable.name: leSetAllLayerSelectable
leSetAllLayerSelectable.desc: Sets the selectability of all layers in technology file d_techFileId as specified by g_isSelectable. If d_techFileId is not specified, the current technology file is used.

leSetAllLayerValid.name: leSetAllLayerValid
leSetAllLayerValid.desc: Sets the validity of all layers in technology file d_techFileId as specified by g_isValid. If d_techFileId is not specified, the current technology file is used.

leSetAllLayerVisible.name: leSetAllLayerVisible
leSetAllLayerVisible.desc: Sets the visibility of all layers in technology file d_techFileId as specified by g_isVisible. If d_techFileId is not specified, the current technology file is used.

leSetAllObjectsSelectable.name: leSetAllObjectsSelectable
leSetAllObjectsSelectable.desc: Sets the selectability of LSW objects in technology file d_techFileId as specified by g_isSelectable. If d_techFileId is not given, the current LSW technology file is used.

leSetAllObjectsVisible.name: leSetAllObjectsVisible
leSetAllObjectsVisible.desc: Sets the visibility of LSW objects in technology file d_techFileId as specified by g_isVisible. If d_techFileId is not given, the current technology file is used.

leSetAreaEstimatorParameters.name: leSetAreaEstimatorParameters
leSetAreaEstimatorParameters.desc: Opens a form to update the parameter list to new values. On pressing OK on the form, the updated parameter list is returned.

leSetEditFigGroup.name: leSetEditFigGroup
leSetEditFigGroup.desc: Sets the Edit-In-Place context for editing a specific group within a nested set of groups. For example, when fgBottom is contained in fgMiddle, and fgMiddle, is contained in fgTop, you can use this function and the figGroup ID for fgBottom to start Edit-in-Place for fgBottom.

leSetEntryLayer.name: leSetEntryLayer
leSetEntryLayer.desc: Sets the entry layer for technology file d_techFileId to the layer specified by l_layerPurposePair, which can be either a list containing a layer name and a layer purpose, or just a layer name (the layer purpose then defaults to drawing). If d_techFileId is not specified, the current technology file is used.

leSetFocusToEditableFieldsInStatusToolba.name: leSetFocusToEditableFieldsInStatusToolbar
leSetFocusToEditableFieldsInStatusToolba.desc: Sets the focus to the editable X field on the Status toolbar of the window, w_windowId.

leSetFormSnapMode.name: leSetFormSnapMode
leSetFormSnapMode.desc: Sets the cursor snap mode in a valid active window.

leSetInstSelectable.name: leSetInstSelectable
leSetInstSelectable.desc: Sets the selectability of instances in the technology file specified by d_techFileId as specified by g_isSelectable. If d_techFileId is not specified, the current technology file is used.

leSetLayerAttributes.name: leSetLayerAttributes
leSetLayerAttributes.syntax:
leSetLayerAttributes( 
d_techFileId 
g_layerPurposePair 
l_attributeList 
) 
=> t / nil
leSetLayerAttributes.desc: Sets the attributes of the specified layer in the technology file d_techFileId as specified by g_layerPurposePair and l_attributeList.

leSetLayerSelectable.name: leSetLayerSelectable
leSetLayerSelectable.syntax:
leSetLayerSelectable( 
l_layerPurposePair 
g_isSelectable 
[ d_techFileId ] 
) 
=> t / nil
leSetLayerSelectable.desc: Sets the selectability of shapes on layer l_layerPurposePair in technology file d_techFileId as specified by g_isSelectable. If d_techFileId is not specified, the current technology file is used. For shapes on a layer to be selectable, the layer must be valid, visible, and selectable.

leSetLayerValid.name: leSetLayerValid
leSetLayerValid.syntax:
leSetLayerValid( 
l_layerPurposePair 
g_isValid 
[ d_techFileId ] 
) 
=> t / nil
leSetLayerValid.desc: Sets the validity of layer l_layerPurposePair as specified by g_isValid. If d_techFileId is not specified, the current technology file is used. Only valid layers are displayed in the Layer Selection Window.

leSetLayerVisible.name: leSetLayerVisible
leSetLayerVisible.syntax:
leSetLayerVisible( 
l_layerPurposePair 
g_isVisible 
[ d_techFileId ] 
) 
=> t / nil
leSetLayerVisible.desc: Sets the visibility of the layer specified by the layer-purpose pair as specified by g_isVisible. If d_techFileId is not specified, the current technology file Layer Selection Window (LSW) is used.

leSetLSWFilter.name: leSetLSWFilter
leSetLSWFilter.desc: Specifies which layer-purpose pairs in the technology database to display in the Layer Selection Window (LSW). You can include one or more of the following types of layers: valid layers, rule layers, user layers.

leSetObjectSelectable.name: leSetObjectSelectable
leSetObjectSelectable.desc: Turns on or off the selectability of the layers used for objectName or updates the selectability of instances or pins as specified by g_isSelectable.

leSetObjectVisible.name: leSetObjectVisible
leSetObjectVisible.desc: Turns on or off the visibility of the layers used for objectName or updates the visibility of instances or pins as specified by g_isVisible.

leSetPinSelectable.name: leSetPinSelectable
leSetPinSelectable.desc: Sets the selectability of pins in the technology file specified by d_techFileId as specified by g_isSelectable. If d_techFileId is not specified, the current technology file is used.

leSetStopLevelToMaxHierDepth.name: leSetStopLevelToMaxHierDepth
leSetStopLevelToMaxHierDepth.desc: Sets the display stop level to the maximum hierarchy depth, which is 31.

leToggleAutoZoomPan.name: leToggleAutoZoomPan
leToggleAutoZoomPan.desc: Toggles the current value of dynamic zoom for the specified w_windowId. If w_windowId is not specified, the current window is used.

leToggleKeepFirstName.name: leToggleKeepFirstName
leToggleKeepFirstName.desc: Toggles the Keep First Name option on or off on the Create Pin form. When this option is on, you can create multiple pins with the same terminal name.

leToggleMagnifier.name: leToggleMagnifier
leToggleMagnifier.desc: Toggles the visibility of the magnifier between on and off.

leToggleMaintainConnections.name: leToggleMaintainConnections
leToggleMaintainConnections.desc: Turns Maintain Connections on or off.

leToggleRuleGravity.name: leToggleRuleGravity
leToggleRuleGravity.desc: Turns rule gravity on or off.

leToggleSmartSnap.name: leToggleSmartSnap
leToggleSmartSnap.desc: Toggles the smart snap mode of ruler between no snapping (off) and snap to any target (on).

leUnregisterUseGravity.name: leUnregisterUseGravity
leUnregisterUseGravity.desc: Prevents a user-defined SKILL enter function to use gravity. By default, gravity is available only for SKILL enter functions for which gravity has been enabled using the leRegisterUseGravity function.

leUnregUserLayerSelectionFilter.name: leUnregUserLayerSelectionFilter
leUnregUserLayerSelectionFilter.desc: Unregisters user defined layer selection filter.

leUnregUserObjectSelectionFilter.name: leUnregUserObjectSelectionFilter
leUnregUserObjectSelectionFilter.desc: Unregisters user defined object selection filter.

leUnRegAreaEstimator.name: leUnRegAreaEstimator
leUnRegAreaEstimator.desc: Unregisters a particular area estimation function for one or more object types.

leUnRegClusterBdyEstimator.name: leUnRegClusterBdyEstimator
leUnRegClusterBdyEstimator.desc: Unregisters the name of the estimator which will subsequently no longer appear in the cyclic field of the Area Estimator field in the Create Cluster Boundary form in Layout XL.

leZoomToPoint.name: leZoomToPoint
leZoomToPoint.desc: Places the cursor in the window, w_windowId, at the coordinates specified in l_points.

leZoomToSelSet.name: leZoomToSelSet
leZoomToSelSet.desc: Zooms to fit the selected objects in the specified window. If w_windowId is not specified, the current window is used.

leGetRefPoint.name: leGetRefPoint
leGetRefPoint.desc: Returns the reference point of cellview d_cellViewId. The reference point must be active.

leIsRefPointActive.name: leIsRefPointActive
leIsRefPointActive.desc: Checks whether the cellview d_cellViewId contains an active reference point.

leMoveCursor.name: leMoveCursor
leMoveCursor.desc: Moves the cursor in the current window a relative distance specified by f_dX and f_dY.

leMoveCursorToRefPoint.name: leMoveCursorToRefPoint
leMoveCursorToRefPoint.desc: Moves the cursor to the reference point of the cellview contained in the current window.

leSetRefPoint.name: leSetRefPoint
leSetRefPoint.desc: Sets the reference point of cellview d_cellViewId to the point l_point. The reference point is set to be active if it was inactive.

leSetRefPointInactive.name: leSetRefPointInactive
leSetRefPointInactive.desc: Marks the reference point for cellview d_cellViewId as inactive. To make a reference point active again, use leSetRefPoint.

leCARCommand.name: leCARCommand
leCARCommand.syntax:
leCARCommand( 
t_replayFileName 
[ g_enterPointFlag ]
[ g_debugFlag ]
) 
=> l_recordedActions / nil
leCARCommand.desc: (Layout EXL and higher tiers only) Replays the set of actions recorded in a .car file.

leCARReloadReplays.name: leCARReloadReplays
leCARReloadReplays.desc: (Layout EXL and higher tiers only) Reloads the replays in all the open sessions. The replays with .car extension are displayed in the refreshed list of replay buttons.

leCARStartCapture.name: leCARStartCapture
leCARStartCapture.desc: (Layout EXL and higher tiers only) Starts recording the actions that you perform in the current design window.

leCARStopCapture.name: leCARStopCapture
leCARStopCapture.desc: (Layout EXL and higher tiers only) Stops the recording that was started using the leCARStartCapture SKILL function.

leClearAllMeasurement.name: leClearAllMeasurement
leClearAllMeasurement.desc: Deletes all measurements in the specified cellview.

leCreateMeasurement.name: leCreateMeasurement
leCreateMeasurement.syntax:
leCreateMeasurement( 
d_cellViewId 
l_points 
[ g_saveRulers ]
[ t_rulerDisplayType ]
) 
=> d_rulerID / nil
leCreateMeasurement.desc: Creates a measurement in cellview d_cellViewId with the coordinates listed in l_points.

leHiClearMeasurement.name: leHiClearMeasurement
leHiClearMeasurement.desc: Clears the edit cellview measurement for the specified window. If windowId is not specified, the current window is used.

leHiClearMeasurementInHier.name: leHiClearMeasurementInHier
leHiClearMeasurementInHier.desc: Clears the measurements in the hierarchy in the specified window. If windowId is not specified, the current window is used.

leHiCreateMeasurement.name: leHiCreateMeasurement
leHiCreateMeasurement.desc: Starts the create measurement enter function in the edited cellview of the specified window. If windowId is not specified, the current window is used.

leBalloonCycleThru.name: leBalloonCycleThru
leBalloonCycleThru.desc: Cycles through overlapping objects displaying Info Balloon information for the individual objects. By default, the function is registered to Ctrl + i.

leBalloonToggleOnOff.name: leBalloonToggleOnOff
leBalloonToggleOnOff.desc: Turns Info Balloons on or off. Info Balloons opens a window which displays information about an object when the mouse cursor is placed over the object.

leHiEditObjectInfo.name: leHiEditObjectInfo
leHiEditObjectInfo.desc: Opens the Setup tab of the Dynamic Display form. The form allows you to customize data displayed by Info Balloon and Dynamic Measurement.

leRemasterInstances.name: leRemasterInstances
leRemasterInstances.syntax:
leRemasterInstances( 
d_cellViewId 
t_searchLibrary 
t_searchCellview 
t_searchViewName 
t_updateLibrary 
t_updateCellview 
t_updateViewName 
[ g_checkTerminals ]
) 
=> t / nil
leRemasterInstances.desc: Searches for instances based on the view name, cell name, and the library name for a given cellviewID, then re-masters those instances with the master that matches the update library, update cell and update view names you provide. The * wildcard can be used in any search string to replace any number of characters prior to or following the asterisk. If any of the search strings are empty then all matches in the cds.lib are considered, if matches exist. If any of the update strings are empty the update string uses the equivalent search string value. If both the search and the update strings are empty, only exact matches of the respective strings are considered. Due to the extensive changes available when using this command, making a backup copy of your design to guard against errors when replacing data is recommended.

leReplace.name: leReplace
leReplace.syntax:
leReplace( 
d_cellViewId 
l_objects 
l_replaceValues 
) 
=> t / nil
leReplace.desc: Replaces the specified values on the specified list of objects in the cellview d_cellViewId.

leReplaceAnyInstMaster.name: leReplaceAnyInstMaster
leReplaceAnyInstMaster.desc: Changes the master library, cell, or view name for the instance. If you do not want to change any of these names, you must type nil in its place.

leSearchHierarchy.name: leSearchHierarchy
leSearchHierarchy.syntax:
leSearchHierarchy(
d_cellViewId
l_bBox
x_stopLevel
t_objectType
l_criteriaList
)
=> l_objects / nil
leSearchHierarchy.desc: Searches the cellview d_cellViewId for objects that match the type and criteria specified. The search is bound by the specified l_bBox and restricted to the specified x_stopLevel. The search assumes all figures are valid if the Layer Selection Window (LSW) has not been initialized.

leDescend.name: leDescend
leDescend.syntax:
leDescend(
w_windowId 
d_instId 
[ x_row ] 
[ x_column ] 
) 
=> w_windowId / nil
leDescend.desc: Descends through the hierarchy to open the master of instance d_instId. leDescend attempts to open the cellview in the same mode as the current cellview, but if an editable version is not available, leDescend opens the master in read-only mode.

leDoubleClick.name: leDoubleClick
leDoubleClick.desc: Runs the Edit In Place command on the object if the object at the point of double-click is either an instance or a group.

leEditInPlace.name: leEditInPlace
leEditInPlace.desc: Descends through the hierarchy to edit a cell in place.

leEIPZoomAbsoluteScale.name: leEIPZoomAbsoluteScale
leEIPZoomAbsoluteScale.desc: Fits the master cell of the instance you want to edit in the window. This function also supports edit in place for fig groups. The window is redrawn so the edit-in-place cell or fig group fills it.

leUniquifyCellView.name: leUniquifyCellView
leUniquifyCellView.desc: Opens the Uniquify form to specify the library, cell, and view name of the cellview to be uniquified. Alternatively, you can use the Uniquify command on the Tools menu in the CIW. A message displays after the successful uniquification of the cellview. If the cellview is already uniquified or the cellview cannot be opened, the command exits and displays an appropriate message.

leLayerAnd.name: leLayerAnd
leLayerAnd.syntax:
leLayerAnd( 
d_cellViewId 
g_lpp1 
g_lpp2 
g_lpp3 
) 
=> l_shapes / nil
leLayerAnd.desc: Creates shapes in cellview d_cellViewId on layer g_lpp3 that correspond to the intersections of all shapes on layers g_lpp1 and g_lpp2. A layer-purpose pair is a list containing a layer name followed by a layer purpose.

leLayerAndNot.name: leLayerAndNot
leLayerAndNot.syntax:
leLayerAndNot( 
d_cellViewId 
g_lpp1 
g_lpp2 
g_lpp3 
) 
=> l_shapes / nil
leLayerAndNot.desc: Creates shapes in cellview d_cellViewId on layer g_lpp3 that correspond to the shapes on layer g_lpp1 minus the intersections with the shapes on layer g_lpp2. A layer-purpose pair is a list containing a layer name followed by a layer purpose.

leLayerOr.name: leLayerOr
leLayerOr.syntax:
leLayerOr( 
d_cellViewId 
g_lpp1 
g_lpp2 
g_lpp3 
) 
=> l_shapes / nil
leLayerOr.desc: Creates shapes in cellview d_cellViewId on layer g_lpp3 that correspond to the union of shapes on layers g_lpp1 and g_lpp2. A layer-purpose pair is a list containing a layer name followed by a layer purpose.

leLayerSize.name: leLayerSize
leLayerSize.syntax:
leLayerSize( 
d_cellViewId 
g_lpp1 
n_sizeAmount 
g_lpp2 
) 
=> l_shapes / nil
leLayerSize.desc: Creates shapes in cellview d_cellViewId on layer g_lpp2 by over sizing the shapes on layer g_lpp1 by n_sizeAmount number of units, which can be either positive (oversize) or negative (undersize). A layer-purpose pair is either a layer name or a list containing a layer name followed by a layer purpose.

leLayerXor.name: leLayerXor
leLayerXor.syntax:
leLayerXor( 
d_cellViewId 
g_lpp1 
g_lpp2 
g_lpp3 
) 
=> l_shapes / nil
leLayerXor.desc: Creates shapes in cellview d_cellViewId on layer g_lpp3 that are the result of the union of the shapes on layers g_lpp1 and g_lpp2 minus their intersection. A layer-purpose pair is a list containing a layer name followed by a layer purpose.

cmdCtrlOption.name: cmdCtrlOption
cmdCtrlOption.desc: Implements a command option for Virtuoso Layout Suite XLcreating and editing commands when you press the Control key and press the bindkey. The command options are embedded in the Virtuoso Layout Suite XL software and cannot be changed. The default bindkey for this function is the right mouse button. You can change the default to another key.

cmdOption.name: cmdOption
cmdOption.desc: Implements a command option for Virtuoso Layout Suite XL creating and editing commands when you press the bindkey. The command options are embedded in the Virtuoso Layout Suite XL software and cannot be changed. The default bindkey for this function is the right mouse button. You can change the default to another key.

cmdShiftOption.name: cmdShiftOption
cmdShiftOption.desc: Implements a command option for Virtuoso Layout Suite L creating and editing commands when you press the Shift key and press the bindkey. The command options are embedded in the Virtuoso Layout Suite L software and cannot be changed. The default bindkey for this function is the right mouse button. You can change the default to another key.

leArrowFunc.name: leArrowFunc
leArrowFunc.syntax:
leArrowFunc( 
t_keyName
[ g_optionalArg ] 
) 
=> return value from the called function or function bound by default or nil
leArrowFunc.desc: Executes the function specified in the layout environmental variable spaceFuncName, passing the ID of the current window, the key name, and the optional argument. If spaceFuncName is empty, this function executes the current non-enter function binding for the specified key name.

leSelBoxOrStretch.name: leSelBoxOrStretch
leSelBoxOrStretch.desc: The Virtuoso Layout Suite L binds this function to the mouse button DrawThru1 action. The default behavior for mouse button DrawThru1 is select by bBox. When you select using a bBox, rather than a point, the software checks what is under the selected area. If something under the initial point of the bBox is already selected, the software automatically calls the stretch command. If nothing under the cursor is selected, the software selects the bBox you have drawn. If w_windowId is not specified, the current window is used. This function must not be changed.

leSpaceBarFunc.name: leSpaceBarFunc
leSpaceBarFunc.syntax:
leSpaceBarFunc( 
[ w_windowId ] 
[ g_useDefault ] 
[ g_shift ] 
) 
=> return value from the called function
leSpaceBarFunc.desc: Invokes the function specified by name in the Virtuoso Layout Suite L environment variable spaceFuncName when the g_useDefault argument is set to t. When the g_useDefault argument is set to nil the space bar is not used as a bindkey. If w_windowId is not specified, the current window is used.

hiMakeLPChoiceList.name: hiMakeLPChoiceList
hiMakeLPChoiceList.syntax:
hiMakeLPChoiceList( 
d_techFileID 
l_layerName&Purpose 
[ g_layerNum ]
[ g_swatchIcon ]
) 
=> l_iconList / nil
hiMakeLPChoiceList.desc: Creates a layer purpose icon list for use in a form field or menu.

mbGetAction.name: mbGetAction
mbGetAction.desc: Retrieves an action from the menu builder data structure.

mbRegisterAction.name: mbRegisterAction
mbRegisterAction.syntax:
mbRegisterAction(
t_viewType
t_uniqueId
t_name
t_callback
t_enableCB
[ ?iconFile g_iconFile ]
[ ?icon g_icon ]
[ ?checkable g_checkable ]
[ ?checkedCB t_checkedCB ]
)
=> o_action / nil
mbRegisterAction.desc: Creates an action and registers it with the menu builder for future retrieval and use within menus. This action will appear only when mbSetContextData is used to set its visibility location.

mbRegisterCustomMenu.name: mbRegisterCustomMenu
mbRegisterCustomMenu.syntax:
mbRegisterCustomMenu(
t_viewType
t_uniqueId
t_enableCB
t_customCB
)
=> t / nil
mbRegisterCustomMenu.desc: Registers a custom menu with the menu builder for future retrieval and use within menus. A custom menu item is a single or slider menu that is built using the hi function calls, independently of the menu builder. The t_customCB argument is used to specify the function that is responsible for building and returning the menu item. The menu will display only when the mbSetContextData function is called.

mbRegisterHierMenu.name: mbRegisterHierMenu
mbRegisterHierMenu.syntax:
mbRegisterHierMenu(
t_viewType
t_uniqueId
t_name
t_enableCB
)
=> t / nil
mbRegisterHierMenu.desc: Registers a hierarchical menu with the menu builder for future retrieval and use within menus.

mbRegisterMenuItem.name: mbRegisterMenuItem
mbRegisterMenuItem.syntax:
mbRegisterMenuItem(
t_viewType
l_menuItemDef
t_enableCB
)
=> t_menuItemId / nil
mbRegisterMenuItem.desc: Registers a menu item with the menu builder that has been defined using the older menu creation syntax. mbSetContextData needs to be called before the menu item is visible.

mbSetContextData.name: mbSetContextData
mbSetContextData.syntax:
mbSetContextData(
t_viewType
t_uniqueId
t_validObjs
t_validWidgets
t_grouping
[ ?parent t_parent ]
[ ?removeWhenDisabled g_removeWhenDisabled ]
)
=> t / nil
mbSetContextData.desc: Sets various attributes to determine the menus with which the registered action is to be associated.

mbUnregisterAction.name: mbUnregisterAction
mbUnregisterAction.syntax:
mbUnregisterAction(
t_name
[ ?objType t_objType ]
[ ?viewType t_viewType ]
[ ?silent g_silent ]
)
=> t / nil
mbUnregisterAction.desc: Removes the provided menu item from the RMB menu. The optional arguments can be used to limit the removal of a menu item to specific object types or view types for which it is registered.

hiLayerDispMainForm.name: hiLayerDispMainForm
hiLayerDispMainForm.desc: Opens the Layer Purpose Pair Editor form. You can also access this form using the CIW - Tools - Technology File Manager - Edit Layers command.

leCloseWindow.name: leCloseWindow
leCloseWindow.desc: Closes the current layout window. Similar to the hiCloseWindow function. To customize a bindkey you must use leCloseWindow because it is the function used in the callback of the File - Close menu command.

leDesignSummary.name: leDesignSummary
leDesignSummary.syntax:
leDesignSummary( 
d_cellViewId 
t_fileName 
g_append 
[ w_windowId ] 
[ basicSummary ]
[ netStats ]
[ connectivityStats ]
[ routingStats ]
) 
=> t / nil
leDesignSummary.desc: Stores or outputs leHiSummary results to an external specified file.

leEditDesignProperties.name: leEditDesignProperties
leEditDesignProperties.desc: Opens the Edit Cellview Properties form, which lets you change the design properties in the cellview d_cellViewId. If d_cellViewId is not specified, the cellview in the current window is used.

leExportLabel.name: leExportLabel
leExportLabel.desc: Saves the label information in the current cellview to the specified file.

leGetCoordinateForm.name: leGetCoordinateForm
leGetCoordinateForm.desc: Opens the Enter Points form which is used to specify the coordinates required to allow a command to proceed.

leHiAbout.name: leHiAbout
leHiAbout.desc: Opens the product information window, which includes the release number and copyright information.

leHiAddShapeToNet.name: leHiAddShapeToNet
leHiAddShapeToNet.desc: Opens the Add Shape To Net form, which lets you associate a shape with a net. If w_windowId is not specified, the current window is used.

leHiAddToGroup.name: leHiAddToGroup
leHiAddToGroup.desc: Opens the Select Target Group form to add shapes to an existing group.

leHiAlign.name: leHiAlign
leHiAlign.desc: Opens the Align form, and returns the value of t.

leHiAttach.name: leHiAttach
leHiAttach.desc: Attaches a selected object in the specified window to another object in the window. The attached object is called the child object, and the object it is attached to is called the parent object. When you move, copy, or delete the parent, the child is also moved, copied, or deleted. If w_windowId is not specified, the current window is used.

leHiCellviewTrackPatterns.name: leHiCellviewTrackPatterns
leHiCellviewTrackPatterns.desc: Opens the Track Pattern Editor form, which lets you add, update or delete track patterns. If w_windowId is not specified, the current window is used.

leHiChop.name: leHiChop
leHiChop.desc: Opens the Chop form, which lets you remove parts of objects or break objects into multiple objects. If w_windowId is not specified, the current window is used.

leHiClearRuler.name: leHiClearRuler
leHiClearRuler.desc: Clears the rulers that stay in the window when the Keep Ruler option is selected using leHiCreateRuler. If w_windowId is not specified, the current window is used.

leHiConvertInstToMosaic.name: leHiConvertInstToMosaic
leHiConvertInstToMosaic.desc: Starts the Convert To Mosaic command, which lets you convert one or more selected instances either into an equivalent number of mosaics or into a single mosaic. If w_windowId is not specified, the current window is used. You are prompted to select one or more instances to convert into mosaics.

leHiConvertPolygonToPath.name: leHiConvertPolygonToPath
leHiConvertPolygonToPath.desc: Converts a selected polygon in the specified window to a path if a uniform width path can be inferred. If w_windowId is not specified, the current window is used.

leHiConvertShapeToPathSeg.name: leHiConvertShapeToPathSeg
leHiConvertShapeToPathSeg.desc: Converts a selected polygon, rectangle, or path in the specified window to a pathSeg, if a uniform width path can be inferred. If w_windowId is not specified, the current window is used.

leHiConvertShapeToPolygon.name: leHiConvertShapeToPolygon
leHiConvertShapeToPolygon.desc: Converts a selected object in the specified window to a polygon. Converts rectangles, paths, donuts, circles, and ellipses using the number of conic sides specified using leHiEditEditorOptions. If w_windowId is not specified, the current window is used.

leHiCopy.name: leHiCopy
leHiCopy.desc: Opens the Copy form, which lets you copy selected objects in the specified window. If w_windowId is not specified, the current window is used.

leHiCreateAreaBoundary.name: leHiCreateAreaBoundary
leHiCreateAreaBoundary.desc: Opens the Create Area Boundary form, which lets you create an Area Boundary. If w_windowId is not specified, the current window is used.

leHiCreateBend.name: leHiCreateBend
leHiCreateBend.desc: Opens the Transmission Line Bend form, which lets you create a transmission line bend in the specified window. If w_windowId is not specified, the current window is used.

leHiCreateBlockage.name: leHiCreateBlockage
leHiCreateBlockage.desc: Opens the Create Blockage form, which lets you create blockages. If w_windowId is not specified, the current window is used.

leHiCreateChoiceOfPin.name: leHiCreateChoiceOfPin
leHiCreateChoiceOfPin.desc: Opens the Create Pin form in w_windowId. If w_windowId is not specified, the current window is used.

leHiCreateCircle.name: leHiCreateCircle
leHiCreateCircle.desc: Creates a circle in the specified window. You are prompted to point to a location for the center of the circle and the outer edge of the circle. If w_windowId is not specified, the current window is used.

leHiCreateClusterBoundary.name: leHiCreateClusterBoundary
leHiCreateClusterBoundary.desc: Opens the Create Cluster Boundary form, which lets you create a cluster boundary. If w_windowId is not specified, the current window is used.

leHiCreateClusters.name: leHiCreateClusters
leHiCreateClusters.desc: Opens the Create - P&R Objects - Clusters form, which lets you create and edit clusters and sub-clusters. If w_windowId is not specified, the current window is used.

leHiCreateDonut.name: leHiCreateDonut
leHiCreateDonut.desc: Creates a donut in the specified window. You are prompted to point to a location for the center of the donut, the inner edge of the donut, and the outer edge of the donut. If w_windowId is not specified, the current window is used.

leHiCreateEllipse.name: leHiCreateEllipse
leHiCreateEllipse.desc: Creates an ellipse in the specified window. You are prompted to point to the corners of the bounding box for the ellipse. If w_windowId is not specified, the current window is used.

leHiCreateGroup.name: leHiCreateGroup
leHiCreateGroup.desc: Opens the Create Group form to select figures to form a new group.

leHiCreateGuardRing.name: leHiCreateGuardRing
leHiCreateGuardRing.desc: Opens the Create Guard Ring form, which lets you instantiate guard rings. If w_windowId is not specified, the current window is used.

leHiCreateInst.name: leHiCreateInst
leHiCreateInst.desc: Opens the Create Instance form, which lets you create an instance in the specified window. If w_windowId is not specified, the current window is used.

leHiCreateLabel.name: leHiCreateLabel
leHiCreateLabel.desc: Opens the Create Label form, which lets you create a label in the specified window. If w_windowId is not specified, the current window is used.

leHiCreateMPP.name: leHiCreateMPP
leHiCreateMPP.desc: Runs the Create MPP command in the specified window. You can draw the MPP on the canvas or press F3 to open the Create Multipart Path form and specify the settings for creating multipart paths. If w_windowId is not specified, the current window is used.

leHiCreatePath.name: leHiCreatePath
leHiCreatePath.desc: Opens the Create Path form, which lets you create a path in the specified window. If w_windowId is not specified, the current window is used.

leHiCreatePin.name: leHiCreatePin
leHiCreatePin.desc: Opens the Create Pin form, which lets you create a geometric pin in the specified window. If w_windowId is not specified, the current window is used.

leHiCreatePinsFromLabels.name: leHiCreatePinsFromLabels
leHiCreatePinsFromLabels.desc: Opens the Create Pins From Labels form, which lets you create pins from text labels in your layout cellview or selected instances. This command creates pins with terminal names matching labels on a specified text layer with pin dimensions that you specify, centered on the origin of your text label. If you do not specify w_windowId, the layout editor uses the current window.

leHiCreatePlacementArea.name: leHiCreatePlacementArea
leHiCreatePlacementArea.desc: Opens the Create - P&R Objects - Custom Placement Area form, which lets you create a placement area in one of three modes: Manual, Assisted, or Auto. This form contains a Dressing Template Editor button to bring up the Dressing Template Editor subform. To activate this subform with SKILL, use the SKILL ~> operator like this: leHiCreatePlacementArea~>Dressing~>value=1. If w_windowId is not specified, the current window is used.

leHiCreatePolygon.name: leHiCreatePolygon
leHiCreatePolygon.desc: Opens the Create Polygon form, which lets you create a polygon in the specified window. If w_windowId is not specified, the current window is used.

leHiCreatePRBoundary.name: leHiCreatePRBoundary
leHiCreatePRBoundary.desc: Opens the Create P&R Boundary form, which lets you create a P&R boundary. If w_windowId is not specified, the current window is used.

leHiCreateRect.name: leHiCreateRect
leHiCreateRect.desc: Creates a rectangle in the specified window. You are prompted to point to two coordinates for the opposite corners of the rectangle. If w_windowId is not specified, the current window is used.

leHiCreateRow.name: leHiCreateRow
leHiCreateRow.desc: Makes sure the cellview is writable and opens the Create - P&R Objects - Create Row form, which lets you create a row in the specified window. Prerequisite: site definitions must already exist in your technology file. This form contains a Dressing Template Editor button to bring up the Dressing Template Editor subform. To activate this subform with SKILL, use the SKILL ~> operator like this: leHiCreateRow~>Dressing~>value=1.If w_windowId is not specified, the current window is used.

leHiCreateRuler.name: leHiCreateRuler
leHiCreateRuler.desc: Opens the Create Measurement form, which lets you create a ruler in the specified window. If w_windowId is not specified, the current window is used.

leHiCreateSnapBoundary.name: leHiCreateSnapBoundary
leHiCreateSnapBoundary.desc: Opens the Create Snap Boundary form, which lets you create a snap boundary. If w_windowId is not specified, the current window is used.

leHiCreateTaper.name: leHiCreateTaper
leHiCreateTaper.desc: Opens the Transmission Line Taper form, which lets you create a transmission line taper in the specified window. If w_windowId is not specified, the current window is used.

leHiCreateTrl.name: leHiCreateTrl
leHiCreateTrl.desc: Opens the Transmission Line form, which lets you create a transmission line in the specified window. If w_windowId is not specified, the current window is used.

leHiCreateVia.name: leHiCreateVia
leHiCreateVia.desc: Starts the Create - Via command and opens the Create Via form, which lets you create a via in the specified window. If w_windowId is not specified, the current window is used.

leHiDelete.name: leHiDelete
leHiDelete.desc: Deletes selected objects in the specified window. If you delete a net selected using the Navigator assistant, all shapes on the net, except for pins, are also deleted. If you do not specify w_windowId, the layout editor uses the current window.

leHiDeleteAllAreaViewLevel.name: leHiDeleteAllAreaViewLevel
leHiDeleteAllAreaViewLevel.desc: Removes all special display areas in window w_windowId. If you do not specify w_windowId, the layout editor uses the current window.

leHiDeleteAreaViewLevel.name: leHiDeleteAreaViewLevel
leHiDeleteAreaViewLevel.desc: Displays all currently defined area view levels using the layer-purpose pair hilight drawing1, and prompts you to point at the area to be removed. If you do not specify w_windowId, the layout editor uses the current window.

leHiDeleteShapeFromNet.name: leHiDeleteShapeFromNet
leHiDeleteShapeFromNet.desc: Opens the Remove Shape From Net form, which lets you remove the selected shape from the net. If w_windowId is not specified, the current window is used.

leHiDescend.name: leHiDescend
leHiDescend.desc: Lets you push down one level into the design hierarchy. You can preselect the instance to descend into. If no instances are selected, you are prompted to select an instance. If you do not specify w_windowId, the layout editor uses the current window.

leHiDisplayPadOpeningInfoForm.name: leHiDisplayPadOpeningInfoForm
leHiDisplayPadOpeningInfoForm.desc: Opens the Pad Opening Info form, which you can use to find pad shapes at lower levels of your hierarchical cellview, generate reports and labels for the pad shapes that are found, and promote the generated labels to the top level of the cellview.

leHiDisplayTechGraphForm.name: leHiDisplayTechGraphForm
leHiDisplayTechGraphForm.desc: Opens the Technology Database Graph form. You can also access this form using the CIW - Tools - Technology File Manager - Graph command.

leHiEditDisplayOptions.name: leHiEditDisplayOptions
leHiEditDisplayOptions.desc: Opens the Display Options form, which lets you change the display options in the specified window. If you do not specify w_windowId, the layout editor uses the current window.

leHiEditDRDOptions.name: leHiEditDRDOptions
leHiEditDRDOptions.desc: Opens the DRD Options form, which lets you select the rules that are to be considered by the Design Rule Driven Editing. You can also set the other DRD options, such as mode, hierarchy depth, display, through the DRD Options form. Corresponds to the F7 bindkey in the leBindkeys.il file.

leHiEditDRDRuleOptions.name: leHiEditDRDRuleOptions
leHiEditDRDRuleOptions.desc: Opens the DRD Options form, which lets you select the rules that are to be considered by the Design Rule Driven Editing. You can also set the other DRD options, such as mode, hierarchy depth, display, through the DRD Options form. Corresponds to the F7 bindkey in the leBindkeys.il file.

leHiEditDynamicMeasurementOptions.name: leHiEditDynamicMeasurementOptions
leHiEditDynamicMeasurementOptions.desc: Opens the Dynamic Display form, which lets you change the dynamic measurement display options. This form turns dynamic measurement on or off, and sets which measurements will display, and the height of the text display in pixels.

leHiEditEditorOptions.name: leHiEditEditorOptions
leHiEditEditorOptions.desc: Opens the Layout Editor Options form, which lets you change the layout editor environment. You can also set these variables in your .cdsenv file, so the layout editor defaults to these options on start up.

leHiEditInPlace.name: leHiEditInPlace
leHiEditInPlace.desc: Lets you edit an instance's master while viewing it in the context of the instance placement. If you do not specify w_windowId, the layout editor uses the current window. You can preselect the instance to be edited in place. If no instance is selected, you are prompted to point at a shape contained in the instance to be edited in place. If you point at several shapes at different levels of the hierarchy, the shape in the higher-level instance is the one that is used.

leHiEditProp.name: leHiEditProp
leHiEditProp.desc: Opens the Edit Properties form, which lets you edit the properties set in the specified window. You are prompted to select objects whose properties you want to edit. If you do not specify w_windowId, the layout editor uses the current window.

leHiFlatten.name: leHiFlatten
leHiFlatten.desc: Opens the Flatten form, which lets you explode a cell instance or array, moving the contents of the cell or array up one or more levels into the current level of the hierarchy. If you do not specify w_windowId, the layout editor uses the current window.

leHiFlip.name: leHiFlip
leHiFlip.desc: Opens the Flip form that you can use to flip an object horizontally or vertically in the specified window.

leHiIncrementalViolationUpdater.name: leHiIncrementalViolationUpdater
leHiIncrementalViolationUpdater.desc: Enables you to iterate between the violations of the command.

leHiLayerGen.name: leHiLayerGen
leHiLayerGen.desc: Opens the Layer Generation form, which lets you create new shapes by performing logical operations on selected objects in the specified layers. If you do not specify w_windowId, the layout editor uses the current window.

leHiLayerTap.name: leHiLayerTap
leHiLayerTap.desc: Starts the Tools - Tap command and opens the Tap form when Options Displayed When Commands Start is set to on. Tapping sets the entry layer to the layer of an indicated shape in the current window. You can also use the tap command to seed create forms with information such as nets and attributes of objects. You are prompted to point at a shape with attributes to be tapped. You can point to shapes anywhere in the hierarchy. If the shape you want to select is overlapped by other shapes, you can cycle through the shapes until the shape you want is displayed, by setting the environment variable layerTapCycle to t, which takes precedence over Select from overlaps. If layerTapCycle is nil and layerTapPick is t, then the Select from overlaps form will appear if you click more than one overlapped shape. If you do not point to any shapes that are on valid layers, the function calls hiGetAttention and prompts you again. If you do not specify w_windowId, the layout editor uses the current window.

leHiMakeCell.name: leHiMakeCell
leHiMakeCell.desc: Opens the Make Cell form, which lets you create a cell from the selected objects in the specified window. If you do not specify w_windowId, the layout editor uses the current window.

leHiMerge.name: leHiMerge
leHiMerge.desc: Merges selected objects that touch or overlap each other into one object. You can merge shapes of different types that are on the same layer. You cannot merge shapes on different layers. Pins cannot be merged. If you do not specify w_windowId, the layout editor uses the current window.

leHiModifyCorner.name: leHiModifyCorner
leHiModifyCorner.desc: Opens the Modify Corner form, which lets you modify corners of rectangles and polygons in the specified window. If you do not specify w_windowId, the layout editor uses the current window.

leHiMousePopUp.name: leHiMousePopUp
leHiMousePopUp.desc: Opens the layout editor Middle Mouse Button Pop Up form. It is context sensitive. Returns t if the current window is a layout window, returns nil if the current window is not a layout window.

leHiMove.name: leHiMove
leHiMove.desc: Opens the Move form, which lets you move an object in the specified window to another location or layer in the same window or in a different window. If you do not specify w_windowId, the layout editor uses the current window.

leHiMoveOrigin.name: leHiMoveOrigin
leHiMoveOrigin.desc: Enter this function with only the window ID argument; the system prompts you to point to the new origin. If you do not specify w_windowId, the layout editor uses the current window.

leHiOptionLayer.name: leHiOptionLayer
leHiOptionLayer.desc: Opens the LSW Option form. Returns t when you click OK, returns nil when you click Cancel.

leHiPaste.name: leHiPaste
leHiPaste.desc: Opens the Paste form, which lets you place the contents of the yank buffer in the specified window. If you do not specify w_windowId, the layout editor uses the current window.

leHiPlotQueueStatus.name: leHiPlotQueueStatus
leHiPlotQueueStatus.desc: Opens the Plot Job Queue form, which shows the status of the plot job queue.

leHiPropagateNets.name: leHiPropagateNets
leHiPropagateNets.desc: Opens the Connectivity tab of the property editor for the selected instances. The tab lets you promote net information from pins in selected blocks one level down in the hierarchy up to the top level where the router can recognize and route the nets. You use this command when you do not have a schematic for your layout cellview. If you do not specify w_windowId, the layout editor uses the current window.

leHiQuery.name: leHiQuery
leHiQuery.desc: Invokes the Query command to initiate a query in which you can select a shape to have descriptive data about it displayed.

leHiQuickAlign.name: leHiQuickAlign
leHiQuickAlign.desc: Starts the Quick Align command in the specified window. You are prompted to select a reference edge, centerline, or point. In the post-select mode, you can select the reference edge, centerline, or point after selecting the reference set objects. You can press F3 to open the Quick Align form and specify the settings for alignment.

leHiReShape.name: leHiReShape
leHiReShape.desc: Opens the Reshape form, which lets you modify the vertices of rectangles, polygons, paths, and transmission lines. You can add vertices, remove vertices, or modify vertex locations. The modified shape is stored in its most efficient form. For example, if a polygon is modified to have a rectangular shape, it is converted into a rectangle. If you do not specify w_windowId, the layout editor uses the current window.

leHiRemasterInstances.name: leHiRemasterInstances
leHiRemasterInstances.desc: Opens the Remaster Instances form, in which you specify instances to search for based on the view name, cell name, and the library name for a given cellviewID, then re-masters those instances with the master that matches the update library, update cell and update view names you provide in the form. If you do not specify w_windowId, the layout editor uses the current window.

leHiRemoveFromGroup.name: leHiRemoveFromGroup
leHiRemoveFromGroup.desc: This function operates only when nested within the leHiEditInPlace function. After executing the leHiEditInPlace function, select the group from which you want to remove a figure, and then execute leHiRemoveFromGroup, which prompts you to select figures to remove from the current group. If you select all of the figures in the group, you can exit the function with an escape or by starting another function. However, if you select fewer figures than the group contains, you must exit Edit-In-Place mode with the leReturnToLevel function (Edit - Hierarchy - Return To Level).

leHiRepeatCopy.name: leHiRepeatCopy
leHiRepeatCopy.desc: Starts the Repeat Copy command in the specified window.

leHiRotate.name: leHiRotate
leHiRotate.desc: Opens the Rotate form, which lets you change the orientation of geometric objects. If w_windowId is not specified, the current window is used.

leHiSave.name: leHiSave
leHiSave.desc: Executes the File - Save command, which saves the current cellview.

leHiSaveACopy.name: leHiSaveACopy
leHiSaveACopy.desc: Opens the Save As Copy form, which lets you copy the current cellview to another library, cellview name, and/or view name. If you do not specify w_windowId, the layout editor uses the current window.

leHiSaveHier.name: leHiSaveHier
leHiSaveHier.desc: Enables you to save a hierarchical instance that is modified without running the Edit In Place or Descend Edit command.

leHiSearch.name: leHiSearch
leHiSearch.desc: Opens the Find/Replace form, which lets you search the specified window for objects that match user-specified query requests. If you do not specify w_windowId, the layout editor uses the current window.

leHiSetAreaViewLevel.name: leHiSetAreaViewLevel
leHiSetAreaViewLevel.desc: Opens the Set Area View Level form, which lets you create a special display area in the window. This lets you override the window's display start and stop levels for a specified area. If you do not specify w_windowId, the layout editor uses the current window.

leHiSetRefPoint.name: leHiSetRefPoint
leHiSetRefPoint.desc: Sets a reference point in the specified window. You are prompted to point to location for the reference point. If you do not specify w_windowId, the layout editor uses the current window.

leHiShowAngles.name: leHiShowAngles
leHiShowAngles.desc: Runs the Show Angles command in the specified window. You are prompted to point to a vertex, an edge, or an object to view the angle formed at the intersection of two edges. If w_windowId is not specified, the current window is used.

leHiShowCoords.name: leHiShowCoords
leHiShowCoords.desc: Runs the Show Coordinates command in the specified window. You are prompted to point to a vertex, an edge, or an object to view the coordinates of the selected shape. If w_windowId is not specified, the current window is used.

leHiShowSelSet.name: leHiShowSelSet
leHiShowSelSet.desc: Displays information about the selected set in the specified window. If you do not specify w_windowId, the layout editor uses the current window.

leHiSize.name: leHiSize
leHiSize.desc: Opens the Size form, which lets you enlarge or reduce a shape in the specified window. If you do not specify w_windowId, the layout editor uses the current window.

leHiSplit.name: leHiSplit
leHiSplit.desc: Opens the Split form, which lets you reshape an object by stretching part of it relative to a split line in the specified window. If you do not specify w_windowId, the layout editor uses the current window.

leHiStretch.name: leHiStretch
leHiStretch.desc: Opens the Stretch form, which lets you stretch objects in the specified window. If you do not specify w_windowId, the layout editor uses the current window.

leHiSubmitPlot.name: leHiSubmitPlot
leHiSubmitPlot.desc: Opens the Submit Plot form, which lets you submit plots to a plotter.

leHiSummary.name: leHiSummary
leHiSummary.desc: Displays information about the specified window. If you do not specify w_windowId, the layout editor uses the current window.

leHiTree.name: leHiTree
leHiTree.desc: Displays information about the design hierarchy in the specified window. If you do not specify w_windowId, the layout editor uses the current window.

leHiUngroup.name: leHiUngroup
leHiUngroup.desc: Starts the Edit - Group - Ungroup command and prompts you to point at the group you want to ungroup.

leHiYank.name: leHiYank
leHiYank.desc: Opens the Yank Form, which lets you copy a set of objects in a cellview into the yank buffer for later pasting. A yank shape defines the area enclosing the objects to copy. If you do not specify w_windowId, the layout editor uses the current window.

leiDiscardEdits.name: leiDiscardEdits
leiDiscardEdits.desc: Discards all edits you made since the last time you saved. Corresponds to the cellview window Design - Discard Edits command.

lePinModelInitFunction.name: lePinModelInitFunction
lePinModelInitFunction.desc: Opens the Pin Connectivity Model graphical user interface, which you can use to set the connectivity model for the pins and terminals in your design.

updateReturnPopupMenuItem.name: updateReturnPopupMenuItem
updateReturnPopupMenuItem.desc: Adds the Return menu item to the pop up menu specified.

leHiDisplayStartRouterForm.name: leHiDisplayStartRouterForm
leHiDisplayStartRouterForm.desc: Opens the Virtuoso Chip Assembly Router form.

leStartRouter.name: leStartRouter
leStartRouter.syntax:
leStartRouter( 
[ ?layoutLCV list(t_libraryName t_cellName t_viewName) ]
[ ?layoutRoutedLCV list(t_libraryName t_cellName t_viewName) ]
[ ?constraintGroup t_constraintGroupName ]
[ ?doFile S_doFile ]
[ ?initCommand S_initCommand ]
[ ?showGraphics g_showGraphics ]
[ ?quitAtFinish g_quitAtFinish ]
[ ?useStartupFiles g_useStartupFiles ]
[ ?usePreroutes g_usePreroutes ]
[ ?usePreroutedIO g_usePreroutedIO ]
[ ?stripOrphanShapes g_stripOrphanShapes ]
[ ?checkAtStartup g_checkAtStartup ]
[ ?cutKeepoutByClearance g_cutKeepoutByClearance ]
[ ?cutKeepoutToImageEdge g_cutKeepoutToImageEdge ]
[ ?createDidFile g_createDidFile ]
[ ?didFile S_didFile ]
[ ?messageFile S_messageFile ]
[ ?statusFile S_statusFile ]
[ ?startupOptions S_startupOptions ]
) 
=> t / nil
leStartRouter.desc: Starts the Virtuoso Chip Assembly Router with specified data and startup options.

viaFindTransitions.name: viaFindTransitions
viaFindTransitions.syntax:
viaFindTransitions(
t_constraintGroupSetup
t_topLayerName
t_bottomLayerName
) 
=> l_viaTransitionsObject / nil
viaFindTransitions.desc: Returns the list of transitions of the given constraint group setup object found between the specified top and bottom layers.

viaGenerateViasAtPoint.name: viaGenerateViasAtPoint
viaGenerateViasAtPoint.syntax:
viaGenerateViasAtPoint(
w_windowId | d_cellViewId
l_point
t_viaOptionsObject
[ ?topAndBottomLayers lt_topAndBottomLayers ]
[ ?startLevel x_startLevel ]
[ ?stopLevel x_stopLevel ]
) 
=> l_via / nil
viaGenerateViasAtPoint.desc: Generates vias with the specified options at a given location in the specified window or cellview.The figures present at the given location are queried, and if they form valid overlaps, vias are created to connect the figures.

viaGenerateViasFromShapes.name: viaGenerateViasFromShapes
viaGenerateViasFromShapes.syntax:
viaGenerateViasFromShapes(
w_windowId | d_cellViewId
l_shapes
t_viaOptionsObject
[ ?topAndBottomLayers lt_topAndBottomLayers ]
[ ?startLevel x_startLevel ]
[ ?stopLevel x_stopLevel ]
) 
=> l_via / nil
viaGenerateViasFromShapes.desc: Generates vias from the specified shapes with the given via options in the specified window or cellview. If the specified shapes form valid overlaps, vias are created to connect the shapes.

viaGenerateViasInArea.name: viaGenerateViasInArea
viaGenerateViasInArea.syntax:
viaGenerateViasInArea(
w_windowId | d_cellViewId
l_ptArray
t_viaOptionsObject
[ ?topAndBottomLayers lt_topAndBottomLayers ]
[ ?startLevel x_startLevel ]
[ ?stopLevel x_stopLevel ]
) 
=> l_via / nil
viaGenerateViasInArea.desc: Generates vias with the specified options within a given area in the specified window or cellview. The figures present at the given location are queried, and if they form valid overlaps, vias are created to connect the figures.

viaGetViaOptions.name: viaGetViaOptions
viaGetViaOptions.desc: Returns a via options object from the specified constraint group. This via options object can be used by any SKILL procedure enabling generation or re-computation of vias.

viaLoadViaVariants.name: viaLoadViaVariants
viaLoadViaVariants.desc: Loads the via variants from the specified cellview for the Create Via command.

viaRecomputeVias.name: viaRecomputeVias
viaRecomputeVias.syntax:
viaRecomputeVias(
w_windowId | d_cellViewId
l_via
t_viaOptionsObject
[ ?startLevel x_startLevel ]
[ ?stopLevel x_stopLevel ]
) 
=> l_via / nil
viaRecomputeVias.desc: Recomputes the via list with the given via options in the specified window or cellview. The figures connected by the vias are searched and the vias are recomputed with the via options specified to connect the figures.

viaRecomputeViasAtPoint.name: viaRecomputeViasAtPoint
viaRecomputeViasAtPoint.syntax:
viaRecomputeViasAtPoint(
w_windowId | d_cellViewId
l_point
t_viaOptionsObject
[ ?startLevel x_startLevel ]
[ ?stopLevel x_stopLevel ]
) 
=> l_via / nil
viaRecomputeViasAtPoint.desc: Recomputes vias with the specified options at a given location in the specified window or cellview. The vias present at the given location are queried along with the figures connected by the vias. The vias are then recomputed with the via options specified to connect the figures.

viaRecomputeViasInArea.name: viaRecomputeViasInArea
viaRecomputeViasInArea.syntax:
viaRecomputeViasInArea(
w_windowId | d_cellViewId
l_ptArray
t_viaOptionsObject
[ ?startLevel x_startLevel ]
[ ?stopLevel x_stopLevel ]
) 
=> l_via / nil
viaRecomputeViasInArea.desc: Recomputes vias with the specified options within a given area in the specified window or cellview. The vias present at the given location are queried along with the figures connected by the vias. The vias are then recomputed with the via options specified to connect the figures.

viaRegisterCreateViaInitCallback.name: viaRegisterCreateViaInitCallback
viaRegisterCreateViaInitCallback.desc: Registers the function to be called each time the Create Via form is opened. The registered function name should be a valid SKILL procedure and the init procedure that is registered should be defined without arguments.

viaRegisterPostViaEngineCallback.name: viaRegisterPostViaEngineCallback
viaRegisterPostViaEngineCallback.desc: Registers the function name to be called after the viaEngine processing. The registered function name should be a valid SKILL procedure. The postViaEngine procedure that is registered should be declared with one argument, the viaEngineContext. This argument is a user type representing the context of the viaEngine call. The viaRegisterPostViaEngineCallback function that is registered should be declared with the viaEngineContext argument. This argument is a user type representing the context of the viaEngine call. The function returns t or nil. If nil is returned by the viaRegisterPostViaEngineCallback function registered, vias are not created.

viaRegisterPostViaServerCallback.name: viaRegisterPostViaServerCallback
viaRegisterPostViaServerCallback.desc: Registers the function name to be called after the via server processing. The function should be a valid SKILL procedure. The postViaServer procedure that is registered should be declared with three arguments, the constraintGroup, the overlapInfo, and the list of viaViaDef user type computed by the via server. The postViaServer procedure returns a list of viaViaDef user types. You can update all viaViaDefs specified in the viaViaDef argument. You also have the option to modify the sequence of the viaViaDef list.

viaRegisterPreViaEngineCallback.name: viaRegisterPreViaEngineCallback
viaRegisterPreViaEngineCallback.desc: Registers the function name to be called before via engine processing. The registered function name should be a valid SKILL procedure. The preViaEngine procedure that is registered should be declared with one argument, viaEngineContext. This argument is a user type representing the context of the viaEngine call. The viaRegisterPreViaEngineCallback function that is registered should be declared with the viaEngineContext argument. This argument is a user type representing the context of the viaEngine call. The function returns t or nil. If nil is returned by the viaRegisterPreViaEngineCallback function registered, vias are not created.

viaSaveViaVariants.name: viaSaveViaVariants
viaSaveViaVariants.desc: Saves the via variants from the Create Via command into the specified cellview.

viaSetDefaultCutClasses.name: viaSetDefaultCutClasses
viaSetDefaultCutClasses.syntax:
viaSetDefaultCutClasses(
t_techLibName
[ t_constraintGroupName ]
((bottomLayer topLayer cutClass) ...)
[ g_reset ]
) 
=> t / nil
viaSetDefaultCutClasses.desc: Sets the default cut classes to be used for each layer.

viaSetDefaultValidViaDefs.name: viaSetDefaultValidViaDefs
viaSetDefaultValidViaDefs.syntax:
viaSetDefaultValidViaDefs(
t_techLibName
t_constraintGroupName
l_viaDef
[ g_reset ]
) 
=> t / nil
viaSetDefaultValidViaDefs.desc: Sets the default vias to be used by Wire Edit and Create Via commands from the list of valid vias of the specified constraint group.

viaUnregisterCreateViaInitCallback.name: viaUnregisterCreateViaInitCallback
viaUnregisterCreateViaInitCallback.desc: Unregisters the createVia initialization procedure if it has been registered. If it has not been registered, this function does nothing.

viaUnregisterPostViaEngineCallback.name: viaUnregisterPostViaEngineCallback
viaUnregisterPostViaEngineCallback.desc: Unregisters the postViaEngine procedure if it has been registered. If it has not been registered, this function does nothing.

viaUnregisterPostViaServerCallback.name: viaUnregisterPostViaServerCallback
viaUnregisterPostViaServerCallback.desc: Unregisters the postViaServer procedure if it has been registered.

viaUnregisterPreViaEngineCallback.name: viaUnregisterPreViaEngineCallback
viaUnregisterPreViaEngineCallback.desc: Unregisters the preViaEngine procedure if it has been registered. If it has not been registered, this function does nothing.

leHiMarkNet.name: leHiMarkNet
leHiMarkNet.desc: Starts the Connectivity - Nets - Mark command and opens the MarkNet Options form in w_windowId, which lets you mark a net which you are prompted to select. If w_windowId is not specified, the current window is used.

leHiSaveAllHighLightMarkNet.name: leHiSaveAllHighLightMarkNet
leHiSaveAllHighLightMarkNet.desc: Opens the Save All Mark Nets form.

leHiUnmarkNet.name: leHiUnmarkNet
leHiUnmarkNet.desc: Opens the Unmark Net form. If w_windowId is not specified, the current window is used.

leHiUnmarkNetAll.name: leHiUnmarkNetAll
leHiUnmarkNetAll.desc: Deletes the highlighting of all marked nets in w_windowId. If w_windowId is not specified, the current window is used.

leIsAnyMarkNetHighLighted.name: leIsAnyMarkNetHighLighted
leIsAnyMarkNetHighLighted.desc: Checks if the specified window has a marked net.

leMarkNet.name: leMarkNet
leMarkNet.syntax:
leMarkNet( 
l_point
[ ?startLevel startLevel ]
[ ?stopLevel stopLevel ]
[ ?highlightIncrementally highlightIncrementally ]
[ ?saveViaInfo saveViaInfo ]
[ ?thickLine thickLine ]
[ ?optionFile optionFile ]
[ ?startLpp startLpp ]
[ ?markNetColor markNetColor ]
)
=> t / nil
leMarkNet.desc: Marks a net in the current cellview. It traces the physical connectivity of a net(s) in a layout design starting from the input point (l_point) and highlights the traced net(s).

leMarkNetGetNumThreads.name: leMarkNetGetNumThreads
leMarkNetGetNumThreads.desc: Returns the thread mode of the Mark Net command. In Layout L, the Mark Net command always runs in a mono thread mode. In Layout XL and higher tiers, this command can run in auto or customizable thread mode.

leSaveMarkNet.name: leSaveMarkNet
leSaveMarkNet.syntax:
leSaveMarkNet(
cellName
[ ?libName t_libName ]
[ ?viewName t_viewName ]
[ ?pt l_pt ]
)
=> t / nil
leSaveMarkNet.desc: Saves a particular highlighted net at the specified point (l_point). If no point is specified, all the highlighted nets in current cellview are saved in the specified cellview (lib/cell/view).

leUnmarkNet.name: leUnmarkNet
leUnmarkNet.desc: Deletes the highlighting of the marked nets in the current cellview. This function can delete the highlights of a particular net at the specified point (l_point). If no point is specified, the highlights of all the marked nets in current cellview are deleted.

leGetWirebondProfileVisible.name: leGetWirebondProfileVisible
leGetWirebondProfileVisible.desc: (Virtuoso RF Option) Returns the visibility setting of the specified wirebond profile.

leSetWirebondProfileVisible.name: leSetWirebondProfileVisible
leSetWirebondProfileVisible.desc: (Virtuoso RF Option) Sets the visibility of the specified wirebond profile.

pteClearSearchHistory.name: pteClearSearchHistory
pteClearSearchHistory.desc: Clears the search history for the specified Palette panel.

pteCloseLayerSetEdition.name: pteCloseLayerSetEdition
pteCloseLayerSetEdition.desc: Closes layer set editing mode for the specified window, or for the current window if no window ID is specified.

pteCloseMPTSupportMode.name: pteCloseMPTSupportMode
pteCloseMPTSupportMode.desc: Hides the MPT-support-related Palette UI options.

pteCollapse.name: pteCollapse
pteCollapse.syntax:
pteCollapse(
t_rowPath
t_panelName
[ w_windowId ]
)
=> t / nil
pteCollapse.desc: Collapses the specified item in the specified Palette panel in the specified window.

pteCollapseAll.name: pteCollapseAll
pteCollapseAll.desc: Collapses all items in the specified Palette panel.

pteContextMenu.name: pteContextMenu
pteContextMenu.desc: Displays the contextual menu for the specified Palette panel.

pteDeleteLayerSet.name: pteDeleteLayerSet
pteDeleteLayerSet.desc: Deletes the specified layer set and the corresponding layer set file.

pteDeselect.name: pteDeselect
pteDeselect.syntax:
pteDeselect(
t_rowPath
t_panelName
[ w_windowId ]
)
=> t / nil
pteDeselect.desc: Deselects an individual item in the specified Palette panel.

pteDeselectAll.name: pteDeselectAll
pteDeselectAll.desc: Deselects all items in the specified Palette panel.

pteDiscardLayerSetEdition.name: pteDiscardLayerSetEdition
pteDiscardLayerSetEdition.desc: Discards the changes made to the validity or membership state of a layer-purpose pair during the current layer set editing session.

pteEditLayerSet.name: pteEditLayerSet
pteEditLayerSet.desc: Enables addition or deletion of layer-purpose pairs in a layer set.

pteEditLayerSetValidity.name: pteEditLayerSetValidity
pteEditLayerSetValidity.desc: Enables you to edit the validity and membership state of layer-purpose pairs in the selected layer sets.

pteExpand.name: pteExpand
pteExpand.syntax:
pteExpand(
t_rowPath
t_panelName
[ w_windowId ]
) 
=> t / nil
pteExpand.desc: Expands the specified item in the specified Palette panel in the specified window.

pteExpandAll.name: pteExpandAll
pteExpandAll.desc: Expands all objects in the specified Palette panel.

pteExportLayerSet.name: pteExportLayerSet
pteExportLayerSet.syntax:
pteExportLayerSet(
t_layerSetName
t_layerSetRepositoryPath
t_layerSetFilePath
[ g_overwrite ]
)
=> t / nil
pteExportLayerSet.desc: Exports a layer set from a Palette layer set repository to the file system.

pteFindNext.name: pteFindNext
pteFindNext.desc: Finds and sets as active the next layer-purpose pair that matches the search string, in the specified panel. This function works only if the Search Mode option in the Palette Options form is set to Filter.

pteFindPrev.name: pteFindPrev
pteFindPrev.desc: Finds and sets as active the previous layer-purpose pair that matches the search string, in the specified panel. This function works only if the Search Mode option in the Palette Options form is set as Filter.

pteGetActiveScopeModes.name: pteGetActiveScopeModes
pteGetActiveScopeModes.desc: Returns a list containing the scope modes that are set as active in the specified window.

pteGetAllActiveLayerSets.name: pteGetAllActiveLayerSets
pteGetAllActiveLayerSets.desc: Returns a list containing the layer sets that are set as active in the design open in the specified window.

pteGetAllLayerSets.name: pteGetAllLayerSets
pteGetAllLayerSets.desc: Returns a list containing all the layer sets available in the design open in the specified window.

pteGetCurrentPanel.name: pteGetCurrentPanel
pteGetCurrentPanel.desc: Retrieves the name of the currently active Palette panel.

pteGetLayerPath.name: pteGetLayerPath
pteGetLayerPath.desc: Retrieves the element path of the specified layer-purpose pair when the View By mode is applied to the Palette. The result can be used to provide the t_paletteElementPath argument needed by the pteSetVisible, pteSetSelectability, pteSetValidity, pteSetOnlyVisible, pteSetOnlySelectable, ptePropagateVisibility, and ptePropagateSelectability functions in the View By mode.

pteGetLayerSetColoredLpp.name: pteGetLayerSetColoredLpp
pteGetLayerSetColoredLpp.desc: Returns the layer-purpose pair associated with the specified layer set.

pteGetLayerSetMembers.name: pteGetLayerSetMembers
pteGetLayerSetMembers.desc: Returns the attribute settings for layer-purpose pairs, objects, and grids that are members of the specified layer set. For layer-purpose pairs, attributes include visibility, selectability, validity, priority, and routing direction (if set). For objects, attributes include visibility and selectability; and for grids, the attribute returned is visibility.

pteGetLPPDisplayedInPalette.name: pteGetLPPDisplayedInPalette
pteGetLPPDisplayedInPalette.desc: Lists the layer-purpose pairs currently displayed in the Layers panel.
