pteGetLSAtPosition.name: pteGetLSAtPosition
pteGetLSAtPosition.desc: Displays the name of the layer set that is listed at the specified position in the Layer Set Manager.

pteGetMPTSupportMode.name: pteGetMPTSupportMode
pteGetMPTSupportMode.desc: Determines if MPT support is enabled in the window with the specified ID.

pteGetNextLayerSets.name: pteGetNextLayerSets
pteGetNextLayerSets.desc: Returns the layer set listed immediately below the layer set if only one layer set is selected in the Layer Set Manager. If multiple layer sets are selected in the Layer Set Manager, returns a list comprising layer sets listed immediately below each selected layer set.

pteGetPrevLayerSets.name: pteGetPrevLayerSets
pteGetPrevLayerSets.desc: Returns the layer set listed immediately above the layer set if only one layer set is selected in the Layer Set Manager. If multiple layer sets are selected in the Layer Set Manager, returns a list comprising layer sets listed immediately above each selected layer set.

pteGetSelection.name: pteGetSelection
pteGetSelection.desc: Retrieves a list of the selected layer-purpose pairs, objects, or grids from the specified panel.

pteHideAllTools.name: pteHideAllTools
pteHideAllTools.desc: Hides all Palette tools and toolbars.

pteImportLayerSet.name: pteImportLayerSet
pteImportLayerSet.syntax:
pteImportLayerSet(
t_layerSetFilePath
t_layerSetRepositoryPath
t_layerSetName
[ g_overwrite ]
)
=> t / nil
pteImportLayerSet.desc: Imports the specified layer set file from the file system to the Palette repository and saves it with the specified name.

pteInfraGetPaletteMode.name: pteInfraGetPaletteMode
pteInfraGetPaletteMode.desc: Returns the container type of the Palette that is currently active.

pteIsSelectable.name: pteIsSelectable
pteIsSelectable.desc: Retrieves the selectability state for the specified layer-purpose pair or object.

pteIsVisible.name: pteIsVisible
pteIsVisible.desc: Retrieves the visibility state for the specified layer-purpose pair, object, or grid.

pteLoadConfig.name: pteLoadConfig
pteLoadConfig.desc: Loads the specified Palette configuration file. A Palette configuration file contains Palette-related information, such as the columns and toolbars to be displayed and their location.

pteLoadDefaults.name: pteLoadDefaults
pteLoadDefaults.desc: Loads the display context with the default values. A display context determines display properties, such as visibility and selectability of layer-purpose pairs, objects, and grids.

pteLoadFromTechFile.name: pteLoadFromTechFile
pteLoadFromTechFile.desc: Loads the display context from the technology file into the Palette. A display context determines display properties such as visibility and selectability of layer-purpose pairs, objects, and grids.

pteLoadGDSNumber.name: pteLoadGDSNumber
pteLoadGDSNumber.desc: Loads the GDS number layermap file from the specified location into the Palette.

pteLoadLayerSet.name: pteLoadLayerSet
pteLoadLayerSet.desc: Loads a layer set from a layer set file existing in a palette repository.

pteLoadLSWInfo.name: pteLoadLSWInfo
pteLoadLSWInfo.desc: Loads the specified Layer Selection Window (LSW) information file into the Palette. The visibility and selectability settings stored in the LSW information file for layer-purpose pairs and objects are loaded into the Palette.

pteMapWindow.name: pteMapWindow
pteMapWindow.desc: Displays, if hidden, the specified Palette panel.

pteMinimizeSingleWindowPalette.name: pteMinimizeSingleWindowPalette
pteMinimizeSingleWindowPalette.desc: Minimizes the Palette, but only if the Palette container type is set to Single Window.

pteMoveLayerSelection.name: pteMoveLayerSelection
pteMoveLayerSelection.desc: Moves the layer-purpose pairs selected in the Layers panel to the specified position. This function works only if the View By mode is set to None.

pteMoveSingleWindowPalette.name: pteMoveSingleWindowPalette
pteMoveSingleWindowPalette.desc: Places the upper-left corner of the Palette at the specified x- and y-coordinate, if the Palette container type is set to Single Window.

pteMPTSupportMode.name: pteMPTSupportMode
pteMPTSupportMode.desc: Displays the MPT-support-related Palette UI options.

ptePropagateSelectability.name: ptePropagateSelectability
ptePropagateSelectability.syntax:
ptePropagateSelectability(
{ t_layerPurposeName | t_paletteElementPath }
g_selectabilityState
t_panelName
[ w_windowId ]
)
=> t / nil
ptePropagateSelectability.desc: Propagates selectability changes to child items when the parent and child items are in a desynchronized state. Specify either t_layerPurposeName or t_paletteElementPath.

ptePropagateVisibility.name: ptePropagateVisibility
ptePropagateVisibility.syntax:
ptePropagateVisibility(
{ t_layerPurposeName | t_paletteElementPath }
g_visibilityState
t_panelName
[ w_windowId ]
)
=> t / nil
ptePropagateVisibility.desc: Propagates visibility changes to child items when the parent and child items are in a desynchronized state. Specify either t_layerPurposeName or t_paletteElementPath.

pteRaiseSingleWindowPalette.name: pteRaiseSingleWindowPalette
pteRaiseSingleWindowPalette.desc: Places the Palette on top of the other open windows, if the Palette container type is set to Single Window.

pteRegisterUserLSManagerTrigger.name: pteRegisterUserLSManagerTrigger
pteRegisterUserLSManagerTrigger.desc: Registers a trigger, which is a user-defined SKILL procedure, from CIW. This trigger is called with an argument list containing modifier, mouseButton, event, editedLS, and activeLSList when an action (other than a drag-and-drop action) is performed in the Layer Set Manager.

pteRegisterUserSelectionTrigger.name: pteRegisterUserSelectionTrigger
pteRegisterUserSelectionTrigger.desc: Registers a trigger, which is a user-defined SKILL procedure, from CIW. This trigger is called with an argument list containing windowId, layerName, purposeName, mouseButton, and modifier for every selection action. Valid values for mouseButton are Left, Right, and Middle; valid values for modifier are None, Shift, and Ctrl.

pteReloadLayerSet.name: pteReloadLayerSet
pteReloadLayerSet.desc: Reloads the layer set file for the layer set that is currently in use. This resynchronizes the visibility and selectability status of the layers, objects, or grids items with that available in the layer set file.

pteResizeSingleWindowPalette.name: pteResizeSingleWindowPalette
pteResizeSingleWindowPalette.desc: Resizes the Palette by using the specified width and height values, if the Palette container type is set to Single Window.

pteSaveAsLayerSet.name: pteSaveAsLayerSet
pteSaveAsLayerSet.syntax:
pteSaveAsLayerSet(
t_layerSetName
t_layerSetRepositoryPath
[ g_overwrite ]
[ w_windowId ]
)
=> t / nil
pteSaveAsLayerSet.desc: Saves the layer set currently in use with a new name.

pteSaveAsSynchronizedLayerSet.name: pteSaveAsSynchronizedLayerSet
pteSaveAsSynchronizedLayerSet.syntax:
pteSaveAsSynchronizedLayerSet(
t_layerSetName
t_layerSetRepositoryPath
[ g_overwrite ]
[ w_windowId ]
)
=> t / nil
pteSaveAsSynchronizedLayerSet.desc: Saves the layer set currently in use, as a synchronized layer set, with the specified name in the specified layer set repository. The newly saved layer set is set as active.

pteSaveConfig.name: pteSaveConfig
pteSaveConfig.syntax:
pteSaveConfig(
t_configFilePath
[ g_overwrite ]
[ w_windowId ]
) 
=> t / nil
pteSaveConfig.desc: Saves the Palette configuration information in the specified file. This includes information about the Palette settings, such as the columns and toolbars currently displayed in the Palette.

pteSaveGDSNumber.name: pteSaveGDSNumber
pteSaveGDSNumber.desc: Saves the active GDSII number layermap file.

pteSaveLayerSet.name: pteSaveLayerSet
pteSaveLayerSet.desc: Saves the changes made to the layer set that is currently in use.

pteSaveLayerSetList.name: pteSaveLayerSetList
pteSaveLayerSetList.desc: Saves the list of layer sets displayed in the Layer Set Manager to a file named layerset.order. The order in which the layer sets are listed and the enable state of each layer set is also saved.

pteSaveLayerSetListInRepository.name: pteSaveLayerSetListInRepository
pteSaveLayerSetListInRepository.syntax:
pteSaveLayerSetListInRepository(
t_layerSetRepositoryPath
[ g_overwrite ]
[ w_windowId ]
)
=> t / nil
pteSaveLayerSetListInRepository.desc: Saves the list of layer sets displayed in the Layer Set Manager to a file named layerset.order in the specified repository. The order in which the layer sets are listed and their state-whether enabled or disabled-is also saved.

pteSaveLSWInfo.name: pteSaveLSWInfo
pteSaveLSWInfo.syntax:
pteSaveLSWInfo(
t_configFilePath
[ g_overwrite ]
[ w_windowId ]
)
=> t / nil
pteSaveLSWInfo.desc: Saves the current LSW Info file at the specified location. This file contains information about the state of the Palette. It does not store the color and lock information of layer-purpose pairs.

pteSaveToTechFile.name: pteSaveToTechFile
pteSaveToTechFile.desc: Saves the display context from the Palette to the technology file. A display context determines display properties such as visibility and selectability of layer-purpose pairs, objects, and grids. The display context stored in individual layer sets is not considered.

pteSelect.name: pteSelect
pteSelect.syntax:
pteSelect(
t_rowPath
t_panelName
[ w_windowId ]
)
=> t / nil
pteSelect.desc: Selects the specified layer, object, or grid. An item selected previously is not deselected when you run the command again to select another item. This function works only if the Selection Mode is set to Multi Selection.

pteSelectAll.name: pteSelectAll
pteSelectAll.desc: Selects all items in the specified Palette panel. This function works only if the Selection Mode is set to Multi Selection.

pteSetActiveLpp.name: pteSetActiveLpp
pteSetActiveLpp.desc: Sets the specified layer-purpose pair as active. A layer that is not defined in the technology file is not displayed in the Palette, and an invalid layer cannot be set as active. Therefore, ensure that the specified layer is defined in the technology file and is valid.

pteSetActiveLppColor.name: pteSetActiveLppColor
pteSetActiveLppColor.desc: Sets the specified color for the active layer-purpose pair. The lock state is set to unlocked.

pteSetActiveLppColorLock.name: pteSetActiveLppColorLock
pteSetActiveLppColorLock.desc: Locks or unlocks the color on the current active layer-purpose pair.

pteSetAllLayerSetMember.name: pteSetAllLayerSetMember

=> l_spdef / nil
wspSPDefFind.desc: Finds all the snapPatternDefs (SPDefs) that apply to the specified routing layer name. In a cellview, one SPDef or widthSpacingSnapPatternDefs (WSSPDef) per layer is enabled as a global grid. With the optional argument g_enabledOnly set to t, WSSPDefs that are enabled as global for the specified routing layer are returned.

wspWSPFindByName.name: wspWSPFindByName
wspWSPFindByName.syntax:
wspWSPFindByName (
d_cellViewId 
t_wspname 
[ cellViewOnly g_cellViewOnly ]
) 
=> d_wspId
wspWSPFindByName.desc: Finds a width spacing pattern (WSP) by name in a cellview or in the technology database.

wspWSPGetFlatAttr.name: wspWSPGetFlatAttr
wspWSPGetFlatAttr.desc: Returns the attributes of a width spacing pattern (WSP) as a DPL.

wspWSPGroupFindByName.name: wspWSPGroupFindByName
wspWSPGroupFindByName.syntax:
wspWSPGroupFindByName (
d_cellViewId 
t_wspname 
[ cellViewOnly g_cellViewOnly ]
) 
=> d_wspGroupId
wspWSPGroupFindByName.desc: Finds a width spacing pattern (WSP) group by its name in a cellview or in the technology database.

wspWSSPDefAddToAllowedPatternGroups.name: wspWSSPDefAddToAllowedPatternGroups
wspWSSPDefAddToAllowedPatternGroups.syntax:
wspWSSPDefAddToAllowedPatternGroups(	
d_cellViewId 
t_wsspDefName 
t_patternGroupName
)
=> t / nil
wspWSSPDefAddToAllowedPatternGroups.desc: Adds a width spacing pattern (WSP) group to the list of allowed pattern groups for a WSSPDef.

wspWSSPDefAddToAllowedPatterns.name: wspWSSPDefAddToAllowedPatterns
wspWSSPDefAddToAllowedPatterns.syntax:
wspWSSPDefAddToAllowedPatterns(
d_cellViewId 
t_wsspDefName 
t_patternName
)
=> t / nil
wspWSSPDefAddToAllowedPatterns.desc: Adds a width spacing pattern (WSP) to the allowed patterns for a widthSpacingSnapPatternDefs (WSSPDef).

wspWSSPDefAddToEnabled.name: wspWSSPDefAddToEnabled
wspWSSPDefAddToEnabled.desc: Adds a list of widthSpacingSnapPatternDefs (WSSPDefs) to the list of WSSPDefs enabled as global grids in the specified cellview. This will filter out any duplicate, undefined wsspDefs, and wsspDefs with direction mis-match.

wspWSSPDefClearEnabledOverrides.name: wspWSSPDefClearEnabledOverrides
wspWSSPDefClearEnabledOverrides.desc: Removes any global grid overrides from the specified cellview.

wspWSSPDefFind.name: wspWSSPDefFind
wspWSSPDefFind.desc: Returns a list of widthSpacingSnapPatternDefs (WSSPDefs) that apply to a given routing layer name. The WSSPDefs may exist in the cellview or in the technology database. With the optional argument g_enabledOnly set to t, routing WSSPDefs that are enabled as global for the given layer are returned.

wspWSSPDefFindByName.name: wspWSSPDefFindByName
wspWSSPDefFindByName.desc: Finds a widthSpacingSnapPatternDefs (WSSPDef) by its name in a cellview or technology database.

wspWSSPDefGetActivePattern.name: wspWSSPDefGetActivePattern
wspWSSPDefGetActivePattern.desc: Returns the active pattern name for a widthSpacingSnapPatternDefs (WSSPDef) in the specified cellview. The active pattern may be set by a constraint in the cellview or from the WSSPDef in the cellview or technology database.

wspWSSPDefGetAllowedPatternGroups.name: wspWSSPDefGetAllowedPatternGroups
wspWSSPDefGetAllowedPatternGroups.desc: Returns a list with the names of the allowed pattern groups for the specified widthSpacingSnapPatternDefs (WSSPDef).

wspWSSPDefGetAllowedPatterns.name: wspWSSPDefGetAllowedPatterns
wspWSSPDefGetAllowedPatterns.desc: Returns a list of names of allowed width spacing patterns (WSPs) for a given widthSpacingSnapPatternDefs (WSSPDef) in the specified cellview. A WSSPDef has a list of allowed patterns and allowed pattern groups. The effective set of allowed patterns is a combination of the allowed WSPs and a WSP that is a member of an allowed pattern group. By default, this function returns the effective set of allowed patterns. You can use the g_excludeGroups argument to get only the directly allowed WSPs.

wspWSSPDefGetAttr.name: wspWSSPDefGetAttr
wspWSSPDefGetAttr.desc: The attributes of the specified widthSpacingSnapPatternDefs (WSSPDef) are converted to a DPL format. All the attribute representations are the same as the source representation, except the snappingLayers attribute, which is stored as an association table for layer-purpose pair lookup.

wspWSSPDefGetEnabledOverrides.name: wspWSSPDefGetEnabledOverrides
wspWSSPDefGetEnabledOverrides.desc: Returns the names of all the widthSpacingSnapPatternDefs (WSSPDefs) in the specified direction that are enabled as global grids. The WSSPDef direction is orthogonal to the routing direction. This filters out any duplicates, undefined wsspDefs, and wsspDefs with a direction mis-match.

wspWSSPDefRemoveFromAllowedPatternGroups.name: wspWSSPDefRemoveFromAllowedPatternGroups
wspWSSPDefRemoveFromAllowedPatternGroups.syntax:
wspWSSPDefRemoveFromAllowedPatternGroups(
d_cellViewId
t_wsspDefName
t_patternGroupName
)
=> t / nil
wspWSSPDefRemoveFromAllowedPatternGroups.desc: Removes a pattern group from the allowed pattern groups of a widthSpacingSnapPatternDefs (WSSPDef).

wspWSSPDefRemoveFromAllowedPatterns.name: wspWSSPDefRemoveFromAllowedPatterns
wspWSSPDefRemoveFromAllowedPatterns.syntax:
wspWSSPDefRemoveFromAllowedPatterns(	
d_cellViewId
t_wsspDefName
t_patternName

=> t / nil
wspWSSPDefRemoveFromAllowedPatterns.desc: Removes a width spacing pattern (WSP) from the allowed patterns of the specified cellview. This function only removes the directly-allowed WSP. If a pattern is allowed because it is a member of an allowed pattern group, then no update is made.

wspWSSPDefRemoveFromEnabled.name: wspWSSPDefRemoveFromEnabled
wspWSSPDefRemoveFromEnabled.desc: Removes the specified widthSpacingSnapPatternDefs (WSSPDefs) from the list of WSSPDefs that are enabled as global grids in the cellview.

wspWSSPDefRename.name: wspWSSPDefRename
wspWSSPDefRename.desc: Renames a widthSpacingSnapPatternDefs (WSSPDef) by deleting and re-creating it. So, the DB ID may change. This function updates the global grid and any regions that reference the WSSPDef.

wspWSSPDefSetActivePattern.name: wspWSSPDefSetActivePattern
wspWSSPDefSetActivePattern.syntax:
wspWSSPDefSetActivePattern(
d_cellViewId 
t_wsspDefName
t_defaultActiveName
)
=> t / nil
wspWSSPDefSetActivePattern.desc: Sets the default active width spacing pattern (WSP) for a widthSpacingSnapPatternDefs (WSSPDef) in the specified cellview.

wspWSSPDefSetAllowedPatternGroups.name: wspWSSPDefSetAllowedPatternGroups
wspWSSPDefSetAllowedPatternGroups.syntax:
wspWSSPDefSetAllowedPatternGroups(
d_cellViewId 
t_wsspDefName
l_patternGroupNames
)
=> t / nil
wspWSSPDefSetAllowedPatternGroups.desc: Sets the allowed pattern groups for a widthSpacingSnapPatternDefs (WSSPDef) in the specified cellview.

wspWSSPDefSetAllowedPatterns.name: wspWSSPDefSetAllowedPatterns
wspWSSPDefSetAllowedPatterns.syntax:
wspWSSPDefSetAllowedPatterns(
d_cellViewId 
t_wsspDefName
l_patternNames
[ ?keepGroups g_keepGroups ]
)
=> t / nil
wspWSSPDefSetAllowedPatterns.desc: Sets the allowed patterns for a widthSpacingSnapPatternDefs (WSSPDef) in the specified cellview. If the WSSPDef is enabled as global, the patterns apply to the global grid of the WSSPDef and to any regions for the WSSPDef for which the allowed patterns are not overridden.

wspWSSPDefSetEnabledOverrides.name: wspWSSPDefSetEnabledOverrides
wspWSSPDefSetEnabledOverrides.syntax:
wspWSSPDefSetEnabledOverrides(
d_cellViewId 
l_wsspDefNames
[ ?direction t_direction ]
)
=> t / nil
wspWSSPDefSetEnabledOverrides.desc: Overrides the global grid in the specified cellview and by enabling the specified list of widthSpacingSnapPatternDefs (WSSPDefs) as global grids. If the l_wsspDefNames argument does not contain any WSSPDef in a direction, there is no global grid for that direction even if the technology database specifies a global grid for that direction.

tpaDeselect.name: tpaDeselect
tpaDeselect.desc: Deselects the specified items on the Track Pattern Assistant.

tpaSelect.name: tpaSelect
tpaSelect.desc: Selects the specified item on the Track Pattern Assistant.

tpaSelectWSSPDef.name: tpaSelectWSSPDef
tpaSelectWSSPDef.desc: Selects the specified widthSpacingSnapPatternDefs (WSSPDef) on the Track Pattern Assistant. This is similar to selecting the WSSPDef in the Track Pattern Assistant.

tpaSetActivePattern.name: tpaSetActivePattern
tpaSetActivePattern.desc: Sets the active pattern for the given width spacing snap pattern definition (WSSPDef).

tpaSetAllDefsVisible.name: tpaSetAllDefsVisible
tpaSetAllDefsVisible.desc: Sets the visibility of the active width spacing snap pattern definitions (WSSPDefs) to All Visible (AV) or None Visible (NV) for a cellview.

tpaSetDefVisible.name: tpaSetDefVisible
tpaSetDefVisible.desc: Sets the visibility of the active pattern for the given width spacing snap pattern definition (WSSPDef) or snap pattern definition (SPDef) in the Track Pattern table. If the WSSPDef or SPDef is enabled in the Track Pattern table, this also controls the visibility of the active pattern in the canvas.

tpaSetFilterByName.name: tpaSetFilterByName
tpaSetFilterByName.desc: Sets the related snap pattern (RSP) filter by name or by other filters specified in the Track Pattern assistant.

tpaSetFilterByNumber.name: tpaSetFilterByNumber
tpaSetFilterByNumber.desc: Sets the Track Pattern Assistant Filter field using the list order number for the desired setting.

tpaSetRegionActivePattern.name: tpaSetRegionActivePattern
tpaSetRegionActivePattern.syntax:
tpaSetRegionActivePattern(
t_regionName
t_wsspDefName
t_wspName
)
=> t / nil
tpaSetRegionActivePattern.desc: Sets the active width spacing pattern (WSP) of the specified width spacing snap pattern definition (WSSPDef) on a local region.

tpaSetRegionDefVisible.name: tpaSetRegionDefVisible
tpaSetRegionDefVisible.syntax:
tpaSetRegionDefVisible(
t_regionName
t_defName 
g_visible
)
=> t / nil
tpaSetRegionDefVisible.desc: Sets the visibility of the width spacing snap pattern definition (WSSPDef) or snap pattern definition (SPDef) on a local region.

tpaSetRegionWireType.name: tpaSetRegionWireType
tpaSetRegionWireType.syntax:
tpaSetRegionWireType(
t_regionName
t_wspDefName 
l_wireTypeNames 
)
=> t / nil
tpaSetRegionWireType.desc: Sets the active wire types of the specified width spacing snap pattern definition (WSSPDef) on a local region.

tpaSetWireType.name: tpaSetWireType
tpaSetWireType.desc: Sets the active wire types for the active width spacing pattern (WSP) of the given width spacing snap pattern definition (WSSPDef).

tpaToggleDef.name: tpaToggleDef
tpaToggleDef.desc: Enables or disables the specified WSSPDef or SPDef.

tpaToggleLayer.name: tpaToggleLayer
tpaToggleLayer.desc: Sets the visibility for the active pattern of the enabled WSSPDef or SPDef on the given snapping layer.

tpaToggleRegionLayer.name: tpaToggleRegionLayer
tpaToggleRegionLayer.syntax:
tpaToggleRegionLayer(
t_regionName
t_layerName 
g_visible 
)
=> t / nil
tpaToggleRegionLayer.desc: Sets the visibility for the layer of the specified region.

ttrGetCurrentScope.name: ttrGetCurrentScope
ttrGetCurrentScope.desc: Returns the names of the active scopes. An active scope can be enabled for tracking by using the ttrStartTracking SKILL function.

ttrGetScopes.name: ttrGetScopes
ttrGetScopes.desc: Returns the list of child scope names for a given scope.

ttrGetTime.name: ttrGetTime
ttrGetTime.desc: Returns the accumulated tracking time data for the given scope.

ttrStartTracking.name: ttrStartTracking
ttrStartTracking.desc: Starts tracking the time spent on various operations in the given scope. The tracking continues until it is stopped using ttrStopTracking.

ttrStopTracking.name: ttrStopTracking
ttrStopTracking.desc: Stops tracking the time for the given scope name.

leIsEXLAppOrAbove.name: leIsEXLAppOrAbove
leIsEXLAppOrAbove.desc: Specifies whether the given application is Layout EXL or a higher tier application.

leIsLayoutAppOrAbove.name: leIsLayoutAppOrAbove
leIsLayoutAppOrAbove.desc: Specifies whether the given application is Layout Viewer or a higher tier application.

leIsMXLAppOrAbove.name: leIsMXLAppOrAbove
leIsMXLAppOrAbove.desc: Specifies whether the given application is Layout MXL or a higher tier application.

leIsXLAppOrAbove.name: leIsXLAppOrAbove
leIsXLAppOrAbove.desc: Specifies whether the given application is Layout XL or a higher tier application.

leLayoutAppNames.name: leLayoutAppNames
leLayoutAppNames.desc: Returns a list of all the layout application tiers in your Virtuoso environment. If appName is specified, it returns the name of the specified application and the higher tiers.

leLayoutViewTypes.name: leLayoutViewTypes
leLayoutViewTypes.desc: Returns a list of the layout view types in your Virtuoso environment.

abGetAssistant.name: abGetAssistant
abGetAssistant.desc: Returns the Annotation Browser window associated with the specified window.

abGetCurrentIncompleteNetFilter.name: abGetCurrentIncompleteNetFilter
abGetCurrentIncompleteNetFilter.desc: Returns the incomplete net filter currently applied on the specified window. An incomplete net filter is used to control the display of incomplete net markers in the Connectivity tab of the Annotation Browser assistant by showing or hiding a subset of net names.

abHiFindMarker.name: abHiFindMarker
abHiFindMarker.desc: In the specified window, selects the row corresponding to a marker in the Annotation Browser when the corresponding marker object is clicked in the layout canvas. Even though the marker object is selected in the layout canvas, this does not modify the selection in the canvas. If the corresponding marker is not displayed in the Annotation Browser due to the applied filtering, nothing is selected in the Annotation Browser. If a window ID is not specified, the current window is used.

abSetColorOnSelection.name: abSetColorOnSelection
abSetColorOnSelection.desc: Sets the specified color as the highlight color for all selected rows in the Annotation Browser tree view.

abSetIncompleteNetFilter.name: abSetIncompleteNetFilter
abSetIncompleteNetFilter.syntax:
abSetIncompleteNetFilter(
w_windowID
t_filterState { Show | Hide }
l_netNamess
g_enable
)
=> t / nil
abSetIncompleteNetFilter.desc: Sets the specified incomplete net filter state for the specified list of nets in the given window. An incomplete net filter is used to control the display of incomplete net markers in the Connectivity tab of the Annotation Browser assistant by showing or hiding a subset of net names.

bndAddInstsBindingByName.name: bndAddInstsBindingByName
bndAddInstsBindingByName.syntax:
bndAddInstsBindingByName(
d_schCellViewID 
t_schInstName 
d_layCellViewID 
t_layInstName 
)
=> t / nil
bndAddInstsBindingByName.desc: Adds a named instance to an existing binding. If no binding exists, a new one is created. The schematic and layout instances must both be leaf instances. You can also use bndSetInstsBindingByName() to add the first binding and then add additional bindings to the same source or target instance by using the bndAddInstBindingByName() SKILL function.

bndAddObjectsBinding.name: bndAddObjectsBinding
bndAddObjectsBinding.desc: Adds one or more objects to an existing binding. If no binding exists, a new binding is created. The specified objects must all be leaf-level instances. On the layout side, a leaf instance is an instance in the top level. On the schematic side, a leaf instance is the level at which the CPH stops such that INV1/P0 instance can bind to INV1|P0, but INV1 instance cannot bind to INV1|P0. For transparent instances, such as INV1, you can use INV1/N0 to add a binding to the nmos inside.

bndGetBoundObjects.name: bndGetBoundObjects
bndGetBoundObjects.desc: Returns a list of objects bound to a specified object. The object ID of the bound objects can be specified in different formats. See the argument description for more information.

bndGetSiblingBoundObjects.name: bndGetSiblingBoundObjects
bndGetSiblingBoundObjects.syntax:
bndGetSiblingBoundObjects(
d_dbID
[ d_layCV ]
)
=> ( dbID membInst row col ) / ( list_of_dbIDs )
bndGetSiblingBoundObjects.desc: Returns the objects bound in the same many-to-many relationship as the specified object, or the objects bound to the same mfactored, sfactored, folded or lxCombination instance as the specified object. However, the specified object is not included in the result. The object ID can be specified in different formats. See the argument description for more information.

bndRemoveInstBindingByName.name: bndRemoveInstBindingByName
bndRemoveInstBindingByName.syntax:
bndRemoveInstBindingByName(
d_dbCellViewID
t_objName
[ d_dbCellViewID ]
)
=> t / nil
bndRemoveInstBindingByName.desc: Removes the binding of a named instance.

bndRegRemoveDeviceGetSurvivingNet.name: bndRegRemoveDeviceGetSurvivingNet
bndRegRemoveDeviceGetSurvivingNet.desc: Registers a user-defined SKILL function that takes a list of net IDs and returns the ID of the single net that survives when devices are removed during layout generation.

bndRemoveObjectBinding.name: bndRemoveObjectBinding
bndRemoveObjectBinding.desc: Removes the binding of the specified objects. The object ID can be specified in different formats. See the argument description for more information.

bndRemoveTermBindingByName.name: bndRemoveTermBindingByName
bndRemoveTermBindingByName.desc: Removes the binding from a named terminal.

bndReplaceInstsBindingByName.name: bndReplaceInstsBindingByName
bndReplaceInstsBindingByName.syntax:
bndReplaceInstsBindingByName(
d_schCellViewID
t_schInstName
d_layCellViewID
t_layInstName
)
=> t / nil
bndReplaceInstsBindingByName.desc: Sets a binding between specified schematic and layout instances, replacing any existing bindings in the process. The specified instances must all be leaf instances. On the layout side, a leaf instance is an instance in the top level. On the schematic side, a leaf instance is the level at which the CPH stops such that INV1/P0 instance can bind to INV1|P0, but INV1 instance cannot bind to INV1|P0. For transparent instances, such as INV1, you can use INV1/N0 to add a binding to the nmos inside.

bndReplaceObjectsBinding.name: bndReplaceObjectsBinding
bndReplaceObjectsBinding.desc: Sets a binding between specified schematic and layout objects, replacing any existing bindings in the process. The specified objects must all be lead objects. On the layout side, a leaf instance is an instance in the top level. On the schematic side, a leaf instance is the level at which the CPH stops such that INV1/P0 instance can bind to INV1|P0, but INV1 instance cannot bind to INV1|P0. For transparent instances, such as INV1, you can use INV1/N0 to add a binding to the nmos inside.

bndReplaceTermsBindingByName.name: bndReplaceTermsBindingByName
bndReplaceTermsBindingByName.syntax:
bndReplaceTermsBindingByName(
d_schCellViewID
t_schTermName
d_layCellViewID
t_layTermName
)
=> t / nil
bndReplaceTermsBindingByName.desc: Sets a binding between specified schematic and layout terminals, replacing any existing bindings in the process. The specified terminals must all be leaf objects. On the layout side, a leaf instance is an instance in the top level. On the schematic side, a leaf instance is the level at which the CPH stops such that INV1/P0 instance can bind to INV1|P0, but INV1 instance cannot bind to INV1|P0. For transparent instances, such as INV1, you can use INV1/N0 to add a binding to the nmos inside.

bndSetInstsBindingByName.name: bndSetInstsBindingByName
bndSetInstsBindingByName.syntax:
bndSetInstsBindingByName(
d_schCellViewID
t_schInstName
d_layCellViewID
t_layInstName
)
=> t / nil
bndSetInstsBindingByName.desc: Sets a binding between specified schematic and layout instances. Any existing bindings are removed and a new one created. The specified instances must all be leaf instances.

bndSetObjectsBinding.name: bndSetObjectsBinding
bndSetObjectsBinding.desc: Set a binding between schematic and layout objects. The specified objects must be lead instances and must not be bound already. The object ID can be specified in different formats. See the argument description for more information.

bndSetTermsBindingByName.name: bndSetTermsBindingByName
bndSetTermsBindingByName.syntax:
bndSetTermsBindingByName(
d_schCellViewID
t_schTermName
d_layCellViewID
t_layTermName
)
=> t / nil
bndSetTermsBindingByName.desc: Sets a binding between specified schematic and layout terminals. The specified terminals must not already be bound.

bndUnregRemoveDeviceGetSurvivingNet.name: bndUnregRemoveDeviceGetSurvivingNet
bndUnregRemoveDeviceGetSurvivingNet.desc: Unregisters the user-defined SKILL function that is used to get the ID of the surviving net when devices are removed during layout generation.

lceAddSimpleStopLayers.name: lceAddSimpleStopLayers
lceAddSimpleStopLayers.desc: Adds simple derived layers to the validLayers section of the technology file that has the virtuosoDefaultExtractorSetup constraint group defined. This SKILL function can be useful for adding simple stop layers in memory when the technology file cannot be edited on disk. If a stop layer is added and the second layer has an unknown material, the material is automatically changed to recognition. If you add an invalid stop layer, you must close the design or launch a new Virtuoso session to refresh the memory.

lceClearLogicalConn.name: lceClearLogicalConn
lceClearLogicalConn.desc: Removes the logical connectivity on the specified cellview, such as nets that are not attached to terminals, and the nets and lxStickyNet property on all routes, shapes, and vias. In addition, the function clears all connectivity on instTerms and removes the markers created by the extractor.

lceDestroyVoidShapes.name: lceDestroyVoidShapes
lceDestroyVoidShapes.desc: Destroys void shapes in the given layout cellview.

lceExtract.name: lceExtract
lceExtract.syntax:
lceExtract(
d_layCellViewID
[ ?reportType reportType ]
[ ?disableAnnotationChecking { t | nil } ]
)
=> t / nil
lceExtract.desc: Runs the Layout XL connectivity extractor on the specified cellview.

lceExtractArea.name: lceExtractArea
lceExtractArea.syntax:
lceExtractArea(
d_layCellViewID
l_points
[ ?reportType reportType ]
)
=> t / nil
lceExtractArea.desc: Extracts connectivity for a specified area of the design.

lceExtractAreas.name: lceExtractAreas
lceExtractAreas.syntax:
lceExtractAreas(
d_layCellViewID
l_points
[ ?reportType reportType ]
)
=> t / nil
lceExtractAreas.desc: Extracts connectivity for the specified areas of the design.

lceExtractNet.name: lceExtractNet
lceExtractNet.syntax:
lceExtractNet(
net
[ ?reportType reportType ]
[ ?disableAnnotationChecking {t | nil } ]
)
=> t / nil
lceExtractNet.desc: Runs the Layout XL connectivity extractor on the specified net.

lceExtractNets.name: lceExtractNets
lceExtractNets.syntax:
lceExtractNets(
l_nets
[ ?reportType reportType ]
[ ?disableAnnotationChecking {t | nil } ]
)
=> t / nil
lceExtractNets.desc: Runs the Layout XL connectivity extractor on the specified nets.

lceExtractUnverifiedAreas.name: lceExtractUnverifiedAreas
lceExtractUnverifiedAreas.desc: Extracts connectivity for the unverified areas that are defined by the bounding box of the specified markers.

lceGetExtractLayers.name: lceGetExtractLayers
lceGetExtractLayers.desc: Lists the extractable layer-purpose pairs (LPPs) defined for a specified layout cellview. Layout XL can extract through the LPPs that are listed.

lceGetFracturedShapes.name: lceGetFracturedShapes
lceGetFracturedShapes.syntax:
lceGetFracturedShapes(
d_dbFigID
[ g_points ]
[ g_floatingOnly ]
[ d_netID ]
)
=> t / nil
lceGetFracturedShapes.desc: Generates a report of the geometry and connectivity of fractured shapes that exist within a figure (shape or prBoundary).

lceGetFracturedShapesFromNet.name: lceGetFracturedShapesFromNet
lceGetFracturedShapesFromNet.desc: Generates a report of fractured shapes corresponding to a specific net.

lceGetIncompleteNets.name: lceGetIncompleteNets
lceGetIncompleteNets.desc: Returns the list of incomplete net IDs corresponding to the specified cellview.

lceGetIncompleteNetMarkers.name: lceGetIncompleteNetMarkers
lceGetIncompleteNetMarkers.desc: Generates a list of open markers on the specified incomplete nets. If a single net is specified, the opens on that net are returned. If multiple nets are specified, the opens on each net in the list are returned. If no nets are specified, all the opens in the design are returned.

lceGetNetNamesFromArea.name: lceGetNetNamesFromArea
lceGetNetNamesFromArea.syntax:
lceGetNetNamesFromArea(
d_layCellViewID
l_region
l_layerNames
[ ?stopLevel x_stopLevel ]
[ ?maxNumNets n_maxNumNets ]
[ ?numChasedShapesLimit n_numChasedShapesLimit ]
) 
=> l_netNames
lceGetNetNamesFromArea.desc: Returns a list of the net names corresponding to the effective connectivity of the shapes on the specified layers overlapping a specified area.

lceGetOption.name: lceGetOption
lceGetOption.desc: Returns the value of the specified Connectivity Extractor option for the current or given cellview.

lceGetShortMarkers.name: lceGetShortMarkers
lceGetShortMarkers.desc: Prints a list of short markers between the passed nets. If a single net is specified, the shorts between this net and all the other nets are returned. If two nets are specified, the shorts between these two nets are returned. If more nets are specified, the shorts between pairs of nets in the list are returned.

lceHiExtract.name: lceHiExtract
lceHiExtract.desc: Opens the Extract Layout form, which you can use to extract the design either at the top level or hierarchically.

lceHierExtract.name: lceHierExtract
lceHierExtract.desc: Performs connectivity extraction of a hierarchy of cellviews from bottom to top.

args.name:
g_reportType 
[ g_extractPCells { t | nil } ]
[ g_disableAnnotationChecking { t | nil } ]

lceIsExtractLayer.name: lceIsExtractLayer
lceIsExtractLayer.desc: Checks whether the specified layer or layer-purpose pair (LPP) is extractable.

lceIsShapeTrimmed.name: lceIsShapeTrimmed
lceIsShapeTrimmed.desc: Checks if the specified shape has been trimmed during connectivity extraction.

lcePrintConstraintGroupWarnings.name: lcePrintConstraintGroupWarnings
lcePrintConstraintGroupWarnings.desc: Prints the warnings issued by the connectivity extractor for the specified technology library. The constraint group for which the warnings are issued is the one defined using the setupConstraintGroup environment variable.

lcePrintExtractLayers.name: lcePrintExtractLayers
lcePrintExtractLayers.syntax:
lcePrintExtractLayers(
d_layCellViewID
[ ?cgName d_cgName ]
[ ?verifyWellSubstrateConnections { t | nil } ]
[ ?useOverlappingLabelsAsConnectivitySources { t | nil } ]
[ ?enableVirtualConnections { t | nil } ]
[ ?fileName t_fileName ]
[ ?appendToFile { t | nil } ]
)
=> t / nil
lcePrintExtractLayers.desc: Generates a report about the extractable layers. See Diagnostics Report (Connectivity form).

lcePrintExtractVias.name: lcePrintExtractVias
lcePrintExtractVias.syntax:
lcePrintExtractVias(
d_layCellViewID
[ ?cgName d_cgName ]
[ ?verifyWellSubstrateConnections { t | nil } ]
[ ?useOverlappingLabelsAsConnectivitySources { t | nil } ]
[ ?enableVirtualConnections { t | nil } ]
[ ?fileName t_fileName ]
[ ?appendToFile { t | nil } ]
)
=> t / nil
lcePrintExtractVias.desc: Generates a report about the extractable vias.

lcePrintTechDiagnostics.name: lcePrintTechDiagnostics
lcePrintTechDiagnostics.syntax:
lcePrintTechDiagnostics(
d_layCellViewID
[ ?cgName d_cgName ]
[ ?verifyWellSubstrateConnections { t | nil } ]
[ ?useOverlappingLabelsAsConnectivitySources { t | nil } ]
[ ?enableVirtualConnections { t | nil } ]
[ ?fileName t_fileName ]
[ ?appendToFile { t | nil } ]
)
=> t
lcePrintTechDiagnostics.desc: Generates a report about the connectivity extractor technology diagnostics and indicates if the technology file has been correctly set up for extraction. See Diagnostics Reports (Connectivity form).

lceRegenerateVoidShapes.name: lceRegenerateVoidShapes
lceRegenerateVoidShapes.desc: Regenerates void shapes in the given layout cellview.

lceSetOption.name: lceSetOption
lceSetOption.syntax:
lceSetOption(
name
value
[ cvID ]

)
=> t / nil
lceSetOption.desc: Sets the specified Connectivity Extractor option for the current or given cellview.

lceShortLocatorChaseAndSave.name: lceShortLocatorChaseAndSave
lceShortLocatorChaseAndSave.syntax:
lceShortLocatorChaseAndSave(
d_winID
g_shapes
g_hierStart
t_viewName
)
=> t / nil
lceShortLocatorChaseAndSave.desc: Chases islands from the specified start shapes and saves them along with the shortest paths between their points of stickiness.

lceShortLocatorRaiseForm.name: lceShortLocatorRaiseForm
lceShortLocatorRaiseForm.desc: Opens the Short Locator form, which you can use to locate the shapes in a layout that are causing shorts.

lntComputeNeighbors.name: lntComputeNeighbors
lntComputeNeighbors.syntax:
lntComputeNeighbors(
w_window
n_distance
[ s_layers ]
[ s_netNameMethod ]
)
=> t
lntComputeNeighbors.desc: Finds neighboring shapes for the existing traces in the specified window, within the given distance, on the same layer or any extractable layer and creates highlights for the overlapped portions.

lntContSteps.name: lntContSteps
lntContSteps.desc: Generates the complete trace from the current step to the last when the Net Tracer is invoked in Step trace mode.

lntGetAllTraces.name: lntGetAllTraces
lntGetAllTraces.desc: Lists all the traces in the specified cellview.

lntGetCurrentStep.name: lntGetCurrentStep
lntGetCurrentStep.desc: Returns the current step value when the Net Tracer is invoked in Step trace mode.

lntGetSavedViewNames.name: lntGetSavedViewNames
lntGetSavedViewNames.desc: Returns the list of views saved in the specified library and cell.

lntGetTailVal.name: lntGetTailVal
lntGetTailVal.desc: Returns the current value of the tail of a trace when the Net Tracer is invoked in Step trace mode.

lntGetTraceInfo.name: lntGetTraceInfo
lntGetTraceInfo.desc: Returns information for a specified trace. The returned information contains the trace container, its name, color, and visibility status, and the number of chased shapes.

lntHideNeighbors.name: lntHideNeighbors
lntHideNeighbors.desc: Hides displayed neighbors for the specified window. The computed neighbors are retained and can be displayed again using the lntShowNeighbors command. Use lntClearNeighbors to delete all neighbors.

lntHiEditTrace.name: lntHiEditTrace
lntHiEditTrace.desc: Invokes the Net Tracer Edit In Place command that lets you edit in place the instances that contain the traced objects.

lntHiNetTracer.name: lntHiNetTracer
lntHiNetTracer.desc: Invokes the Net Tracer command, which you can use to add, update, or delete traces in a layout window.

lntIsNeighborsVisible.name: lntIsNeighborsVisible
lntIsNeighborsVisible.desc: Checks whether Net Tracer neighbors are visible in the specified window.

lntIsStepTrace.name: lntIsStepTrace
lntIsStepTrace.desc: Checks whether the specified trace was created using Step mode.

lntNeighbors.name: lntNeighbors
lntNeighbors.desc: Displays the Net Tracer Neighbors form, which you can use to compute all neighboring shapes within a given distance for all the traces in the window.

lntNextStep.name: lntNextStep
lntNextStep.desc: Increments the current step value by one when the Net Tracer is invoked in Step trace mode.

lntNextToSetStep.name: lntNextToSetStep
lntNextToSetStep.desc: Forwards tracing of all Step mode traces to the newly specified step value. For information about how the SKILL function behaves differently for each trace, depending on the maximum step value for the trace, see Additional Information.

lntPrevStep.name: lntPrevStep
lntPrevStep.desc: Decrements the current step value by one when the Net Tracer is invoked in Step trace mode.

lntRemoveAll.name: lntRemoveAll
lntRemoveAll.desc: Removes all traces created by the Net Tracer command from the current layout window.

lntRemoveAllTraces.name: lntRemoveAllTraces
lntRemoveAllTraces.desc: Removes all traces from the specified window.

lntRemoveTrace.name: lntRemoveTrace
lntRemoveTrace.desc: Removes the specified trace from the specified window.

lntSaveTraces.name: lntSaveTraces
lntSaveTraces.syntax:
lntSaveTraces(
w_windowID
l_traceID
libName
cellName
viewName
[ g_saveNeighbors ]
[ g_appendTraces ]
[ g_replaceSameNameTrace ]
[ ?oneViewPerTrace g_oneViewPerTrace ]
)
=> t / nil
lntSaveTraces.desc: Saves the shapes of the specified traces that are displayed in the library cellview open in the specified window.

lntSetCurrentStep.name: lntSetCurrentStep
lntSetCurrentStep.desc: Sets the current step value for a trace when the Net Tracer is invoked in Step trace mode.

lntSetTailVal.name: lntSetTailVal
lntSetTailVal.desc: Sets the current value of the tail for all traces when the Net Tracer is invoked in Step trace mode.

lntSetTraceColor.name: lntSetTraceColor
lntSetTraceColor.syntax:
lntSetTraceColor(
x_traceID
t_color
[ w_window ]
)
=> t / nil
lntSetTraceColor.desc: Changes the color of the specified trace to the specified color in the given window.

lntSetTraceVisibility.name: lntSetTraceVisibility
lntSetTraceVisibility.syntax:
lntSetTraceVisibility(
x_traceID
x_visibility
[ w_window ]
)
=> t / nil
lntSetTraceVisibility.desc: Sets the visibility of the specified trace in the specified window.

lntShowHideAllTraces.name: lntShowHideAllTraces
lntShowHideAllTraces.desc: Shows or hides all traces in the cellview contained in the specified window.

lntShowNeighbors.name: lntShowNeighbors
lntShowNeighbors.desc: Displays computed neighbors for the specified window. The computed neighbors can be hidden using the lntHideNeighbors SKILL function. Use lntClearNeighbors to delete all neighbors.

lxAbutGetNeighbors.name: lxAbutGetNeighbors
lxAbutGetNeighbors.syntax:
lxAbutGetNeighbors(
{ ld_instId | d_instId }
[ ?direction { 'up | 'down | 'left | 'right | 'horizontal | 'vertical | 'all } ]
[ ?depth { 0 ... INT_MAX } ]
[ ?stopGroup d_stopGroup ]
[ ?select { t | nil } ]
)
=> ld_instId / nil
lxAbutGetNeighbors.desc: The traversal can be restricted by providing a maximum traversal depth. A value of 0 or nil indicates no restriction. If an abutment group object is supplied via the ?stopGroup argument, the group is not traversed. The ?select argument, when true, selects the returned instances.

lxChain.name: lxChain
lxChain.syntax:
lxChain(
l_insts
l_point
[ ?groups l_groups ]
[ ?preserveExistingChains { t | nil } ]
[ ?useDeviceOrder { t | nil } ]
[ ?interdigitateChains { t | nil } ]
[ ?mirror { t | nil } ]
[ ?permute { t | nil } ]
[ ?allowSingleBulk { t | nil } ]
[ ?dummyFlexBothEndNets { t | nil } ]
[ ?syncChains { t | nil } ]
[ ?mirrorEquivOrients { t | nil } ]
[ ?preserveRows { t | nil } ]
[ ?useAbutSpacing { t | nil } ]
[ ?maxChainSize x_maxChainSize ]
[ ?contacts { 0 | 1 | 2 } ]
[ ?chainAlignPMOS { Top | Center | Bottom } ]
[ ?chainAlignNMOS { Top | Center | Bottom } ]
[ ?chainLeftNet { Source | Drain | Either } ]
[ ?abutStrategy { sdFirst | dummyFirst } ]
[ ?optimize { Tracks | Abutments | Both } ]
[ ?multiRow { NP | PN | NPPN | PNNP } ]
[ ?effort { Minimal | Nominal | Maximal } ]
)
=> l_chains / nil
lxChain.desc: Chains a list of instances and places the generated chains at the specified position in the layout. Using the optional arguments will override the existing settings of the environment variables: chainPreserveExistingChains, chainUseDeviceOrder, lxAllowPseudoParallelNets, chainMirror, chainPermutePins, chainAllowSingleBulk, chainDummyFlexBothEndNets, chainSyncChains, chainMirrorEquivOrients, chainPreserveRows,chainUseAbutSpacing, lxChainAlignPMOS, lxChainAlignNMOS, chainLeftNet and chainAbutStrategy.

lxChainAnchor2D.name: lxChainAnchor2D
lxChainAnchor2D.desc: Specifies the pins or instances to be used as anchors to derive connectivity information to chain devices until no further chains can be formed.

lxCheck.name: lxCheck
lxCheck.syntax:
lxCheck(
d_layCV
[ ?schCV d_schCV ]
[ ?checkDevices { t | nil } ]
[ ?checkExtractLayout { t | nil } ]
[ ?extractStopLevel [0-32] ]
)
=> 0 - 100 / -1
lxCheck.desc: Checks the layout for XL compliance and reports binding status in an Info pop-up box. It is recommended to use the lxCheck SKILL function to look for any possible problems in the design if the Navigator XL Status column is not clean. After the issues reported by lxCheck are resolved, running the Connectivity - Update Binding command should give an improved XL Status.

lxCheckAgainstSource.name: lxCheckAgainstSource
lxCheckAgainstSource.syntax:
lxCheckAgainstSource(
d_schCellViewID
d_layCellViewID
[ ?masterDiff { t | nil } ]
[ ?paramDiff { t | nil } ]
[ ?unboundInsts { t | nil } ]
[ ?connectivity { t | nil } ]
[ ?maxDiffsLimit x_maxDiffsLimit ]
[ ?logFileName t_logFileName ]
[ ?appendToLog { t | nil } ]
[ ?nameDiff { t | nil } ]
[ ?dummyDiff { t | nil } ]
[ ?busTermDiff { t | nil } ]
[ ?virtualHierDiff { t | nil } ]
)
=> t / nil
lxCheckAgainstSource.desc: Generates a report highlighting the differences between the schematic and the layout cellview. If you use the optional arguments, they override the existing environment variable settings in the .cdsenv file.

lxCheckAndUpdate.name: lxCheckAndUpdate
lxCheckAndUpdate.syntax:
lxCheckAndUpdate(
t_libNameOrLayCV
[ ?schCV d_schematicCellview  ]
[ ?update g_update ]
[ ?app t_appName ]
[ ?layoutComplete g_layoutComplete ]
[ ?binder t_binderValue ]
[ ?svdbPath t_lvsSvdbPath ]
[ ?svdbScale n_lvsScale ]
[ ?extract g_Extract ] 
[ ?extractStopLevel n_stoplevel) }  ]
[ ?onlyCheckUpdate g_onlyCheckUpdate  ]
[ ?allCellsInDesign g_allCellsInDesign  ]
[ ?allCellsInLibrary g_allCellsInLibrary ]
[ ?excludeCells t_excludeCells  ]
[ ?includeCells t_includeCells  ]
[ ?leafCells t_leafCells  ]
[ ?withoutSchematic g_cellsWithoutSchematic  ]
[ ?filterMessage l_filterMessage ]
[ ?createHTML g_createHTMLReport ]
[ ?openHTML g_openHTMLReport ]
[ ?logFile g_logFile  ]
[ ?logFileDirectory t_logFileDirectoryPath  ]
[ ?detailedReturn g_detailedReturn  ]
[ ?report { t | nil }   ]
[ ?reportOptions { t| nil }  ]
[ ?graphical { t| nil }   ]
[ ?targetWindow { w_windowId | nil }  ]
)
=> nil | l_testResult | n_percentageClean
lxCheckAndUpdate.desc: Runs the application readiness check and updates the specified cellviews for the specified applications.

lxCheckAndUpdateRegister.name: lxCheckAndUpdateRegister
lxCheckAndUpdateRegister.syntax:
lxCheckAndUpdateRegister(
t_appName
g_path
g_check
g_update
[ ?severity t_severity ]
[ ?object t_objectType ]
[ ?checkFunction t_checkFunction ]
[ ?updateFunction t_updateFunction ]
[ ?configCB t_arcCallBackFunction ]
[ ?master g_callCheckUpdateMaster ]
[ ?subMaster g_callCheckUpdateSubmaster ]
[ ?markers g_createMarkers ]
)
=> t / nil
lxCheckAndUpdateRegister.desc: Registers any user-defined SKILL check and update functions needed for the application readiness check.

lxCheckAndUpdateRemove.name: lxCheckAndUpdateRemove
lxCheckAndUpdateRemove.desc: Removes the specified application or test from the application readiness checks.

lxCheckAndUpdateSet.name: lxCheckAndUpdateSet
lxCheckAndUpdateSet.syntax:
lxCheckAndUpdateSet(
t_appName
g_path
?check g_check
?update g_update
?severity g_severity
)
=> t / nil
lxCheckAndUpdateSet.desc: Sets check, update, and severity values for the Application Readiness Checker form.

lxCheckLib.name: lxCheckLib
lxCheckLib.syntax:
lxCheckLib(
libName
[ ?checkBindings { t | nil } ]
[ ?checkExtractLayout { t | nil } ]
[ ?summaryLogFileName t_summaryLogFileName ]
[ ?extractStopLevel [0-32] ]
)
=> 0 - 100 / -1
lxCheckLib.desc: Checks the layouts in the specified library for opens and shorts when extracted to extractStopLevel, and displays the results in CIW and in the Info window. CAD engineers are advised to run this SKILL function to identify the instances that are likely to cause issues with Update Binding.

lxCmdOptions.name: lxCmdOptions
lxCmdOptions.desc: Implements a command option for the listed Virtuoso Layout Suite XL commands when the right-mouse button bindkey is pressed. For other Layout XL commands, the right-mouse button bindkey performs the operations as supported by cmdOptions.

lxCmdShiftOptions.name: lxCmdShiftOptions
lxCmdShiftOptions.desc: Activates the bindkeys associated with Shift-click and Shift-right click during the operation of enterFunction commands. Typing this command in the Command Interpreter Window has no effect.

lxComputeViaParams.name: lxComputeViaParams
lxComputeViaParams.syntax:
lxComputeViaParams(
d_viaDefID
d_objID
[ ds_constraintGroup ]
[ l_params ]
[ f_pathWidth1 ]
[ t_pathDirection1 ]
[ f_pathWidth2 ]
[ t_pathDirection2 ]
[ l_options ]
)
=> list_of_params | nil
lxComputeViaParams.desc: Returns a list of DRC-correct via parameters for a specified standard via definition or a custom via definition that references either a cdsVia or a correctly-defined syEnhContact. The via parameters returned are: n_cutWidth, n_cutHeight, l_cutSpacing (X and Y), l_layer1Enc and l_layer2Enc (top, bottom, left, and right).

lxConvertSlotToPolygon.name: lxConvertSlotToPolygon
lxConvertSlotToPolygon.syntax:
lxConvertSlotToPolygon(
[ ?all { t | nil } ]
[ ?region l_region ]
[ ?layers l_layers ]
)
=> t / nil
lxConvertSlotToPolygon.desc: Converts the metal shapes on the drawing purpose to one slotted metal polygon by creating holes where the slot purpose shapes cover the original metal shapes. The original metal shapes and the slot purpose shapes are removed.

lxCreateBndFile.name: lxCreateBndFile
lxCreateBndFile.syntax:
lxCreateBndFile(
[ t_ixfFile ]
[ t_netFile ]
[ t_bndFile ]
[ d_layId ]
[ g_graphical ]
)
=> t / nil
lxCreateBndFile.desc: Creates a binding file based on the PVS instance cross-reference file and the extracted netlist file.

lxCreateGroupArray.name: lxCreateGroupArray
lxCreateGroupArray.syntax:
lxCreateGroupArray(
d_cvId
l_figList 
[ ?name t_name ]
[ ?rows x_rows ]
[ ?columns x_cols ]
[ ?X x_xValue ]
[ ?Y x_yValue ]
[ ?orients l_orientList ]
[ ?mode 'pitch | 'spacing ]
[ ?lpp l_refLPP ]
)
=> d_groupArrayId / nil
lxCreateGroupArray.desc: Creates a group array with the specified parameters.

lxCreateSynchronousClonesFromFigGroups.name: lxCreateSynchronousClonesFromFigGroups
lxCreateSynchronousClonesFromFigGroups.syntax:
lxCreateSynchronousClonesFromFigGroups(
( figGroupList )
[ dumpConsistencyCheckMsg ]
[ dumpNonClonableFigGroups ]
)
=> t / nil
lxCreateSynchronousClonesFromFigGroups.desc: Creates a new clone family from a list of basic figGroups. When the clone family is created, the function runs the Clone Consistency Checker to verify that the figGroups are effectively synchronous. The checks that are run include verifying that the figGroups are identical, which means their shapes exist on the same layer, instances belong to the same master, and have the same relative position, and so on.

lxDeleteSchematicDummies.name: lxDeleteSchematicDummies
lxDeleteSchematicDummies.syntax:
lxDeleteSchematicDummies(
[ ?schCV d_schCellViewID ]
[ ?layCV d_layCellViewID ]
[ ?layInsts l_insts ]
[ ?useMFactor { t | nil } ]
)
=> t / nil
lxDeleteSchematicDummies.desc: Deletes bound back annotated schematic instances for the specified dummy layout instances. For mfactored layout devices that have all the layout dummies included in the layout selected set, the SKILL function deletes the schematic dummy instances corresponding to the layout dummies. If all the layout dummy instances of the mfactored device are not included in the selected set, the SKILL function decrements the mfactor to reflect the removal of the selected dummies.

lxDeleteSynchronousCloneFamily.name: lxDeleteSynchronousCloneFamily
lxDeleteSynchronousCloneFamily.desc: Deletes the specified family of synchronous clones. As a result, the member clones are desynchronized and they behave as basic groups.

lxFold.name: lxFold
lxFold.syntax:
lxFold(
l_insts
l_point
x_numFolds
[ ?widths l_widths ]
[ ?chainFolds { t | nil } ]
[ ?ignoreMFactor { t | nil } ]
[ ?chainAlignPMOS { Top | Center | Bottom } ]
[ ?chainAlignNMOS { Top | Center | Bottom } ]
[ ?enforceWidthMatch { t | nil } ]
[ ?keepFolds { t | nil } ]
)
=> l_chains / nil
lxFold.desc: Folds a list of valid instances into the specified number of folds and places them at the specified location. If the disableFolding environment variable is set and the folding threshold for the component type is set to 0, folding is disabled.

lxGenerateFinish.name: lxGenerateFinish
lxGenerateFinish.syntax:
lxGenerateFinish(
d_schId
d_layId
[ ?extractSchematic { t | nil } ]
)
=> t / nil
lxGenerateFinish.desc: Finishes the layout generation process by executing the Generate All From Source command with the form values supplied by lxSet* functions and after the previous call to lxGenerateStart.

lxGenerateStart.name: lxGenerateStart
lxGenerateStart.syntax:
lxGenerateStart(
d_schId
d_layId
[ ?extractSchematic { t | nil } ]
)
=> t / nil
lxGenerateStart.desc: Starts the Generate All From Source command, building the Generate Layout form without displaying it to the screen.

lxGenFromSource.name: lxGenFromSource
lxGenFromSource.syntax:
lxGenFromSource(
d_schCellViewID
[ ?layLibName t_layLibName ]
[ ?layCellName t_layCellName ]
[ ?layViewName t_layViewName ]
[ ?configLib t_configLib ]
[ ?configCell t_configCell ]
[ ?configView t_configView ]
[ ?initCreateInstances { t | nil } ]
[ ?initDoStacking { t | nil } ]
[ ?initDoFolding { t | nil } ]
[ ?initCreatePins { t | nil } ]
[ ?initGlobalNetPins { t | nil } ]
[ ?initCreatePadPins { t | nil } ]
[ ?initCreateBoundary { t | nil } ]
[ ?initCreateSnapBoundary { t | nil } ]
[ ?lxPositionMinSep n_lxPositionMinSep ]
[ ?lxGenerateInBoundary { t | nil } ]
[ ?initCreateMTM { t | nil } ]
[ ?extractAfterGenerateAll { t | nil } ]
[ ?extractSchematic { t | nil } ]
[ ?ignoreSchematicCheck { t | nil } ]
[ ?initPrBoundaryShape t_initPrBoundaryShape ]
[ ?initPrBoundaryOrigin l_initPrBoundaryOrigin ]
[ ?initPrBoundaryPoints l_initPrBoundaryPoints ]
[ ?initAreaSource1 t_initAreaSource1 ]
[ ?areaCalc t_areaCalc ]
[ ?initAreaSource2 t_initAreaSource2 ]
[ ?initAreaSource1Val n_initAreaSource1Val ]
[ ?initAreaSource2Val n_initAreaSource2Val ]
[ ?virtualHierarchy { t | nil } ]
[ ?softBlocks { t | nil } ]
[ ?softBlockArea { t | nil } ]
[ ?useAreaBoundaryUtilization { t | nil } ]
[ ?areaBoundaryEnclosure n_areaBoundaryEnclosure ]
[ ?allAreaBoundaries { t | nil } ]
)
=> dbCellViewID
lxGenFromSource.desc: Generates a layout from a specified schematic cellview. If you do not specify the layout library, cell, and view names, the layout view is created with the same name as the schematic cell. If you do not specify the physConfig library, cell and view names, the layout view is created with the same name as the layout cell with physConfig as the default physConfigView. If you use the optional arguments, they override the existing environment variables set in the .cdsenv file.

lxGetAvailablePinLPPs.name: lxGetAvailablePinLPPs
lxGetAvailablePinLPPs.desc: Lists the valid layer-purpose pairs to use for setting the pin layer. This function must always be called between calls to lxGenerateStart and lxGenerateFinish or lxUpdateComponentsAndNetsStart and lxUpdateComponentsAndNetsFinish. It is typically used to find a layer-purpose pair to pass to lxSetNetPinSpecs.

lxGetCloneFamilyName.name: lxGetCloneFamilyName
lxGetCloneFamilyName.desc: Returns the family name of the specified clone.

lxGetConnRef.name: lxGetConnRef
lxGetConnRef.desc: Gets the connectivity reference for the specified layout cellview or for the layout cellview opened in the specified window. The layout cellview does not need to be open in a Layout XL session for the connectivity reference to be returned.

lxGetEditedSyncClone.name: lxGetEditedSyncClone
lxGetEditedSyncClone.desc: Returns the database ID of the synchronous clone currently being edited in the specified layout cellview. If the function finds a currently-edited layout group which is not a synchronous clone, it recursively checks to determine if its parent group is a synchronous clone. If it is, the function returns the ID of the parent synchronous clone.

lxGetGroupArrayParams.name: lxGetGroupArrayParams
lxGetGroupArrayParams.desc: Returns parameters of the specified group array.

lxGetOtherClonesInFamily.name: lxGetOtherClonesInFamily
lxGetOtherClonesInFamily.desc: The generated list does not contain the specified clone.

lxGetPermutedInstTerms.name: lxGetPermutedInstTerms
lxGetPermutedInstTerms.desc: Returns the list of database IDs of instance terminals that have been permuted on a specified layout instance. The function can identify instance terminals that have been permuted, even if there is no permuteRule property on the schematic or layout instances or their masters.

lxGetPinNets.name: lxGetPinNets
lxGetPinNets.desc: Lists the pin net names from the Generate Layout or Update Components and Nets form. This function must always be called between calls to lxGenerateStart and lxGenerateFinish or lxUpdateComponentsAndNetsStart and lxUpdateComponentsAndNetsFinish. It is typically used to find net names to pass to lxSetNetPinSpecs.

lxGetSchematic.name: lxGetSchematic
lxGetSchematic.desc: Returns either the schematic currently open in an existing Layout XL session, the schematic defined by the connectivity reference returned by lxGetConnRef, or the schematic in the same library and cell as the layout when no connectivity reference is defined.

lxGetSource.name: lxGetSource
lxGetSource.desc: Returns the source (schematic) cellview ID for the specified layout window ID or layout cellview ID in the current Layout XL session. If the schematic reference for the specified layout window has changed since the current Layout XL session was started, Layout XL must be relaunched for lxGetSource to return the updated schematic reference.

lxGetSyncClone.name: lxGetSyncClone
lxGetSyncClone.desc: Returns the database ID of the synchronous clone to which the specified object belongs. If the object belongs to a layout group which is not a synchronous clone, the function recursively checks to determine if its parent group is a synchronous clone. If it is, the function returns the ID of the parent synchronous clone.

lxGetValidViaDefs.name: lxGetValidViaDefs
lxGetValidViaDefs.syntax:
lxGetValidViaDefs(
d_objID
[ ds_constraintGroup ]
[ ltx_bottomLayer ]
[ ltx_topLayer ]
)
=> list_of_viaDefs / nil
lxGetValidViaDefs.desc: Returns a list of via definitions associated with a specified design object. You can restrict the list to include only vias defined in a specified constraint group or which feature a specific top and/or bottom layer. If you specify a technology file, no constraint groups, and no layers, the function returns all the via definitions in the technology database. If you specify both top and bottom layers, the function returns only via definitions featuring those layers. If you specify either a top or bottom layer, the function returns only via definitions featuring the layer in question.

lxGroupArrayCreatePreset.name: lxGroupArrayCreatePreset
lxGroupArrayCreatePreset.syntax:
lxGroupArrayCreatePreset(
t_presetName
t_orientPattern
t_presetDesc
g_isEditable
)
=> t / nil
lxGroupArrayCreatePreset.desc: Creates an orientation pattern for group arrays.

lxHiBackAnnotateDummies.name: lxHiBackAnnotateDummies
lxHiBackAnnotateDummies.desc: Launches the interactive backannotation enter function to create dummy instances from the layout view into the corresponding schematic view.

lxHierCheck.name: lxHierCheck
lxHierCheck.syntax:
lxHierCheck(
layCV
[ ?checkDevices { t | nil } ]
[ ?checkExtractLayout { t | nil } ]
[ ?extractStopLevel [0-32] ]
[ ?hierSummaryLogFileName t_hierSummaryLogFileName ]
)
=> 0 - 100 / -1

lxHierCheckAgainstSource.name: lxHierCheckAgainstSource
lxHierCheckAgainstSource.syntax:
lxHierCheckAgainstSource(
d_layCellViewID
[ ?masterDiff { t | nil } ]
[ ?paramDiff { t | nil } ]
[ ?unboundInsts { t | nil } ]
[ ?connectivity { t | nil } ]
[ ?maxDiffsLimit x_maxDiffsLimit ]
[ ?logFileName t_logFileName ]
[ ?appendToLog { t | nil } ]
[ ?nameDiff { t | nil } ]
[ ?dummyDiff { t | nil } ]
)
=> t / nil
lxHierCheckAgainstSource.desc: Generates a report highlighting the differences between the schematic and layout cellviews for unique layout masters in the specified layout hierarchy. If you use the optional arguments, they override the existing environment variables set in the .cdsenv file. This SKILL function always skips any layouts that have no instances. If a log file name is specified for the hierSummaryLogFileName environment variable, the SKILL function prints the summary information to the specified log file, in addition to printing the information to the default Virtuoso log file.

lxHierUpdateComponentsAndNets.name: lxHierUpdateComponentsAndNets
lxHierUpdateComponentsAndNets.syntax:
lxHierUpdateComponentsAndNets(
d_layCellViewID
[ ?initCreatePins { t | nil } ]
[ ?initGlobalNetPins { t | nil } ]
[ ?initCreatePadPins { t | nil } ]
[ ?initCreateInstances { t | nil } ]
[ ?initCreateBoundary { t | nil } ]
[ ?initCreateSnapBoundary { t | nil } ]
[ ?initDoStacking { t | nil } ]
[ ?initDoFolding { t | nil } ]
[ ?initCreateMTM { t | nil } ]
[ ?deleteUnmatchedInsts { t | nil } ]
[ ?deleteUnmatchedPins { t | nil } ]
[ ?updateReplacesMasters { t | nil } ]
[ ?updateWithMarkers { t | nil } ]
[ ?updateLayoutParameters { t | nil } ]
[ ?updateNetSigType { t | nil } ]
[ ?updateNetMinMaxVoltage { t | nil } ]
[ ?updateNetsOnly { t | nil } ]
[ ?virtualHierarchy { t | nil } ]
[ ?skipLeafs { t | nil } ]
[ ?extractSchematic { t | nil } ]
)
=> t / nil
lxHierUpdateComponentsAndNets.desc: Updates the components and nets for all unique layout masters in the specified layout cellview hierarchy. The layouts are automatically opened in edit mode for update. If a log file name is specified for the hierSummaryLogFileName environment variable, the SKILL function prints the summary information to the specified log file, in addition to printing the information to the default Virtuoso log file.

lxHiAbout.name: lxHiAbout
lxHiAbout.desc: Opens the product information window for Layout XL, which includes the release number and the copyright information.

lxHiAlign.name: lxHiAlign
lxHiAlign.desc: Opens the Align form, in which you can specify how selected objects are to be aligned in the layout window design area.

lxHiBackAnnotateAllActiveDummies.name: lxHiBackAnnotateAllActiveDummies
lxHiBackAnnotateAllActiveDummies.syntax:
lxHiBackAnnotateAllActiveDummies(
[ ?schCV d_schCellViewId ]
[ ?layCV d_layCellViewId ]
[ ?autoSchExtract { t | nil } ]
)
=> t
lxHiBackAnnotateAllActiveDummies.desc: Backannotates to schematic the symbols of all the active dummy devices-dummy devices that are not tied to a power or ground net and are not bound in the current layout view. If the schematic and the layout cellview IDs are not supplied, Virtuoso tries to determine them automatically.

lxHiBackAnnotateSelectedDummies.name: lxHiBackAnnotateSelectedDummies
lxHiBackAnnotateSelectedDummies.syntax:
lxHiBackAnnotateSelectedDummies(
[ ?schCV d_schCellViewId ]
[ ?layCV d_layCellViewId ]
[ ?autoSchExtract { t | nil } ]
[ ?figs l_figs ]
)
=> t
lxHiBackAnnotateSelectedDummies.desc: Backannotates to schematic the symbols of selected active dummy devices-dummy devices that are not tied to a power or ground net and are not bound in the current layout view. If the schematic and the layout cellview IDs are not supplied, Virtuoso tries to determine them automatically.

lxHiChain.name: lxHiChain
lxHiChain.desc: Opens the Generate Chained Devices form, which you can use to specify the transistors in the design to be chained, and starts the interactive chaining function on the design in the specified window. If you do not specify a window, it operates on the design in the current window.

lxHiCheck.name: lxHiCheck
lxHiCheck.desc: Checks XL compliance of the layout when called using the Connectivity - Check - XL Compliance command.

lxHiCheckAllTerminalInterfaces.name: lxHiCheckAllTerminalInterfaces
lxHiCheckAllTerminalInterfaces.desc: Checks the interface and physical-only status of all the scalar terminals in the currently edited layout cellview. Markers are created in the layout for any mismatches found.

lxHiClone.name: lxHiClone
lxHiClone.desc: Opens the Generate Clones form, which you can use to specify cloning parameters, and starts the interactive cloning function, which lets you replicate a section of the layout in such a way that the new piece of layout material can be placed at more than one location, with each part preserving the hierarchical structure and connectivity of the source. You can clone devices, pins, and (if selected from the layout window) interconnect structures such as wires and paths made of shapes. The interactive cloning function operates on the design in the specified window. If you do not specify a window, the function operates on the design in the current window.

lxHiConnectInstPin.name: lxHiConnectInstPin
lxHiConnectInstPin.desc: Opens the Assign Nets form and starts the Assign Nets command, which let you assign instance pins to nets in the design.

lxHiConvertMosaicToGroupArray.name: lxHiConvertMosaicToGroupArray
lxHiConvertMosaicToGroupArray.desc: Converts the selected mosaic to a group array. If a mosaic is not selected in the window, it starts the command and prompts you to select the mosaic that you want to convert to a group array.

lxHiCreateGroup.name: lxHiCreateGroup
lxHiCreateGroup.desc: Creates a figGroup using the selected set of components, if the selected set is not already inside an existing figGroup. If the selected set is inside a virtual hierarchy in a cellview opened in Virtuoso Layout Suite EXL, the SKILL function creates a virtual group.

lxHiCreateInstFromSch.name: lxHiCreateInstFromSch
lxHiCreateInstFromSch.desc: Opens the Generate Selected Components form and starts the interactive command which lets you generate selected schematic components in the layout view. The function operates on the design in the specified window. If you do not specify a window, the function operates on the current window.

lxHiCreateMPP.name: lxHiCreateMPP
lxHiCreateMPP.desc: Opens the Create Multipart Path form, which you can use to specify the parameters for creating a multipart path, and starts the interactive command which lets you create a path in the layout window. The function operates on the design in the specified window. If you do not specify a window, the function operates on the design in the current window.

lxHiCreatePinsFromLabels.name: lxHiCreatePinsFromLabels
lxHiCreatePinsFromLabels.desc: Creates pins in the layout from labels for those schematic terminals that do not have a corresponding layout pin. Additionally, creates pins for terminals that already have pins but labels are swapped in the layout.

lxHiDefineDeviceCorr.name: lxHiDefineDeviceCorr
lxHiDefineDeviceCorr.desc: Opens the Define Device Correspondence form, which lets you bind schematic devices to layout devices.

lxHiEditComponentTypes.name: lxHiEditComponentTypes
lxHiEditComponentTypes.desc: Opens the Configure Physical Hierarchy window in Component Types mode, which lets you define component types and assign cells to them. The function operates on the design in the specified layout window. If you do not specify a layout window, it operates on the design in the current one; if there is no current layout window, the function exits.

lxHiGenerateSelectedFromLayout.name: lxHiGenerateSelectedFromLayout
lxHiGenerateSelectedFromLayout.desc: Starts the Generate Selected From Layout enter function, which lets you generate selected layout components in the corresponding schematic cellview. The layout window from which the components are selected is specified. If the layout window is not specified, the function operates on the current window.

lxHiIChain.name: lxHiIChain
lxHiIChain.desc: Starts the enter function available through the shortcut menu of selected instances, pins, or a group of abutted instances to support incremental interactive chaining. The selected instances, pins, or a single group of abutted objects are considered as anchors to start the chain and the subsequent user-specified points are then used to interactively chain the instances and top-level pins until the Esc key is pressed to stop the function.

lxHiLockSelected.name: lxHiLockSelected
lxHiLockSelected.desc: Sets the placement status of the currently selected objects to locked. Each object is locked at its current location and orientation in the layout view.

lxHiMoveAutomatically.name: lxHiMoveAutomatically
lxHiMoveAutomatically.desc: Runs the Place As In Schematic command, which moves all of the components into the design boundary, maintaining the relative positions of the components in the schematic. If there is no connectivity reference, the Update Connectivity Reference form is opened.

lxHiProbe.name: lxHiProbe
lxHiProbe.desc: Opens the Probe Options form and starts the XL Probe command, which lets you select a component in either the layout or schematic and highlights the corresponding component the other cellview of the pair.

lxHiReInitDesign.name: lxHiReInitDesign
lxHiReInitDesign.desc: Opens the Generate Layout form, which you can use to specify which layout components are to be generated from the schematic cellview, or clears the existing layout cellview so that you can restart.

lxHiSetOptions.name: lxHiSetOptions
lxHiSetOptions.desc: Opens the Connectivity form. The form opens with the General tab on top, unless you specify a different tab using the optional argument.

lxHiStack.name: lxHiStack
lxHiStack.desc: Opens the Generate Folded Devices form and starts the Generate Folded Devices command, which lets you fold a single transistor or an abutted group of MOS transistors into two or more fingers. The command operates on the design in the specified window. If you do not specify a window, it operates on the design in the current window.

lxHiSwap.name: lxHiSwap
lxHiSwap.desc: Swaps instances and figGroups by launching the Swapping Components command. You can pre-select, partial-select, or post-select instances and figGroups. You can use the function to swap by origin with an option to swap with transform, or you can select one of the nine points on a bounding box: lower-left, center-left, upper-left, lower-center, center-center, upper-center, lower-right, center-right, or upper-right.

lxHiUnlockSelected.name: lxHiUnlockSelected
lxHiUnlockSelected.desc: Changes the placement status of the selected objects from locked, placed, or firm to unplaced.If the original placement status is unknown or unplaced, this command does not change it.

lxHiUpdateAllTerminalInterfaces.name: lxHiUpdateAllTerminalInterfaces
lxHiUpdateAllTerminalInterfaces.desc: Updates the scalar terminals in the currently edited layout cellview to correct mismatches in the interface or physical-only status.

lxHiUpdateBusTerminals.name: lxHiUpdateBusTerminals
lxHiUpdateBusTerminals.desc: Updates the implicit bus terminals in the layout cellview based on the corresponding explicit bus terminals in the schematic cellview. The update is important to support interoperability of the layout cellviews with the designs created using the Innovus Implementation System.

lxHiUpdateCellViewPair.name: lxHiUpdateCellViewPair
lxHiUpdateCellViewPair.syntax:
lxHiUpdateCellViewPair(
[ d_cellviewID ]
)
=> ( { t_source t_lib t_cell t_view [ t_topcell ] | nil } )
lxHiUpdateCellViewPair.desc: Starts the Update Connectivity Reference command and opens the Update Connectivity Reference form, where you can specify which schematic view provides the connectivity source for the specified layout view. If you do not specify a layout cellview, the function uses the current layout cellview.

lxHiUpdateComponentsAndNets.name: lxHiUpdateComponentsAndNets
lxHiUpdateComponentsAndNets.desc: Starts the Update Components and Nets command, which lets you update the devices and pins in the layout view based on the devices in the schematic cellview.

lxHiUpdateLayoutConstraints.name: lxHiUpdateLayoutConstraints
lxHiUpdateLayoutConstraints.desc: Runs the Update Layout Constraints command, which transfers constraints from the schematic view to the layout view. Constraints that have been created in the schematic but not yet saved are also transferred. Constraints are transferred only to the top-level layout view and are made read-only.

lxHiUpdateLayoutParameters.name: lxHiUpdateLayoutParameters
lxHiUpdateLayoutParameters.desc: Starts the Update Layout Parameters command, which updates the parameters and values in the layout view to match those set in the schematic view.

lxHiUpdateSchematicParameters.name: lxHiUpdateSchematicParameters
lxHiUpdateSchematicParameters.desc: Starts the Update Schematic Parameters command, which updates the parameters and values in the schematic view to match those set in the layout view.

lxHiUpdateTerminalNetExpressions.name: lxHiUpdateTerminalNetExpressions
lxHiUpdateTerminalNetExpressions.desc: Corrects mismatches in the terminal net expressions between layout and schematic reported by the Check Against Source command.

lxHiVerifyDesign.name: lxHiVerifyDesign
lxHiVerifyDesign.desc: Starts the Check Against Source command and opens the Check Against Source dialog where you can specify how Layout XL is to check the current layout implementation against corresponding schematic view. When you accept the dialog, the command checks the schematic cellview for any changes made since the layout cellview was last changed. It also opens an Info window detailing the differences between the views.

lxIsGroupArray.name: lxIsGroupArray
lxIsGroupArray.desc: Checks whether the given object is a group array.

lxIsGroupArrayEnabled.name: lxIsGroupArrayEnabled
lxIsGroupArrayEnabled.desc: Checks whether the group array functionality is available.

lxIsGroupArrayLocked.name: lxIsGroupArrayLocked
lxIsGroupArrayLocked.desc: Checks whether the given group array is locked.

lxIsGroupArrayRegular.name: lxIsGroupArrayRegular
lxIsGroupArrayRegular.desc: Checks whether the given group array is a regular group array. For a regular group array, the number of cells can be modified by updating the number of rows or columns. For a non-regular group array, the number of cells is fixed.

lxHiPRBoundaryInteriorHalo.name: lxHiPRBoundaryInteriorHalo
lxHiPRBoundaryInteriorHalo.desc: Displays an options form to specify if and on which layer a PR boundary interior halo shape should be created during when the Generate All From Source command is run.

lxLaunchLayoutEXL.name: lxLaunchLayoutEXL
lxLaunchLayoutEXL.desc: Launches Layout EXL from a specified schematic window. If you do not specify a window ID, Layout EXL is launched from the window returned by the hiGetCurrentWindow() function, but only if it is a schematic window.

lxLaunchLayoutXL.name: lxLaunchLayoutXL
lxLaunchLayoutXL.desc: Launches Layout XL from a specified schematic window. If you do not specify a window ID, Layout XL is launched from the window returned by the hiGetCurrentWindow() function, but only if it is a schematic window.

lxLaunchLayoutMXL.name: lxLaunchLayoutMXL
lxLaunchLayoutMXL.desc: Launches Layout MXL from a specified schematic window. If you do not specify a window ID, Layout MXL is launched from the window returned by the hiGetCurrentWindow() function, but only if it is a schematic window.

lxMakeDummy.name: lxMakeDummy
lxMakeDummy.desc: Starts the Make Dummy enter function for the selected set of instances which can include mosaics. The function requires a reference point and a position for the created dummy devices. The dummy devices are tied to the named net passed in via netName.

lxMakePrBoundarySelectable.name: lxMakePrBoundarySelectable
lxMakePrBoundarySelectable.desc: Makes the place and route boundary in the current layout selectable.

lxMakePrBoundaryUnselectable.name: lxMakePrBoundaryUnselectable
lxMakePrBoundaryUnselectable.desc: Makes the place and route boundary in the current layout unselectable.

lxPermPermutePins.name: lxPermPermutePins
lxPermPermutePins.desc: Starts the Permute Pins command, which lets you swap the connectivity or net connections of the pins of a component. You specify the pins you want to permute by selecting them when prompted by the function. The pins to be permuted must belong to different nets and must first be defined as permutable terminals using the permuteRule property for the device.

lxProbeRemoveAll.name: lxProbeRemoveAll
lxProbeRemoveAll.desc: Removes all probes from the layout cellview.

lxRegPostUpdateComponentsAndNets.name: lxRegPostUpdateComponentsAndNets
lxRegPostUpdateComponentsAndNets.desc: Registers a SKILL function to be used as a post-function hook for lxUpdateComponentsAndNets to enable replacement of pins that have their layer and width characteristics defined using the Design Intent tool. lxRegPostUpdateComponentsAndNetsFn, when used in combination with lxRegPostUpdateComponentsAndNetsFn, avoids the need for deleting the pins defined in Design Intent before the pins can be updated.

lxRegPrePosition.name: lxRegPrePosition
lxRegPrePosition.syntax:
lxRegPrePosition(
t_lib
t_cell
t_view
s_skillFunction 
)
=> t / nil
lxRegPrePosition.desc:
