Registers a SKILL function for a schematic Pcell to be called for newly generated layout instances corresponding to each instance of the schematic Pcell when Generate All From Source, Generate Selected from Source, or Update Components and Nets commands are run. Registration is done once before generation. The registered SKILL function is called after instance generation but before positioning.

Only one SKILL function can be registered per schematic Pcell.

lxRegPreUpdateComponentsAndNets.name: lxRegPreUpdateComponentsAndNets
lxRegPreUpdateComponentsAndNets.desc: Registers a SKILL function to be used as a pre-function hook for lxUpdateComponentsAndNets to enable replacement of pins that have their layer and width characteristics defined using the Design Intent tool. lxRegPreUpdateComponentsAndNetsFn, when used in combination with lxRegPostUpdateComponentsAndNetsFn, avoids the need for deleting the pins defined in Design Intent before the pins can be updated.

lxRemoveSynchronousCloneFromFamily.name: lxRemoveSynchronousCloneFromFamily
lxRemoveSynchronousCloneFromFamily.desc: Removes a specified synchronous clone from its family. As a result, the clone is desynchronized and it behaves as a basic group. If a clone that belongs to a two-member synchronous family is removed from the family, the other member clone is also removed and the family is deleted.

lxRunCmdInVXL.name: lxRunCmdInVXL
lxRunCmdInVXL.syntax:
lxRunCmdInVXL(
d_layCV 
u_cmd 
g_cmdArgs 
[ ?schCV d_schCV ]
)
=> t / nil
lxRunCmdInVXL.desc: This function is being maintained only to support backward compatibility. Cadence recommends that you use lxRunCmdInXL instead. If you were to use lxRunCmdInVXL, use it to run a user-supplied command in Layout XL, with CPH and the Binder enabled, without opening the windows. The PhysConfig used is obtained from the layout cellview. If you want to work in Automatic mode, the schematic cellview, an optional argument, is required. The batch function does not work with the following: Interactive editing, Incremental binding, and Incremental extraction.

lxRunCmdInXL.name: lxRunCmdInXL
lxRunCmdInXL.syntax:
lxRunCmdInXL(
d_layCV 
u_cmd 
[ ?cmdArgs g_cmdArgs ] 
[ ?hierarchical {t | nil} ]
[ ?editLayout {t | nil} ]
[ ?editSchematic {t | nil} ]
[ ?skipLeafs {t | nil} ]
[ ?noSchematic {t | nil} ]
)
=> t / nil
lxRunCmdInXL.desc: Runs a user-defined command in Layout XL in the current layout or for each unique layout master in the specified layout cellviews hierarchy. When the lxRunCmdInXL SKILL function is run, the CPH and the binder are enabled, but no windows open. The physConfig and the schematic connectivity reference is obtained from the layout cellviews by setting the SKILL functions lxSetConnRef and lxSetConfigRef. The lxRunCmdInXL function does not support the following commands: interactive edits, incremental binding, and incremental extraction. The user-supplied command must have at least two arguments-the schematic cellview ID and the layout cellview ID for the Layout XL session.

lxSelectedDeleteNetRouting.name: lxSelectedDeleteNetRouting
lxSelectedDeleteNetRouting.desc: Deletes routing of the selected nets.

lxSelectedExtendChain.name: lxSelectedExtendChain
lxSelectedExtendChain.desc: Extends the current selection to all the instances abutted to a selected instance such that the entire chain is selected.

lxSelectedExtendExpanded.name: lxSelectedExtendExpanded
lxSelectedExtendExpanded.desc: Extends the current selection to any related instances, terminals, and nets.

lxSelectedExtendSchematic.name: lxSelectedExtendSchematic
lxSelectedExtendSchematic.desc: Extends the current selection of instances to include any instances that are part of the bound top-level schematic.

lxSelectedLock.name: lxSelectedLock
lxSelectedLock.desc: Locks the nets currently selected in the layout cellview.

lxSelectedLockNet.name: lxSelectedLockNet
lxSelectedLockNet.desc: Locks the nets attached to the shapes currently selected in the layout cellview

lxSelectedRemoveIgnore.name: lxSelectedRemoveIgnore
lxSelectedRemoveIgnore.desc: Removes the ignore property on selected instances and pins.

lxSelectedRoute.name: lxSelectedRoute
lxSelectedRoute.desc: Routes the nets currently selected in the layout cellview.

lxSelectedRouteNet.name: lxSelectedRouteNet
lxSelectedRouteNet.desc: Routes the nets attached to the shapes currently selected in the layout cellview.

lxSelectedSelectAttachedGlobalNets.name: lxSelectedSelectAttachedGlobalNets
lxSelectedSelectAttachedGlobalNets.desc: Selects the power, ground, or global nets attached to the objects currently selected in the layout cellview.

lxSelectedSelectAttachedNets.name: lxSelectedSelectAttachedNets
lxSelectedSelectAttachedNets.desc: Selects the nets attached to the objects currently selected in the layout cellview.

lxSelectedSelectAttachedSignalNets.name: lxSelectedSelectAttachedSignalNets
lxSelectedSelectAttachedSignalNets.desc: Selects nets other than power, ground, or global nets attached to the objects currently selected in the layout cellview.

lxSelectedSelectExternalGlobalNets.name: lxSelectedSelectExternalGlobalNets
lxSelectedSelectExternalGlobalNets.desc: Selects any power, ground, or global nets that are externally connected to the groups, clones, or modgens currently selected in the layout cellview. An external net connects an object within a group to an object outside the group.

lxSelectedSelectExternalNets.name: lxSelectedSelectExternalNets
lxSelectedSelectExternalNets.desc: Selects the external nets for the groups, clones, or modgens currently selected in the layout cellview. An external net connects an object within a group to an object outside the group.

lxSelectedSelectExternalSignalNets.name: lxSelectedSelectExternalSignalNets
lxSelectedSelectExternalSignalNets.desc: Selects any nets other than power, ground, or global nets that are externally connected to the groups, clones, or modgens currently selected in the layout cellview. An external net connects an object within a group to an object outside the group.

lxSelectedSelectInternalGlobalNets.name: lxSelectedSelectInternalGlobalNets
lxSelectedSelectInternalGlobalNets.desc: Selects any power, ground, or global nets that are internal to the groups, clones, or modgens currently selected in the layout view. An internal net connects objects contained within a group.

lxSelectedSelectInternalNets.name: lxSelectedSelectInternalNets
lxSelectedSelectInternalNets.desc: Selects the internal nets for the groups, clones, or modgens currently selected in the layout view. An internal net connects objects contained within a group.

lxSelectedSelectInternalSignalNets.name: lxSelectedSelectInternalSignalNets
lxSelectedSelectInternalSignalNets.desc: Selects any nets other than power, ground, or global nets that are internal to the groups, clones, or modgens currently selected in the layout view. An internal net connects objects contained within a group.

lxSelectedSelectNetsShapes.name: lxSelectedSelectNetsShapes
lxSelectedSelectNetsShapes.desc: Selects all the shapes attached to the nets currently selected in the layout cellview.

lxSelectedUnlock.name: lxSelectedUnlock
lxSelectedUnlock.desc: Unlocks the nets currently selected in the layout cellview.

lxSelectedUnlockNet.name: lxSelectedUnlockNet
lxSelectedUnlockNet.desc: Unlocks the nets attached to the shapes currently selected in the layout cellview.

lxSelectedUpdateFromSource.name: lxSelectedUpdateFromSource
lxSelectedUpdateFromSource.desc: Updates the masters, connectivity, and parameters of the instances currently selected in the layout cellview.

lxSelectedUpdateIgnore.name: lxSelectedUpdateIgnore
lxSelectedUpdateIgnore.desc: Sets the ignore property on selected instances and pins.

lxSelectSynchronousFamily.name: lxSelectSynchronousFamily
lxSelectSynchronousFamily.desc: Selects all the clones in the layout canvas and the Navigator that are members of the specified clone family. If all the family members are already selected, no more clones are selected on the canvas or in the Navigator. If any new clones are identified, they are selected on the canvas and in the Navigator.

lxSetAreaEstimationOptions.name: lxSetAreaEstimationOptions
lxSetAreaEstimationOptions.syntax:
lxSetAreaEstimationOptions(
[ ?source1 t_source1 ]
[ ?source1Val source1Val ]
[ ?source2 t_source2 ]
[ ?source2Val source2Val ]
[ ?calcMethod t_calcMethod ]
[ ?areaCalc t_areaCalc ]
)
=> t / nil
lxSetAreaEstimationOptions.desc: Sets the area estimation options to be used in generating a rectangular boundary in either the Generate Layout or Update Components and Nets form. The function is valid only if you specify a rectangular boundary using the lxSetBoundaryOptions function. It must be called between calls to lxGenerateStart and lxGenerateFinish or lxUpdateComponentsAndNetsStart and lxUpdateComponentsAndNetsFinish.

lxSetBoundaryOptions.name: lxSetBoundaryOptions
lxSetBoundaryOptions.syntax:
lxSetBoundaryOptions(
[ ?shape t_shape ]
[ ?origin g_origin ]
[ ?points lg_points ]
)
=> t / nil
lxSetBoundaryOptions.desc: Sets the boundary options in the Generate Layout and Update Components and Nets forms. It must be called between calls to lxGenerateStart and lxGenerateFinish or lxUpdateComponentsAndNetsStart and lxUpdateComponentsAndNetsFinish.

lxSetCloneFamilyName.name: lxSetCloneFamilyName
lxSetCloneFamilyName.desc: Sets a new name for the family to which the specified clone belongs.

lxSetConfigRef.name: lxSetConfigRef
lxSetConfigRef.syntax:
lxSetConfigRef(
t_layLib 
t_layCell
t_layView 
t_referenceType
[ ?cfgLib t_cfgLib ]
[ ?cfgCell t_cfgCell ]
[ ?cfgView t_cfgView ]
[ ?closeLay g_closeLay  ]
)
=> t / nil
lxSetConfigRef.desc: Sets or unsets the physical configuration cellview for a specified layout cellview. You specify the layout cellview in question and whether the reference type is NONE or physConfig. If the reference type is physConfig, specify the library, cell, and view names of the physical configuration to use.

lxSetConnRef.name: lxSetConnRef
lxSetConnRef.syntax:
lxSetConnRef(
t_layLib 
t_layCell
t_layView 
t_sourceType { CELLVIEW | NONE }
[ ?schLib t_schLib ]
[ ?schCell t_schCell ]
[ ?schView t_schView ]
[ ?closeLay g_closeLay ]
)
=> t / nil
lxSetConnRef.desc: Sets or unsets the connectivity reference for a specified layout cellview without opening the layout view graphically. You must specify the layout view and whether the source type is NONE or CELLVIEW. If the source type is CELLVIEW, you can specify the schematic cellview to use (by default it is set to the schematic view in the same library and cell). The function also saves the layout cellview, but only if had not been modified prior to lxSetConnRef being called.

lxSetGenerateOptions.name: lxSetGenerateOptions
lxSetGenerateOptions.syntax:
lxSetGenerateOptions(
[ ?pins { t | nil } ]
[ ?instances { t | nil } ]
[ ?boundary { t | nil } ]
[ ?snapBoundary { t | nil } ]
[ ?stacks { t | nil } ]
[ ?folds { t | nil } ]
[ ?posMinSep n_posMinSep ]
[ ?inBoundary { t | nil } ]
[ ?mtm { t | nil } ]
[ ?extract { t | nil } ]
[ ?virtualHierarchy { t | nil } ]
)
=> t
lxSetGenerateOptions.desc: Tells Generate All From Source or Update Components And Nets what types of objects to generate. You can call it between calls to lxGenerateStart and lxGenerateFinish or lxUpdateComponentsAndNetsStart and lxUpdateComponentsAndNetsFinish.

lxSetGroupArrayLocked.name: lxSetGroupArrayLocked
lxSetGroupArrayLocked.desc: Sets the lock attribute on the given group array. If a group array is locked, its X and Y spacing attributes cannot be modified.

lxSetGroupArrayRegular.name: lxSetGroupArrayRegular
lxSetGroupArrayRegular.desc: Sets the given group array as regular. For a regular group array, the number of cells can be modified by updating the number of rows or columns. For a non-regular group array, the number of cells is fixed.

lxSetNetPinSpecs.name: lxSetNetPinSpecs
lxSetNetPinSpecs.syntax:
lxSetNetPinSpecs(
[ ?nets lt_nets ]
[ ?lpp lt_lpp ]
[ ?width n_width ]
[ ?height n_height ]
[ ?numPins x_numPins ]
[ ?create g_create ]
)
=> t / nil
lxSetNetPinSpecs.desc: Takes a list of nets and with the specified parameters sets the pin information in either the Generate Layout or Update Components and Nets form. This function must always be called between calls to lxGenerateStart and lxGenerateFinish or lxUpdateComponentsAndNetsStart and lxUpdateComponentsAndNetsFinish. If optional arguments are not supplied the normal default values for the form fields apply.

lxSetPreserveFloorplanningOptions.name: lxSetPreserveFloorplanningOptions
lxSetPreserveFloorplanningOptions.syntax:
lxSetPreserveFloorplanningOptions(
[ ?preserve { all | none } ]
[ ?rows { t | nil } ]
[ ?blockages { t | nil } ]
[ ?areaBoundaries { t | nil } ]
[ ?trackPatterns { t | nil } ]
[ ?clusters { t | nil } ]
[ ?clusterBoundaries { t | nil } ]
[ ?prBoundary { t | nil} 
[ ?snapBoundary { t | nil } ]
[ ?snapPatterns { t | nil } ]
)
=> t / nil
lxSetPreserveFloorplanningOptions.desc: Sets the preserve floorplanning objects options in the Generate Layout form. This function must be called between calls to lxGenerateStart and lxGenerateFinish.

lxSetSchematicDriven.name: lxSetSchematicDriven
lxSetSchematicDriven.desc: Sets the various schematic-driven options that are controlled by the Configure tab on the Virtuoso Layout Suite XL Connectivity form. The SKILL function can be used to control the following environment variables: lxSchematicDefaultApp, openConnRefTab, extractEnabled, constraintAwareEditing, flightLineEnable, autoUpdateFlightlines, netNameDisplayEnabled.

lxSetUpdateOptions.name: lxSetUpdateOptions
lxSetUpdateOptions.syntax:
lxSetUpdateOptions(
[ ?deletePins { t | nil } ]
[ ?deleteInstances { t | nil } ]
[ ?replaceMaster { t | nil } ]
[ ?withMarkers { t | nil } ]
[ ?netsOnly { t | nil } ]
[ ?selected nil { t | nil } ]
[ ?layoutParameters { t | nil } ]
[ ?layoutConstraints { t | nil } ]
[ ?sigType { t | nil } ]
[ ?netVoltage { t | nil } ]
)
=> t / nil
lxSetUpdateOptions.desc: Sets the options in the Update group box of the Update Components and Nets form. It must be called between calls to lxUpdateComponentsAndNetsStart and lxUpdateComponentsAndNetsFinish.

lxShapeSlotting.name: lxShapeSlotting
lxShapeSlotting.syntax:
lxShapeSlotting( 
[ ?cv d_cellViewId ] 
[ ?all { t | nil } ]
[ ?region l_region ]
[ ?layers l_layers 
[ ?widthThreshold n_widthThreshold ]
[ ?slotLength n_slotLength ]
[ ?slotWidth n_slotWidth ]
[ ?lSpacing n_lSpacing ]
[ ?wSpacing n_wSpacing ]
[ ?slotToEdge n_slotToEdge ]
[ ?slotVia { t | nil } ]
[ ?windowSize n_windowSize ]
[ ?stepSize n_stepSize ]
[ ?maxDensity n_maxDensity ]
[ ?slotStaggered { t | nil } ]
[ ?lengthWidthRatio n_lengthWidthRatio ]
[ ?excludePins { t | nil } ]
[ ?slotSpacingAtTurn n_slotSpacingAtTurn ]
[ ?onlyComplexPolygons { t | nil }
[ ?halfManhattan { t | nil } ]
[ ?halfManhattanStyle l_halfManhattanStyle ]
[ ?directionalSlotPattern l_directionalSlotPattern ]
[ ?shapes l_shapes ]
[ ?turnSlotPattern l_turnSlotPattern ]
) 
=> t / nil
lxShapeSlotting.desc: Creates slots on shapes to ensure that wide wires are in compliance with maxDensity and maxWidth constraint rules. It also preserves viable electromigration and resistance attributes by creating rectangular slots in the direction of the current over the wires and square slots at turns (same layer or changed layer). There are two modes depending on the arguments specified: Geometric and Density Aware. In Geometric mode, the slotting shapes are fully specified (size, spacing, and step size), while in Density Aware mode, the slotting shape geometries are automatically computed based on the maxDensity specification. Also, in Geometric mode, you can create slots on shapes on non-metal layers. It is still possible to override any of the geometric information, such as the width, length, or spacing.

lxShowCommonIncompleteNetsForSelectedIns.name: lxShowCommonIncompleteNetsForSelectedInsts
lxShowCommonIncompleteNetsForSelectedIns.desc: Runs the Enter function named Show Common Incomplete Nets for Selected Instances, which displays the incomplete nets that are common to the instances selected in the layout. The SKILL function can also be run in pre-select mode on the set of instances that are already selected in the layout. The post-selection mode is supported when only one instance is pre-selected.

lxShowHideIncompleteNets.name: lxShowHideIncompleteNets
lxShowHideIncompleteNets.desc: Shows and hides any incomplete nets associated with selected objects in the specified layout window. The function establishes the incomplete nets associated with the selected objects and toggles the visibility of the markers representing those incomplete nets on or off depending on their previous state.

lxToggleLocalAbutment.name: lxToggleLocalAbutment
lxToggleLocalAbutment.desc: Changes the state of the lxLocalAbutment environment variable and honors the change immediately in Layout XL. Use this function to switch local abutment on and off without having to restart the software.

lxToggleShowAllIncompleteNets.name: lxToggleShowAllIncompleteNets
lxToggleShowAllIncompleteNets.desc: Toggles the visibility of all the incomplete nets displayed in the design canvas.

lxToggleShowIncompleteNets.name: lxToggleShowIncompleteNets
lxToggleShowIncompleteNets.desc: Toggles the visibility of the current set of incomplete nets displayed in the design canvas. The first time you run the command, it hides all currently visible incomplete nets and stores the list of incomplete nets for later retrieval. The next time you run the command, it restores the visibility of the stored set of incomplete nets.

lxUnfold.name: lxUnfold
lxUnfold.desc: Deletes all the folds of the selected folded device and creates a single, unfolded device at the same coordinates in the layout as the selected fold. The width of the new unfolded device is determined based on the width of the corresponding schematic device, if one exists. If the corresponding schematic device does not exist and the unfoldUseLayoutWidths environment variable is set to t, the sum of the fold widths is used to determine the total width of the unfolded device.

lxUnregMasterDiffName.name: lxUnregMasterDiffName
lxUnregMasterDiffName.desc: Unregisters the SKILL function used to return a name for a master difference reported by the Check Against Source command.

lxUnregPrePosition.name: lxUnregPrePosition
lxUnregPrePosition.desc: Unregisters the SKILL function previously registered using lxRefPrePosition for the specified schematic Pcell.

lxUnSlotVia.name: lxUnSlotVia
lxUnSlotVia.syntax:
lxUnSlotVia(
[ ?cv d_cellViewId ] 
[ ?all { t | nil } ]
[ ?region l_region ]
[ ?layers l_layers ]
) 
=> t / nil
lxUnSlotVia.desc: Restores the via that has been slotted by the command lxShapeSlotting.

lxUpdateAllPhysBinding.name: lxUpdateAllPhysBinding
lxUpdateAllPhysBinding.desc: Updates the physical bindings of all the instances in the specified layout cellview.

lxUpdateBinding.name: lxUpdateBinding
lxUpdateBinding.syntax:
lxUpdateBinding(
d_layCV
[ ?schCV d_schCV ]
[ ?nameOnly { t | nil } ]
[ ?currentLevel { t | nil } ]
[ ?extract { t | nil } ]
[ ?clearConn { t | nil } ]
[ ?extractStopLevel [0-32] ]
[ ?preserveUserBindings { t | nil } ]
[ ?preserveLayoutHierarchy { t | nil } ]
[ ?flattenLayoutCreate { Synchronized Family | Grouped Objects| Free Objects } ]
[ ?bindingFile t_fileName ]
[ ?crossRefFile t_fileName ]
[ ?extractedNetlistFile t_fileName ]
[ ?PVSRulesFile t_fileName ]
[ ?PVSScale n_PVSScale ]
[ ?correctMaster { t | nil } ]
[ ?ignoreRouteCells { t | nil } ]
[ ?ignoreDummies { t | nil } ]
[ ?preserveExistingBindings { t | nil } ]
[ ?hierarchical { t | nil } ]
[ ?allCellsInDesign { t | nil } ]
[ ?createTransparent { t | nil } ]
[ ?createPinsFromLabels { t | nil } ]
[ ?checkDuplicateObjects { t | nil } ]
[ ?removeDuplicateObjects { t | nil } ]
)
=> 0 - 100 / -1
lxUpdateBinding.desc: Improves the binding between the schematic and the layout by setting options that control how the connectivity, the manual bindings, and the design hierarchy is processed. If a log file name is specified for the hierSummaryLogFileName environment variable, the SKILL function prints the summary information to the specified log file, in addition to printing the information to the default Virtuoso log file

args.name: ?flattenLayoutCreate { Synchronized Family | Grouped Objects| Free Objects }

lxUpdateComponentsAndNets.name: lxUpdateComponentsAndNets
lxUpdateComponentsAndNets.syntax:
lxUpdateComponentsAndNets(
d_schCellViewID
d_layCellViewID
[ ?initCreatePins { t | nil } ]
[ ?initGlobalNetPins { t | nil } ]
[ ?initCreatePadPins { t | nil } ]
[ ?initCreateInstances { t | nil } ]
[ ?initCreateBoundary { t | nil } ]
[ ?initCreateSnapBoundary { t | nil } ]
[ ?initDoStacking { t | nil } ]
[ ?initDoFolding { t | nil } ]
[ ?initCreateMTM { t | nil } ]
[ ?deleteUnmatchedInsts { t | nil } ]
[ ?deleteUnmatchedPins { t | nil } ]
[ ?updateReplacesMasters { t | nil } ]
[ ?updateWithMarkers { t | nil } ]
[ ?updateLayoutParameters { t | nil } ]
[ ?updateNetSigType { t | nil } ]

[ ?updateNetsOnly { t | nil } ]
[ ?virtualHierarchy { t | nil } ]
[ ?extractSchematic { t | nil } ]
)
=> t / nil
lxUpdateComponentsAndNets.desc: Updates the components and nets for the specified schematic and layout cellviews. If you use the optional arguments, they override the existing environment variables set in the .cdsenv file. The default value for each optional argument corresponds to the default value of the associated environment variable.

lxUpdateComponentsAndNetsFinish.name: lxUpdateComponentsAndNetsFinish
lxUpdateComponentsAndNetsFinish.syntax:
lxUpdateComponentsAndNetsFinish(
d_schId
d_layId
[ ?extractSchematic { t | nil } ]
)
=> t / nil
lxUpdateComponentsAndNetsFinish.desc: Finishes the update process by executing the Update Components And Nets command with the form values supplied by lxSet* functions and after the previous call to lxUpdateComponentsAndNetsStart.

lxUpdateComponentsAndNetsStart.name: lxUpdateComponentsAndNetsStart
lxUpdateComponentsAndNetsStart.syntax:
lxUpdateComponentsAndNetsStart(
d_schId
d_layId
[ ?extractSchematic { t | nil } ]
)
=> t / nil
lxUpdateComponentsAndNetsStart.desc: Starts the Update Components And Nets command, building the Update Components and Nets form without displaying it to the screen.

lxUpdateGroupArrayParams.name: lxUpdateGroupArrayParams
lxUpdateGroupArrayParams.syntax:
lxUpdateGroupArrayParams(
d_groupArrayId
[ ?rows x_rows ]
[ ?columns x_cols ]
[ ?X x_xValue ]
[ ?Y x_yValue ]
[ ?orients l_orientList ]

[ ?lpp l_refLPP ]
)
=> t / nil
lxUpdateGroupArrayParams.desc: Updates the specified parameters of a group array.

lxUpdatePhysBinding.name: lxUpdatePhysBinding
lxUpdatePhysBinding.desc: Updates the physical bindings of the currently selected instances in the specified layout cellview.

lxUpdatePlacementStatus.name: lxUpdatePlacementStatus
lxUpdatePlacementStatus.desc: Updates the placement status of instances and pins in the current cellview. Instances and pins that are wholly inside the PR boundary with status unknown are updated to status placed. Instances and pins wholly outside the PR boundary with status placed are updated to unknown.

lxVerifyCloneFamily.name: lxVerifyCloneFamily
lxVerifyCloneFamily.desc: Runs a consistency check on the specified synchronous clone family to verify if the family members are identical to each other.

nclRunConstraintValidation.name: nclRunConstraintValidation
nclRunConstraintValidation.desc: Validates the constraints supported by constraint-aware editing mode in the specified cellview.

nclToggleCAEMode.name: nclToggleCAEMode
nclToggleCAEMode.desc: Toggles constraint-aware editing mode, which causes figures in the layout to move in a constraint-correct fashion. For example, moving a device that is part of a symmetry constraint moves its constrained partner devices appropriately.

soiEnableDrcDfm.name: soiEnableDrcDfm
soiEnableDrcDfm.desc: Enables the DRC/DFM tab in the Annotation Browser and the DRC/DFM commands in the Optimize menu in Layout XL.

techGetLxExtractLayers.name: techGetLxExtractLayers
techGetLxExtractLayers.desc: Returns the list of extract layers from the virtuosoDefaultExtractorSetup constraint group in the specified technology file. These layers are listed as validLayers in the interconnect subsection of the constraint group.

techGetLxNoOverlapLayers.name: techGetLxNoOverlapLayers
techGetLxNoOverlapLayers.desc: Lists the pairs of layers that cannot overlap.

techIsLxExtractLayer.name: techIsLxExtractLayer
techIsLxExtractLayer.desc: Indicates whether the specified layer is listed as an extract layer in the virtuosoDefaultExtractorSetup constraint group in the specified technology file. The extract layers are listed under validLayers in the interconnect subsection of the constraint group.

techIsLxNoOverlapLayer.name: techIsLxNoOverlapLayer
techIsLxNoOverlapLayer.syntax:
techIsLxNoOverlapLayer(
d_techFileID
tx_layer1
tx_layer2
)
=> t / nil
techIsLxNoOverlapLayer.desc: Indicates whether the specified pair of layers is a derived no overlap layer in the specified technology file. The order in which the layers is specified does not matter.

techSetLxExtractLayer.name: techSetLxExtractLayer
techSetLxExtractLayer.desc: Adds the specified layer to the list of extract layers in the virtuosoDefaultExtractorSetup constraint group in the specified technology file. The extract layers are listed under validLayers in the interconnect subsection of the constraint group. If any of the necessary technology file sections do not already exist, this function creates them.

techSetLxExtractLayers.name: techSetLxExtractLayers
techSetLxExtractLayers.desc: Adds the specified layers to the list of extract layers in the virtuosoDefaultExtractorSetup constraint group in the specified technology file. The extract layers are listed under validLayers in the interconnect subsection of the constraint group. If any of the necessary technology file sections do not already exist, this function creates them.

techSetLxNoOverlapLayer.name: techSetLxNoOverlapLayer
techSetLxNoOverlapLayer.syntax:
techSetLxNoOverlapLayer(
d_techFileID
tx_layer1
tx_layer2
)
=> t / nil
techSetLxNoOverlapLayer.desc: Derives a no overlap layer by performing an AND operation on the two specified layers, and flags it as an error layer in the virtuosoDefaultExtractorSetup constraint group in the specified technology file. The derived layer is defined in the techDerivedLayers subsection in the layerDefinitions section of the technology file and is listed as an errorLayer in the interconnect subsection of the constraint group. No overlap layers are named and numbered consecutively; each is named noOverlapLayern, where n is the next available consecutive integer. If any of the necessary technology file sections does not already exist, the function creates them.

techSetLxNoOverlapLayers.name: techSetLxNoOverlapLayers
techSetLxNoOverlapLayers.desc: Creates a list of layers that cannot overlap. The function creates a derived layer by performing an AND operation on each pair of layers and flags the resultant layer as an error layer in the virtuosoDefaultExtractorSetup constraint group in the specified technology file. Each derived layer is defined in the techDerivedLayers subsection in the layerDefinitions section of the technology file and is listed as an errorLayer in the interconnect subsection of the constraint group.

tpoIsLayoutXL.name: tpoIsLayoutXL
tpoIsLayoutXL.desc: Checks if the specified window is open in Layout XL or a higher tier.

tpoIsLayoutEXL.name: tpoIsLayoutEXL
tpoIsLayoutEXL.desc: Checks if the specified window is open in Layout EXL or a higher tier.

vfoAbut.name: vfoAbut
vfoAbut.syntax:
vfoAbut(
g_obj
l_instsList
[ @rest l_args ]
)
=> t / nil
vfoAbut.desc:
Abuts the instances provided in the l_instList. You can pass optional arguments to this SKILL API.
Note: The Abut command does not call the vfoAbut function for fluid devices.

vfoAdvGRUpdateCDF.name: vfoAdvGRUpdateCDF
vfoAdvGRUpdateCDF.syntax:
vfoAdvGRUpdateCDF(
g_obj
t_libName
t_cellName
t_viewName
)
=> l_cdfParams
vfoAdvGRUpdateCDF.desc: Helps to modify the existing CDFs on a FGR device and add more CDFs on it. The function can be defined for subclasses of vfoAdvGuardRing. It works based on callback mechanism, that is, the user defines it and the infrastructure calls it.

vfoAllocateProtocolObj.name: vfoAllocateProtocolObj
vfoAllocateProtocolObj.desc: Allocates and returns the newly allocated and initialized instance of the vfo protocol class of the Pcell. You can use the vfoGetProtocolClassName SKILL function to determine the name of the protocol class.

vfoAllocateShapeData.name: vfoAllocateShapeData
vfoAllocateShapeData.desc: Returns a newly allocated and initialized instance of the subclass of the vfoShapeData  class for the specified database shape ID.

vfoChopInstance.name: vfoChopInstance
vfoChopInstance.syntax:
vfoChopInstance(
g_obj
d_instId
chopShapeData
[ @rest l_args ]
)
=> t / nil
vfoChopInstance.desc:
Chops the fluid shape of a given instance. The information of the chop rectangle or polygon is provided by chopShapeData which is a class object of vfoShapeData. The shape data points are in the design coordinates. This function transforms the chopShapeData before chopping the fluid shape.

Note: The Chop command for fluid Pcells does not pass these arguments. This function updates the relevant Pcell parameters. If the chop operation results in multiple shapes, it may need to create multiple Pcell instances.

vfoConvertToPolygon.name: vfoConvertToPolygon
vfoConvertToPolygon.syntax:
vfoConvertToPolygon( 
g_obj
d_instId
[ @rest l_args ]
) 
=> t / nil
vfoConvertToPolygon.desc: Converts the fluid shape of the given instance to a polygon. This is used for instances containing path type fluid shape. The Convert to Polygon command for fluid Pcells does not pass these arguments. This function updates the relevant Pcell parameters.

vfoCreateAutoFGR.name: vfoCreateAutoFGR
vfoCreateAutoFGR.desc: Wraps obstacles in wrap mode on clicking an obstacle if AUTO mode is selected in the Device field of the Create Guard Ring form. This function is used to specify the bindkey for creation of FGR in auto mode.

vfoCreateObstruction.name: vfoCreateObstruction
vfoCreateObstruction.syntax:
vfoCreateObstructions(
g_obj
d_instId
layerPurposePair
obstructionShapeData
[ @rest l_args ]
) 
=> t / nil
vfoCreateObstruction.desc:
Creates obstruction or tunnel on a given instance that has an associated fluid shape. A tunnel helps you to cut a specific layer-purpose of a guard ring device for connectivity purpose. There are four types of tunneling mechanisms-Path, Rectangle, Polygon, and Overlapping Shape. For procedural details about creating tunnels using GUI, refer to the Creating a Tunnel Through a Fluid Guard Ring section in the Editing Fluid Guard Rings chapter of the Virtuoso Fluid Guard Ring User Guide.

Note: To remove any existing obstructions, use the vfoDeleteObstruction SKILL function.

vfoCreateObstructions.name: vfoCreateObstructions
vfoCreateObstructions.syntax:
vfoCreateObstructions(
g_obj
d_instId
l_lppPoint
[ @rest l_args ]
) 
=> nil
vfoCreateObstructions.desc:
Creates obstruction or tunnel on a given instance that has an associated fluid shape. A tunnel helps you to cut a specific layer-purpose of a guard ring device for connectivity purpose. There are four types of tunneling mechanisms-Path, Rectangle, Polygon, and Overlapping Shape. For procedural details about creating tunnels using GUI, refer to the Creating a Tunnel Through a Fluid Guard Ring section in the Editing Fluid Guard Rings chapter of the Virtuoso Fluid Guard Ring User Guide.

Note: To remove any existing obstructions, use the vfoDeleteObstruction SKILL function.

vfoCreateShapeData.name: vfoCreateShapeData
vfoCreateShapeData.desc: Allocates, initializes, and returns an instance of the subclass of the vfoShapeData of the given shape type.

vfoDeleteObstruction.name: vfoDeleteObstruction
vfoDeleteObstruction.syntax:
vfoDeleteObstruction(
g_obj
d_instId
layerPurposePair
obstructionShapeData
[ @rest l_args ]
) 
=> t / nil
vfoDeleteObstruction.desc:
Deletes the obstruction or tunnel on a given instance that has an associated fluid shape. This SKILL function is equivalent to healing.

For procedural details about healing an obstruction using GUI, refer to the Healing a Fluid Guard Ring section in the Editing Fluid Guard Rings chapter of the Virtuoso Fluid Guard Ring User Guide.

Note: To create an obstruction, use the vfoCreateObstruction SKILL function.

vfoDoSnapToSnapPattern.name: vfoDoSnapToSnapPattern
vfoDoSnapToSnapPattern.desc: Snaps the fluid object to the snap pattern.

vfoDrawFluidShape.name: vfoDrawFluidShape
vfoDrawFluidShape.syntax:
vfoDrawFluidShape(
g_shapeObj
cellView
layerPurposePair
)
=> d_obj / nil
vfoDrawFluidShape.desc: Creates a dbObject corresponding to shapeData object in the given cellview on the given layer purpose pair.

vfoGetDeviceClassParam.name: vfoGetDeviceClassParam
vfoGetDeviceClassParam.syntax:
vfoGetDeviceClassParam( 
t_libName
t_deviceName
t_classParam
) 
=> value / nil
vfoGetDeviceClassParam.desc: Returns the class parameter of the specified cdsGuardRing device. This SKILL function also supports the incremental technology database (ITDB). Therefore, the information is retrieved for FGR devices in both the library and the referenced library.

vfoGetDeviceFormalParam.name: vfoGetDeviceFormalParam
vfoGetDeviceFormalParam.syntax:
vfoGetDeviceFormalParam( 
t_libName
t_deviceName
t_formalParam
) 
=> value / nil
vfoGetDeviceFormalParam.desc: Returns the implementation formal parameter of the specified cdsGuardRing device. This SKILL function also supports ITDB. Therefore, the information is retrieved for FGR devices in both the library and the referenced library.

vfoGetFileListWithLoadSequence.name: vfoGetFileListWithLoadSequence
vfoGetFileListWithLoadSequence.desc: Returns a list of vfo*.ils filenames with their loading sequence.

vfoGetImplementationClassName.name: vfoGetImplementationClassName
vfoGetImplementationClassName.desc: Returns the value of the vfoGRImpl class parameter, that is the implementation class name, of an FGR device from the specified library. This SKILL function also supports the incremental technology database (ITDB). Therefore, the information is retrieved for FGR devices in both the library and the referenced library.

vfoGetInstWithMissingCache.name: vfoGetInstWithMissingCache
vfoGetInstWithMissingCache.desc: Returns three lists of dbIDs. The first is the list of dbIDs of all instances whose submaster is not found in index.pcl file. The second is the list of dbIDs of all instances whose submaster is found in index.pcl file but not found in cache.pcl file because the file is corrupt or missing. The third is the list of dbIDs of instances whose submaster is not found because the supermaster has been updated after instance creation.

vfoGetParam.name: vfoGetParam
vfoGetParam.desc: Returns the value of a CDF parameter for the given object.

vfoGetProtocolClassName.name: vfoGetProtocolClassName
vfoGetProtocolClassName.desc: Returns the symbol naming the protocol class to use with the fluid Pcell functions.

vfoGetVersion.name: vfoGetVersion
vfoGetVersion.desc: Returns the version of the VFO SKILL code used in Virtuoso. This SKILL function is available from IC6.1.6 ISR2 and ICADV12.1 ISR4 onwards.

vfoGRCleanVersionCache.name: vfoGRCleanVersionCache
vfoGRCleanVersionCache.syntax:
vfoGRCleanVersionCache(
t_libName
[ ?cellName t_cellName ]
[ ?viewName t_viewName ]
)
=> t / nil
vfoGRCleanVersionCache.desc: Updates the index.pcl and cache.pcl files by removing any unused entries of sub-masters from these files. This is an alternative to cleaning the cache if you have disabled the automatic FGR cache cleaning mechanism described in the Automatic Cache Cleaning section, or even if the Automatic Cache Cleaning mechanism is enabled by you and would like to clean the FGR caches on-demand.

vfoGRCompareParams.name: vfoGRCompareParams
vfoGRCompareParams.syntax:
vfoGRCompareParams(
g_obj
d_inst1
d_inst2
) 
=> t / nil
vfoGRCompareParams.desc: Checks the equality of FGR instances. You override this function and can define its new  equality for FGR instances. By default, it checks the value of the following parameters: verticalPitch, horizontalPitch, verticalSegWidth, and horizontalSegWidth. This function is called by the Merge command. For the Merge command to succeed, this function should return t for the two FGR instances being compared.

vfoGrCreateCDF.name: vfoGrCreateCDF
vfoGrCreateCDF.desc: Creates fluid guard ring CDF parameters on the given library, cell view of the fluid guard ring device. It deletes any existing CDF parameters on the device.

vfoGRCreateDeviceClass.name: vfoGRCreateDeviceClass
vfoGRCreateDeviceClass.desc: Creates the device class definition for fluid guard ring (cdsGuardRing) in the given technology file. If the device class already exists in the technology file, it is updated when override is set to true.

vfoGRDisableVersionCache.name: vfoGRDisableVersionCache
vfoGRDisableVersionCache.syntax:
vfoGRDisableVersionCache(
l_FGRcellDDID
t_libName
[ ?cellName t_cellName ]
[ ?viewName t_viewName ]
)
=> t / nil
vfoGRDisableVersionCache.desc: Disables version cache for all instances that belong to the specified super-master list and found in the specified library, cell, or view. All instances are updated and the value of their createVersionCache parameter is set to 0.

vfoGREnableVersionCache.name: vfoGREnableVersionCache
vfoGREnableVersionCache.syntax:
vfoGREnableVersionCache(
l_FGRcellDDID
t_libName
[ ?cellName t_cellName ]
[ ?viewName t_viewName ]
)
=> t / nil
vfoGREnableVersionCache.desc: Enables version cache on all instances currently not cache-enabled that belong to the specified list of FGR super-masters and found in the in the specified library, cell, or view. The createVersionCache parameter of such instances will get updated from 0 to the VFO version of the current Virtuoso session.

vfoGRGetCreateFormFieldProp.name: vfoGRGetCreateFormFieldProp
vfoGRGetCreateFormFieldProp.desc: Gets the value of a property assigned to an existing field or GUI component displayed on the Create Guard Ring form.

vfoGRGetCreateFormIdentifier.name: vfoGRGetCreateFormIdentifier
vfoGRGetCreateFormIdentifier.desc: Returns the unique identifier string used for creating the Create Guard Ring form.

vfoGRGetCreateFormPointer.name: vfoGRGetCreateFormPointer
vfoGRGetCreateFormPointer.desc: Returns the form pointer corresponding to the unique identifier that creates the Create Guard Ring form.

vfoGRGetCommonQPtr.name: vfoGRGetCommonQPtr
vfoGRGetCommonQPtr.desc: Returns the common queue pointer of the Create Guard Ring form customized by you.

vfoGRGetExtraArgument.name: vfoGRGetExtraArgument
vfoGRGetExtraArgument.desc: Retrieves the value of user-defined fields, that is, list of `key value' pair set using the vfoGRSetExtraArgument SKILL function.

vfoGRGetExtraArgumentName.name: vfoGRGetExtraArgumentName
vfoGRGetExtraArgumentName.desc: Returns the extra parameter names in a list. The end user should override this function for its class that has been extended from vfoAdvGuardRing.

vfoGRGetQueuePointer.name: vfoGRGetQueuePointer
vfoGRGetQueuePointer.desc: Returns the pointer corresponding to the name of the queue of the customized Create Guard Ring form.

vfoGRGeometry.name: vfoGRGeometry
vfoGRGeometry.desc:
Calls three generic functions in the following order: vfoSfInitialize(pcell), vfoSfDraw(pcell), and then vfoSfFinalize(pcell) for drawing the fluid Pcell geometry.

NOTE: This is the top-level entry point to the vfo space-filling Pcell.

vfoGRMaximizeShapes.name: vfoGRMaximizeShapes
vfoGRMaximizeShapes.desc: Tries all possible combinations of fillStyle and decompositionMode to find the combination that maximizes the number of shapes, and thereby the number of contact cuts.

vfoGRNewCreateForm.name: vfoGRNewCreateForm
vfoGRNewCreateForm.syntax:
vfoGRNewCreateForm(
t_uniqueFormIdentifier
t_formType
[ l_callbackList ]
) 
=> r_formPointer / nil
vfoGRNewCreateForm.desc: Creates the new Create Guard Ring form, that is, a new form pointer along with the unique fields and form symbol.

vfoGRRegCreateFormUpdateCallback.name: vfoGRRegCreateFormUpdateCallback
vfoGRRegCreateFormUpdateCallback.desc: Registers the user-defined form customization procedure. This procedure gets called for the particular form pointer after the vfoGRUpdateCreateForm trigger is called.

vfoGRSetCreateFormAllFieldsInvisible.name: vfoGRSetCreateFormAllFieldsInvisible
vfoGRSetCreateFormAllFieldsInvisible.desc: Sets the visible property for the predefined system fields, except the Technology and Device fields, on the Create Guard Ring form. This function cannot be used to set the properties of fields that you add while customizing the Create Guard Ring form.

vfoGRSetCreateFormFieldProp.name: vfoGRSetCreateFormFieldProp
vfoGRSetCreateFormFieldProp.desc: Sets the properties of the fields or components displayed on the Create Guard Ring form.

vfoGRSetExtraArgument.name: vfoGRSetExtraArgument
vfoGRSetExtraArgument.desc: Makes the values of the user-defined GUI components available for processing to the FGR infrastructure that resides in Virtuoso, and sets the corresponding CDF parameters. This SKILL function helps in binding the front-end data for back-end processing.

vfoGRSmoothen.name: vfoGRSmoothen
vfoGRSmoothen.desc: Removes the small notches in the given direction from the fluid shape of the given fluid Pcell instance. The temporary shapes are created on tmpLpp.

vfoGRUpdateCreateFormSize.name: vfoGRUpdateCreateFormSize
vfoGRUpdateCreateFormSize.desc: Resizes the Create Guard Ring forms, including the form used for modgens. This function updates the size of all tabs and subtabs proportionately. However, there is no change in the size of the fields on the form.

vfoGRUpdateTunnelLPPs.name: vfoGRUpdateTunnelLPPs
vfoGRUpdateTunnelLPPs.desc: Returns the layer-purpose pairs on which tunnelling is allowed. The VFO infrastructure selects common layer-purpose present in the FGR and LPPs returned by the function vfoGRUpdateTunnelLPPs. If the function vfoGRUpdateTunnelLLPs returns nil, all FGR layer-purposes are displayed on the Create Tunnel in Fluid Object form.

vfoGRUpdateTunnelOptions.name: vfoGRUpdateTunnelOptions
vfoGRUpdateTunnelOptions.desc: Returns the list of supported options for FGR tunnel shape types. VFO infrastructure uses options returned by this function and checks with the existing options. The first value returned by this function is selected by default when the Create Tunnel in Fluid Object form opens. If the vfoGRUpdateTunnelOptions function is not defined, returns nil, or any invalid option is returned, all tunnel options are displayed on the Create Tunnel in Fluid Object form.

vfoGRUpdateVersionCache.name: vfoGRUpdateVersionCache
vfoGRUpdateVersionCache.syntax:
vfoGRUpdateVersionCache(
l_FGRcellDDID
t_libName
[ ?cellName t_cellName ]
[ ?viewName t_viewName ]
)
=> t / nil
vfoGRUpdateVersionCache.desc: Updates the vfoCreateVersion parameter of an instance to the current Virtuoso version. If the vfoCreateVersion parameter is set to 0, the vfoGRUpdateVersionCache function does not update the vfoCreateVersion parameter to the latest Virtuoso version. You have to call the vfoGREnableVersionCache function to update this parameter to the latest Virtuoso version. If the vfoCreateVersion parameter is set to an older Virtuoso version and the image of the sub-master is not found in the cache files, cache.pcl and index.pcl, the vfoGRUpdateVersionCache function does not update the vfoCreateVersion parameter to the latest Virtuoso version. You have to call the vfoGRDisableVersionCache function and then the vfoGREnableVersionCache function to update this parameter to the latest Virtuoso version.

vfoInstallFluidDeviceFiles.name: vfoInstallFluidDeviceFiles
vfoInstallFluidDeviceFiles.syntax:
vfoInstallFluidDeviceFiles( 
[ ?installPath t_installPath ]
[ ?overwrite { t | nil } ]
[ ?showMsg { t | nil } ]
) 
=> t / nil
vfoInstallFluidDeviceFiles.desc: Loads a set of Cadence-supplied SKILL files in a specific sequence in the Virtuoso environment. These files are required to work with fluid guard rings. These files are automatically loaded when you start Virtuoso.

vfoIsCommandInDragMode.name: vfoIsCommandInDragMode
vfoIsCommandInDragMode.desc: Returns t if the vfo-related command is in drag mode, else returns nil.

vfoIsGuardRing.name: vfoIsGuardRing
vfoIsGuardRing.desc: Returns t if the object to be queried is a valid guard ring instance, else returns nil.

vfoMergeInstances.name: vfoMergeInstances
vfoMergeInstances.syntax:
vfoMergeInstances(
g_obj
d_inst1
d_inst2
[ @rest l_args ]
) 
=> dbId / nil
vfoMergeInstances.desc: Merges the fluid Pcell instances inst1 and inst2. The Merge command for fluid Pcells does not pass these arguments. This function updates the relevant Pcell parameters.

vfoPostChopCBHandler.name: vfoPostChopCBHandler
vfoPostChopCBHandler.desc: Registers or deregisters a user-defined callback function that is called after the chop command completes on an FGR instance. You can do post-processing on the edited FGR instance in the registered callback function.

vfoPostReshapeCBHandler.name: vfoPostReshapeCBHandler
vfoPostReshapeCBHandler.desc: Registers or deregisters a user-defined callback function that is called after the reshape command completes on an FGR instance. You can do post-processing on the edited FGR instance in the registered callback function.

vfoPostSplitCBHandler.name: vfoPostSplitCBHandler
vfoPostSplitCBHandler.desc: Registers or deregisters a user-defined callback function that is called after the split command completes on an FGR instance. You can do post-processing on the edited FGR instance in the registered callback function.

vfoPostStretchCBHandler.name: vfoPostStretchCBHandler
vfoPostStretchCBHandler.desc: Registers or deregisters a user-defined callback function that is called after the stretch command completes on an FGR instance. You can do post-processing on the edited FGR instance in the registered callback function.

vfoReInstallAllFluidGuardRingDevices.name: vfoReInstallAllFluidGuardRingDevices
vfoReInstallAllFluidGuardRingDevices.desc: Reinstalls all the FGR devices in the specified technology file.

vfoReInstallGuardRingDevice.name: vfoReInstallGuardRingDevice
vfoReInstallGuardRingDevice.desc: Reinstalls the specified FGR devices in the specified technology file.

vfoRotateInstance.name: vfoRotateInstance
vfoRotateInstance.syntax:
vfoRotateInstance(
g_obj
d_inst1
x_angle_in_degrees
[ @rest l_args ]
) 
=> t / nil
vfoRotateInstance.desc: Applies the rotation angle on the FGR instance. This function applies to Pcells.

vfoSetParam.name: vfoSetParam
vfoSetParam.syntax:
vfoSetParam(
obj
s_param
value
) 
=> value / nil
vfoSetParam.desc: Sets the value of a CDF parameter to the given value and triggers the callback, if any. The callback is triggered recursively so that if the callback changes another parameter, that callback is also triggered, recursively.

vfoSetParams.name: vfoSetParams
vfoSetParams.desc: Sets the value of multiple parameters in a single call. The l_paramlist argument contains a list of parameter name and value pairs.

vfoSetProtocolClassName.name: vfoSetProtocolClassName
vfoSetProtocolClassName.desc: Sets the protocol class for fluid Pcell for the given Pcell supermaster. This function gets called in the Pcell code for creating the supermaster of a fluid guard ring device in a text file.

vfoSfDraw.name: vfoSfDraw
vfoSfDraw.desc: Draws the Pcell geometries using the information populated by the vfoSfInitialize function.

vfoSfInitialize.name: vfoSfInitialize
vfoSfInitialize.desc: This is the initialization function that is called during space-filling Pcell evaluation. This function initializes the slots and populates other required information for Pcell drawing (vfoSfDraw).

vfoSfOuterEdgeCornerContRemoval.name: vfoSfOuterEdgeCornerContRemoval
vfoSfOuterEdgeCornerContRemoval.desc: Removes the ear-vertex and end-corner contacts from the corners of an FGR to ensure it is created with a smaller footprint. This is achieved by allowing specification of enclosure values lesser than the maximum value, but greater than the minimum value of the minOppExtension rule.

vfoSmoothen.name: vfoSmoothen
vfoSmoothen.syntax:
vfoSmoothen(
d_shape
s_direction
[ ?tmpLpp t_tmpLpp ]
) 
=> t / nil
vfoSmoothen.desc: Smoothens the given polygon shape. If the shape is not a polygon, then the shape is returned unchanged.

vfoSupportsAbut?.name: vfoSupportsAbut?
vfoSupportsAbut?.desc: Checks if the Abut operation is supported on the given instance.

vfoSupportsChop?.name: vfoSupportsChop?
vfoSupportsChop?.desc: Checks if the Chop operation is supported on the given instance.

vfoSupportsConvertToPolygon?.name: vfoSupportsConvertToPolygon?
vfoSupportsConvertToPolygon?.desc: Checks if the Convert to Polygon operation is supported on the given instance.

vfoSupportsCreateObstruction?.name: vfoSupportsCreateObstruction?
vfoSupportsCreateObstruction?.desc: Checks if the Create Obstruction (Tunnel) operation is supported on the given instance.

vfoSupportsCreateObstructions?.name: vfoSupportsCreateObstructions?
vfoSupportsCreateObstructions?.desc: Checks if the Create Obstruction (Tunnel) operation is supported on the given instance.

vfoSupportsDeleteObstruction?.name: vfoSupportsDeleteObstruction?
vfoSupportsDeleteObstruction?.desc: Checks if the Delete Obstruction (Heal) operation is supported on the given instance.

vfoSupportsMerge?.name: vfoSupportsMerge?
vfoSupportsMerge?.desc: Checks if the Merge operation is supported on the given instance.

vfoSupportsRotation.name: vfoSupportsRotation
vfoSupportsRotation.desc: Checks of the Pcell instance supports rotation.

vfoSupportsUpdateModelShape?.name: vfoSupportsUpdateModelShape?
vfoSupportsUpdateModelShape?.desc: Checks if the fluid shape of the given instance can be modified. This function is called by commands that directly update the fluid shape, such as Stretch, Reshape, Split, and Align.

vfoSupportsVersionCache.name: vfoSupportsVersionCache
vfoSupportsVersionCache.desc: Checks whether the Version Cache Management feature is supported on the specified instance.

vfoTransformFluidShape.name: vfoTransformFluidShape
vfoTransformFluidShape.desc: Applies the transform to the given shapeData. This function modifies the given shapeData object and returns it.

vfoTunnelHigherMetalLayers.name: vfoTunnelHigherMetalLayers
vfoTunnelHigherMetalLayers.desc: Enables tunneling of high metal layers in a stacked metal fluid guard ring device. This function is called during the Pcell evaluation of fluid guard ring devices.

vfoUpdateModelShape.name: vfoUpdateModelShape
vfoUpdateModelShape.syntax:
vfoUpdateModelShape( 
g_obj
d_instId
shapeId
newShapeType
newPointList
[ @rest l_args ]
) 
=> t / nil
vfoUpdateModelShape.desc: Updates the given fluid shape of the Pcell instance. The new shape type and points are specified in the newShapeType and newPointList arguments, respectively. The newPointList points are in the design coordinates. This function transforms the newPointList before updating the fluid shape. The Edit command for fluid shapes does not pass these arguments. This function updates the relevant Pcell parameters.

xfgrAddOption.name: xfgrAddOption
xfgrAddOption.syntax:
xfgrAddOption( 
?optionName g_optionName
?optionLabel g_optionLabel
?optionType g_optionType
?optionWidgetType g_optionWidgetType
?optionDefaultValue g_optionDefaultValue
?supportedOptionValue g_supportedOptionValue
?groupName g_groupName
?deviceName g_deviceName
) 
=> t / nil
xfgrAddOption.desc: Adds a new field as specified in the option name to the Create Fluid Guard Ring form.

xfgrConfigureOptionsCB.name: xfgrConfigureOptionsCB
xfgrConfigureOptionsCB.desc: Registers or de-registers the specified user-defined callback function against xfgrConfigureOptions.

xfgrDisableOption.name: xfgrDisableOption
xfgrDisableOption.desc: Disables the specified option on the Create Fluid Guard Ring form.

xfgrEnableOption.name: xfgrEnableOption
xfgrEnableOption.desc: Enables the specified option on the Create Fluid Guard Ring form.

xfgrGetAvailableValues.name: xfgrGetAvailableValues
xfgrGetAvailableValues.desc: Returns the available values for the specified option name. The options are combo box, spin box, or radio button.

xfgrGetOptionValue.name: xfgrGetOptionValue
xfgrGetOptionValue.desc: Returns the current value for the specified option.

xfgrHideAllGroups.name: xfgrHideAllGroups
xfgrHideAllGroups.desc: Hides all groups in the Create Fluid Guard Ring form.

xfgrHideAllOptions.name: xfgrHideAllOptions
xfgrHideAllOptions.desc: Hides all current groups in the Create Fluid Guard Ring form.

xfgrHideGroup.name: xfgrHideGroup
xfgrHideGroup.desc: Hides the options in the specified group from the Create Fluid Guard Ring form.

xfgrHideOption.name: xfgrHideOption
xfgrHideOption.desc: Hides the specified option from the Create Fluid Guard Ring form.

xfgrInitializeOptionsCB.name: xfgrInitializeOptionsCB
xfgrInitializeOptionsCB.desc: Registers or de-registers a user-defined callback function to be called during the initialization of option values in the Create Fluid Guard Ring form.

xfgrOptionValueChangeCB.name: xfgrOptionValueChangeCB
xfgrOptionValueChangeCB.syntax:
xfgrOptionValueChangeCB( 
t_mode
s_callbackFunction
[ g_optionName ]
) 
=> t / nil
xfgrOptionValueChangeCB.desc: Registers or de-registers user-defined callback function to be called when the value of any option on the Create Fluid Guard Ring form changes.

xfgrPostCreateCB.name: xfgrPostCreateCB
xfgrPostCreateCB.desc: Registers or de-registers a user-defined callback function after the creation of the fluid guard ring instance.

xfgrPreCreateCB.name: xfgrPreCreateCB
xfgrPreCreateCB.desc: Registers or de-registers the user-defined callback function before the creation of the fluid guard ring instance.

xfgrSetAvailableValues.name: xfgrSetAvailableValues
xfgrSetAvailableValues.desc: Specified the list of valid values for the specified option.

xfgrSetOptionValue.name: xfgrSetOptionValue
xfgrSetOptionValue.desc: Sets the specified value for the option.

xfgrSetTableCellValue.name: xfgrSetTableCellValue
xfgrSetTableCellValue.syntax:
xfgrSetTableCellValue( 
t_tableName
t_rowNumber
t_columnNumber
t_value
) 
=> t / nil
xfgrSetTableCellValue.desc: Sets the value of the specified row and column of the specified table with the specified value in the Create Fluid Guard Ring form.

xfgrShowAllGroups.name: xfgrShowAllGroups
xfgrShowAllGroups.desc: Displays all groups in the Create Fluid Guard Ring form.

xfgrShowGroup.name: xfgrShowGroup
xfgrShowGroup.desc: Displays the options in the specified group on the Create Fluid Guard Ring form.

xfgrShowOption.name: xfgrShowOption
xfgrShowOption.desc: Displays the specified option on the Create Fluid Guard Ring form.

iccIsConnected.name: iccIsConnected
iccIsConnected.desc: Indicates if a connection from the Virtuoso Studio Design Environment to the router has been established.

iccSendCommand.name: iccSendCommand
iccSendCommand.desc: Sends a command to the router command line interpreter.

iccSendSkillCommand.name: iccSendSkillCommand
iccSendSkillCommand.desc: Sends a SKILL command to the router.

lxDressingTemplateEditor.name: lxDressingTemplateEditor
lxDressingTemplateEditor.desc: Invokes the Dressing Template Editor form.

lxEditPinPlacement.name: lxEditPinPlacement
lxEditPinPlacement.desc: Opens the Pin Placement form in which you can view pin information, constrain a pin to a boundary edge, order and fix pins, specify the pitch for pin placement, and start the Pin Placement function.

lxEditPlacementStyle.name: lxEditPlacementStyle
lxEditPlacementStyle.desc: Opens the Placement Planning form in which you can plan the placement of CMOS, standard cells, or a mixture of CMOS and standard cells. Each of the three modes generates rows based on the parameters you enter in the form.

lxHiAutoPlace.name: lxHiAutoPlace
lxHiAutoPlace.desc: Opens the Auto Placer form in which you can set placement parameters and run the Virtuoso Custom Digital Placer automatic placement function.

lxHiPlaceBoundaryCell.name: lxHiPlaceBoundaryCell
lxHiPlaceBoundaryCell.desc: Opens the Boundary Cell Placement form.

lxHiPlaceFiller.name: lxHiPlaceFiller
lxHiPlaceFiller.desc: Displays the Insert/Delete Filler Cells form.

lxMovePorts.name: lxMovePorts
lxMovePorts.desc: Moves top-level ports over components based on their connectivity.

vcpfeCreateRows.name: vcpfeCreateRows
vcpfeCreateRows.syntax:
vcpfeCreateRows(
d_cv
t_mode
[ ?partitionName t_partitionName ]
[ ?area l_area ] 
[ ?createRows g_createRows ]
[ ?insertTapCells g_insertTapCells ]
[ ?insertBoundaryCells g_insertBoundaryCells ]
)
=> t / nil
vcpfeCreateRows.desc: Estimates and creates rows according to the specified arguments. This command also places tap cells and boundary cells after row creation, which can be controlled using arguments.

vcpfePlaceBoundaryCells.name: vcpfePlaceBoundaryCells
vcpfePlaceBoundaryCells.syntax:
vcpfePlaceBoundaryCells(
d_cvId
t_mode { insert | delete }
[ ?regionList l_list ]
[ ?leftCell t_name ]
[ ?rightCell t_name ]
[ ?leftBottomCornerCell t_name ]
[ ?rightBottomCornerCell t_name ]
[ ?leftTopCornerCell t_name ]
[ ?rightTopCornerCell t_name ]
[ ?topEdgeCell t_name ]
[ ?bottomEdgeCell t_name ]
[ ?leftMirror { t | nil } ]
[ ?rightMirror { t | nil } ]
[ ?leftCornerMirror { t | nil } ]
[ ?rightCornerMirror { t | nil } ]
[ ?outside { t | nil } ]
[ ?topBotRowPlaceable { t | nil } ]
[ ?boundaryCompTypes t_name ]
[ ?libraryFilter t_name ]
[ ?selectedBoundaryCells t_name ]
)
=> l_cellIDs / nil
vcpfePlaceBoundaryCells.desc: Places boundary cells around core cells to isolate the core cells from each other.

vcpfePlaceConstraintGroup.name: vcpfePlaceConstraintGroup
vcpfePlaceConstraintGroup.desc: Returns the name of the constraint group that will be used when the placer is run on the specified cellview.

vcpfePlaceFillers.name: vcpfePlaceFillers
vcpfePlaceFillers.desc: Inserts or deletes filler cells from the specified cellview.

vcpfePlaceTapCells.name: vcpfePlaceTapCells
vcpfePlaceTapCells.syntax:
vcpfePlaceTapCells(
d_cv
t_mode {insert | delete}
[ ?partitionName t_name ]
[ ?tapCompTypes t_types ]
[ ?tapCellNames t_cellNames ]
[ ?tapToTapSpacing f_value ]
[ ?tapBackOff f_value ]
[ ?minTapSpacing f_value ]
[ ?tapPattern {Regular | Checker Board} ] 
[ ?skipRow x_number ]
[ ?tapRowOffset f_value ]
[ ?tapRowEndOffset f_value ]
[ ?periodicTap {t | nil} ]
[ ?lockTap {t | nil} ]
[ ?avoidAbutment {t | nil} ] 
[ ?ignoreBlockages {t | nil} ]
)
=> l_tapCellIDs / nil
vcpfePlaceTapCells.desc: Inserts tap cells in the empty spaces between standard cells in the specified cellview as per the specified arguments. When t_mode is set to delete, all tap cells in the given cellview are deleted.

vcpfeRegisterPostPlacementProc.name: vcpfeRegisterPostPlacementProc
vcpfeRegisterPostPlacementProc.desc: Registers the specified user-defined post-placement procedure. The procedure is called after running automatic placement.

vcpfeRunCustomDigitalPlacer.name: vcpfeRunCustomDigitalPlacer
vcpfeRunCustomDigitalPlacer.syntax:
vcpfeRunCustomDigitalPlacer(
d_schCvID
d_layCvID
[ ?groupCMOSPairs { t | nil } ]
[ ?preserveChains { t | nil } ]
[ ?groupMFactors { t | nil } ]
[ ?allowRotation { t | nil } ]
[ ?selectedCompList l_selectedCompList ]
[ ?placementMode { Auto Placement | ECO Placement } ]
[ ?optimization { none | basic | moderate | optimized } ]
[ ?ecoModeImpact { none | localized | maximized } ]
[ ?insertSubstrateContacts { t | nil } ]
[ ?saveAs { t | nil } ]
[ ?saveAsLibName t_libName ]
[ ?saveAsCellName t_cellName ]
[ ?saveAsViewName t_viewName ]
[ ?overwrite { t | nil } ]
[ ?intraRowSpacer { t | nil } ]
[ ?interRowSpacer t | nil } ]
[ ?adjustBdy { t | nil } ]
[ ?reserveTracksForRouting { -1 | 0 | 1 ... 10 } ]
[ ?vcpRulesConstraintGroup t_constraintGroupName ]
[ ?minBoundaryOffset f_offset ]
[ ?maxPinsPerNet x_numPins ]
[ ?mixedMode { t | nil } ]
[ ?placeCluster t_clusterName ]
[ ?componentEdge { Boundary | Bounding Box } ]
)
=> t
vcpfeRunCustomDigitalPlacer.desc: Runs the custom digital placer, specifying the type of placement that is done, the technology rules to be used, any automatic spacing adjustments to be done, and how the modified cellview is saved.

rdeCloseSession.name: rdeCloseSession
rdeCloseSession.desc: This function terminates the current Virtuoso Routing IDE session and closes the Virtuoso Routing IDE window. The rdeCloseSession function returns the GXL tokens if it was checked out by the rdeShow function.

rdeCreateChamferFill.name: rdeCreateChamferFill
rdeCreateChamferFill.syntax:
rdeCreateChamferFill(
[ ?all { t | nil } ] 
[ ?cv d_cvid ]
[ ?region l_region ] 
[ ?layer lt_layer ] 
[ ?lengthThreshold f_length ] 
[ ?chamferValue1 {f_value1 | l_chamfer1} ]
[ ?chamferValue2 {f_value2 | l_chamfer2} ]
[ ?extendViaChamfer { t | nil } ]
[ ?allowViolation { t | nil } ]
[ ?outputPurpose t_purposeName ]
[ ?materialRemovalPurpose t_purposeName ]
[ ?chamferFilter l_filterCriteria ]
[ ?useEdgeLength { t | nil } ]
)
=> t / nil
rdeCreateChamferFill.desc: Creates chamfer fill on wires (pathSegs). The chamfer fill mechanism removes 90-degree corners by filling the corners of wires that form T-junctions, L-shaped wires, wire-to-via, wire-to-rectangle, and wire-to-polygon connections. T-junctions and L shapes created using only rectangles or polygons are not considered for chamfer fill.

rdeCreateWireChamfer.name: rdeCreateWireChamfer
rdeCreateWireChamfer.syntax:
rdeCreateWireChamfer(
[ ?all { t | nil } ]
[ ?cv d_cvid ]
[ ?region l_region ] 
[ ?layer lt_layer ] 
[ ?lengthThreshold f_length ]
[ ?chamferValue1 {f_value1 | l_chamfer1} ]
[ ?chamferValue2 {f_value2 | l_chamfer2} ]
[ ?allowViolation { t | nil } ]
[ ?innerChamfer { t | nil } ]
[ ?chamferFilter l_filterCriteria ]
[ ?chamferEndOfStripe { t | nil } ]
)
=> t / nil
rdeCreateWireChamfer.desc: Creates chamfers on wires (pathSegs). The wire chamfer mechanism replaces 90-degree wires with 45-degree wires.

rdeDone.name: rdeDone
rdeDone.desc: This function closes the Virtuoso Routing IDE system.

rdeEval.name: rdeEval
rdeEval.desc: This function evaluates the Tcl expression that is supplied. There are no arguments to open the current design and also perform a checkpoint once the Tcl expression is evaluated.

rdeGetVar.name: rdeGetVar
rdeGetVar.desc: This function returns the Virtuoso Routing IDE environment variable. The Virtuoso Routing IDE environment variables are independent of the dfII environment package.

rdeHide.name: rdeHide
rdeHide.desc: This function terminates the current Virtuoso Routing IDE session and closes the Virtuoso Routing IDE window. The rdeHide function returns the GXL tokens if it was checked out by the rdeShow function.

rdeInspect.name: rdeInspect
rdeInspect.desc: This function displays the Virtuoso Routing IDE property inspector GUI. If a dbObject is supplied, then the inspector will show that object and its properties. If no object is supplied, then the currently open geWindow's cellview will be inspected.

rdeOpenCurrentDesign.name: rdeOpenCurrentDesign
rdeOpenCurrentDesign.desc: This function will open the Virtuoso Routing IDE window and start the Virtuoso Routing IDE environment on the cellview that the geWindow has currently loaded. It will also make the current Virtuoso window ReadOnly until the window is closed.

rdeRemoveChamferFill.name: rdeRemoveChamferFill
rdeRemoveChamferFill.syntax:
rdeRemoveChamferFill(
[ ?all { t | nil } ] 
[ ?region l_region ] 
[ ?layer lt_layer ] 
[ ?outputPurpose t_purposeName ]
[ ?materialRemovalPurpose t_purposeName ]
[ ?concaveOnly { t | nil }
)
=> t / nil
rdeRemoveChamferFill.desc: Removes all the right-angled triangle shapes of purposes specified by outputPurpose and materialRemovalPurpose (except if concaveOnly is true). Usually, these shapes are created by the command rdeCreateChamferFill.

rdeReplay.name: rdeReplay
rdeReplay.desc: This function reads the supplied file name and send each line one-at-a-time to the Tcl interpreter. This is in contrast to rdeSource, in which the entire Tcl file is read into the interpreter and then executed. It may be useful in determining which line of a script file had an error, in case an error occurs. Since each line is executed independently, it is not possible to create expressions (such as function definitions) that span more than one line.

rdeSequencer.name: rdeSequencer
rdeSequencer.desc: This function will display the auto router sequencer dialog box. It will obtain some values from the current geWindow. If there is no current geWindow, it will return nil.

rdeSetVar.name: rdeSetVar
rdeSetVar.desc: This function sets the Virtuoso Routing IDE environment variable to the supplied value. The Virtuoso Routing IDE environment variables are independent of the dfII environment package.

rdeShow.name: rdeShow
rdeShow.desc: This function displays the Virtuoso Routing IDE window.

rdeSource.name: rdeSource
rdeSource.desc: This function sources the Tcl expression that is supplied. There are arguments to open the current design and also perform a checkpoint once the Tcl file has been sourced.

rteCheckAntenna.name: rteCheckAntenna
rteCheckAntenna.syntax:
rteCheckAntenna(
[ ?cv d_cvid ]
[ ?all g_all ]
[ ?nets l_nets ]
[ ?set g_set ]
[ ?excludeNets l_excludeNets ]
[ ?model l_models ]
) ;
=> t / nil
rteCheckAntenna.desc: Checks for process antenna violations for the entire design, specific nets, or nets in a set. You can choose to ignore specific nets.

rteCheckDataForRouting.name: rteCheckDataForRouting
rteCheckDataForRouting.syntax:
rteCheckDataForRouting(
[ ?mode t_mode ]
[ ?designRuleSpec t_designRuleSpec ]
[ ?fromRoutingLayer t_fromRoutingLayer ]
[ ?toRoutingLayer t_toRoutingLayer ]
[ ?annotate g_annotate ]
[ ?reportFileName t_reportFileName ]
[ ?selected g_selected ]
) ;
=> t / nil
rteCheckDataForRouting.desc: Checks the technology data and the design data to ensure that the VSR router is able to perform correctly.

rteCheckRoutability.name: rteCheckRoutability
rteCheckRoutability.syntax:
rteCheckRoutability(
[ ?cv d_cvId ]
[ ?noBlockageCheck g_noBlockageCheck ]
[ ?noMinSpaceCheck g_noMinSpaceCheck ]
[ ?noMinWidthCheck g_noMinWidthCheck ]
[ ?noViaCheck g_noViaCheck ]
) ;
=> t / nil
rteCheckRoutability.desc: Checks the design for known conditions that can cause potential routing problems. Design Rule Checks applied to pins and some routability checks are performed primarily to determine the accessibility of pins. You can exclude any of the checks by specifying the appropriate argument. Annotations are automatically created for violations.

rteComposeTrunks.name: rteComposeTrunks
rteComposeTrunks.desc: Converts pathSegs and vias to power trunks usable by both the power and signal routers. The function uses the current cellview and the selected set.

rteCoverObstructionHilite.name: rteCoverObstructionHilite
rteCoverObstructionHilite.desc: Turns on the cover obstruction hilite sets if at least one cover obstruction has been defined in the top-level or masters.

rteCoverObstructionUnHilite.name: rteCoverObstructionUnHilite
rteCoverObstructionUnHilite.desc: Turns off the cover obstruction hilite sets for the ones that are already turned on, if at least one cover obstruction has been defined in the top-level or masters.

rteCreateBlockRingScheme.name: rteCreateBlockRingScheme
rteCreateBlockRingScheme.syntax:
rteCreateBlockRingScheme(
[ ?name s_name ]
[ ?contour g_contour ]
[ ?channel g_channel ]
[ ?blockClearance f_blockClearance ]
[ ?horiLayer t_horiLayer ]
[ ?vertLayer t_vertLayer ]
[ ?latticeStyle g_latticeStyle ]
[ ?netClearance f_netClearance ]
[ ?netWidth f_netWidth ]
) ;
=> t / nil
rteCreateBlockRingScheme.desc: Creates a block ring routing scheme.

rteCreateCellRowsScheme.name: rteCreateCellRowsScheme

vfpReportIOPadLocation.desc: Prints the IO pad information in formatted manner for all the pads which are placed in the IO rows within the design.

vfpSbDefineObstruction.name: vfpSbDefineObstruction
vfpSbDefineObstruction.syntax:
vfpSbDefineObstruction(
l_PhysLCV
t_obstructionType
[ ?topOffset  n_topOffset ]
[ ?bottomOffset n_BottomOffset ]
[ ?leftOffset n_LeftOffset ]
[ ?rightOffset n_RightOffset ]
[ ?layerName t_layerName ]
)
=> t / nil
vfpSbDefineObstruction.desc: Creates placement, routing, or other obstructions based on the obstructionType argument. All conditions that are enforced for these obstructions through GUI-based flow are applicable here. For example, only one placement blockage would be applied per soft block. If a second placement blockage is applied through this API, a warning is issued. The latest applied placement blockage will not replace the existing placement blockage.

[ ?layerName t_layerName ]
)
=> t / nil

[ ?width n_width ]

[ ?criticality x_criticality ]
[ ?sigType t_sigType ]
)
=> t / nil
vfpSbEditIOPin.desc: Edits attributes of the pin that is associated with the specified termName.

vfpSbEditSoftBlockType.name: vfpSbEditSoftBlockType
vfpSbEditSoftBlockType.desc: Edits the blockType of the specified soft block.

vfpSbSetPolygonalBoundary.name: vfpSbSetPolygonalBoundary
vfpSbSetPolygonalBoundary.syntax:
vfpSbSetPolygonalBoundary(
l_PhysLCV
l_ listOfPolygonPoints
)
=> t / nil
vfpSbSetPolygonalBoundary.desc: Specifies the boundary attributes of soft blocks that are polygonal in shape.

vfpSbSetRectangularBoundary.name: vfpSbSetRectangularBoundary
vfpSbSetRectangularBoundary.syntax:
vfpSbSetRectangularBoundary(
l_PhysLCV
n_width
n_height
)
=> t  / nil
vfpSbSetRectangularBoundary.desc: Specifies the boundary vertices of the rectangular soft block.

vpaOptimizePins.name: vpaOptimizePins
vpaOptimizePins.syntax:
vpaOptimizePins(
?cv d_cellViewId
?layoutLCV l_LCVName
[ ?cphId g_cphId ]
[ ?selectedOnly g_selectedOnly ]
