electDeleteDatasets.desc: Deletes electrical data from the specified design. This function can be used for both layout and schematic view of a design.

eadDeleteScratchLib.name: eadDeleteScratchLib
eadDeleteScratchLib.desc: Deletes all data from the scratch library that contains data related to the scratch layout.

elecGetEnableEADMode.name: elecGetEnableEADMode
elecGetEnableEADMode.desc: Returns the current status of the Enable Electrical Data Capture for EAD Flow check box in the EAD Setup form for the specified session and history name.

elecSetEnableEADMode.name: elecSetEnableEADMode
elecSetEnableEADMode.syntax:
elecSetEnableEADMode(
t_sessionName
g_value
[ ?historyName t_historyName ]
)
=> t / nil
elecSetEnableEADMode.desc: Selects or deselects the Enable Electrical Data Capture for EAD Flow check box in the EAD Setup form for the specified session and history name.

elecGetCurrentData.name: elecGetCurrentData
elecGetCurrentData.syntax:
elecGetCurrentData( 
t_libName
t_cellName
t_viewName
t_dataSetName 
t_terminalName
[ t_measurementType ]
)
=> t / nil
elecGetCurrentData.desc: Gets the electrical data for the specified terminal in the given cellview. The data is retrieved from the specified dataset.

elecGetDataSetNames.name: elecGetDataSetNames
elecGetDataSetNames.syntax:
elecGetDataSetNames( 
t_libName
t_cellName
t_viewName
[ t_dataSetType ]
)
=> l_dataSetNames / nil
elecGetDataSetNames.desc: Gets the list of available result datasets for a given design. Also see EM Dataset.

elecGetDataSetParamsPropValue.name: elecGetDataSetParamsPropValue
elecGetDataSetParamsPropValue.syntax:
elecGetDataSetParamsPropValue( 
t_libName
t_cellName
t_viewName
t_dataSetName
t_paramName
)
=> t_paramValue / nil
elecGetDataSetParamsPropValue.desc: Gets the value for the given parameter from the property list of the given dataset saved for the given cellview.

elecMakeDefaultDatasetName.name: elecMakeDefaultDatasetName
elecMakeDefaultDatasetName.syntax:
elecMakeDefaultDatasetName(
t_sessionName
t_historyName
t_dutLibName
t_dutCellName
t_dutViewName
t_dutInstance
t_cornerName
t_temperature
t_designPoint
t_testName
)
=> t_defaultDatasetName
elecMakeDefaultDatasetName.desc: Returns the user-defined default name of the dataset to be displayed in the DUT Dataset field of the EAD results view.

elecUpdateDataSetParamsPropValue.name: elecUpdateDataSetParamsPropValue
elecUpdateDataSetParamsPropValue.syntax:
elecUpdateDataSetParamsPropValue( 
t_libName
t_cellName
t_viewName
t_dataSetName
t_paramName
t_paramValue
)
=> t / nil
elecUpdateDataSetParamsPropValue.desc: Updates the value for a parameter/property of the given dataset saved for the given cellview. You can use this function to modify the value of a dataset property for a schematic or layout view.

elecGetVsyncEnabled.name: elecGetVsyncEnabled
elecGetVsyncEnabled.desc: Returns whether the creation of post-simulation voltage constraints is enabled or disabled.

elecSetVsyncEnabled.name: elecSetVsyncEnabled
elecSetVsyncEnabled.desc: Enables or disables the creation of post-simulation voltage constraints.

elecVdrCreateConstraints.name: elecVdrCreateConstraints
elecVdrCreateConstraints.desc: Creates a post-simulation voltageSyncedNet constraint at the DUT level when called from a user-defined function, which has been specified using the customVoltageConstraintFunc environment variable.

elecVdrCreateDeltaV.name: elecVdrCreateDeltaV
elecVdrCreateDeltaV.desc: Creates a post-simulation deltaVoltage constraint at the DUT level when called from a user-defined function, which has been specified using the customVoltageConstraintFunc environment variable.

eadAddNetsToNetGroup.name: eadAddNetsToNetGroup
eadAddNetsToNetGroup.syntax:
eadAddNetsToNetGroup(
x_cellViewID
t_groupName
?netNames l_netNames
?regExp t_regExp
?file t_fileName
)
=> t / nil
eadAddNetsToNetGroup.desc: Adds the specified nets to an existing net group for the given cellview.

eadCreateDataSetFromLayCSV.name: eadCreateDataSetFromLayCSV
eadCreateDataSetFromLayCSV.syntax:
eadCreateDataSetFromLayCSV(
d_cvId
t_datasetName
t_fileName
)
=> t / nil
eadCreateDataSetFromLayCSV.desc: Creates a user-defined dataset, with the specified name, in the given layout cellview using the electrical current values from the specified layout CSV file.

eadCreateDataSetFromSchCSV.name: eadCreateDataSetFromSchCSV
eadCreateDataSetFromSchCSV.syntax:
eadCreateDataSetFromSchCSV(
d_cvId
t_datasetName
t_fileName
)
=> t / nil
eadCreateDataSetFromSchCSV.desc: Creates a user-defined dataset, with the specified name, in the given layout cellview using the electrical current values from the specified schematic CSV file.

eadCreateDataSetLayCSVTemplate.name: eadCreateDataSetLayCSVTemplate
eadCreateDataSetLayCSVTemplate.desc: Creates a CSV template file for a given layout cellview in a format that can be used later to fill in current values and to create a user-defined EAD dataset from it.

eadCreateNetGroup.name: eadCreateNetGroup
eadCreateNetGroup.syntax:
eadCreateNetGroup(
x_cellViewID
t_groupName
?netNames l_netNames
?regExp t_regExp
?file t_fileName
)
=> t / nil
eadCreateNetGroup.desc: Creates a new net group by the given name in the given cellview. If given, it can also contain the nets.

eadDeleteNetGroup.name: eadDeleteNetGroup
eadDeleteNetGroup.desc: Deletes a net group from the given cellview.

eadExtractParasiticsForDesign.name: eadExtractParasiticsForDesign
eadExtractParasiticsForDesign.desc: Extracts parasitics for the specified layout window if the EAD Browser is initialized. You can configure extraction options on the EAD Options form.

eadGetNetsInNetGroup.name: eadGetNetsInNetGroup
eadGetNetsInNetGroup.desc: Lists all the nets contained in the specified net group of the given cellview.

eadGetTriggerDesc.name: eadGetTriggerDesc
eadGetTriggerDesc.desc: Provides a description about the given event and the arguments required by the SKILL triggers registered for that event.

eadGetLocCurrentLimit.name: eadGetLocCurrentLimit
eadGetLocCurrentLimit.syntax:
eadGetLocCurrentLimit(
w_winId
l_point
t_layerName
[ ?direction t_direction ]
[ ?pulseWidth n_pulseWidth ]
[ ?dutyCycleRatio n_dutyCycleRatio ]
[ ?rmsMetalLineNum n_rmsMetalLineNum ]
[ ?hiEM n_hiEM ]
)
=> l_limit / nil
eadGetLocCurrentLimit.desc: Returns the current carrying EM limit of a resistor on the specified location. Additional arguments, such as ?pulseWidth and ?hiEM can be specified to match specific EM rules in the EAD technology file or the ICT-EM file.

eadJobClose.name: eadJobClose
eadJobClose.desc: Collects results from the batch jobs submitted to computer farms or dedicated servers for distributed computation. When all the distributed jobs are completed successfully, you can use this command to collect extraction results from each job. The parasitic results from individual batch run are combined into one OA database and automatically displayed in the EAD browser summary table.

eadJobStatus.name: eadJobStatus
eadJobStatus.desc: Returns the status of batch jobs submitted to computer farms or dedicated servers for distributed computation.

eadJobSubmit.name: eadJobSubmit
eadJobSubmit.desc: Submits batch jobs to computer farms or dedicated servers for distributed computation.

eadLoadSetup.name: eadLoadSetup
eadLoadSetup.desc: Initializes the EAD Browser in the specified layout window with the given setup file.

eadPreEMSetUserStopCVList.name: eadPreEMSetUserStopCVList
eadPreEMSetUserStopCVList.desc: Sets all or the specified cells of user-specified libraries as stop views. The instances of the specified cells are not descended further during the pre-EM checks.

eadRegTrigger.name: eadRegTrigger
eadRegTrigger.syntax:
eadRegTrigger(
t_eventName
t_callbackProcName
n_priority
)
=> t / nil
eadRegTrigger.desc: Registers a user-defined callback SKILL function for the specified event or trigger with the given priority. You can create custom callback functions to perform necessary updates when these events are triggered.

eadRegisterCustomEMVariable.name: eadRegisterCustomEMVariable
eadRegisterCustomEMVariable.desc: Registers a variable as a custom variable for the purpose of EM calculation. By using the eadSetEMVariable function, you can vary the value of the registered variable before running EM checks. If a variable is not registered, modifying its values does affect EM calculations.

eadRemoveNetsFromNetGroup.name: eadRemoveNetsFromNetGroup
eadRemoveNetsFromNetGroup.syntax:
eadRemoveNetsFromNetGroup(
x_cellViewID
t_groupName
?netNames l_netNames
?regExp t_regExp
?file t_fileName
)
=> t / nil
eadRemoveNetsFromNetGroup.desc: Removes the given nets from the specified net group of the given cellview.

eadRemoveParasitics.name: eadRemoveParasitics
eadRemoveParasitics.syntax:
eadRemoveParasitics(
t_libName
t_cellName
t_viewName
)
=> t / nil
eadRemoveParasitics.desc: Deletes the parasitic information associated with the specified layout design and saves the design (provided there were no other unsaved changes prior to calling the function).

eadSetEMVariable.name: eadSetEMVariable
eadSetEMVariable.syntax:
eadSetEMVariable(
g_varName
[ g_varValue ]
[ g_layerName ]
[ g_analysisPointName ]
)
=> t / nil
eadSetEMVariable.desc: Sets the value of a custom variable registered by eadRegisterCustomEMVariable. The value is used by the EM limit calculation expressions in the ICT-EM file.

elecTransferDataSets.name: elecTransferDataSets
elecTransferDataSets.syntax:
elecTransferDataSets(
t_libName
t_cellName
t_viewName
[ ?dataSetList l_dataSetList ]
[ ?dataSetType t_dataSetType ]
[ ?schLCV g_schLCV ]
[ ?needToSave g_needToSave ]
)
=> t / nil
elecTransferDataSets.desc: Transfers datasets from schematic to layout. By default, the function transfers all the datasets from schematic to layout. You can use the key arguments to transfer specific datasets.

eadUnregTrigger.name: eadUnregTrigger
eadUnregTrigger.desc: Removes the entry for the specified SKILL trigger from the registered list of triggers for the given event. When the specified event occurs, the remaining registered triggers, if any, for that event get executed in their order of priority.

eadInitializeDesign.name: eadInitializeDesign
eadInitializeDesign.syntax:
eadInitializeDesign(
t_layoutDesignCellViewId
t_eadSetupFile
t_cornerName
)
=> t / nil
eadInitializeDesign.desc: Initializes the specified layout design with the specified EAD setup and corner name.

eadExtractParasitics.name: eadExtractParasitics
eadExtractParasitics.desc: Extracts parasitics from the specified layout design.

eadRemoveDesignParasitics.name: eadRemoveDesignParasitics
eadRemoveDesignParasitics.desc: Removes the parasitics extracted from the specified layout design.

vdrCheckVoltageLabels.name: vdrCheckVoltageLabels
vdrCheckVoltageLabels.syntax:
vdrCheckVoltageLabels(
d_cellviewID
[ t_reportFilename ]
[ g_enablePopup ]
)
=> t / nil
vdrCheckVoltageLabels.desc: Verifies that all top-level nets in the specified layout cellview are correctly labeled on the canvas.

vdrCreateUserdvConstraintsFromFile.name: vdrCreateUserdvConstraintsFromFile
vdrCreateUserdvConstraintsFromFile.syntax:
vdrCreateUserdvConstraintsFromFile(
t_libName
t_cellName
t_viewName
t_fileName
)
=> nil
vdrCreateUserdvConstraintsFromFile.desc: Creates User Delta Voltage (userdv) constraints in the specified source schematic cellview based on information from the given CSV file. The schematic view is opened in read-only mode.

vdrCreateVoltageLabel.name: vdrCreateVoltageLabel
vdrCreateVoltageLabel.syntax:
vdrCreateVoltageLabel(
d_cellviewID
lt_datasetName
t_lowVPurposeName
t_highVPurposeName
[ f_labelHeight ]
[ g_externalNets ]
[ g_internalNets ]
[ g_update ]
[ g_generateLabels ]
[ g_overrideMode ]
[ x_hierStopLevel ]
[ u_customFunc ]
[ u_postLabelCreationCB ]
[ t_voltageInfoFile ]
[ t_layerPurposeFile ]
[ g_verbose ]
[ t_logFile ]
[ g_propagateNetVoltages ]
[ lt_sourceName ]
[ g_schematicCSV ]
)
=> t / nil
vdrCreateVoltageLabel.desc: Creates labels on the nets in a layout design reflecting the minimum and maximum voltages from simulation data or a specified list of sources. Labels can also be generated for nets on which no geometry exists if the vdrZeroShapeNets environment variable is set to t.

vdrCreateVoltageLabelEx.name: vdrCreateVoltageLabelEx
vdrCreateVoltageLabelEx.syntax:
vdrCreateVoltageLabelEx(
d_cellviewID
lt_datasetName
t_lowVPurposeName
t_highVPurposeName
[ ?labelHeight f_labelHeight ]
[ ?externalNet { t | nil } ]
[ ?internalNet { t | nil } ]
[ ?update { t | nil } ]
[ ?generateLabel { t | nil } ]
[ ?overrideMode { t | nil } ]
[ ?hierStopLevel x_hierStopLevel ]
[ ?customFunc u_customFunc ]
[ ?postLabelCreationCB u_postLabelCreationCB ]
[ ?dataFile t_voltageInfoFile ]
[ ?lppFile t_layerPurposeFile ]
[ ?verbose { t | nil } ]
[ ?logFile t_logFile ]
[ ?propagateNetVoltages { t | nil } ]
[ ?source lt_sourceName ]
[ ?schematicCSV { t | nil } ]
)
=> t / nil
vdrCreateVoltageLabelEx.desc: Creates labels on the nets in a layout design reflecting the minimum and maximum voltages from simulation data or a specified list of sources. Labels can also be generated for nets on which no geometry exists if the vdrZeroShapeNets environment variable is set to t.

vdrCreateVoltageLabelOnNets.name: vdrCreateVoltageLabelOnNets
vdrCreateVoltageLabelOnNets.syntax:
vdrCreateVoltageLabelOnNets(
d_cellviewID
ld_netIDs
t_lowVPurposeName
t_highVPurposeName
[ f_labelHeight ]
[ u_customFunc ]
[ lt_ignoreZeroVoltNets ]
[ u_postLabelCreationCB ]
[ t_layerPurposeFile ]
)
=> t / nil
vdrCreateVoltageLabelOnNets.desc: Creates labels from the voltage values entered manually in the Property Editor assistant for the specified top-level nets in the given cellview. The labels are created on the geometry of the net in question. Where there is no geometry, the labels are created on all the Pcell and instance terminals connected to the net. The command works only in Layout XL and higher tiers.

vdrCreateVoltageMarkers.name: vdrCreateVoltageMarkers
vdrCreateVoltageMarkers.syntax:
vdrCreateVoltageMarkers(
d_cellviewID
t_voltagePurposeFile
[ ?dataset t_datasetName ]
[ ?update { t | nil } ]
[ ?override_mode { t | nil } ]
[ ?size f_markerHeight ]
[ ?externalNet { t | nil } ]
[ ?internalNet { t | nil } ]
[ ?hierStopLevel x_hierStopLevel ]
[ ?postMarkerCreationCB u_postMarkerCreationCB ]
[ ?csvFile t_voltageInfoFile ]
[ ?voltageRounding { roundOff | floor | ceiling } ]
[ ?mode { maxVoltage | minVoltage | bothVoltage } ]
)
=> t / nil
vdrCreateVoltageMarkers.desc: Creates markers for minimum and/or maximum voltages on the nets in the specified design. Voltage information can be taken from simulation datasets, from user-defined voltages on nets, or from a voltage information file. The voltage purpose file specifies on which layer-purpose pair a marker is created depending on the voltage value in question.

vdrCreateVoltageMarkersOnNets.name: vdrCreateVoltageMarkersOnNets
vdrCreateVoltageMarkersOnNets.syntax:
vdrCreateVoltageMarkersOnNets(
d_cellviewID
ld_netIDs
t_voltagePurposeFile
[ ?size f_markerHeight ]
[ ?postMarkerCreationCB t_postMarkerCreationCB ]
[ ?voltageRounding { roundOff | floor | ceiling } ]
[ ?voltageMode { maxVoltage | minVoltage | bothVoltage } ]
[ ?ignoreZeroVoltNets lt_netNames ]
)
=> t / nil
vdrCreateVoltageMarkersOnNets.desc: Creates markers from the voltage values entered manually in the Property Editor assistant for the specified top-level nets in the given cellview.

vdrCreateVSyncConstraintsFromFile.name: vdrCreateVSyncConstraintsFromFile
vdrCreateVSyncConstraintsFromFile.syntax:
vdrCreateVSyncConstraintsFromFile(
t_libName
t_cellName
t_viewName
t_fileName
)
=> nil
vdrCreateVSyncConstraintsFromFile.desc: (ICADVM20.1 Only) Creates Voltage Synced Net (vsync) constraints in the specified source schematic cellview based on information from the given CSV file. The schematic view is opened in read-only mode.

vdrDeleteGUI.name: vdrDeleteGUI
vdrDeleteGUI.desc: Opens the Delete VDR Objects form, where you can select Labels/Markers, VSync Shapes, and Userdv Shapes check boxes to delete voltage labels and markers, VSync shapes, and Userdv shapes, respectively.

vdrDeleteLabels.name: vdrDeleteLabels
vdrDeleteLabels.desc: Deletes from the specified cellview all the labels and markers created using the VDR flows.

vdrDisplaySchematicGUI.name: vdrDisplaySchematicGUI
vdrDisplaySchematicGUI.desc: Opens the Voltage Dependent Rules form, which you can use to transfer voltage data on schematic nets from the specified simulation voltage datasets. This function works only in Layout XL and higher tiers.

vdrGenerateLabelsGUI.name: vdrGenerateLabelsGUI
vdrGenerateLabelsGUI.desc: Opens the Voltage Dependent Rules form, which you can use to create voltage labels or markers on nets. The command works only in Layout XL and higher tiers.

vdrGenerateUserdvShapes.name: vdrGenerateUserdvShapes
vdrGenerateUserdvShapes.syntax:
vdrGenerateUserdvShapes(
d_cellviewID
[ ?verbose { t | nil } ]
[ ?logFile t_logFile ]
)
=> t / nil
vdrGenerateUserdvShapes.desc: (ICADVM20.1 EXL Only) Creates User Delta Voltage (Userdv) shapes between nets that are constrained by a User Delta Voltage constraint. The Userdv marker shape and associated text label that are created correspond to each User Delta Voltage constraint. You can optionally print messages relating to problems encountered during Userdv shape creation and save these messages to a specified log file if required.

vdrGenerateVSyncShapes.name: vdrGenerateVSyncShapes
vdrGenerateVSyncShapes.syntax:
vdrGenerateVSyncShapes(
d_cellviewID
[ ?verbose { t | nil } ]
[ ?logFile t_logFile ]
)
=> t / nil
vdrGenerateVSyncShapes.desc: (ICADVM20.1 EXL Only) Creates voltage sync (vsync) shapes between nets that are constrained by a common voltage sync constraint. You can optionally print messages relating to problems encountered during vsync shape creation and save these messages to a specified log file if required.

vdrGetValidLayers.name: vdrGetValidLayers
vdrGetValidLayers.desc: Returns the list of valid layers on which labels or markers can be generated. The list was specified previously using the vdrSetValidLayers function.

vdrRunSanityChecker.name: vdrRunSanityChecker
vdrRunSanityChecker.syntax:
vdrRunSanityChecker(
d_cellviewID
[ g_checkMarkers ]
[ g_checkAgainstLayout ]
[ f_tolerance ]
[ g_isToleranceAbsolute ]
[ t_logFile ]
[ t_csvName ]
[ l_datasets ]
[ t_checkAgainstSource ]
[ g_completeHierarchy ]
)
=> t / nil
vdrRunSanityChecker.desc: Checks constrained voltage labels in the layout against the voltage values stored in the schematic or layout net properties and reports any discrepancies between the values. You can optionally apply a threshold up to which mismatches are tolerated and not reported. You can also specify the location and name of a log file in which the report is captured.

vdrRunUserdvSanityChecker.name: vdrRunUserdvSanityChecker
vdrRunUserdvSanityChecker.desc: (ICADVM20.1 EXL Only) Checks whether there are valid User Delta Voltage (Userdv) shapes on nets that are constrained by a common Userdv constraint. The checker reports any Userdv shapes that are wrongly created and any nets that have a Userdv constraint defined but no Userdv shape between them.

vdrRunVSyncSanityChecker.name: vdrRunVSyncSanityChecker
vdrRunVSyncSanityChecker.desc: (ICADVM20.1 EXL Only) Checks whether there are valid voltage sync (vsync) shapes on nets that are constrained by a common vsync constraint. The checker reports any vsync shapes that are wrongly created and any nets that have a vsync constraint defined but no vsync shape between them.

vdrSanityCheckerGUI.name: vdrSanityCheckerGUI
vdrSanityCheckerGUI.desc: Opens the VDR Sanity Checker form, which you can use to check constrained VDR voltage labels in the layout view and report any labels that are missing or which have values different from the values specified for the net in the schematic or layout design.

vdrSetNetVoltageRange.name: vdrSetNetVoltageRange
vdrSetNetVoltageRange.syntax:
vdrSetNetVoltageRange(
t_libName
t_cellName
l_viewList
[ ?netVoltages l_netVoltages ]
[ ?voltageDataFile t_voltageInfoFile ]
[ ?verbose { t | nil } ]
[ ?logFile t_logFile ]
)
=> t / nil
vdrSetNetVoltageRange.desc: (ICADVM20.1 Only) Sets net voltages in the specified list of cellviews. The voltages can be either specified directly as a list when the command is called or read from voltage information file.

vdrSetValidLayers.name: vdrSetValidLayers
vdrSetValidLayers.desc: Specifies a list of valid layers on which labels or markers can be generated. The software creates labels or markers only for nets on one of the listed layers. Each subsequent call to the function overrides all the previously set layers.

vdrTransferVSyncConstraints.name: vdrTransferVSyncConstraints
vdrTransferVSyncConstraints.desc: Transfers Voltage Synced Net (vsync) constraints from a specified source cellview to the specified target cellviews without opening any of the cellviews involved. If there is no target cellview specified, then the constraints are transferred to all open cellviews.

vdrVsyncVisualizerGUI.name: vdrVsyncVisualizerGUI
vdrVsyncVisualizerGUI.desc: (ICADVM20.1 EXL Only) Opens the VDR Constraints Visualizer form, which you can use to create Voltage Synced Net (vsync) constraints from the contents of a CSV file, list the vsync constraints currently present in the layout view, and delete those that are no longer required.

verifAddDocument.name: verifAddDocument
verifAddDocument.desc: Adds a file to the documents directory of the Verifier cellview.

verifAddImage.name: verifAddImage
verifAddImage.desc: Adds a file to the images directory of the Verifier cellview.

verifAddReq.name: verifAddReq
verifAddReq.syntax:
verifAddReq(
g_sessionId
t_title
[ ?reqId t_reqId ]
[ ?parentId t_parentId ]
[ ?pos x_pos ]
)
=> t / nil
verifAddReq.desc: Adds a new requirement with the title to the specified Verifier session.

verifCompareImportedFiles.name: verifCompareImportedFiles
verifCompareImportedFiles.desc: Compares the requirements from the Verifier session with the requirements from the imported files.

verifCreateRandomId.name: verifCreateRandomId
verifCreateRandomId.desc: Creates a string of random characters that can be used as a unique requirement ID.

verifDeleteReqSignoff.name: verifDeleteReqSignoff
verifDeleteReqSignoff.desc: Deletes the signoff setup of the specified requirement in a Verifier session.

verifDocumentExists.name: verifDocumentExists
verifDocumentExists.desc: Checks if the given file exists in the documents directory of the Verifier cellview.

verifExportJson.name: verifExportJson
verifExportJson.syntax:
verifExportJson(
g_sessionId
[ ?filename t_filename ]
[ ?compact g_compact ]
)
=> t_filename / nil
verifExportJson.desc: Exports the Verifier session as a json file. The json file contains details about the session, including the requirements, implementations, mappings, and simulation results.

verifExportReqsToFile.name: verifExportReqsToFile
verifExportReqsToFile.syntax:
verifExportReqsToFile(
g_sessionId
t_fileName
[ ?fileType t_fileType ]
[ ?fields t_fields ]
)
=> t / nil
verifExportReqsToFile.desc: Exports the requirements to either an Excel or CSV file. It can also export the results to an imported file.

verifGetCustomFieldNames.name: verifGetCustomFieldNames
verifGetCustomFieldNames.desc: Retrieves a list of custom field names for a Verifier session.

verifGetCustomFieldValue.name: verifGetCustomFieldValue
verifGetCustomFieldValue.desc: Retrieves the value of a custom field available in a Verifier session.

verifGetDocuments.name: verifGetDocuments
verifGetDocuments.desc: Returns the list of files that have been added to the documents directory of the Verifier cellview.

verifGetImages.name: verifGetImages
verifGetImages.desc: Returns the list of image files that have been added to images directory of the Verifier cellview.

verifGetImportedFiles.name: verifGetImportedFiles
verifGetImportedFiles.desc: Returns a list of all imported files that are associated with the specified session. If no imported files have been defined, nil is returned.

verifGetReferencedCellViews.name: verifGetReferencedCellViews
verifGetReferencedCellViews.desc: Returns a list of all the referenced Verifier cellviews that can be associated with the specified session. If no referenced Verifier cellviews are defined, nil is returned.

verifGetReqCustomFieldNames.name: verifGetReqCustomFieldNames
verifGetReqCustomFieldNames.desc: Retrieves the list of the custom fields available to the requirements in a Verifier session.

verifGetReqCustomFieldValue.name: verifGetReqCustomFieldValue
verifGetReqCustomFieldValue.syntax:
verifGetReqCustomFieldValue(
g_sessionId
t_reqId
t_fieldName
)
=> l_fieldValue / nil
verifGetReqCustomFieldValue.desc: Retrieves the value of the specified custom field of a requirement in a Verifier session.

verifGetReqParent.name: verifGetReqParent
verifGetReqParent.desc: Returns the ID of the parent of the specified requirement.

verifGetReqProp.name: verifGetReqProp
verifGetReqProp.syntax:
verifGetReqProp(
g_sessionId
t_reqId
t_propName
[ g_inherited ]

)
=>t_propValue / nil
verifGetReqProp.desc: Returns the value of the specified property of a requirement in a Verifier session.

verifGetReqProps.name: verifGetReqProps
verifGetReqProps.desc: Returns all the properties of a requirement in a Verifier session.

verifGetReqs.name: verifGetReqs
verifGetReqs.syntax:
verifGetReqs(
g_sessionId
[ ?type t_type ]
[ ?owner t_owner ]
[ ?inHier t_parentReqId ]
[ ?mappable g_mappable ]
[ ?mapped g_mapped ]
[ ?domain g_domain ]
)
=> l_reqs / nil
verifGetReqs.desc: Retrieves the list of requirements from a Verifier session that have the same type, owner, hierarchy, mappable or mapped property, and domain as specified.

verifGetReqSignoff.name: verifGetReqSignoff
verifGetReqSignoff.desc: Retrieves the signoff setup of the specified requirement in a Verifier session. The retrieved information includes the name of the person who signed off the signoff validity period, comments, and if the signoff is enabled for use or disabled.

verifGetReqStatus.name: verifGetReqStatus
verifGetReqStatus.desc: Returns the overall status of a requirement in a Verifier session.

verifGetSetupLibrary.name: verifGetSetupLibrary
verifGetSetupLibrary.desc: Retrieves the name of the setup library cellview bound to the given Verifier session.

verifImageExists.name: verifImageExists
verifImageExists.desc: Checks if the given file exists in the images directory of the Verifier cellview.

verifImportFile.name: verifImportFile
verifImportFile.syntax:
verifImportFile(
g_sessionId
t_fileName
[ ?fileType t_fileType ]
[ ?headerRows x_headerRows ]

t_cellName
t_viewName
[ g_readOnly ]

slaRemoveSweepVariable.name: slaRemoveSweepVariable

slaRemoveVerificationSpace.name: slaRemoveVerificationSpace

Invoking the slaSaveAndCloseView() function releases or checks in the ADE Verifier license.

verifCompareImplementationsFromSnapshot.desc: Compares the differences between implementations from snapshots. The implementation comparison targets include the ADE Assembler setup, design (schematic or configurations) and simulation files (model or definition files). You can view the differences in a form or retrieve the list of differences through this SKILL function

cpdCreateDeviceInfo.name: cpdCreateDeviceInfo
cpdCreateDeviceInfo.desc: Creates a label in the specified cellview as libName_cellName_viewName on the layer defined in Device Map file. It generates customizable auCdl view as defined in the argument. It creates a device signature and extraction rules for the custom passive device.

[?devicesFile t_devicesFile]

cpdGenerateDerivedShapes.desc: Generates new shapes in the specified cellview using the derived shape generation rules specified for a device in a device configuration file. If the file is not specified, the rules from the previously loaded device file (using cpdLoadDerivedShapesRules) are used.

cpdLoadDerivedShapesRules.name: cpdLoadDerivedShapesRules
cpdLoadDerivedShapesRules.desc: Loads the derived shapes generation rules into the memory of devices specified in the given file. The newly loaded list of rules overrides the previously defined list of rules for the devices.

cpdPegasusPreFormTrigger.desc: Pre-fill the Pegasus LVS form with custom passive device related configurations required to run LVS for custom passive devices.

edifinMakeRenameString.name: edifinMakeRenameString

poCellNameMap.desc: Passes the library name, cell name and the view name for each cell in the library to a user-defined procedure.

poLayerMap.name: poLayerMap
poLayerMap.desc: This is a user-defined function that passes the layer number and datatype for each layer in the input Stream file, when it is called. Stream Out interprets the output of the procedure in the same way it interprets the OpenAccess name and purpose. However, Stream Out checks for this function only if the layer map file (-layerMap option) is not specified. If the layer map file is specified, the poLayerMap function is ignored. For more information, see the Layer Map File section.

textFontMap.name: textFontMap
textFontMap.desc: Passes each font type in a Design Framework II library to a user-defined procedure.

piCellNameMap.name: piCellNameMap
piCellNameMap.desc: Passes the cell name for each cell name in the input file to a user-defined procedure.

piLayerMap.name: piLayerMap

Stream In interprets the output of the procedure in the same way it interprets the OpenAccess name and purpose. However, Stream In checks for this function only if the layer map file (-layerMap option) is not specified. If the layer map file is specified, the piLayerMap function is ignored. For more information, see the Layer Map File section.

poTextMap.name: poTextMap

xstInGetVMLibs.desc: Returns the list of virtual memory libraries created by XStream In. Only the primary libraries created by XStream In are returned. xstInSaveVMLib.desc: Saves the specified virtual memory library, t_vmLibName, to either the specified directory, t_path, or the current working directory, if t_path is not specified. vmtCompareSipToOa.desc: Compares the contents of the specified Allegro SiP layout file and Virtuoso module layout and generates a new layout cellview containing only the parts of the two designs that are different. This is done by performing an XOR boolean operation for an Allegro SiP layout file and a Virtuoso module layout (OpenAccess layout) to create a new layout with XOR shapes and the merged shapes from the SiP layout and OpenAccess layout or database. The comparison is done with the saved representation of the Virtuoso layout not the unsaved OpenAccess database in memory.

The library contains TILPs, footprints, and schematic symbols for dies, packages, SMDs, embedded components, and padstacks in a SiP layout file. When importing a layout from the Allegro platform to the Virtuoso Studio, the ratio of DataBase Unit Per User Unit remains 1:1. This means the resolution of a layout remains during the import. While creating the library, if files or cellviews are checked in, autocheckin is added as a comment by the Library Manager.

)
=> numErrors / nil
vmtValidateUnifiedLibrary.desc: Validates the existence of required views and cross-view consistency in the cells of a library or the master libraries for all the instances in a design. If a library name is provided, all the cells in the library that match the specified list of views are opened and added to a list for validation. If a cellview is specified, the specific cell is added to a list for validation. If no library name or cellview is provided, no validation is performed.

vrfCheckTILPVersion.name: vrfCheckTILPVersion
vrfCheckTILPVersion.syntax:
vrfCheckTILPVersion(
x_dbId
[ ?reportAll g_reportAll ]
[ ?fileName g_fileName ]
)
=> t / nil
vrfCheckTILPVersion.desc: Checks the version of the TILP from the given ID, which can be of an instance, cellview, library, or sub-master cellview. There are warnings and errors generated when checks are performed. Warning messages are issued for the TILP versions that are compatible with the current version of the tool. You need to upgrade the TILP only if the associated features are going to be used. For example, if you want to use a new feature, the die TILP needs to be updated. Error messages indicate that the TILP versions must be updated before use in the current version of the tool. Otherwise, the tool does not work as expected. For example, die TILP V1 is not compatible with the tool version post ICADVM18.1ISR10.

vrfComplianceAudit.name: vrfComplianceAudit
vrfComplianceAudit.syntax:
vrfComplianceAudit(
g_cellViewId
[ ?dieAuditTemplateFile t_dieAuditTemplateFile ]
[ ?libCheck g_libCheck ]
[ ?termsCheck g_termsCheck ]
[ ?icSymbolCheck g_icSymbolCheck ]
[ ?ioCheck g_ioCheck ]
[ ?otherChecks g_otherChecks ]
)
=> t / nil
vrfComplianceAudit.desc: Performs various preliminary checks on an IC layout with the use of a template file.

vrfExportLayoutSkill.name: vrfExportLayoutSkill
vrfExportLayoutSkill.syntax:
vrfExportLayoutSkill(
g_cellViewId
t_frontPinLayer
t_backPinLayer
[ ?dieInterfaceType t_dieInterfaceType ]
[ ?includeUnconnectedBump g_includeUnconnectedBump ]
[ ?pinNumbering t_pinNumbering ]
[ ?pinNumberFile t_pinNumberFile ]
[ ?abstractLib t_abstractLib ]
[ ?attachSParam g_attachSParam ]
[ ?sParamView t_sParamView ]
[ ?modelFile t_modelFile ]
[ ?shortPinLib t_shortPinLib ]
[ ?shortPinCell t_shortPinCell ]
[ ?frontLabelLPP t_frontLabelLPP ]
[ ?backLabelLPP t_backLabelLPP ]
[ ?csvFileName t_csvFileName ]
[ ?areaTransferFile t_areaTransferFile ]
[ ?abstractViewCell t_exportNoBumpTerm ]
[ ?exportNoBumpTerm g_exportNoBumpTerm ]
[ ?deleteViewsBeforeExport g_deleteViewsBeforeExport ]
[ ?outputMode t_outputMode ]
)
=> t / nil
vrfExportLayoutSkill.desc: Exports the die for IC layouts. The function supports both IO cell and Shape with overlapping label as Die Interface Type. It generates a package type library that contains abstract, Technology Independent Layout Pcells (TILPs), schematic, and symbol views. The abstract view is the base cellview for the Pcell generated layout, that is, TILP. The schematic is the wrapper schematic for the IC symbol. The symbol view is used to instantiate the generated die symbol in a package schematic.

vrfExportPackage.name: vrfExportPackage
vrfExportPackage.syntax:
vrfExportPackage(
g_cellViewId
t_frontPinLayer
t_backPinLayer
[ ?instanceNames t_instanceNames ]
[ ?abstractLib t_abstractLib ]
[ ?ecoMode g_ecoMode ]
[ ?attachSParam g_attachSParam ]
[ ?sParamView t_sParamView ]
[ ?modelFile t_modelFile ]
[ ?shortPinLib t_shortPinLib ]
[ ?shortPinCell t_shortPinCell ]
[ ?csvFileName t_csvFileName ]
[ ?abstractViewCell t_abstractViewCell ]
)
=> t / nil
vrfExportPackage.desc: Exports the specified package layout if its sipObjectType value is set to package. Use the instanceNames argument to specify the instance names to search master views for identifying candidate IO cells to be exported. The IO cells to be exported should have the cellType defined as coverBump or pad. The shapes in the master views must match the front or back layer-purpose pairs specified in the SKILL function arguments. Only the sub-master views of the package instances and IO cells are processed, not the super-master views. To export a package layout, there should be top-level terminals in the layout. Also, all the package type instances in a package layout must be fully connected to top-level terminals.

vrfLowerPriority.name: vrfLowerPriority
vrfLowerPriority.desc: Lowers the priority of a specified dynamic shape so that it is one unit less than the lowest priority currently set for dynamic shapes on the layer.

vrfHiUpdate.name: vrfHiUpdate
vrfHiUpdate.desc: Starts to process diestacks after creating a stackable object. This function must be used when instances are created in a script.

vrfRaisePriority.name: vrfRaisePriority
vrfRaisePriority.desc: Raises the priority of a specified dynamic shape so that it is one unit higher than the maximum priority currently set for dynamic shapes on the layer.

vrfSipSet.name: vrfSipSet
vrfSipSet.syntax:
vrfSipSet(
d_objID
t_attrName
g_attrValue
)
=> t / nil
vrfSipSet.desc: Sets attributes for a specified object.

vrfSipGet.name: vrfSipGet
vrfSipGet.desc: Retrieves values of a specified attribute of an object.

vrfTLineAbut.name: vrfTLineAbut
vrfTLineAbut.syntax:
vrfTLineAbut(
t_instA
t_instB
t_pinA
t_pinB
t_pinAside
t_conn
n_event
d_group
d_chain
)
=> t / nil
vrfTLineAbut.desc: Abuts two transmission line instances with the required specifications and issues a warning if the device cannot be abutted.

vrfUpdateTILPVersion.name: vrfUpdateTILPVersion
vrfUpdateTILPVersion.syntax:
vrfUpdateTILPVersion(
x_dbId
[ ?types g_types ]
[ ?cells g_cells ]
[ ?fileName g_fileName ]
)
=> t / nil
vrfUpdateTILPVersion.desc: Updates the super-master cellviews that have version lower than the latest version of the given TILP from the given ID, which can be of an instance, cellview, library, or sub-master cellview.

ciAddHierarchicalNotes.name: ciAddHierarchicalNotes
ciAddHierarchicalNotes.syntax:
ciAddHierarchicalNotes( 
t_libName
t_cellName
t_viewName
[ g_hierarchical ]
)
=> t / nil
ciAddHierarchicalNotes.desc: Adds notes to the templates and constraints for a single cellview or all along the hierarchy beginning from the given cellview.

ciAddLeadingSlash.name: ciAddLeadingSlash
ciAddLeadingSlash.desc: Adds a forward slash (/) to the beginning of the passed string if it does not already have one.

ciAddProcessRules.name: ciAddProcessRules
ciAddProcessRules.syntax:
ciAddProcessRules( 
d_Id
l_rules
[ t_parameterType ]
)
=> t / nil
ciAddProcessRules.desc: Adds the specified process rules to the front of the rules associated with the given object.

ciAddRuleGroup.name: ciAddRuleGroup
ciAddRuleGroup.syntax:
ciAddRuleGroup( 
[ d_techID | d_cellViewID ]
t_name
)
=> t / nil
ciAddRuleGroup.desc: Creates an oaConstraint group, with a given name, for technology or design files.

ciAddTrailingSlash.name: ciAddTrailingSlash
ciAddTrailingSlash.desc: Adds a forward slash (/) to the end of the passed string if it does not already have one.

ciAllCellViewsInHierarchy.name: ciAllCellViewsInHierarchy
ciAllCellViewsInHierarchy.syntax:
ciAllCellViewsInHierarchy( 
d_cellViewDBId
[ t_pathToCurrentCellView ]
[ t_pathFilter ]
[ t_depth ]
[ s_predicate ]
)
=> list / nil
ciAllCellViewsInHierarchy.desc: Returns a list of disembodied property lists containing the path and database ID of each cellview in the hierarchy, or to a specific depth starting from a given cellview and path to that cellview.

ciAxisCreate.name: ciAxisCreate
ciAxisCreate.syntax:
ciAxisCreate( 
u_cache
t_axisName
[ l_parameterList ]
)
=> t / nil

ciAxisDelete.name: ciAxisDelete
ciAxisDelete.syntax:
ciAxisDelete( 
u_cache
t_axisName
[ g_forceDelete ]
)
=> t / nil
ciAxisDelete.desc: Deletes an axis from the specified cache.

ciAxisExists.name: ciAxisExists
ciAxisExists.desc: Returns t (true) if the named axis exists in the cache. Access to axes is only provided through the axis name. No direct reference to an axis object is provided.

ciAxisListCon.name: ciAxisListCon
ciAxisListCon.desc: Lists all the constraints that are attached to a given axis.

ciAxisListParams.name: ciAxisListParams
ciAxisListParams.syntax:
ciAxisListParams( 
u_cache
t_axisName
[ g_includeDefaults ]
)
=> parameterList / nil
ciAxisListParams.desc: Lists the parameters associated with an axis.

ciAxisReplaceParams.name: ciAxisReplaceParams
ciAxisReplaceParams.syntax:
ciAxisReplaceParams( 
u_cache
t_axisName
l_parameterList
)
=> t / nil
ciAxisReplaceParams.desc: Replaces all axis constraint parameters with a new set of parameters.

ciCacheCellName.name: ciCacheCellName
ciCacheCellName.desc: Returns the cell name of the specified constraint cache. The cache library, cell, and view refers to the schematic, configuration, physical configuration, or layout view that the constraint cache is associated with.

ciCacheConstraintCellName.name: ciCacheConstraintCellName
ciCacheConstraintCellName.desc: Returns the constraint cell name of the specified constraint cache. The constraint library, cell, and view refers to the storage location of the constraints, which might be a constraint view or layout.

ciCacheConstraintLibName.name: ciCacheConstraintLibName
ciCacheConstraintLibName.desc: Returns the constraint library name of the specified constraint cache. The constraint library, cell, and view refers to the storage location of the constraints, which might be a constraint view or layout.

ciCacheConstraintViewName.name: ciCacheConstraintViewName
ciCacheConstraintViewName.desc: Returns the constraint view name of the specified constraint cache. The constraint library, cell, and view refers to the storage location of the constraints, which might be a constraint view or layout.

ciCacheDiscardEdits.name: ciCacheDiscardEdits
ciCacheDiscardEdits.desc: Discards changes made to the constraint cache in the memory and returns a new constraint cache ID. This function does not apply to layout constraint caches.

ciCacheFind.name: ciCacheFind
ciCacheFind.syntax:
ciCacheFind( 
d_dbCellViewId | t_libName t_cellName t_viewName
)
=> u_cache / nil
ciCacheFind.desc: Finds an existing constraint cache for a given design specified using library, cell, and view names. Alternatively, pass the dbCellViewId of the required design.

ciCacheGet.name: ciCacheGet
ciCacheGet.syntax:
ciCacheGet( 
d_dbCellViewId | t_libName t_cellName t_viewName
)
=> u_cache / nil
ciCacheGet.desc: Finds an existing constraint cache. If it cannot find an existing cache, it creates and populates a cache for the given design, using library, cell, and view names. Alternatively, pass the dbCellViewId of the required design.

ciCacheGetAllNetNames.name: ciCacheGetAllNetNames
ciCacheGetAllNetNames.desc: Returns a sorted list of all the net names in the cellview associated with the constraints cache. By default, the iterated net names are expanded.

ciCacheGetCellView.name: ciCacheGetCellView
ciCacheGetCellView.desc: Returns the cellview associated to the specified cache.

ciCacheGetEnabledNotifications.name: ciCacheGetEnabledNotifications
ciCacheGetEnabledNotifications.desc: Returns a list of cache notifications that ciCacheNotifications enabled.

ciCacheIsLayout.name: ciCacheIsLayout
ciCacheIsLayout.desc: Returns t if the passed cache is a layout cache.

ciCacheIsModified.name: ciCacheIsModified
ciCacheIsModified.desc: Checks whether a constraint cache has been modified.

ciCacheIsWritable.name: ciCacheIsWritable
ciCacheIsWritable.desc: Checks whether a constraint cache is writable.

ciCacheLCV.name: ciCacheLCV
ciCacheLCV.desc: Returns a list containing the library, cell, and view names of the specified constraint cache. The cache library, cell, and view refers to the schematic, configuration, physical configuration, or layout view that the constraint cache is associated with.

ciCacheLibName.name: ciCacheLibName
ciCacheLibName.desc: Returns the library name of the specified constraint cache. The cache library, cell, and view refers to the schematic, configuration, physical configuration, or layout view that the constraint cache is associated with.

ciCacheListAxesNames.name: ciCacheListAxesNames
ciCacheListAxesNames.desc: Lists all axes names in a cache. Access to axes is only provided through the axis name, no direct reference to an axis object is provided.

ciCacheListCon.name: ciCacheListCon
ciCacheListCon.desc: Lists all the constraints from a given cache.

ciCacheListConstrainedObjects.name: ciCacheListConstrainedObjects
ciCacheListConstrainedObjects.desc: Lists the name and type of all constrained objects.

ciCacheListConstrainedObjectNames.name: ciCacheListConstrainedObjectNames
ciCacheListConstrainedObjectNames.desc: Lists the names of the constrained objects (without the type of object).

ciCacheListTemplates.name: ciCacheListTemplates
ciCacheListTemplates.desc: Lists all templates, of an optional given type, from a cache.

ciCacheListTypeNames.name: ciCacheListTypeNames
ciCacheListTypeNames.desc: Lists all the names of the constraint types that are legal for the given cache.

ciCacheListTypes.name: ciCacheListTypes
ciCacheListTypes.desc: Lists all constraint types in a cache.

ciCacheMakeEditable.name: ciCacheMakeEditable
ciCacheMakeEditable.desc: Reopens the constraint cache for edit and returns a new constraint cache ID. This function does not apply to layout constraint caches.

ciCacheMakeReadOnly.name: ciCacheMakeReadOnly
ciCacheMakeReadOnly.desc: Reopens the constraint cache in read-only mode and returns a new constraint cache ID. Any in modifications to the memory are discarded. This function does not apply to layout constraint caches.

ciCacheNeedRefresh.name: ciCacheNeedRefresh
ciCacheNeedRefresh.desc: Checks if the constraint cache has changed on the disk and needs to be refreshed.

ciCacheNotifications.name: ciCacheNotifications
ciCacheNotifications.desc: Enables or disables notifications related to the constraint cache. This function helps CAD teams in debugging.

ciCachep.name: ciCachep
ciCachep.desc: Checks if an object is a valid constraint cache ID.

ciCachePurge.name: ciCachePurge
ciCachePurge.desc: Purges a constraint cellview from virtual memory.

ciCacheTopCellName.name: ciCacheTopCellName
ciCacheTopCellName.desc: Returns the top cell name of the specified constraint cache. The top library, cell, and view refers to the schematic or layout cellview. If the cache is associated with a configuration or physical configuration, it is the top cell specified by the configuration.

ciCacheTopLibName.name: ciCacheTopLibName
ciCacheTopLibName.desc: Returns the top library name of the specified constraint cache. The top library, cell, and view refers to the schematic or layout cellview. If the cache is associated with a configuration or physical configuration, it is the top cell specified by the configuration.

ciCacheTopViewName.name: ciCacheTopViewName
ciCacheTopViewName.desc: Returns the top view name of the specified constraint cache. The top library, cell, and view refers to the schematic or layout cellview. If the cache is associated with a configuration or physical configuration, it is the top cell specified by the configuration.

ciCacheTransfer.name: ciCacheTransfer
ciCacheTransfer.syntax:
ciCacheTransfer(
u_fromCache
u_toCache
?conTypes s_conTypes
)
=> t / nil
ciCacheTransfer.desc:
Transfers constraints from the source cache to the specified target cache. The transfer can be restricted to constraints of a specified type. It cannot be used to transfer constraints between two schematics or two layouts.

Note: Before you run ciCacheTransfer, ensure that the schematic and layout windows are open in XL or a higher tier.

ciCacheTransferSelection.name: ciCacheTransferSelection
ciCacheTransferSelection.desc:
Transfers the selected constraints and templates from the source cache to the target cache in a session run in XL or above tier. If there are no selected constraints in the source cache, all the constraints and templates from the source cache are transferred to an editable target cache. When a constraint is transferred, the template within which it exists is also transferred along with all the other constraints inside the template.

Note: Before you run ciCacheTransferSelection, ensure that the schematic and layout windows are open in XL or above tier. The Constraint Manager assistant should also be open in the window from where the constraints need to be transferred.

ciCacheViewName.name: ciCacheViewName
ciCacheViewName.desc: Returns the view name of the specified constraint cache. The cache library, cell, and view refers to the schematic, configuration, physical configuration, or layout view that the constraint cache is associated with.

ciCheckConstraints.name: ciCheckConstraints
ciCheckConstraints.desc: Runs the constraint checker on the passed schematic or layout cellview if the cellview contains constraints.

ciCombineInstNetsPins.name: ciCombineInstNetsPins
ciCombineInstNetsPins.desc: This function is used within Circuit Prospector constraint generator expressions to turn a list of sub-lists into a single simple list. When the instsNetsPins information is represented as a list of sub-lists there is one sub-list each for instances, nets, pins, and instTerms. In addition, this function effectively flattens the sub-lists to leave a combined list of all the instances, nets, pins, and instTerms without sub-lists. The flattened list is in a form suitable to be used as the member list for ciConCreate.

ciConAppendOneMember.name: ciConAppendOneMember
ciConAppendOneMember.desc: Appends one constraint member to the given contstraint. The new member is added in the last position in the member list.

ciConBaseName.name: ciConBaseName
ciConBaseName.desc: Extracts and returns the basename from the specified constraint name. A constraint name consists of the basename and the counter added as a suffix. For example, in the constraint name, myConstraint_2, the basename is myConstraint and the counter is _2.

ciConCallbackIsRegistered.name: ciConCallbackIsRegistered
ciConCallbackIsRegistered.desc:
Checks whether a constraint callback has been registered.

See also ciConRegisterCallback, ciConUnregisterCallback, and ciConUpdateCallback.

ciConCreate.name: ciConCreate
ciConCreate.syntax:
ciConCreate( 
u_cache
d_constraintType
[ ?members l_memberList ]
[ ?params l_parameterList ]
[ ?name g_constraintName ]
[ ?axis g_axisName ]
[ ?note g_constraintNote ]
[ ?verbose g_verbose ]
)
=> u_constraint / nil

ciConCreateExpanded.name: ciConCreateExpanded
ciConCreateExpanded.syntax:
ciConCreateExpanded( 
u_cache
d_constraintType
[ ?members l_memberList]
[ ?params l_parameterList ]
[ ?name t_constraintName ]
[ ?axis t_axisName ]
[ ?note g_constraintNote ]
[ ?verbose g_verbose ]
)
=> l_constraints / nil
ciConCreateExpanded.desc: Expands vector names into groups of vector bit names in a constraint specific manner (when a constraint's member list contains vector names). Constraints are then created for each vector bit name grouping.

ciConDelete.name: ciConDelete
ciConDelete.desc: Deletes a constraint. After deleting the constraint, the u_constraint will be invalid.

ciConDeleteAll.name: ciConDeleteAll
ciConDeleteAll.desc: Deletes the specified constraints in a cellview.

ciConFind.name: ciConFind
ciConFind.desc: Finds a constraint in a given cache.

ciConGetAxisName.name: ciConGetAxisName
ciConGetAxisName.desc: Returns, for a given constraint, the axis name if one is associated with the given constraint.

ciConGetCache.name: ciConGetCache
ciConGetCache.desc: Returns the constraint cache that contains the given constraint.

ciConGetComment.name: ciConGetComment
ciConGetComment.desc: Returns the comment parameter of a constraint.

ciConGetCreatedTime.name: ciConGetCreatedTime
ciConGetCreatedTime.desc: Returns the created time of a constraint.

ciConGetMembersOfType.name: ciConGetMembersOfType
ciConGetMembersOfType.desc: Returns the constraint member list filtered by the passed member type.

ciConGetName.name: ciConGetName
ciConGetName.desc: Returns the name of a constraint.

ciConGetNote.name: ciConGetNote
ciConGetNote.desc: Returns the note parameter of a constraint.

ciConGetOwner.name: ciConGetOwner
ciConGetOwner.desc: Returns the library name, cell name, and view name of the cell where the passed constraint was created.

ciConGetPriority.name: ciConGetPriority
ciConGetPriority.desc: Returns the priority value of a constraint.

ciConGetStatus.name: ciConGetStatus
ciConGetStatus.desc: Returns the status of a constraint.

ciConIsInContext.name: ciConIsInContext
ciConIsInContext.desc: Returns the current context status of a constraint. A constraint is in context if all its members are in the database. For example, a net member can become out of context if the net is deleted from the database.

ciConIsOutOfContext.name: ciConIsOutOfContext
ciConIsOutOfContext.desc: Returns the current context status of a constraint. A constraint is out of context if one or more of its members are not in the database. For example, a net member can become out of context if the net is deleted from the database.

ciConIsOverridden.name: ciConIsOverridden
ciConIsOverridden.desc: Returns whether a constraint has been overridden.

ciConIsWritable.name: ciConIsWritable
ciConIsWritable.desc: Returns whether the constraint is writable.

ciConListMembers.name: ciConListMembers
ciConListMembers.syntax:
ciConListMembers( 
u_constraint
[ g_includeParameters ]
[ g_includeDefaults ]
)
=> l_memberList / nil
ciConListMembers.desc: Returns a list of constraint members and their member parameters, if any.

ciConListMemberNames.name: ciConListMemberNames
ciConListMemberNames.desc: Returns a list of strings where each string is a constraint member name. This function will only return member names as opposed to ciConListMembers which returns tuples containing member names and types.

ciConListParams.name: ciConListParams
ciConListParams.desc: Returns all parameters for a constraint.

ciConListParamNames.name: ciConListParamNames
ciConListParamNames.desc: Returns the legal parameter names for a given constraint.

ciConListTemplates.name: ciConListTemplates
ciConListTemplates.desc: Returns the list of templates of which the given constraint is a member.

ciConp.name: ciConp
ciConp.desc: Checks if an object is a valid constraint ID.

ciConRegisterCallback.name: ciConRegisterCallback
ciConRegisterCallback.desc:
Registers a constraint callback.

See also ciConCallbackIsRegistered, ciConUnregisterCallback, and ciConUpdateCallback.

ciConRemoveMembers.name: ciConRemoveMembers
ciConRemoveMembers.desc: Removes a list of members from a constraint.

ciConResetAllParams.name: ciConResetAllParams
ciConResetAllParams.desc: Resets all parameters on a constraint to their default values. Parameters can only be reset if the constraint view is currently writable.

ciConResetParams.name: ciConResetParams
ciConResetParams.desc: Resets a list of parameters to their default values.

ciConSetAxis.name: ciConSetAxis
ciConSetAxis.desc: Associates a given constraint with the named axis. If the constraint does not accept an axis, nil is returned, and if the axis does not exist it will be created.

ciConSetNote.name: ciConSetNote
ciConSetNote.desc: Replaces the note parameter of a constraint.

ciConSetPriority.name: ciConSetPriority
ciConSetPriority.desc: Sets the priority for a constraint.

ciConSetStatus.name: ciConSetStatus
ciConSetStatus.syntax:
ciConSetStatus( 
u_constraint
t_statusSymbol
g_statusValue
)
=> t / nil
ciConSetStatus.desc: Sets a given status flag for a constraint.

ciConstraintsForType.name: ciConstraintsForType
ciConstraintsForType.desc: Filters the list of constraints and returns the constraints of the specified type.

ciConstraintLCV.name: ciConstraintLCV
ciConstraintLCV.desc: Returns a list containing the library, cell, and view names of the specified constraint cache. The constraint library, cell, and view refers to the storage location of the constraints, which may be a constraint view or layout.

ciConstraintViewLessp.name: ciConstraintViewLessp
ciConstraintViewLessp.desc: Specifies a predicate function for sorting the constraint caches based on their library, cell, and view names.

ciConTypeHasNamedParameter.name: ciConTypeHasNamedParameter
ciConTypeHasNamedParameter.desc: Returns t if the passed constraint type has a parameter with a name matching the passed parameter name.

ciConUnregisterCallback.name: ciConUnregisterCallback
ciConUnregisterCallback.desc:
Unregisters a constraint callback.

See also ciConCallbackIsRegistered, ciConRegisterCallback, and ciConUpdateCallback.

ciConUpdateCallback.name: ciConUpdateCallback
ciConUpdateCallback.syntax:
ciConUpdateCallback( 
?name t_name
?type t_type
[ ?enabled g_enabled ]
)
=> t / nil
ciConUpdateCallback.desc:
Enables or disables a constraint callback.

See also ciConCallbackIsRegistered, ciConRegisterCallback, and ciConUnregisterCallback.

ciConUpdateMemberParams.name: ciConUpdateMemberParams
ciConUpdateMemberParams.desc: Updates the specified constraint member parameters with the given values without impacting other member parameters.

ciConUpdateMembers.name: ciConUpdateMembers
ciConUpdateMembers.desc: Used to update members and their parameters by replacing the members with the list contained in l_memberList.

ciConUpdateParams.name: ciConUpdateParams
ciConUpdateParams.desc: Updates parameter values with those values listed in l_parameterList.

ciConUprevCellBoundary.name: ciConUprevCellBoundary
ciConUprevCellBoundary.desc: Converts deprecated boundaryArea and areaUtilization constraints to cellBoundary constraints.

ciConVerify.name: ciConVerify
ciConVerify.desc: Runs the consistency checker on demand. The behavior of the consistency checker is based on the values provided for each argument.

ciConvertNestedNetClassToNetClassHierGro.name: ciConvertNestedNetClassToNetClassHierGroup
ciConvertNestedNetClassToNetClassHierGro.desc: Converts one or all nested Net Class constraints in a cache to corresponding Net Class Hier Group constraints. The name, members, and parameters of the original nested Net Class constraint remain the same after the conversion.

ciCreateFilter.name: ciCreateFilter
ciCreateFilter.desc: Defines a filter to show/hide constraints in the Constraint Manager.

ciCurrentPathIterator.name: ciCurrentPathIterator
ciCurrentPathIterator.desc: Finds the current path structure in Circuit Prospector. It is an iterator function that does not support hierarchy.

ciDefaultParamToMatchFilter.name: ciDefaultParamToMatchFilter
ciDefaultParamToMatchFilter.desc: The function for the default filter in the Match Subset Editor.

ciDeleteModgenTopologies.name: ciDeleteModgenTopologies
ciDeleteModgenTopologies.desc:
Deletes the database topology objects associated with the specified modgen along with the constraints on those topology objects.

See also ciSetModgenTopology for an example of how to create database topology objects for a modgen.

ciDeleteUnreferencedObjects.name: ciDeleteUnreferencedObjects
ciDeleteUnreferencedObjects.desc:
Deletes the unreferenced objects.

When a design contains unreferenced objects and you try to create contraints in it, the constraints might be out-of-context. In such a scenario, use this function before you start to create the constraints.

ciDesignLCV.name: ciDesignLCV
ciDesignLCV.desc: Returns a list containing the library, cell, and view names of the specified constraint cache. The design library, cell, and view refers to the schematic or layout cellview. If the cache is associated with a configuration or physical configuration, it is the top cell specified by the configuration.

ciEnableAutoConstraintNotes.name: ciEnableAutoConstraintNotes
ciEnableAutoConstraintNotes.desc: Provides an API alternative that allows you to enable or disable auto constraint notes.

ciExpandMembers.name: ciExpandMembers
ciExpandMembers.desc:
Expands any iterated or repeated member in the passed member list. For example, MN1<0:2> gets expanded to MN1<0>, MN1<1>, and MN1<2>. 

In the case of net repetitions, such as <*3>inp, by default these get expanded N times as inp, inp, inp. However, if the optional compress argument is set to t, then <*3>inp will be expanded to just inp. The same applies to net bundles that contain repetitions, such as <*3>inp, a, b, c, inp, inp will by default be expanded to inp, inp, inp, a, b, c, inp, inp but with compress set to t will be expanded to inp, a, b, c.

ciExpandName.name: ciExpandName
ciExpandName.desc:
This function is used within constraint generators to expand iterated, repeated, and bundled names for instances, nets, and pins into a list of individual bit names. This is necessary if these names are to be used in calls to ciConCreate(). 

As an alternative to calling ciExpandName() and prior to calling ciConCreate(), call ciConCreateExpanded(), which does a default expansion of the iterated, repeated, and bundled names.

ciFindOpenCellView.name: ciFindOpenCellView
ciFindOpenCellView.syntax:
ciFindOpenCellView( 
t_libName
t_cellName
t_viewName
t_constraintViewName
)
=> u_cache / nil
ciFindOpenCellView.desc:
Returns the open constraint cache for the library, cell, view, and constraint view. If the constraint cache is not already open, this SKILL function returns nil.

See also ciCacheFind that finds the constraint cache based on the constraint viewNameList.

See also ciFindOpenCellViews that allows a wider range of criteria to be matched.

ciFindConsWithDuplicateMembers.name: ciFindConsWithDuplicateMembers
ciFindConsWithDuplicateMembers.desc: Finds constraints with duplicate members and displays them in a list.

ciFindOpenCellViews.name: ciFindOpenCellViews
ciFindOpenCellViews.syntax:
ciFindOpenCellViews( 
[ ?cacheLib t_cacheLib ]
[ ?cacheCell t_cacheCell ]
[ ?cacheView t_cacheView ]
[ ?designLib t_designLib ]
[ ?designCell t_designCell ]
[ ?designView t_designView ]
[ ?constraintLib t_constraintLib ]
[ ?constraintCell t_constraintCell ]
[ ?constraintView t_constraintView ]
)
=> l_cacheIds / nil
ciFindOpenCellViews.desc:
Returns a list of open constraint caches that match the criteria specified by the optional keyed arguments. A constraint cache can be associated with the following three views:

1. The cache library, cell, and view refers to the schematic, configuration, physical configuration, or layout view that the constraint cache is associated with.

2. The design library, cell, and view refers to the schematic or layout cellview. If the cache is associated with a configuration or physical configuration, it is the top cell specified by the configuration.

3. The constraint library, cell, and view refers to the storage location of the constraints, which can be a constraint view or layout.

ciGetCellTermDefaultNetName.name: ciGetCellTermDefaultNetName
ciGetCellTermDefaultNetName.desc: Returns the default net name registered with a terminal for the cell name and terminal name that is passed.

ciGetCellView.name: ciGetCellView
ciGetCellView.syntax:
ciGetCellView( 
[ ?window d_window ]
[ ?findOnly g_findOnly ]
[ @rest rest ])
=> u_cache / nil
ciGetCellView.desc: Returns the constraint cellview associated with a schematic or layout window.

ciGetCellViewForObjectPath.name: ciGetCellViewForObjectPath
ciGetCellViewForObjectPath.desc: Retrieves the cellview ID from the specified path to an object. This function is used within constraint generators.

ciGetConnectedInsts.name: ciGetConnectedInsts
ciGetConnectedInsts.syntax:
ciGetConnectedInsts( 
d_cvID
l_nets
u_constraint
)
=> l_instsNets / nil
ciGetConnectedInsts.desc: Finds the instances to which all the nets in a constraint are connected and the corresponding connecting nets on which the constraint can be propagated.

ciGetCustomFilterNames.name: ciGetCustomFilterNames
ciGetCustomFilterNames.desc: Returns a list of registered custom filters (including the Default filter) for the Match Subset Editor.

ciGetDefaultNetName.name: ciGetDefaultNetName
ciGetDefaultNetName.desc: Returns the default net name registered with a terminal by specifying and an instance ID and a terminal name.

ciGetFoundryRules.name: ciGetFoundryRules
ciGetFoundryRules.desc: Returns the foundry constraint group for the given technology file.

ciGetMatchParam2DList.name: ciGetMatchParam2DList
ciGetMatchParam2DList.desc: Returns a 2D list (name-value pair) of CDF parameters present on the given instances as well as in the given holder list.

ciGetMembersOfType.name: ciGetMembersOfType
ciGetMembersOfType.syntax:
ciGetMembersOfType( 
l_instsNetsPins
s_type
[ ?includeType g_includeType ]
[ ?removeLeadingSlash g_removeLeadingSlash ]
[ ?expand g_expand ]
)
=> l_filteredList
ciGetMembersOfType.desc: Filters the instsNetsPins list used by constraint generators to only include members of a specified type. See also, ciConGetMembersOfType.

ciGetObjectCellView.name: ciGetObjectCellView
ciGetObjectCellView.desc: Used within constraint generators to retrieve the cellview associated with a particular object path. This SKILL function is similar to ciGetCellViewForObjectPath, but uses the cellview information associated with the cache if the object path does not contain a hierarchical path.

ciGetOpenCellViews.name: ciGetOpenCellViews
ciGetOpenCellViews.desc: Returns a list of open constraint caches in the virtual memory.

ciGetRuleGroupByName.name: ciGetRuleGroupByName
ciGetRuleGroupByName.syntax:
ciGetRuleGroupByName( 
[ d_techfile | d_cellView ]
t_name
)
=> oaConstraintGroup / nil
ciGetRuleGroupByName.desc: Returns the constraint group from the specified design or technology database with the specified name.

ciGetRuleGroupName.name: ciGetRuleGroupName
ciGetRuleGroupName.desc: Returns the string name of a constraint group from a given constraint group pointer.

ciGetRuleGroups.name: ciGetRuleGroups
ciGetRuleGroups.desc: Returns a list of oaConstraintGroup pointers for a given technology or design file.

ciGetWidgetProperties.name: ciGetWidgetProperties
ciGetWidgetProperties.desc: Returns the widget properties set on the constraint generator arguments, genArgs.

ciHasCellAnyRegTerm.name: ciHasCellAnyRegTerm
ciHasCellAnyRegTerm.desc: Returns information on whether or not the given cell has at least one terminal registered with a default net.

ciHaveSameBulkNets.name: ciHaveSameBulkNets
ciHaveSameBulkNets.desc: Returns t if the passed list of devices have the same bulk connection.

ciHierCompareConstraint.name: ciHierCompareConstraint
ciHierCompareConstraint.syntax:
ciHierCompareConstraint( 
u_sourceCons
u_targetCache
[ ?paths l_occurrencePaths ]
[ ?recursive g_recursive ]
)
=> constraintComparisons / nil
ciHierCompareConstraint.desc: Copies and compares applicable pushed or pulled constraints in the layout hierarchy. The copied constraint members, such as nets, terminals, instance terminals, and so on correspond to the original constraint members as they are physically connected.

ciHierCompareConstraints.name: ciHierCompareConstraints
ciHierCompareConstraints.syntax:
ciHierCompareConstraints( 
u_sourceCache
u_targetCache
[ ?paths l_occurrencePaths ]
[ ?recursive g_recursive ]
)
=> constraintComparisons / nil
ciHierCompareConstraints.desc: Compares applicable pushed or pulled constraints in the layout hierarchy. The copied constraint members (nets, terminals, instance terminals, and so on) correspond to the original constraint members because they are physically connected.

ciHierUpdateConstraints.name: ciHierUpdateConstraints
ciHierUpdateConstraints.syntax:
ciHierUpdateConstraints( 
u_sourceCache
u_targetCache
[ ?paths l_occurrencePaths ]
[ ?recursive g_recursive ]
)
=> t / nil
ciHierUpdateConstraints.desc: Used in sync with the pushed and pulled constraints with their source constraints. After push or pull the constraint parameters have been modified, you can use this SKILL function to update the pushed or pulled constraints.

ciIsNetSuperType.name: ciIsNetSuperType
ciIsNetSuperType.desc: Tests whether or not the given net type is a super-type.

ciLoadConfigXML.name: ciLoadConfigXML
ciLoadConfigXML.desc:
Loads the specified constraint config.xml file. In the process, the new entries get merged into the existing config.xml files that have already been loaded and the existing entries are overwritten.

When you start Virtuoso, all config.xml files found in the Cadence Search Path are loaded and merged based on the order in which they are found in the setup.loc file. By using this function, you can load a config.xml on demand after Virtuoso has been started, such as when a design library or PDK is loaded.

See also ciLoadDotCadenceFiles, ciLoadIcon, and ciLoadIcons.

ciLoadConfigXMLFromString.name: ciLoadConfigXMLFromString
ciLoadConfigXMLFromString.desc:
Loads the string representation of a config.xml file. If a new entry does not match an existing entry, the new entry gets added into the config.xml files that have already been loaded. However, if the new entry matches an existing entry, the new entry overwrites the old one.

When you start Virtuoso, all config.xml files found in the Cadence Search Path are loaded and merged based on the order in which they are found in the setup.loc file. By using this function, you can load a config.xml on demand after Virtuoso has been started, such as when a design library or PDK is loaded.

See also ciLoadConfigXML, ciLoadDotCadenceFiles, ciLoadIcon, and ciLoadIcons.

ciLoadConstrFrom.name: ciLoadConstrFrom
ciLoadConstrFrom.syntax:
ciLoadConstrFrom( 
t_sourceCache
t_targetCache
t_mode
)
=> t / nil
ciLoadConstrFrom.desc: Loads the constraints from the source cache to the target cache of the same type.

ciLoadDotCadenceFiles.name: ciLoadDotCadenceFiles
ciLoadDotCadenceFiles.desc: Loads all constraint-related files within the hierarchy of the specified .cadence directory.

ciLoadIcon.name: ciLoadIcon
ciLoadIcon.desc: Loads a specific PNG format icon file from the specified directory so that it can be used by the Constraint Manager. The file should have a .png extension.

ciLoadIcons.name: ciLoadIcons
ciLoadIcons.desc: Loads all PNG format icon files from the specified directory so that these can be used by the Constraint Manager. The file should have a .png extension.

ciListEditors.name: ciListEditors
ciListEditors.desc: Generates a list of the current constraint editors that are available from the Constraint Manager's Constraint Generator toolbar option.

ciListTypes.name: ciListTypes
ciListTypes.desc: Generates a list of the current definitions for each constraint type in the config.xml files, the name of the constraint, and a list of legal constraint parameters and their default values.

ciListProcessRules.name: ciListProcessRules
ciListProcessRules.desc: Lists all process rules associated with the given object.

ciLxComparisonReport.name: ciLxComparisonReport
ciLxComparisonReport.syntax:
ciLxComparisonReport( 
[ ?layoutCV g_layoutCV ]
[ ?showReport g_showReport ]
[ ?useViewNames g_useViewNames ]
[ ?useTimeStamp g_useTimeStamp ]
[ ?path g_path ]
[ ?filename g_filename ]
)
=> t / nil
ciLxComparisonReport.desc: Prints a comparison report between a layout and its corresponding VLS XL schematic and/or top configuration.

ciModgenMergeLayersFromArgs.name: ciModgenMergeLayersFromArgs
ciModgenMergeLayersFromArgs.syntax:
ciModgenMergeLayersFromArgs( 
l_args 
[ ?layersPresetArgName t_layersPresetArgName ]
[ ?mergeLayersArgName t_mergeLayersArgName ]
)
=> t_modgenLayers / null_string
ciModgenMergeLayersFromArgs.desc: Returns a string with the list of layers from a property list, where each layer is separated by a comma.

ciModgenListFingerSplitCons.name: ciModgenListFingerSplitCons
ciModgenListFingerSplitCons.desc:
Returns a list of fingerSplit constraints that exist on the passed modgen members. This SKILL function can be used in a template create or check callback function to include the fingerSplit constraints within a template.
Note: The fingerSplit constraints are not visible in the Constraint Manager assistant.

ciModgenRefreshStorage.name: ciModgenRefreshStorage
ciModgenRefreshStorage.desc: Reinitializes the internal modgen storage. When the ci SKILL functions are used to update a modgen constraint in layout or the modgen previewer, the internal modgen storage needs to be reinitialized to ensure it is in a consistent state. Modgen constraint updates include adding/removing members, updating parameters, and adding/removing guard rings.

ciModgenSplitFingers.name: ciModgenSplitFingers
ciModgenSplitFingers.syntax:
ciModgenSplitFingers( 
g_cache
g_modgen
l_instsNetsPins
g_split
)
=> l_instsNetsPins
ciModgenSplitFingers.desc: Splits or unsplits the device fingers for the instances specified in the instsNetsPins list associated with the passed modgen. When called in a layout view, the physical device instances are split or unsplit and the modgen figGroups are updated accordingly. When called in a schematic view, the finger split information is stored in the schematic constraints cache. This information is used while transferring the schematic constraints to layout, and splitting or unsplitting the instances in layout.

ciModgenTemplateFingerSplitPreDestroy.name: ciModgenTemplateFingerSplitPreDestroy
ciModgenTemplateFingerSplitPreDestroy.desc: Ensures that the split device instance fingers are unsplit and that the modgen figGroup is updated before the specified template is deleted. This high-level function should be used where modgens are contained within templates that control finger splitting on those modgens. To call this function before the template is deleted, it should be registered as the preDestroySymbolName of the template when the template is defined by using ciTemplateCreateDefinition.

ciObjectIsInContext.name: ciObjectIsInContext
ciObjectIsInContext.syntax:
ciObjectIsInContext( 
u_cache
t_designObjectName
t_designObjectType
)
=> t / nil
ciObjectIsInContext.desc: Returns the current context status of an object. If an object is in context, it is present in the database.

ciObjectListCon.name: ciObjectListCon
ciObjectListCon.syntax:
ciObjectListCon( 
u_cache
t_designObjectName
t_designObjectType
)
=> constraintIdList / nil
ciObjectListCon.desc: Lists all constraints that refer to a given design object as a member.

ciObjectPathAndName.name: ciObjectPathAndName
ciObjectPathAndName.desc: This function is used in constraint generators to separate the object path and name from a string. The result is returned as a disembodied property list with properties, such as objectPath and objectName. The objectPath property is a list of strings that represent the full hierarchical path to the object including the objects name.

ciOpenCellView.name: ciOpenCellView
ciOpenCellView.syntax:
ciOpenCellView(
t_libName
t_cellName
t_viewName
t_constraintViewName
t_mode
)
=> u_cache / nil
ciOpenCellView.desc:
Opens the constraint cache for the library, cell, view, and constraint view in read or edit mode as specified, and returns the constraint cache ID or returns nil if the constraint cache could not be opened. 

ciOpenCellView allows the mode to be specified. However, it does not downgrade the mode to read if the constraint cache is already open in edit mode. In this case, ciReopenCellView can be used to change the mode, if required. 

See also ciCacheGet that finds or opens the constraint cache based on the current constraint viewNameList instead of specifying a particular constraint view.

ciOpenPanicCellView.name: ciOpenPanicCellView
ciOpenPanicCellView.syntax:
ciOpenPanicCellView( 
t_libName
t_cellName
t_viewName
t_constraintViewName
)
=> u_cache / nil
ciOpenPanicCellView.desc: Restores the constraint cellview (associated with a schematic cellview) that was saved in panic state, which is when Virtuoso exited unexpectedly, in the hierDesign.oa- file. The restored constraint cellview opens in append mode. You can use the Constraint Manager to view this constraint cellview. This SKILL function returns a cache pointer of the restored constraint cellview. Use this cache pointer as an argument with the ciCacheSave SKILL function to save the restored constraint cellview. You can then open the recovered constraint cellview in the Constraint Manager.

ciPrintReport.name: ciPrintReport
ciPrintReport.syntax:
ciPrintReport( 
d_sourceCache
d_targetCache
[ t_fileName ]
[ g_includeDefaultParam ]
)
=> t / nil
ciPrintReport.desc: Generates an HTML report containing constraint differences between two designs.

ciPullConstraint.name: ciPullConstraint
ciPullConstraint.syntax:
ciPullConstraint( 
u_cons
u_targetCache
[ ?paths l_paths ]
[ ?autoTag g_autoTag ]
[ ?recursive g_recursive ]
[ ?update g_update ]
)
=> constraintIdList / nil
ciPullConstraint.desc: Copies a single constraint up the layout hierarchy.

ciPullConstraints.name: ciPullConstraints
ciPullConstraints.syntax:
ciPullConstraints( 
u_sourceCache
u_targetCache
[ ?paths l_paths ]
[ ?autoTag g_autoTag ]
[ ?recursive g_recursive ]
[ ?update g_update ]
)
=> constraintIdList / nil
ciPullConstraints.desc: Copies all applicable constraints up a layout hierarchy.

ciPushConstraint.name: ciPushConstraint
ciPushConstraint.syntax:
ciPushConstraint( 
u_constraint
[ ?paths l_paths ]
[ ?autoTag g_autoTag ]
[ ?recursive g_recursive ]
[ ?update g_update ]
)
=> constraintIdList / nil
ciPushConstraint.desc: Copies a single of constraint down a layout hierarchy.

ciPushConstraints.name: ciPushConstraints
ciPushConstraints.syntax:
ciPushConstraints( 
u_cache
[ ?paths l_paths ]
[ ?autoTag g_autoTag ]
[ ?recursive g_recursive ]
[ ?update g_update ]
)
=> constraintIdList / nil
ciPushConstraints.desc: Copies a set of constraints down a layout hierarchy.

ciRefreshCellView.name: ciRefreshCellView
ciRefreshCellView.desc: Refreshes the constraint cache in the virtual memory with the most current copy from the disk if it has changed.

ciRegisterConstraintEditor.name: ciRegisterConstraintEditor
ciRegisterConstraintEditor.syntax:
ciRegisterConstraintEditor( list(nil
'name t_name
'description t_description
'constraintType t_constraintType
'constraintParams l_constraintParams
'editorAvailableExpression t_editorAvailableExpression
'startEditorExpression t_startEditorExpression
'iconName t_iconName
'addToToolbar g_addToToolbar

'useForTemplateEdit g_useForTemplateEdit
'useForConstraintCreation g_useForConstraintCreation

'editableConstraintParams l_editableConstraintParams
)
=> t / nil
ciRegisterConstraintEditor.desc: Registers a constraint editor with the Constraint Manager assistant and, optionally, adds a button to the Constraint Manager toolbar. This button can be used to open the registered constraint editor. An entry is also added to the Constraint Editor submenu that appears on the context-sensitive menu of the Constraint Manager.

args.name:
list(nil
'name t_name
'description t_description
'constraintType t_constraintType
'constraintParams l_constraintParams
'editorAvailableExpression t_editorAvailableExpression
'startEditorExpression t_startEditorExpression
'iconName t_iconName
'addToToolbar g_addToToolbar
'templateTypes l_templateTypes
'useForTemplateEdit g_useForTemplateEdit
'useForConstraintCreation g_useForConstraintCreation
'useForConstraintParamEdit g_useForConstraintParamEdit
'editableConstraintParams l_editableConstraintParams

ciRegisterCustomDeviceFilter.name: ciRegisterCustomDeviceFilter
ciRegisterCustomDeviceFilter.desc: Registers a custom filter or modifies an existing filter.

ciRegisterNetSuperType.name: ciRegisterNetSuperType
ciRegisterNetSuperType.desc: This function creates a net type that automatically includes the names, regular expressions, and predicates registered in other net types. The new net type is known as a super-type, and the net types included in it as sub-types.

ciRegTypeBindingParameter.name: ciRegTypeBindingParameter
ciRegTypeBindingParameter.desc: Registers a binding parameter for a user-defined constraint type from a config.xml file. The parameter value must match for the constraints of that type to be considered equivalent between schematic and layout. Specifying an empty parameter name string unregisters the binding parameter.

ciRemoveConstrainedPinNetsFromRails.name: ciRemoveConstrainedPinNetsFromRails
ciRemoveConstrainedPinNetsFromRails.desc: Deletes any constraints on pins where the net on the pin is also a member of a rail constraint because this is currently not supported by the Analog Placer.

ciRemoveHierarchicalNotes.name: ciRemoveHierarchicalNotes
ciRemoveHierarchicalNotes.syntax:
ciRemoveHierarchicalNotes( 
t_libName
t_cellname
t_viewname
[ g_hierarchical ]
)
=> t / nil
ciRemoveHierarchicalNotes.desc: Removes the existing notes from the templates and constraints for a single cellview or all along the hierarchy beginning from the given cellview.
