[ ?listCellView g_listCellView ]
[ ?listOccurrences g_listOccurrences ]
) 
=> l_netExprEvalNames
schNetExprEvalNames.desc: Returns a list of evaluated names for all occurrences specified.

schPinListToSchem.name: schPinListToSchem
schPinListToSchem.syntax:
schPinListToSchem( 
t_libName 
t_cellName 
t_viewName 
g_pinList 
)
=> t / nil
schPinListToSchem.desc: Generates a schematic cellview from a pin list.

schPinListToSchemGen.name: schPinListToSchemGen
schPinListToSchemGen.syntax:
schPinListToSchemGen( 
t_libName 
t_cellName 
t_viewName 
g_pinList 
)
=> t / nil
schPinListToSchemGen.desc: Opens the Create Schematic form if t_viewName is a schematic.

schPinListToSymbol.name: schPinListToSymbol
schPinListToSymbol.syntax:
schPinListToSymbol( 
t_libName 
t_cellName 
t_viewName 
g_pinList 
)
=> t / nil
schPinListToSymbol.desc: Generates a symbol cellview from a pin list.

schPinListToSymbolGen.name: schPinListToSymbolGen
schPinListToSymbolGen.syntax:
schPinListToSymbolGen( 
t_libName 
t_cellName 
t_viewName 
g_pinList 
)
=> t / nil
schPinListToSymbolGen.desc: Generates a symbol cellview from a pin list.

schPinListToVerilog.name: schPinListToVerilog
schPinListToVerilog.syntax:
schPinListToVerilog( 
t_libName 
t_cellName 
t_viewName 
g_pinList 
)
=> t / nil
schPinListToVerilog.desc: Generates a Verilog HDL cellview from a pin list. The generated Verilog HDL cellview can be used with the Verilog integration.

schPinListToView.name: schPinListToView
schPinListToView.syntax:
schPinListToView( 
t_libName 
t_cellName 
t_viewName 
g_pinList 
t_toFunc 
)
=> t / nil
schPinListToView.desc: Generates a cellview from a pin list.

schPlot.name: schPlot
schPlot.desc: Generates a plot. The plot is defined in the t_file plot template file. If you do not specify t_file, this function uses the plot options stored in the schPlotOptions property list. If you backannotate the schematic and you specify w_windowId, the generated plot has backannotated values.

schProduceCVHierConfig.name: schProduceCVHierConfig
schProduceCVHierConfig.syntax:
schProduceCVHierConfig( 
s_visitCB
h_configId
[ h_pathVectId ]
)
=> t / nil
schProduceCVHierConfig.desc: Traverses a configuration design hierarchy and invokes a callback for each unique cellview.

schProduceUniqueCVHier.name: schProduceUniqueCVHier
schProduceUniqueCVHier.syntax:
schProduceUniqueCVHier( 
s_visitCB
d_topCellView
g_viewNameList
[ g_viewStopList ]
)
=> t / nil
schProduceUniqueCVHier.desc: Traverses a design hierarchy and invokes a procedure callback for each unique cellview.

schRegisterCheckGroup.name: schRegisterCheckGroup
schRegisterCheckGroup.syntax:
schRegisterCheckGroup( 
[ ?name s_name ]
[ ?title t_title ] 
[ ?description t_description ]
[ ?enabled g_enabled ]
)
=> r_checkgroup / nil
schRegisterCheckGroup.desc: Creates and registers a new custom schematic checker group. Each new group appears as a discrete tab in the Schematic Rules Checks Setup form. Calling the function with the same group name as an existing group overwrites that group and all its rules.

schRegisterCheckRule.name: schRegisterCheckRule
schRegisterCheckRule.syntax:
schRegisterCheckRule( 
[ ?title t_title ]
[ ?name s_name ]
[ ?groupName s_groupName ]
[ ?checkCB u_checkCB ]
[ ?configCB u_customCB ]
[ ?severity s_severity ]
[ ?description t_description ]
)
=> r_checkrule / nil
schRegisterCheckRule.desc: Creates and registers a new schematic rule checker. Calling this function with the same rule name as an existing rule in the same group overwrites that rule.

schReportCheckFailure.name: schReportCheckFailure
schReportCheckFailure.syntax:
schReportCheckFailure( 
[ ?object d_object ]
[ ?checkRule r_checkRule ]
[ ?message t_message ]
[ ?short t_short ]
)
=> t / nil
schReportCheckFailure.desc: Report the failure of a custom schematic check rule.

schRegisterFixedMenu.name: schRegisterFixedMenu
schRegisterFixedMenu.syntax:
schRegisterFixedMenu( 
t_category 
r_menuHandle 
[ s_disableTrigger ] 
[ s_enableTrigger ] 
)
=> t / nil
schRegisterFixedMenu.desc: Registers a vertical fixed-menu handle for specific cellview types to customize the schematic and symbol editor fixed menus. This function also registers triggers to enable and disable specific items in the fixed menu based on whether the editor window is in edit or read mode.

schRegisterPopUpMenu.name: schRegisterPopUpMenu
schRegisterPopUpMenu.syntax:
schRegisterPopUpMenu( 
t_category 
r_menuHandle 
t_mode 
)
=> t / nil
schRegisterPopUpMenu.desc: Replaces the object-sensitive menus (OSMs) of the schematic canvas with a specific object category and edit mode. This function should only be called after a schematic cellview has been opened and the schematic editor has been initialized. To ensure this, call schRegisterPopUpMenu() from a callback registered using deRegUserTriggers().

schRegPostCheckTrigger.name: schRegPostCheckTrigger
schRegPostCheckTrigger.desc: Registers a function that will be called after a schematic is checked using the Check - Current Cellview or Check - Hierarchy commands. The called function must be defined to accept three arguments: the cellview ID of the schematic, the number of errors encountered, and the number of warnings encountered during the check.

schRegPreCheckTrigger.name: schRegPreCheckTrigger
schRegPreCheckTrigger.desc: Registers a function that will be called before a schematic is checked using the Check - Current Cellview or Check - Hierarchy commands. The called function must be defined to accept one argument; that is the cellview ID of the schematic.

schReinitializeShapeStyles.name: schReinitializeShapeStyles
schReinitializeShapeStyles.desc: Updates the style of all schematic shapes in the current session to reflect any changes made in the Display Resource Editor. Use this function to refresh non-default shape styles, for example, custom wire line styles and colors.

schRemoveIgnoreProp.name: schRemoveIgnoreProp
schRemoveIgnoreProp.desc: Removes the specified ignore property from the registered ignore property set. You can view the registered ignore properties in the Ignore Properties tab by clicking Options - Editor.

schRenumberAllSheet.name: schRenumberAllSheet
schRenumberAllSheet.desc: Resequences all sheets starting at 1 and fills any holes in the sequence.

schRenumberInstances.name: schRenumberInstances
schRenumberInstances.syntax:
schRenumberInstances( 
g_objId 
[ t_scope ]
[ g_verbose ]
[ t_sequence ]
[ x_startIndex ]
[ t_applyTo [ t_libraryName t_cellName t_viewName ] ] 
)
=> t / nil
schRenumberInstances.desc: Resequences instances using the format instNamePrefix number that results in unique numbering indexes for each component name prefix encountered. Any voids in a numbering sequence are resolved by renaming instances with the highest numbers to fill the voids.

schRenumberSheet.name: schRenumberSheet
schRenumberSheet.syntax:
schRenumberSheet( 
d_cvId 
x_from 
x_to 
)
=> t / nil
schRenumberSheet.desc: Changes the number of a sheet in a multisheet schematic and changes the cell name of the renumbered schematic to match the destination sheet number. If a sheet already exists with the destination number, the new sheet is inserted before it and all succeeding sheets are renumbered accordingly.

schReplaceProperty.name: schReplaceProperty
schReplaceProperty.syntax:
schReplaceProperty( 
l_objId 
t_propName 
t_propValue 
)
=> t / nil
schReplaceProperty.desc: Changes the value of t_propName to t_propValue for the object. This function checks if the net, pin terminal, and master properties exist for the object.

schSaveCurrentPlotOptions.name: schSaveCurrentPlotOptions
schSaveCurrentPlotOptions.desc: Writes the current plot settings to a file.

schSchemToPinList.name: schSchemToPinList
schSchemToPinList.desc: Generates a pin list from a schematic cellview.

schSelectAllFig.name: schSelectAllFig
schSelectAllFig.desc: Selects all objects in a cellview that pass the selection filter.

schSelectPoint.name: schSelectPoint
schSelectPoint.syntax:
schSelectPoint( 
w_windowId 
l_pt 
g_isPartial 
g_isAdditive 
x_timeDelay 
)
=> t / nil
schSelectPoint.desc: Interactively selects the object under the cursor. With single selection, this function first deselects all objects on the selected set. With additive selection, this function maintains the selected set and adds the current object to the selected set.

schSetAndLoadTsgTemplateType.name: schSetAndLoadTsgTemplateType
schSetAndLoadTsgTemplateType.desc: Sets the tsgTemplateType environment variable and loads the corresponding tsg template file.

schSetBundleDisplayMode.name: schSetBundleDisplayMode
schSetBundleDisplayMode.desc: Takes a label Id whose display mode is to be changed and applies either a vertical or horizontal display value. This will only work when the cellview is editable.

schSetCmdOption.name: schSetCmdOption
schSetCmdOption.syntax:
schSetCmdOption( 
g_form 
s_field 
l_fieldValues 
x_key 
t_mousePrompt 
)
=> t / nil
schSetCmdOption.desc: Customizes which form fields are modified by calls to schCmdOption, middle mouse button, and schShiftCmdOption, Shift-middle mouse button, when the command is active.

schSetEnv.name: schSetEnv
schSetEnv.desc: Sets the value of a schematic environment variable.

schSetIgnorePropEnabled.name: schSetIgnorePropEnabled
schSetIgnorePropEnabled.desc: Enables or disables a particular ignore property. When you enable an ignore property, this property is applied on an instance while ignoring that instance.

schSetOrigin.name: schSetOrigin
schSetOrigin.desc: Repositions all the objects in the specified symbol or schematic cellview relative to the new point.

schSetPropertyDisplay.name: schSetPropertyDisplay
schSetPropertyDisplay.syntax:
schSetPropertyDisplay( 
?object d_object
[?name S_name]
?visibility S_visibility
)
=> l_textDisplays / nil
schSetPropertyDisplay.desc: Shows or hides textDisplays containing the name and value of the attribute, property, or parameter of an object. TextDisplay locations are chosen automatically to avoid overlaps with other textDisplays. For more information, see schGetPropertyDisplay and dbCreateTextDisplay.

schSetShapeStyle.name: schSetShapeStyle
schSetShapeStyle.syntax:
schSetShapeStyle(
d_shape 
[ ?color t_colorName ] 
[ ?lineStyle t_lineStyleName ] 
[ ?stipple t_stippleName ] 
[ ?fillStyle t_fillStyleName ] 
[ ?fillColor t_colorName ] 
)
=> t / nil
schSetShapeStyle.desc: Specifies the style attributes of a shape to override the defaults provided by the Display Resource file. Each attribute value must be valid for the current display name.

schSetSignalTypeIntegrity.name: schSetSignalTypeIntegrity
schSetSignalTypeIntegrity.syntax:
schSetSignalTypeIntegrity( 
t_netSigType
t_termNetSigType
t_termDirection
t_severity
)
=> t / nil
schSetSignalTypeIntegrity.desc: Sets the conflict severity for a signal type integrity check (available as part of Schematic Rule Checks) for connections between nets of a specified signal type, and instance pins of specified signal type and direction.

schSetSplitPrimaryInst.name: schSetSplitPrimaryInst
schSetSplitPrimaryInst.desc: Associates the given split instance with the given split-primary.

schSetSplitSymbol.name: schSetSplitSymbol
schSetSplitSymbol.desc: Sets up special properties on the cellview to make it a split symbol of g_isSplitSymbol is t. However, if  g_isSplitSymbol is nil, the specified cellview is converted to a normal symbol by stripping off the aforementioned properties.

schSetSymbolOrigin.name: schSetSymbolOrigin
schSetSymbolOrigin.desc: Moves all the objects in the specified symbol cellview relative to the given origin point.

schSetTextDisplayBBox.name: schSetTextDisplayBBox
schSetTextDisplayBBox.desc: Sets or updates the value of a bounding box that encloses a given textDisplay object. A text display object displays the string or value based on derived information; for example, the current value of a property. Accordingly, the software must update the bounding box that encloses the text display object when the derived string or value changes.

schSetWireColor.name: schSetWireColor
schSetWireColor.desc: Sets the color used to draw a wire segment.

schSetWireLineStyle.name: schSetWireLineStyle
schSetWireLineStyle.desc: Sets the line style used to draw a wire segment.

schShiftCmdOption.name: schShiftCmdOption
schShiftCmdOption.desc: Cycles through a predefined set of values. By default, this function is bound to the Shift-middle mouse button. When you click the middle mouse button while pressing the Shift key during an active command, the command applies the next value in the predefined set. You can customize the predefined set of values by making calls to schSetCmdOption.

schSingleSelectBox.name: schSingleSelectBox
schSingleSelectBox.desc: Selects objects within a rectangular area from a specified schematic editing window. With no arguments, it prompts you to enter the area to be selected in the current window. Partial selection is performed if the window environment variable partialSelect is set.

schSnapToConn.name: schSnapToConn
schSnapToConn.desc: Interactively connects a wire to the nearest connectivity object during the Create Wire command and the schematic snapEnabled environment variable is set.

schSnapToGrid.name: schSnapToGrid
schSnapToGrid.desc: Places the object on the grid in a schematic or symbol view.

schSolder.name: schSolder
schSolder.desc: Solders two wires together in a schematic. This function places the solder dot over the given point if it is a + or T- wire intersection.

schSplitNumber.name: schSplitNumber
schSplitNumber.desc: Used as an IL label on a split symbol. It provides the split index (starting from 1) to the instance on which the label is attached. When split instances are added to a schematic, it is useful to have a label on the instance that indicates the index of the split out of the total number splits for the device.

schSRC.name: schSRC
schSRC.desc: Runs the schematic rules checker (SRC) on a specified cellview.

schStretch.name: schStretch
schStretch.desc: The schStretch command can be used to stretch objects. The API takes a list of figIds and a transformation, and then stretches the specified figure in figId~>cellView by applying the transformation.

schSubSelectBox.name: schSubSelectBox
schSubSelectBox.syntax:
schSubSelectBox( 
[ w_windowId ] 
[ g_partial ] 
[ l_bBox ] 
)
=> t / nil
schSubSelectBox.desc: Deselects objects within a rectangular area from a specified schematic editor window. Implements the sub mode of area selection. With no arguments, it prompts you to enter the deselection area in the current window. Partial deselection is performed if the window environment variable partialSelect is set.

schSymbolToPinList.name: schSymbolToPinList
schSymbolToPinList.syntax:
schSymbolToPinList( 
t_libName 
t_cellName 
t_viewName 
)
=> g_pinList / nil
schSymbolToPinList.desc: Generates a pin list from a symbol cellview.

schSync.name: schSync
schSync.desc: Synchronizes the schematic and Cadence database (CDB) data representations.

schTraceNet.name: schTraceNet
schTraceNet.syntax:
schTraceNet(
?topCellView td_topCellView
?net td_net
[ ?viewList t_viewList ]
[ ?hierPath lt_hierPath ]
?traceCB su_traceCB
)
=> t / nil
schTraceNet.desc: Traces a schematic hierarchical net through the design hierarchy and calls a user-defined callback at each level of the hierarchy where the net is present. The user-defined callback is passed as an argument, a user type describing the occurrence of the net being traced at a specific location in the design hierarchy.

schUnregisterFixedMenu.name: schUnregisterFixedMenu
schUnregisterFixedMenu.desc: Unregisters the user-registered fixed menu for a specific cellview type and reassigns the default fixed menu.

schUnregisterPopUpMenu.name: schUnregisterPopUpMenu
schUnregisterPopUpMenu.desc: Unregisters the specific category and access mode for object-sensitive menus (OSMs) and reassigns the system default menus.

schUnregPostCheckTrigger.name: schUnregPostCheckTrigger
schUnregPostCheckTrigger.desc: Unregisters a post check trigger routine.

schUpdateUserSRCErrorAndWarn.name: schUpdateUserSRCErrorAndWarn
schUpdateUserSRCErrorAndWarn.desc: Increases the number of errors and warnings that are reported on the Schematic Check dialog box that appears after running the schematic rules checker (SRC) commands. This function is useful if you implement additional checks besides those provided by the schematic rules checker.

schVerilogToPinList.name: schVerilogToPinList
schVerilogToPinList.syntax:
schVerilogToPinList( 
t_libName 
t_cellName 
t_viewName 
)
=> g_pinList / nil
schVerilogToPinList.desc: Generates a pin list from a Verilog HDL cellview.

schVIC.name: schVIC
schVIC.desc: Runs the cross-view checker to check the consistency of the interface of one or more views against the view of the given cellview.

schViewToView.name: schViewToView
schViewToView.syntax:
schViewToView( 
t_sourceLibName 
t_sourceCellName 
t_libName 
t_cellName 
t_viewFrom 
t_viewTo 
t_fromFunc 
t_toFunc 
)
=> t / nil
schViewToView.desc: Generates one type of cellview from another.

schZoomFit.name: schZoomFit
schZoomFit.desc: Performs a zoom-to-fit with the given zoom scale values. If the schematic cellview contains a sheet border, the first zoom scale value is used. The second zoom scale value is used when there is no sheet border.

treeSaveHierarchy.name: treeSaveHierarchy
treeSaveHierarchy.desc: Saves the entire hierarchy including objects that are not visible (filter settings are ignored in the Navigator).

treeSaveScreen.name: treeSaveScreen
treeSaveScreen.desc: Saves the visible hierarchy (filter settings in the Navigator are taken into account).

tsg.name: tsg
tsg.desc: The tsg function is used to generate a schematicSymbol type cellview from a tsg (text-to-symbol generator) file. The tsg file, inputFile, is a simple text file that provides a textual description of the symbol.

lmCheckTerm.name: lmCheckTerm
lmCheckTerm.desc: Checks the consistency of terminal name, type, and wth for all views of each specified cell.

lmCheckView.name: lmCheckView
lmCheckView.desc: Evaluates a sequence of expressions for each specified cellview. Checks the property value for consistency.

lmCloseLib.name: lmCloseLib
lmCloseLib.desc: Closes the previously opened working library.

lmDefTermProp.name: lmDefTermProp
lmDefTermProp.syntax:
lmDefTermProp( 
[ t_cellName ] 
[ t_viewName ] 
( g_terminalList t_propertyName t_propertyValue ... t_propertyName = t_propertyValue ) 
( g_terminalList t_propertyName = t_propertyValue ... t_propertyName t_propertyValue ) 
)
lmDefTermProp.desc: Adds properties to the terminals of the specified cellview. To add terminal properties, add specified properties to the original property list and save the new file.

lmDefViewProp.name: lmDefViewProp
lmDefViewProp.syntax:
lmDefViewProp( 
[ t_cellName ] 
[ t_viewName ] 
( t_propertyName t_propertyValue ... t_propertyName t_propertyValue )
)
lmDefViewProp.desc: Adds properties to the specified cellview. To add properties, add the specified properties to the original property list and save the new file.

lmDeleteTermProp.name: lmDeleteTermProp
lmDeleteTermProp.syntax:
lmDeleteTermProp( 
d_cellList 
t_viewName 
( g_terminalList ... t_propertyName g_terminalList ... t_propertyName ) 
)
lmDeleteTermProp.desc: Deletes specified properties from the terminals of specified views.

lmDeleteViewProp.name: lmDeleteViewProp
lmDeleteViewProp.desc: Deletes specified properties from the specified view.

lmGetValue.name: lmGetValue
lmGetValue.desc: Returns the value of a specified view property in the current referenced view.

lmLoadData.name: lmLoadData
lmLoadData.syntax:
lmLoadData( 
t_file 
t_lib [ { t_path | nil } [ { t_config | nil } [ { t_mode | nil } ] ] ] 
) 
=> t / nil
lmLoadData.desc: Opens a working library, loads the library command file, and closes the library when you are finished.

args.name: { t_path | nil } [ { t_config | nil } [ { t_mode | nil } ] ]

lmOpenLib.name: lmOpenLib
lmOpenLib.syntax:
lmOpenLib( 
t_lib [ { t_path | nil } [ { t_config | nil } [ { t_mode | nil } ] ] ] 
) 
=> t / nil

args.name: { t_path | nil } [ { t_config | nil } [ { t_mode | nil } ] ]

lmPrintLibTermProp.name: lmPrintLibTermProp
lmPrintLibTermProp.desc: Prints terminal properties of the specified view for each cell in the current library.

lmPrintLibViewProp.name: lmPrintLibViewProp
lmPrintLibViewProp.desc: Prints properties of the specified view for each cell in the current library.

lmPrintTerm.name: lmPrintTerm
lmPrintTerm.desc: Prints names, types, and wths of all terminals of the specified cellviews.

lmPrintTermProp.name: lmPrintTermProp
lmPrintTermProp.desc: Prints properties of all terminals of the specified views of a cell.

lmPrintViewProp.name: lmPrintViewProp
lmPrintViewProp.desc: Prints properties of all specified views of a cell.

lmReset.name: lmReset
lmReset.desc: Resets all global variables to their default values.

lmSimView.name: lmSimView
lmSimView.syntax:
lmSimView( 
t_cellName 
t_templateViewName 
t_targetViewName 
[ t_targetViewtype ]
t_propertyName = t_propertyValue ... t_propertyName t_propertyValue 
)
lmSimView.desc: Creates a view with specified properties for the specified cell.

simRep.name: simRep
simRep.syntax:
simRep(
t_cellName 
t_templateViewName 
t_targetViewName 
[ t_targetViewtype ]
t_propertyName = t_propertyValue ... t_propertyName t_propertyValue 
)
simRep.desc: Creates a view with specified properties for the specified cell. Use this function only for backward compatibility with Edge 2.1; otherwise, use the lmSimView function.

asiDigitalSimAutoloadProc.name: asiDigitalSimAutoloadProc
asiDigitalSimAutoloadProc.desc: Automatically loads the context for class and tool initialization when you launch SystemVerilog Netlister.

rodAddMPPChopHole.name: rodAddMPPChopHole
rodAddMPPChopHole.syntax:
rodAddMPPChopHole(
R_rodObj
l_pts
);end rodAddMPPChopHole
=> t / nil
rodAddMPPChopHole.desc: Adds a chop hole to all choppable parts of a ROD multipart path. To define a chop hole, you specify a list of points on the centerline of the master path. The results depend on whether the master path is choppable or not.

rodAddPoints.name: rodAddPoints
rodAddPoints.syntax:
rodAddPoints(
l_point1
l_point2
);end rodAddPoints
=> l_point / nil
rodAddPoints.desc: Adds two points together and returns the resulting point as l_point.

rodAddSubPart.name: rodAddSubPart
rodAddSubPart.syntax:
rodAddSubPart(
R_rodObjId
t_subpartType
l_subpartParamList
);end rodAddSubPart
=> R_rodSubpartId / nil
rodAddSubPart.desc: Creates a new subpart of the type specified by t_subpartType with the given list of parameters (l_subpartParamList) and adds it to an existing multipart path (MPP).

rodAddToX.name: rodAddToX
rodAddToX.syntax:
rodAddToX(
l_point
n_num
);end rodAddToX
=> l_point / nil
rodAddToX.desc: Adds a number to the X coordinate of l_point and returns the resulting point as l_point.

rodAddToY.name: rodAddToY
rodAddToY.syntax:
rodAddToY(
l_point
n_num
);end rodAddToY
=> l_point / nil
rodAddToY.desc: Adds a number to the Y coordinate of l_point and returns the resulting point as l_point.

rodAlign.name: rodAlign
rodAlign.syntax:
rodAlign(		
[ ?alignObj R_alignObj ]
[ ?alignHandle S_alignHandle ]
[ ?refObj R_refObj ]
[ ?refHandle S_refHandle ]
[ ?refPoint l_refPoint ]
[ ?maintain g_maintain ]
[ ?xSep txf_xSep ]
[ ?ySep txf_ySep ]
);end rodAlign
=> R_rodObj / nil
rodAlign.desc: Aligns a named object by a point handle on that object to a specific point or to a point handle on a reference object. You can align objects that are at different levels of hierarchy as long as both objects are in the same top-level layout cellview. You can specify positive or negative separation between alignment points in the direction of both the X and Y axes, either as absolute distances or with Cadence SKILL language expressions. The system applies the offset from the reference point or reference object to the object to be aligned.

rodAssignHandleToParameter.name: rodAssignHandleToParameter
rodAssignHandleToParameter.syntax:
rodAssignHandleToParameter(		
[ ?parameter S_parameter ]
[ ?rodObj R_rodObj ]
[ ?handleName Sl_handleName ]
[ ?displayName S_displayName ]
[ ?displayExpression S_displayExpression ]
[ ?stretchDir S_stretchDir ]
[ ?stretchType S_stretchType ]
[ ?moveOrigin g_moveOrigin ]
[ ?updateIncrement f_updateIncrement ]
[ ?userData g_userData ]
[ ?userFunction Sl_userFunction ]
[ ?stretchKey S_stretchKey ]
[ ?shape S_shape ]
);end rodAssignHandleToParameter
=> t / nil
rodAssignHandleToParameter.desc: Assigns one or more user- or system-defined point handles on a ROD object within a SKILL-based parameterized cell (Pcell) to a single Pcell parameter, so you can change the value of the parameter by graphically stretching the handle(s). Stretching a handle has the same effect as changing the value of the associated parameter for the Pcell instance using the Edit Properties form. You cannot stretch handles on the Pcell master. All rodAssignHandleToParameter statements must occur within the body-of-code section of a SKILL-based Pcell.

rodCheck.name: rodCheck
rodCheck.syntax:
rodCheck(		
d_cvID 
[ g_createMarkers ]
); end rodCheck
=> Rl_rodObj
rodCheck.desc: Searches the specified cellview for multipart paths (MPPs) for which the geometry does not match the definition information, and returns a list of the ROD object IDs. The MPPs found by this function include those that have lost their subshape definition information. By default, this function places warning markers over the potentially affected MPPs. (If you do not want to see warning markers, set the g_createMarkers argument to nil.) Although subparts with missing definition information are still visible graphically, their definitions have been deleted from the database. Editing an affected MPP causes an immediate loss of the subpart graphics.

rodCheckAllMPPsInCellView.name: rodCheckAllMPPsInCellView
rodCheckAllMPPsInCellView.syntax:
rodCheckAllMPPsInCellView(		
t_libName 
t_cellName 
t_viewName 
g_fix 
g_createMarkers
); end rodCheckAllMPPsInCellView
=> l_defectiveMPPIds / nil
rodCheckAllMPPsInCellView.desc: Finds and opens the design specified by t_libName, t_cellName, and t_viewName, and checks if any MPP in the design contains defective internal data. If MPPs containing defective internal data are found, rodCheckAllMPPsInCellView fixes them and creates markers on them depending on the values of g_fix and g_createMarkers arguments.

rodCheckMPPs.name: rodCheckMPPs
rodCheckMPPs.syntax:
rodCheckMPPs(		
d_cellViewId 
R_rodObj | list(R_rodObj ...) 
g_fix 
g_createMarkers
);end rodCheckMPPs
=> l_defectiveMPPIds / nil
rodCheckMPPs.desc: Checks if the given list of multipart paths (MPPs) contains corrupt internal data. If MPPs containing defective internal data are found, rodCheckMPPs fixes or creates markers to highlight them, or does both.

rodCreateHandle.name: rodCreateHandle
rodCreateHandle.syntax:
rodCreateHandle(	
[ ?name S_name ]
[ ?type S_type ]
[ ?value g_value ]
[ ?rodObj R_rodObj ]
);end rodCreateHandle
=> t / nil
rodCreateHandle.desc: Creates a user-defined handle for any ROD object (named shape, instance, or cellview); the object must be at level zero in the hierarchy. For example, you can create a handle for polyRect or for instance I1, but not for I1/polyRect.

rodCreatePath.name: rodCreatePath
rodCreatePath.syntax:
rodCreatePath(	
[ ?name S_name]
[ ?layer txl_layer ]
[ ?width n_width ]
[ ?pts l_pts ]
[ ?justification S_justification ]
[ ?offset n_offset ]
[ ?endType S_endType ]
[ ?beginExt n_beginExt ]
[ ?endExt n_endExt ]
[ ?choppable g_choppable ]
[ ?cvId d_cvId ]
[ ?fromObj Rl_fromObj ]
[ ?size txf_size ]
[ ?startHandle l_startHandle ]
[ ?endHandle l_endHandle ]
[ ?prop l_prop ]
	
[rodConnectivityArgs...  ]
	;start ROD Connectivity Arguments (rodConnectivityArgs)
	[ ?netName S_netName ]
	[ ?termName S_termName ]
	[ ?termIOType S_termIOType ]
	[ ?pin g_pin ]
	[ ?pinAccessDir tl_pinAccessDir ]
	[ ?pinLabel g_pinLabel ]
	[ ?pinLabelHeight n_pinLabelHeight ]
	[ ?pinLabelLayer txl_pinLabelLayer ]
	[ ?pinLabelFont S_pinLabelFont ]
	[ ?pinLabelDrafting g_pinLabelDrafting ]
	[ ?pinLabelOrient S_pinLabelOrient ]
	[ ?pinLabelOffsetPoint l_pinLabelOffsetPoint ]
	[ ?pinLabelJust S_pinLabelJust ]
	[ ?pinLabelRefHandle S_pinLabelRefHandle ]
	;end ROD Connectivity Arguments

[ ?offsetSubPath            l_offsetSubpathArgs... ]
;start Offset Subpath Arguments (l_offsetSubpathArgs)
list(
	list(
		[ ?layer txl_layer ]
		[ ?width n_width ]
		[ ?choppable g_choppable ]
		[ ?sep n_sep ]
		[ ?justification S_justification ]
		[ ?beginOffset n_beginOffset ]
		[ ?endOffset n_endOffset ]
		[ ?prop l_prop ]
		;repeat ROD Connectivity Arguments here
	);end first offset subpath list
		...
	);end offset subpath lists
;end Offset Subpath Arguments

[ ?encSubPath        l_encSubpathArgs...  ]
;start Enclosure Subpath Arguments (l_encSubpathArgs)
list(
	list(
		[ ?layer txl_layer ]
		[ ?enclosure n_enclosure ]
		[ ?choppable g_choppable ]	
		[ ?beginOffset n_beginOffset ]
		[ ?endOffset n_endOffset ]
		[ ?prop l_prop ]
		;repeat ROD Connectivity Arguments here
	);end first enclosure subpath list
		...
	;end of enclosure subpath lists
;end Enclosure Subpath Arguments

[ ?subRect l_subrectArgs...  ]
;start Subrectangle Arguments (l_subrectArgs)
list(
	list(
		[ ?layer txl_layer ]
		[ ?width n_width ]
		[ ?length n_length ]
		[ ?choppable g_choppable ]
		[ ?sep n_sep ]
		[ ?justification S_justification ]
		[ ?space n_space ]	
		[ ?beginOffset n_beginOffset ]
		[ ?endOffset n_endOffset ]
		[ ?beginSegOffset n_beginSegOffset ]
		[ ?endSegOffset n_endSegOffset ]
		[ ?prop l_prop ]
		[ ?gap S_gap ]
		;repeat ROD Connectivity Arguments here
		[ ?diagonal g_diagonalSubRect  ]
	);end first subrectangle list
		 ...		
	;end subrectangle lists
  );end Subrectangle Arguments
);end rodCreatePath

=> R_rodObj / nil
rodCreatePath.desc: Creates a path consisting of one or more parts at level zero in the hierarchy on the same or on different layers from a list of points or from one or more existing objects. A path consisting of multiple parts is called a multipart path. You can use the rodCreatePath function to create one-part paths, simple multipart paths, or complex multipart paths such as guard rings, transistors, buses, and shielded paths. You can assign one or more property names and values to a multipart path.

rodCreatePolygon.name: rodCreatePolygon
rodCreatePolygon.syntax:
rodCreatePolygon(		
[ ?name S_name ]
[ ?layer txl_layer ]
[ ?pts l_pts ]
[ ?cvId d_cvId ]
[ ?fromObj Rl_fromObj ]
[ ?size txf_size ]
[ ?prop l_prop ]
; ROD Connectivity Arguments for Polygons
[ ?netName S_netName ]
[ ?termName S_termName ]
[ ?termIOType S_termIOType ]
[ ?pin g_pin ]
[ ?pinAccessDir tl_pinAccessDir ]
[ ?pinLabel g_pinLabel ]
[ ?pinLabelHeight n_pinLabelHeight ]
[ ?pinLabelLayer txl_pinLabelLayer ]
[ ?pinLabelFont S_pinLabelFont ]
[ ?pinLabelDrafting g_pinLabelDrafting ]
[ ?pinLabelOrient S_pinLabelOrient ]
[ ?pinLabelOffsetPoint l_pinLabelOffsetPoint ]
[ ?pinLabelJust S_pinLabelJust ]
[ ?pinLabelRefHandle S_pinLabelRefHandle ]
);end rodCreatePolygon
=> R_rodObj / nil
rodCreatePolygon.desc: Creates one polygon from a list of points or from one or more named objects. Also creates a ROD object containing information associated with the polygon, including its name and database ID. The associated ROD object is identified by a ROD object ID. The polygon is created at level zero in the hierarchy. You can assign a property name and value, or a list of property names and values, to the polygon. You can specify connectivity for the polygon by associating it with a specific terminal and net. You can also make the polygon into a pin.

rodCreateRect.name: rodCreateRect
rodCreateRect.syntax:
rodCreateRect(	
[ ?name S_name ]
[ ?layer txl_layer ]
[ ?width n_width ]
[ ?length n_length ]
[ ?origin l_origin ]
[ ?bBox l_bBox ]
[ ?elementsX x_elementsX ]
[ ?elementsY x_elementsY ]
[ ?spaceX n_spaceX ]
[ ?spaceY n_spaceY ]
[ ?cvId d_cvId ]
[ ?fillBBox l_fillBBox ]
[ ?fromObj Rl_fromObj ]
[ ?size txf_size ]
[ ?prop l_prop ]
[ ?returnBoolean g_returnBoolean ]
	
[rodRectConnectivityArgs... ]
	; start ROD Connectivity Arguments for Rectangles (rodRectConnectivityArgs)
	[ ?netName S_netName ]
	[ ?termName S_termName ]
	[ ?termIOType S_termIOType ]
	[ ?pin g_pin ]
	[ ?pinAccessDir tl_pinAccessDir ]
	[ ?pinLabel g_pinLabel ]
	[ ?pinLabelHeight n_pinLabelHeight ]
	[ ?pinLabelLayer txl_pinLabelLayer ]
	[ ?pinLabelFont S_pinLabelFont ]
	[ ?pinLabelDrafting g_pinLabelDrafting ]
	[ ?pinLabelOrient S_pinLabelOrient ]
	[ ?pinLabelOffsetPoint l_pinLabelOffsetPoint ]
	[ ?pinLabelJust S_pinLabelJust ]
	[ ?pinLabelRefHandle S_pinLabelRefHandle ]
	;end ROD Connectivity Arguments for Rectangles

[ ?subRectArray     l_subrectArgs... ]
;start l_subrectArgs Subrectangle Arguments (l_subrectArgs)
list(
	list(
		[ ?layer txl_layer  ]
		[ ?width n_width ]
		[ ?length n_length ]
		[ ?gap S_gap ]
		[ ?lowerLeftOffsetX n_lowerLeftOffsetX ]
		[ ?lowerLeftOffsetY n_lowerLeftOffsetY ]
		[ ?upperRightOffsetX n_upperRightOffsetX ]
		[ ?upperRightOffsetY n_upperRightOffsetY ]
		[ ?spaceX n_spaceX ]
		[ ?spaceY n_spaceY ]
		[ ?prop l_prop ]
	;Repeat ROD Connectivity Arguments here
	);end first subrectangle list
	...		
	) ;end all subrectangle lists
;end l_subrectArgs
);end rodCreateRect

=> R_rodObj | t / nil
rodCreateRect.desc: Creates a single named rectangle, one or more rows and/or columns of named rectangles, or fills a bounding box with named rectangles, where each rectangle has ROD attributes. You can create these named rectangles with the arguments S_name through g_returnBoolean. Each named rectangle is a separate object, created at level zero in the hierarchy. You can also create multipart rectangles by specifying one or more arrays of unnamed subrectangles for each named rectangle, where each unnamed subrectangle is an ordinary database shape, with no ROD attributes, created at level zero in the hierarchy. The named rectangles in a multipart rectangle are referred to as master rectangles.

rodDeleteHandle.name: rodDeleteHandle
rodDeleteHandle.syntax:
rodDeleteHandle(	
R_rodObj
S_name
);end rodDeleteHandle
=> t / nil
rodDeleteHandle.desc: Deletes a user-defined handle. You provide the ROD object ID and handle name.

rodDeleteSubPart.name: rodDeleteSubPart
rodDeleteSubPart.syntax:
rodDeleteSubPart(	
R_rodObjId
t_subpartName
);end rodDeleteSubPart
=> t / nil
rodDeleteSubPart.desc: Deletes the named subpart from the given multipart path (MPP).

rodFillBBoxWithRects.name: rodFillBBoxWithRects
rodFillBBoxWithRects.syntax:
rodFillBBoxWithRects(	
[ ?cvId d_cvId ]
[ ?layer txl_layer ]
[ ?fillBBox l_fillBBox ]
[ ?width n_width ]
[ ?length n_length ]
[ ?gap S_gap ]
[ ?spaceX n_spaceX ]
[ ?spaceY n_spaceY ]
[ ?prop l_prop ]
[ ?returnBoolean g_returnBoolean ]
);end rodFillBBoxWithRects
=> d_dbId / t / nil
rodFillBBoxWithRects.desc: Fills a bounding box with rectangles, as many as fit within the bounding box you specify. The rectangles are ordinary unnamed shapes, identified by database IDs; the rectangles have no ROD attributes. You can assign a property name and value, or a list of property names and values, to the set of rectangles. The property or list of properties apply to every rectangle in the bounding box. You specify the return value of the function to be Boolean or a list of the database IDs for the rectangles. When you want to create a one- or two-dimensional array of rectangles, and the rectangles do not need to be ROD objects, use this function instead of rodCreateRect because regular database shapes require less overhead, contributing to faster performance.

rodFillWithRects.name: rodFillWithRects
rodFillWithRects.syntax:
rodFillWithRects(
[ ?shapeId d_shapeID ]
[ ?fillShapeLPP lpp ]
[ ?fillShapeWidth n_width ]
[ ?fillShapeLength n_length ]
[ ?gap S_gap ]
[ ?justification S_justification ]
[ ?keepOut l_ptList ]
[ ?spaceX n_spaceX ]
[ ?spaceY n_spaceY ]
[ ?enclosureX n_encX ]
[ ?enclosureY n_encY ]
[ ?grid n_grid ]
[ ?outputFillShape l_dbId ]
);end rodFillWithRects
=> t / nil
rodFillWithRects.desc: Fills a base shape with rectangles. The base shape can be a rectangle, polygon or a path type.

rodGetBBox.name: rodGetBBox
rodGetBBox.syntax:
rodGetBBox(	
[ ?figId d_figId ]
[ ?layer t_layer ]
[ ?purpose t_purpose ]
[ ?stopLevel x_stopLevel ]
[ ?filterText g_filterText ]
);end rodGetBBox
=> l_bBox / nil
rodGetBBox.desc: Returns the coordinates of the rectangular bounding box enclosing all the elements of a specified figure on a specified layer. You can optionally limit the calculation to include only elements on a specified layer purpose and down to a specified level of design hierarchy. You can also exclude labels and text displays from the calculation.

rodForceUpdate.name: rodForceUpdate
rodForceUpdate.desc: Applies all ROD update requests in the queue.

rodGetHandle.name: rodGetHandle
rodGetHandle.syntax:
rodGetHandle(	
R_rodObj
S_name
);end rodGetHandle
=> g_handleValue / nil
rodGetHandle.desc: Returns the value of a system- or user-defined handle. You specify the handle name and the ROD object ID for the object with which the handle is associated.

rodGetNamedShapes.name: rodGetNamedShapes
rodGetNamedShapes.desc: Returns a list of the ROD object IDs for all named shapes (rectangles, polygons, and paths) at level zero in the hierarchy within the specified cellview that are ROD objects. This function looks only at the top level of hierarchy and does not return the ROD object ID for instances or cellviews.

rodGetObj.name: rodGetObj
rodGetObj.syntax:
rodGetObj(	
S_hierarchicalName | d_dbId
[d_cellViewId]
); end rodGetObj
=> R_rodObj / nil
rodGetObj.desc: Lets you find a named object at any level of hierarchy in your cellview. You must specify either the database ID for the object or its hierarchical name. If you specify the hierarchical name, you must also specify the cellview ID. When you specify a cellview ID, it is not necessary to also specify the database ID; however, if you specify both, the cellview ID must be correct for the database ID you specify. If your rodGetObj statement occurs in the code for a Pcell (in the body of a pcDefinePCell function or tcCreateCDSDeviceClass function call), specifying the cellview ID is optional; if you do not specify it, the cellview ID defaults to pcCellView or tcCellView, respectively.

rodGetSubPart.name: rodGetSubPart
rodGetSubPart.syntax:
rodGetSubPart(	
R_rodObjId
t_subpartName
);end rodGetSubPart
=> R_rodSubpartId / nil
rodGetSubPart.desc: Returns the subpart ID corresponding to the specified subpart name for the multipart path (MPP) specified as rodObjectId.

rodIsFigNameUnused.name: rodIsFigNameUnused
rodIsFigNameUnused.desc: Determines whether the name specified by S_name is a valid name and whether it is already assigned to a ROD object, instance, or mosaic in the cellview specified by d_cvId. A valid name cannot contain hierarchy (indicated by one or more slashes) and cannot be an empty string.

rodIsHandle.name: rodIsHandle
rodIsHandle.syntax:
rodIsHandle(	
R_rodObj
S_name
);end rodIsHandle
=> t / nil
rodIsHandle.desc: Determines whether the name specified for S_name identifies a valid system- or user-defined handle associated with the object specified by R_rodObj. Use this function prior to the rodGetHandle function when you want to verify that the handle exists before you try to access it.

rodIsMasterChoppable.name: rodIsMasterChoppable
rodIsMasterChoppable.desc: Returns the value of the MPP master path choppability attribute.

rodIsObj.name: rodIsObj
rodIsObj.desc: Determines whether the object specified for g_object identifies a valid ROD object. This function is useful for testing variables and parameters to see if they contain a ROD object ID.

rodNameObject.name: rodNameObject
rodNameObject.syntax:
rodNameObject	(
[ ?name S_name ]
[ ?shapeId d_shapeId ]
[ ?permitRename g_permitRename ]
);end rodNameObject
=> R_rodObj / nil
rodNameObject.desc: Assigns a name to an unnamed database shape or renames a ROD shape. Once the object is named, it can identified by a ROD object ID. This is an alias to an existing public function, rodNameShape.

rodNameShape.name: rodNameShape
rodNameShape.syntax:
rodNameShape(	
[ ?name S_name ]
[ ?shapeId d_shapeId ]
[ ?permitRename g_permitRename ]
);end rodNameShape
=> R_rodObj / nil
rodNameShape.desc: Assigns a name to an unnamed database shape or renames a ROD shape. Creates (or updates) a ROD object containing information associated with the shape, including its name and database ID. The associated ROD object is identified by a ROD object ID. Optionally, you can specify whether to rename an existing ROD object.

rodPointX.name: rodPointX
rodPointX.desc: Returns the X coordinate of the point specified by l_point.

rodPointY.name: rodPointY
rodPointY.desc: Returns the Y coordinate of the point specified by l_point.

rodSetMasterChoppable.name: rodSetMasterChoppable
rodSetMasterChoppable.desc: Sets the choppability attribute of an MPP master path to the specified value.

rodSubPoints.name: rodSubPoints
rodSubPoints.syntax:
rodSubPoints(
l_point1	
l_point2
) ;end rodSubPoints
=> l_point / nil
rodSubPoints.desc: Subtracts l_point2 from l_point1 and returns the resulting point as l_point.

rodUnAlign.name: rodUnAlign
rodUnAlign.desc: When you specify only one ROD object ID, removes all alignments for the object specified. When you specify two ROD object IDs, removes only the alignment between the two objects.

rodUnNameShape.name: rodUnNameShape
rodUnNameShape.desc: Removes the name from a named shape or list of named shapes. The ROD object ID for the shape and all user-defined handles associated with it are deleted. If the object is an instance, the instance keeps its name but all user-defined handles associated with the instance are deleted. Also removes all alignment constraints that reference the shape.

rodCoordBisect.name: rodCoordBisect
rodCoordBisect.desc: Divides the input value by two (bisect). You can optionally set the argument that rounds off the calculated value, truncates it, or converts it based on the defined maximum ceiling.

rodCoordCreate.name: rodCoordCreate
rodCoordCreate.syntax:
rodCoordCreate(
g_inputValue [ S_unitType [ S_snapType ] ]
[ x_resolution ]
);end rodCoordCreate
=> o_rodCoordObj
rodCoordCreate.desc: Creates a rodCoord object from the given value, that is, g_inputValue.

rodCoordDefineGrid.name: rodCoordDefineGrid
rodCoordDefineGrid.desc: Defines the grid and the arithmetic resolution factor values, which are used by the rodCoord* API.

rodCoordFix.name: rodCoordFix
rodCoordFix.desc: Fixes the rodCoord object and returns a new rodCoord object using the fix() SKILL function.

rodCoordGetGrid.name: rodCoordGetGrid
rodCoordGetGrid.desc: Returns the grid value (defined by rodCoordDefineGrid) as a rodCoord object.

rodCoordIsOnGrid.name: rodCoordIsOnGrid
rodCoordIsOnGrid.syntax:
rodCoordIsOnGrid(
o_rodCoord
[ n_gridValue ]
);end rodCoordIsOnGrid
=> t / nil
rodCoordIsOnGrid.desc: Checks if the data in the given rodCoord object is on the grid or not.

rodCoordParseString.name: rodCoordParseString
rodCoordParseString.desc: Creates a rodCoord object out of t_rodString generated by the rodCoordToString function.

rodCoordPartition.name: rodCoordPartition
rodCoordPartition.desc: Performs a division on the given arguments - dividend and divisor.

rodCoordSnap.name: rodCoordSnap
rodCoordSnap.syntax:
rodCoordSnap(
o_rodCoord
[[ S_snapType ] 
[ n_gridValue ]]
);end rodCoordSnap
=> o_rodCoord
rodCoordSnap.desc: Snaps a rodCoord object so that its value is on the grid.

rodCoordToFloat.name: rodCoordToFloat
rodCoordToFloat.desc: Returns the rodCoord data in user unit as floating point number.

rodCoordToInt.name: rodCoordToInt
rodCoordToInt.desc: Returns the rodCoord data in user unit as a fixed number.

rodCoordToString.name: rodCoordToString
rodCoordToString.desc: Returns a string containing the rodCoord data in user unit as floating number.

awvAddSubwindow.name: awvAddSubwindow
awvAddSubwindow.desc: Adds a subwindow to the specified Waveform window.

awvAnalog2Digital.name: awvAnalog2Digital
awvAnalog2Digital.syntax:
awvAnalog2Digital(
o_waveform
n_vhi
n_vlo
n_vc
n_timeX
t_thresholdType
[ ?releaseMemory g_releaseMemory ]
=> o_digWave / n_digValue / nil
awvAnalog2Digital.desc: Returns the digital form of the analog input, which can be a waveform, a list or family of waveforms, or a string representation of expressions.

awvAppendExpression.name: awvAppendExpression
awvAppendExpression.syntax:
awvAppendExpression(
w_windowID
t_expr
l_context

[ ?index l_waveIndexList ]
[ ?color l_colorList ]

[ ?dataSymbol l_symbolList ]
[ ?barBase t_barBase ]
[ ?barWidth t_barWidth ]
[ ?barShift t_barShift ]
[ ?subwindow x_subwindow ]
)
=> t / nil
awvAppendExpression.desc: Evaluates the t_expr expression and adds the resulting waveforms to a subwindow.

awvAppendList.name: awvAppendList
awvAppendList.syntax:
awvAppendList(
w_windowID
l_yListList
l_xList
[ ?expr l_exprList ]
[ ?index l_waveIndexList ]
[ ?color l_colorList ]
[ ?lineType l_lineTypeList ]

[ ?showSymbols l_showList ]
[ ?dataSymbol l_symbolList ]
[ ?barBase t_barBase ]
[ ?barWidth t_barWidth ]
[ ?barShift t_barShift ]
[ ?subwindow x_subwindow ]
)
=> t / nil
awvAppendList.desc: Plots y values in l_yListList against x values in l_xListList and adds the resulting waveforms to a subwindow.

awvAppendWaveform.name: awvAppendWaveform
awvAppendWaveform.syntax:
awvAppendWaveform(
w_windowID
l_waveformList

)

awvAppendWaveform.desc: Plots the waveforms in the list l_waveformList and appends them in a subwindow of the specified Waveform window.

awvClearSubwindowHistory.name: awvClearSubwindowHistory
awvClearSubwindowHistory.desc: Erases the contents from a subwindow of the specified Waveform window.

awvClearPlotWindow.name: awvClearPlotWindow
awvClearPlotWindow.desc: Clears the graphs shown in the specified Waveform window. History for the window and the subwindows are maintained.

awvClearWindowHistory.name: awvClearWindowHistory
awvClearWindowHistory.desc: Erases the contents of the specified Waveform window.

awvCloseCalculator.name: awvCloseCalculator
awvCloseCalculator.desc: Closes the Calculator invoked from the current session or from the specified session.

awvCloseWindowMenuCB.name: awvCloseWindowMenuCB
awvCloseWindowMenuCB.desc: Closes the current window. This function is defined in dfII/etc/context/awv.cxt.

awvCreateBusFromWaveList.name: awvCreateBusFromWaveList
awvCreateBusFromWaveList.desc: Creates a digital bus from a list of specified digital waveforms.

awvCreatePlotWindow.name: awvCreatePlotWindow
awvCreatePlotWindow.desc: Creates a Waveform window and returns its window ID.

awvDeleteAllWaveforms.name: awvDeleteAllWaveforms
awvDeleteAllWaveforms.desc: Deletes all waveforms from a subwindow of the specified Waveform window.

awvDeleteMarker.name: awvDeleteMarker
awvDeleteMarker.syntax:
awvDeleteMarker(
w_windowID
t_bookmarkIDs
[ ?subwindow x_subwindow ]
)
=> t / nil
awvDeleteMarker.desc: Deletes the specified bookmarks from a subwindow of the specified Waveform window.

awvDeleteSubwindow.name: awvDeleteSubwindow
awvDeleteSubwindow.desc: Deletes a subwindow from the specified Waveform window.

awvDeleteWaveform.name: awvDeleteWaveform
awvDeleteWaveform.syntax:
awvDeleteWaveform(
w_windowID
x_index
[ ?subwindow x_subwindow ]
)
=> t / nil
awvDeleteWaveform.desc: Deletes the specified waveform from a subwindow of the specified Waveform window.

awvDigital2Analog.name: awvDigital2Analog
awvDigital2Analog.syntax:
awvDigital2Analog(
o_waveform
n_vHi
n_vLo

=> o_waveform / f_avgPower / f_peakPower / nil
rfWrlsCcdfValues.desc: Plots the complementary cumulative distribution function (CCDF) curve or calculates the average or peak power from the results of an envelope (ENVLP) wireless simulation.

rfWrlsCim3Value.name: rfWrlsCim3Value
rfWrlsCim3Value.desc: Returns the value of third-order counter-intermodulation (CIM3) calculated for the specified probe.

rfWrlsCim5Value.name: rfWrlsCim5Value
rfWrlsCim5Value.desc: Returns the value of fifth-order counter-intermodulation (CIM5) calculated for the specified probe.

rfWrlsMeasContour.name: rfWrlsMeasContour
rfWrlsMeasContour.syntax:
rfWrlsMeasContour(
t_sig
[ ?maxValue n_maxVaue ]
[ ?minValue n_minValue ]
[ ?numCont n_numCont ]
[ ?closeCont g_closeCont ]
[ ?modifier t_modifier ]
)
=> n_family / nil
rfWrlsMeasContour.desc: Draws contours of system measurements from simulation results of envelope loadpull analysis.

calcVal.name: calcVal
calcVal.desc: Stores the output value from one test and passes it on to another test.

d2a.name: d2a
d2a.desc: Returns the analog output from a given digital waveform.

dBm.name: dBm
dBm.desc: Returns 10 times the log10 of the specified waveform object plus 30. This function converts a signal, in watts, to dbm, where dbm=10*log(x)+30.

harmonicFreq.name: harmonicFreq
harmonicFreq.desc: Returns the frequency(s) of the harmonic waveform for the specified harmonic. This function is available only in the SKILL mode.

loadpull.name: loadpull
loadpull.desc: Plots load pull contour for the given waveform of PSS analysis. This function works only for two-dimensional sweep PSS results. The inner sweep should be phase and the outer sweep should be magnitude.

risetime.name: risetime
risetime.desc: Returns the rise time for a signal, which is the time taken by a signal to change from a specified low value to a specified high value. Typically, these values are 10% and 90% of the step height.

rms_jitter.name: rms_jitter
rms_jitter.desc: Returns the root mean square jitter value in the specified frequency range. The RMS jitter value is calculated based on the following equation:

dB10.name: dB10
dB10.desc: Converts a signal to dB by using the following equation:

dB20.name: dB20
dB20.desc: Converts a signal to dB by using the following equation:

cosh.name: cosh
cosh.desc: Returns the hyperbolic cosine of a signal.

acosh.name: acosh
acosh.desc: Returns the inverse hyperbolic cosine or hyperbolic arc-cosine of a signal.

sinh.name: sinh
sinh.desc: Returns the hyperbolic sine of a signal.

asinh.name: asinh
asinh.desc: Returns the inverse hyperbolic sine or hyperbolic arc-sine of a signal.

tanh.name: tanh
tanh.desc: Returns the hyperbolic tangent of a signal.

atanh.name: atanh
atanh.desc: Returns the inverse hyperbolic tangent or hyperbolic arc tangent of a signal.

Rn.name: Rn
Rn.desc: Returns the equivalent noise resistance as a function of frequency. This function is available only on a 2-port network from that uses a S-Parameter analysis.

gac_freq.name: gac_freq
gac_freq.desc: Returns the available power gain circles where the gain is fixed and frequency is swept.

gac_gain.name: gac_gain
gac_gain.desc: Returns the available power gain circles where the frequency is fixed and gain is swept.

gpc_freq.name: gpc_freq
gpc_freq.desc: Returns the operating power gain circles where the gain is fixed and frequency is swept.

gpc_gain.name: gpc_gain
gpc_gain.desc: Returns the operating power gain circles where the frequency is fixed and gain is swept.

nc_freq.name: nc_freq
nc_freq.desc: Returns noise circles with fixed gain.

nc_gain.name: nc_gain
nc_gain.desc: Returns noise circles with fixed frequency.

rn.name: rn
rn.desc: Returns the normalized equivalent noise resistance as a function of frequency. This function is available only for a 2-port network from running an S-Parameter analysis.

s11.name: s11
s11.desc: Returns s11 of a two-port network. S-parameters describe the response of an N-port network to voltage signals at each port. The first number in the subscript refers to the responding port, while the second number refers to the incident port. Therefore, S11 means the response at port1 due to a signal at port 1.

s12.name: s12
s12.desc: Returns s12 of a two-port network. S-parameters describe the response of an N-port network to voltage signals at each port. The first number in the subscript refers to the responding port, while the second number refers to the incident port. Therefore, S12 means the response at port1 due to a signal at port 2.

s21.name: s21
s21.desc: Returns s21 of a two-port network. S-parameters describe the response of an N-port network to voltage signals at each port. The first number in the subscript refers to the responding port, while the second number refers to the incident port. Therefore, S21 means the response at port 2 due to a signal at port 1.

s22.name: s22
s22.desc: Returns s22 of a two-port network. S-parameters describe the response of an N-port network to voltage signals at each port. The first number in the subscript refers to the responding port, while the second number refers to the incident port. Therefore, S22 means the response at port 2 due to a signal at port 2.

pcExprToString.name: pcExprToString
pcExprToString.desc: Converts a SKILL expression to a string. The Pcell compiler uses this function to create labels that display the value of an expression as a string enclosed in quotes.

pcTechFile.name: pcTechFile
pcTechFile.desc: Evaluates an expression contained in a string. The Pcell compiler uses this function as an envelope around stretch expressions that access information from a technology file. This function prevents any symbols used in the technology file access expression from being defined as parameters of the Pcell.

auHiUltraPCell.name: auHiUltraPCell
auHiUltraPCell.desc: Displays the Ultra Pcell form to let you create an Ultra Pcell by compiling multiple Pcells into one cell. Optionally, you can save the Ultra Pcell SKILL code in a file by specifying the t_filename argument. For a description of Ultra Pcells, see Make Ultra Pcell Command

pcColinearPoints.name: pcColinearPoints
pcColinearPoints.syntax:
pcColinearPoints(
l_pointList1
l_pointList2
l_pointList3
) 
=> t / nil
pcColinearPoints.desc: Verifies whether the three coordinates specified are collinear lying on or passing through the same straight line and orthogonal parallel to the X or Y axis.

pcConcatOrient.name: pcConcatOrient
pcConcatOrient.desc: Concatenates two specified object orientations into one.

pcDefineCondition.name: pcDefineCondition
pcDefineCondition.syntax:
pcDefineCondition(
d_cvId
l_figs
l_namelist
g_condition
g_stretch
f_adjust 
) 
=> d_condId / nil
pcDefineCondition.desc: Specifies that the conditional inclusion of a list of objects is controlled by a given SKILL expression. Also specifies the inclusion of a dependent stretch control line. If the SKILL expression evaluates to a value other than nil, the objects are included.

pcDefineInheritParam.name: pcDefineInheritParam
pcDefineInheritParam.syntax:
pcDefineInheritParam(
d_instId
s_parameter
g_value
l_namelist
) 
=> d_inheritGroup / nil
pcDefineInheritParam.desc: Specifies that a parameter of an instance of a Pcell takes its value from a parameter definition of the enclosing cellview. The selection filter allows you to select only instances.

pcDefineParamCell.name: pcDefineParamCell
pcDefineParamCell.desc: Allows you to compile a graphical Pcell (super) master in the database from the cellview you specify. If you do not compile a Pcell before you place an instance of it in another design, the system interprets the design as a standard fixed cell instead of a Pcell. Each time you edit a graphical Pcell, you must recompile it so that all placed instances reflect the changes.

pcDefineParamLabel.name: pcDefineParamLabel
pcDefineParamLabel.desc: Defines a parameterized label. A parameterized label is not an instance name, but a label displaying values within a Pcell, such as width and height of gates. This function should be used only when creating graphical Pcells.

pcDefineParamLayer.name: pcDefineParamLayer
pcDefineParamLayer.syntax:
pcDefineParamLayer(
d_cvId
l_shapes
g_layerExpr
l_namelist
[ g_purposeExpr ]
) 
=> d_paramLayerId
pcDefineParamLayer.desc: Specifies that a set of shapes has its layer and purpose determined by a parameter definition in the cellview. The selection filter prevents you from selecting instances or stretch control lines.

pcDefineParamPath.name: pcDefineParamPath
pcDefineParamPath.syntax:
pcDefineParamPath(
d_pathId
S_param
g_margin
g_width
n_defaultWidth
t_snap
l_namelist
) 
=> d_paramShapeId
pcDefineParamPath.desc: Defines a path that has its vertices determined by a parameter of the cell. When you place the Pcell, you enter a coordinate string that is used as the vertices of the parameterized path. You can use this function more than once in a cellview if all paths have the same vertices.

pcDefineParamPolygon.name: pcDefineParamPolygon
pcDefineParamPolygon.syntax:
pcDefineParamPolygon(
d_polygonId
S_param
g_margin
t_snap
l_namelist
) 
=> d_paramShapeId
pcDefineParamPolygon.desc: Defines a polygon that has its vertices determined by a parameter of the cell. When you place the Pcell, you enter a coordinate string that is used as the vertices of the parameterized polygon. You can use this function more than once in a cellview.

pcDefineParamProp.name: pcDefineParamProp
pcDefineParamProp.syntax:
pcDefineParamProp(
d_cvId
t_name
g_expr
) 
=> t / nil
pcDefineParamProp.desc: Defines a parameterized property that can be accessed using a SKILL procedure. You can use this property to store any value within the Pcell.

pcDefineParamRect.name: pcDefineParamRect
pcDefineParamRect.syntax:
pcDefineParamRect(
d_rectangleId
S_param
g_margin
l_namelist
) 
=> d_paramShapeId
pcDefineParamRect.desc: Defines a rectangle that has its vertices determined by a parameter of the cell. When you place the Pcell, you enter two coordinates that are used as the vertices of the parameterized rectangle. You can use this function more than once in a cellview.

pcDefineParamRefPointObject.name: pcDefineParamRefPointObject
pcDefineParamRefPointObject.desc: Specifies that the location of an object or group of objects in the instance is determined by the location of a reference point that is a parameter of the cell. The objects in the instance have the same relationship to the reference point parameter as the objects in the master cellview have to the corresponding reference point in the master cellview.

pcDefineParamSlot.name: pcDefineParamSlot
pcDefineParamSlot.desc: Constructs a parameter DPL, which is used to define a parameter slot of the specified device.

pcDefinePathRefPointObject.name: pcDefinePathRefPointObject
pcDefinePathRefPointObject.desc: Specifies that the location of an object or group of objects in the instance be determined by the location of the endpoint of a parameterized path. The objects in the instance have the same relationship to the endpoint of the digitized path in the instance as the objects in the master cellview have to the corresponding endpoint of the parameterized path in the master cellview.

pcDefinePCell.name: pcDefinePCell
pcDefinePCell.syntax:
pcDefinePCell(
l_cellIdentifier
l_formalArgs
body_of_code
) 
=> d_cellViewId / nil
pcDefinePCell.desc: Creates parameterized (super) master cellview. This function enables you to pass a SKILL definition for a Pcell including a list of its parameters.

pcDefinePPCell.name: pcDefinePPCell
pcDefinePPCell.syntax:
pcDefinePPCell(
l_cellIdentifier
l_overrideCodeParams
l_defaultCodeParams
ls_formalArgs
body_of_code
) 
=> d_cellViewId / nil
pcDefinePPCell.desc:
Creates a parameterized Pcell master cellview (P2cell) that enables you to pass the SKILL definition for a Pcell, including a list of its arguments, similar to the pcDefinePCell function. This function also accepts a code argument declaration list and a code argument override list, where the code parameter can be used in the Pcell code body to create multiple Pcell super masters from a single Pcell code.

Within pcDefinePPCell, the override code parameter is always a simple variable, which receives the input provided by the caller of pcDefinePPCell. This will always be the use model of P2cell because there is always a driver function that calls it. The function should not be used as a top-level function (not inside a procedure) because that will lose the purpose of the new parameterization feature.

pcDefineRepeat.name: pcDefineRepeat
pcDefineRepeat.syntax:
pcDefineRepeat(
d_cvId
l_shapes
l_namelist
g_stepX
g_stepY
g_repeatX
g_repeatY
g_stretchX
g_stretchY
g_adjustX
g_adjustY
t_direction
)
=> d_repeatId
pcDefineRepeat.desc: Defines a repetition parameter to be applied to specified objects. Objects can be repeated in the X direction, Y direction, or both. If the value for the repetition direction, t_direction, is horizontal and vertical, the pcDefineRepeat function creates a two-dimensional array.

pcDefineSteppedObject.name: pcDefineSteppedObject
pcDefineSteppedObject.syntax:
pcDefineSteppedObject(
g_objects
S_param
g_step
g_startOffset
g_endOffset
l_namelist
) 
=> d_stepObjectId
pcDefineSteppedObject.desc: Defines an object or group of objects to be repeated along the length or perimeter of a parameterized shape that has already been defined in the Pcell. The selection filter prevents you from selecting stretch control lines, parameterized shapes, or objects in other repeat-along-shape groups.

pcDefineStretchLine.name: pcDefineStretchLine
pcDefineStretchLine.syntax:
pcDefineStretchLine(
d_lineId
g_paramExpr 
t_direction 
f_defval
f_minval 
f_maxval 
g_stretchRepeated
) 
=> d_StretchId
pcDefineStretchLine.desc: Defines a stretch control line used to control stretching in the X direction or Y direction. Objects repeated in the direction parallel to the stretch direction can be set to stretch.

pcDeleteCondition.name: pcDeleteCondition
pcDeleteCondition.desc: Deletes a previously defined conditional inclusion parameter.

pcDeleteParam.name: pcDeleteParam
pcDeleteParam.desc: Deletes the definition of the parameter identified by t_paramName. It is recommended to use pcHIEditParameters instead of this function.

pcDeleteParamLayer.name: pcDeleteParamLayer
pcDeleteParamLayer.desc: Deletes a parameter associating a set of shapes with a layer parameter.

pcDeleteParamProp.name: pcDeleteParamProp
pcDeleteParamProp.desc: Deletes a parameterized property in the cellview d_cvId.

pcDeleteParamShape.name: pcDeleteParamShape
pcDeleteParamShape.desc: Deletes a parameterized shape directive, causing the specified shape to revert back to a regular (nonparameterized) shape.

pcDeleteRefPoint.name: pcDeleteRefPoint
pcDeleteRefPoint.desc: Deletes a reference point parameter. You can use this command to delete either a reference point defined relative to a parameter of the cell or a reference point defined relative to a parameterized path endpoint.

pcDraw.name: pcDraw
pcDraw.desc: Creates database objects for the specified SKILL++ Pcell class. This method is implemented for each SKILL++ Pcell class. pcDraw is called by the Pcell source code in pcDefinePCell for the associated Pcell.

pcExprToProp.name: pcExprToProp
pcExprToProp.desc: Evaluates the argument and returns a list containing the data type and value of the result.

pcFilterPoints.name: pcFilterPoints
pcFilterPoints.desc: Determines whether the specified list of coordinates represents a manhattan shape.

pcFix.name: pcFix
pcFix.desc: Converts a number to an integer in the format fixnum. When n_num is close to a whole number, the system keeps the integer part of the number and adds a single decimal place equal to zero. Here, close means the value of the number is within the range of plus or minus the value of f_precision of the integer part of the number specified by n_num. When the value is not within this range, the function allows the system to use the value in the first decimal place to round the n_num to an integer in the format number.0; the system ignores all other decimal places. This function is useful for correcting the round-off approximation that can occur with floating-point numbers that are stored in 32 or 64 bits.

pcGetBendAngle.name: pcGetBendAngle
pcGetBendAngle.desc: Determines whether the specified list of three coordinates represents a bend to the left (+90 degrees) or to the right (-90 degrees). The three coordinates must define a 90 degree angle.

pcGetCodeParamNames.name: pcGetCodeParamNames
pcGetCodeParamNames.desc: Returns a list of all the defined code parameter names for the specified design ID.

pcGetCodeParamValue.name: pcGetCodeParamValue
pcGetCodeParamValue.desc: Returns the value of a specified code parameter.

pcGetConditions.name: pcGetConditions
pcGetConditions.desc: Returns a list of identifiers for conditional inclusion parameters in the specified cellview.

pcGetDefaultParamsFromClass.name: pcGetDefaultParamsFromClass
pcGetDefaultParamsFromClass.desc: Displays the defined Pcell parameter list from the specified class name.

pcGetInheritParamDefn.name: pcGetInheritParamDefn
pcGetInheritParamDefn.desc: Returns an identifier for an inherited parameter in the specified cellview.

pcGetInheritParams.name: pcGetInheritParams
pcGetInheritParams.desc: Returns a list of identifiers for inherited parameters in the specified cellview.

pcGetOffsetPath.name: pcGetOffsetPath
pcGetOffsetPath.syntax:
pcGetOffsetPath(
d_cvId
l_vertex_points
n_offset
)
=> l_vertex_points / nil
pcGetOffsetPath.desc: Applies the offset to each vertex of the path to create a list of vertices for a longer or shorter version of the path. Returns a list of points for the vertices of the offset version of the path. This function does not change the original path and does not create the offset version of the path

pcGetOffsetPolygon.name: pcGetOffsetPolygon
pcGetOffsetPolygon.syntax:
pcGetOffsetPolygon(
d_cvId
l_vertex_points
n_offset
)
=> l_vertex_points / nil
pcGetOffsetPolygon.desc: Applies the offset to each edge of the polygon to create a list of the vertices for an oversized or undersized version of the polygon. Returns a list of points for the vertices of the offset version of the polygon. This function does not change the original polygon and does not create the offset version of the polygon

pcGetParameters.name: pcGetParameters
pcGetParameters.desc: Returns a list of parameters and their default values defined in the specified cellview.

pcGetParamLabelDefn.name: pcGetParamLabelDefn
pcGetParamLabelDefn.desc: Returns the parameterized label identifier resulting from a call to pcDefineParamLabel on the specified label.

pcGetParamLabels.name: pcGetParamLabels
pcGetParamLabels.desc: Returns a list of parameterized labels in the specified cellview.

pcGetParamLayerDefn.name: pcGetParamLayerDefn
pcGetParamLayerDefn.desc: Returns the identifier for a layer parameter of a specified shape.

pcGetParamLayers.name: pcGetParamLayers
pcGetParamLayers.desc: Returns a list of identifiers for layer parameters in the specified cellview.

pcGetParamProps.name: pcGetParamProps
pcGetParamProps.desc: Lists parameterized properties in the specified cellview.

pcGetParamShapeDefn.name: pcGetParamShapeDefn
pcGetParamShapeDefn.desc: Returns an identifier for a parameterized shape parameter resulting from a call to pcDefineParamPath, pcDefineParamPolygon, or pcDefineParamRect.

pcGetParamShapes.name: pcGetParamShapes
pcGetParamShapes.desc: Returns a list of identifiers for the parameterized shape parameters in the specified cellview.

pcGetParamSlotType.name: pcGetParamSlotType
pcGetParamSlotType.desc: Checks the type contained in the parameter slot propName of the given device. Parameter type is a string whose value is int, float, string, or iLList.

pcGetParamSlotValue.name: pcGetParamSlotValue
pcGetParamSlotValue.desc: Returns the value of the parameter slot, propName, of the specified device.

pcGetPathRefPoint.name: pcGetPathRefPoint
pcGetPathRefPoint.syntax:
pcGetPathRefPoint(
d_cvId
l_objectVertices
l_pathVertices
t_endpoint
l_offset
)
=> l_newObjVertices / nil
pcGetPathRefPoint.desc: Creates a list of coordinates representing the object specified by the l_objectVertices argument when offset from the specified endpoint of the parameterized path, where the offset is defined by l_offset and the path is defined l_pathVertices.

pcGetRefPointDefn.name: pcGetRefPointDefn
pcGetRefPointDefn.desc: Returns an identifier for the reference point parameter defined in the specified cellview.

pcGetRefPoints.name: pcGetRefPoints
pcGetRefPoints.desc: Returns a list of identifiers for all the reference point parameters in a specified cellview.

pcGetRepeatDefn.name: pcGetRepeatDefn
pcGetRepeatDefn.desc: Returns a list of identifiers for all repetition parameters assigned to an object in the cellview. A single object can be assigned to more than one repetition group.

pcGetRepeats.name: pcGetRepeats
pcGetRepeats.desc: Returns a list of identifiers for repetition parameters in the specified cellview.

pcGetStepDirection.name: pcGetStepDirection
pcGetStepDirection.desc: Returns the direction from the first point in the list to the second point in the list.

pcGetSteppedObjectDefn.name: pcGetSteppedObjectDefn
pcGetSteppedObjectDefn.desc: Returns an identifier for repetition-along-shape parameters resulting from calls to pcDefineSteppedObject. The object cannot be a parameterized shape.

pcGetSteppedObjects.name: pcGetSteppedObjects
pcGetSteppedObjects.desc: Returns a list of identifiers for the repetition-along-shape parameters in the specified cellview.

pcGetStretchDefn.name: pcGetStretchDefn
pcGetStretchDefn.desc: Returns the identifier for a stretch parameter.

pcGetStretches.name: pcGetStretches
pcGetStretches.desc: Returns a list of identifiers for the stretch parameters in the specified cellview.

pcGetStretchSummary.name: pcGetStretchSummary
pcGetStretchSummary.desc: For a parameterized master cell created using the Virtuoso Pcell graphical user interface tool, returns a list of lists, where each list contains the field names and values from the Stretch in X and Stretch in Y forms for each stretch line that was defined for the parameterized cell.

pcGrowBox.name: pcGrowBox
pcGrowBox.desc: Increase or decrease the size of the specified box by the specified margin. The system adds xf_margin to each coordinate in the list and returns a list of the coordinates of the resulting box.

pcGrowPoints.name: pcGrowPoints
pcGrowPoints.desc: Increase or decrease the size of a manhattan polygon by the specified margin. The system adds xf_margin to each coordinate in the list and returns a list of the coordinates of the resulting polygon.

pcHICompileToSkill.name: pcHICompileToSkill
pcHICompileToSkill.desc: Displays the Compile To SKILL form to let you create a SKILL file from the data in the current cellview. The file can then be edited as any SKILL file.

pcHIDefineCondition.name: pcHIDefineCondition
pcHIDefineCondition.desc: Lets you designate specified objects as conditional by prompting you to select one or more objects in the current cellview. When you complete selecting objects, the system displays the Conditional Inclusion form.

pcHIDefineInheritedParameter.name: pcHIDefineInheritedParameter
pcHIDefineInheritedParameter.desc: Lets you designate a Pcell instance whose parameters should be inherited from the Pcell parent in which the instance is placed by prompting you to select the instance in the current cellview. After you select the instance, the system displays the Define/Modify Inherited Parameters form.

pcHIDefineLabel.name: pcHIDefineLabel
pcHIDefineLabel.desc: Displays the Define Parameterized Label form to let you create a parameterized label for Pcell you are currently editing. After you complete the form, the system prompts you to enter an anchor point for the label.

pcHIDefineLayer.name: pcHIDefineLayer
pcHIDefineLayer.desc: Lets you designate specified shapes to be in a parameterized layer group by prompting you to select one or more shapes in the current cellview. When you complete selecting shapes, the system displays the Define Parameterized Layer form.

pcHIDefineParamCell.name: pcHIDefineParamCell
pcHIDefineParamCell.desc: Displays the Compile To Pcell form to let you create a graphical Pcell (super) master in the database from the design in the current window or from the cellview you specify. If you do not compile a Pcell before you place an instance of it in another design, the system interprets the design as a standard fixed cell instead of a Pcell. Each time you edit a graphical Pcell, you must recompile it so that all placed instances reflect the changes.

pcHIDefineParameterizedShape.name: pcHIDefineParameterizedShape
pcHIDefineParameterizedShape.desc: Lets you assign the vertices of a shape as parameters of the Pcell you are currently editing by prompting you to select a shape. You can parameterize paths, polygons, and rectangles. When you place an instance of the Pcell, you supply values for the parameters by entering coordinates.

pcHIDefineParamRefPointObject.name: pcHIDefineParamRefPointObject
pcHIDefineParamRefPointObject.desc: Lets you specify a reference point parameter as the origin point for a selected object or group of objects in the Pcell you are currently editing. The system prompts you for the reference point, then prompts you to select the object(s). When you complete selecting objects, the system displays the Reference Point by Parameter form. There can be only one reference point parameter defined in a Pcell.

pcHIDefinePathRefPointObject.name: pcHIDefinePathRefPointObject
pcHIDefinePathRefPointObject.desc: Lets you specify the end of a parameterized path as the reference point for objects in the Pcell you are currently editing by prompting you to select the objects. When you complete selecting objects, the system displays the Reference Point by Path Endpoint form. There can be only one reference-point-by-path-endpoint parameter defined in a Pcell.

pcHIDefineProp.name: pcHIDefineProp
pcHIDefineProp.desc: Displays the Parameterized Property form to let you specify a property for the Pcell you are currently editing.

pcHIDefineRepeat.name: pcHIDefineRepeat
pcHIDefineRepeat.desc: Lets you define a repetition parameter for specified objects by prompting you to select one or more objects in the current cellview. When you complete selecting objects, the system displays one of the following forms, depending on the value of the t_direction argument: Repeat in X, Repeat in Y, or Repeat in X and Y.

pcHIDefineSteppedObject.name: pcHIDefineSteppedObject
pcHIDefineSteppedObject.desc: Lets you specify an object or group of objects to repeat along the coordinate string controlling a parameterized shape by prompting you to select the objects in the Pcell you are currently editing. The Pcell must already contain a parameterized shape. When you complete selecting objects, the system displays the Repeat Along Shape form.

pcHIDefineStretch.name: pcHIDefineStretch
pcHIDefineStretch.desc: Allows you to define a stretch parameter for specified objects by prompting you to select one or more objects in the current cellview. The argument t_direction determines which form the system displays when you complete selecting objects: Stretch in X or Stretch in Y.

pcHIDeleteCondition.name: pcHIDeleteCondition
pcHIDeleteCondition.desc: Lets you delete an object from a conditional induction group by prompting you to select the object in the current cellview. When you select the object, the system displays the Delete Conditional Inclusion form.

pcHIDeleteLayer.name: pcHIDeleteLayer
pcHIDeleteLayer.desc: Lets you remove a parameterized layer group by prompting you to select a shape in the group. When you select a shape, the system highlights all objects in the parameterized layer group and displays the Delete Parameterized Layer form.

pcHIDeleteParameterizedShape.name: pcHIDeleteParameterizedShape
pcHIDeleteParameterizedShape.desc: Lets you delete a parameterized shape from the Pcell you are currently editing by prompting you to select the parameterized shape. When you delete a parameterized shape, the coordinates of the shape are no longer parameters of the Pcell.

pcHIDeleteProp.name: pcHIDeleteProp
pcHIDeleteProp.desc: Displays the Delete Parameterized Property form to let you specify a property to delete from the Pcell you are currently editing. When there is more than one parameterized property defined for the Pcell, click Next to view another property.

pcHIDeleteRefPointObject.name: pcHIDeleteRefPointObject
pcHIDeleteRefPointObject.desc: Lets you delete either a reference point defined as a parameter of the cellview or a reference point defined relative to the endpoint of a parameterized path by prompting you to select any object in the reference point group. After you select an object, the system highlights all objects in the group and opens either the Delete Reference Point form or the Delete Reference Point By Path form.

pcHIDeleteRepeat.name: pcHIDeleteRepeat
pcHIDeleteRepeat.desc: Lets you delete a repeat group from the Pcell you are currently editing by prompting you to select a shape in the repeat group you want to delete. After you select a shape, the system highlights all shapes in the group and displays one of the following forms, depending on the type of repeat group you selected: Delete Repeat in X, Delete Repeat in Y, or Delete Repeat in X and Y.

pcHIDeleteSteppedObject.name: pcHIDeleteSteppedObject
pcHIDeleteSteppedObject.desc: Lets you delete a repetition along shape group from the Pcell you are currently editing by prompting you to select a member (shape) of the repetition along shape group.

pcHIDisplayCondition.name: pcHIDisplayCondition
pcHIDisplayCondition.desc: Highlights a conditional inclusion group in the current cellview window and displays the Show Conditional Inclusion text window with information about the highlighted group. When there is more than one conditional inclusion group, click OK in the text window to view the next one.

pcHIDisplayInheritedParameter.name: pcHIDisplayInheritedParameter
pcHIDisplayInheritedParameter.desc: Highlights a Pcell instance whose parameters are inherited from the Pcell parent in which the instance is placed and displays the Show Inherited Parameters text window with information about the highlighted instance. When there is more than one Pcell instance with inherited parameters, click OK in the text window to view the next one.

pcHIDisplayLayer.name: pcHIDisplayLayer
pcHIDisplayLayer.desc: Highlights a parameterized layer group in the current cellview window and displays Show Parameterized Layer text window with information about the highlighted group. When there is more than one parameterized layer group, click OK in the text window to view the next one.

pcHIDisplayParameterizedShape.name: pcHIDisplayParameterizedShape
pcHIDisplayParameterizedShape.desc: Highlights a parameterized shape in the current cellview window and displays the Show Parameterized Shape text window with information about the highlighted group. When there is more than one parameterized shape, click OK in the text window to view the next one.

pcHIDisplayParams.name: pcHIDisplayParams
pcHIDisplayParams.desc: Although the pcHIDisplayParams function still displays the Show Parameters text window, the information contained in the window might not be complete. The Show Parameters command has been replaced by the Edit Parameters command. To display information about Pcell parameters, use either the pcHIEditParameters function or the pcHIParamsSummarize function.

pcHIDisplayProp.name: pcHIDisplayProp
pcHIDisplayProp.desc: Displays a Show Parameterized Property text window with information about all parameterized properties defined for the Pcell you are currently editing.

pcHIDisplayRefPointObject.name: pcHIDisplayRefPointObject
