vmsUpdateCellViews.name: vmsUpdateCellViews
vmsUpdateCellViews.syntax:
vmsUpdateCellViews(
[ ?lib t_lib ]
[ ?cell t_cell ]
[ ?view t_view ]
[ ?viewt t_viewType ]
)
=> t / nil
vmsUpdateCellViews.desc: Updates AMS Designer information with the current state of verilog, systemVerilog, veriloga, verilogams and vhdl text views. You might use this function, for example, when you have updated a Verilog-AMS source file outside of the AMS Designer environment. You might also use it when you receive a Verilog-AMS library in a single source file, bring it into the Library.Cell:View structure using xmvlog -use5x, and then need to prepare the library for use in the AMS Designer environment.

annRetrieveFromEffectiveCDF.name: annRetrieveFromEffectiveCDF
annRetrieveFromEffectiveCDF.desc: Retrieves the data from effective CDF. This function is used to match the CDF properties of the graphical window with the global effective CDF properties and needs to be called before annotating CDF properties to reflect the changes done in effective CDF properties.

artEnableAnnotationBalloon.name: artEnableAnnotationBalloon
artEnableAnnotationBalloon.syntax:
artEnableAnnotationBalloon(
g_value 
[ x_firstPoint ]
[ x_lastPoint ]
)
=> t / nil
artEnableAnnotationBalloon.desc: Enables or disables the display of parametric sweep results annotated on the schematic. When enabled, the first six result points are displayed in a pop-up window that appears when you hover the mouse pointer over an instance on the schematic. Use x_firstPoint and x_lastPoint to specify a range of result points to be displayed in the pop-up window.

artGenerateHierSymbolCDF.name: artGenerateHierSymbolCDF
artGenerateHierSymbolCDF.desc: Creates the cell CDF for the specified cellView, in the same way as happens when you create a symbol from a schematic in Composer. The cellView will be examined for any use of pPar() in expressions, and the corresponding parameters will be added to the CDF if they are not already present. Whilst both schematic and symbol cellViews may be passed to this function, it is usually best to pass a schematic cellView, in order to get the pPar()s used into the CDF.

artGetCdfTargetCV.name: artGetCdfTargetCV
artGetCdfTargetCV.desc: This procedure returns the cell view dbobject that is the target of the update instance form or the create instance form. The function requires that either the arm property (armGet 'cdfInfo 'currentCellView) is set to a cellView, or that the variable cdfgForm is bound to a form with a property cellViewId attached (getq cdfgForm cellViewId). If neither of these is bound, nil is returned.

artGetCellViewDesignVarList.name: artGetCellViewDesignVarList
artGetCellViewDesignVarList.desc: Returns the list of design variable name value pairs associated with the top level cell view.

artCurrentInstSimName.name: artCurrentInstSimName
artCurrentInstSimName.desc: This function provides the external instance name for the current instance being formatted in the netlister. The function should only be used for socket netlisters or custom netlist procedures for socket. The routine does not take into consideration case mapping registered for the tool or the prefix for the instance. It does take care of the netlisting mode (FNL, HNL or IHNL).

artListToWaveform.name: artListToWaveform
artListToWaveform.desc: This function takes a list of X,Y points and translates it into a waveform. Each of the X,Y points is also in a list format. If Y points are represented in a list format, they are treated as complex numbers while creating the waveform.

artBlankString.name: artBlankString
artBlankString.desc: Returns true if the given object is equal to nil. If the given object is a string, checks if the string is empty or has blank space characters only and returns true. If the object is not nil and if the string has non-space characters, it returns nil.

artMakeString.name: artMakeString
artMakeString.desc: Converts data of the given data type to a string. The valid data types for the g_anyArg argument include symbol, integer, float, and string. The floating point numbers are converted into strings by using the '%.16g' format specification to produce the most precise output.

artMakeStringPrec15.name: artMakeStringPrec15
artMakeStringPrec15.desc: Converts data of the given data type to a string. The valid data types for the g_anyArg argument include symbol, integer, float, and string. It similar to the function artMakeString, except that it uses the '%.15g' format specification to convert the floating point numbers into strings.

asiAddDesignVarList.name: asiAddDesignVarList
asiAddDesignVarList.desc: Adds a list of variables to the existing session design variable list.

asiAddVerilogArgs.name: asiAddVerilogArgs
asiAddVerilogArgs.desc: For a mixed-signal simulation, this method lets you change the list of arguments that are sent to the Verilog-XL simulator with the -slave option.

asiCheckSimulationSuccess.name: asiCheckSimulationSuccess
asiCheckSimulationSuccess.desc: Determines if a simulation was successful.

asiCreateLogFileVerilog.name: asiCreateLogFileVerilog
asiCreateLogFileVerilog.desc: Creates the file logFileVerilog in the .../psf directory to indicate the analysis result of Verilog-XL in a mixed-signal transient run.

asiDcStore.name: asiDcStore
asiDcStore.desc: Copies the DC node voltages in processId.dc to the name you pass in fileName. This function assumes that your simulator writes the DC node voltages to netlistDir/raw/processId.dc.

asiGetCurrentSession.name: asiGetCurrentSession
asiGetCurrentSession.desc: Returns the session object for the current session.

asiGetDesignVarList.name: asiGetDesignVarList
asiGetDesignVarList.desc: Gets the list of design variables for the design associated with the session you specify.

asiGetFormFieldChoices.name: asiGetFormFieldChoices
asiGetFormFieldChoices.desc: Gets the list of choices for a form field that is set up as a list box.

asiGetFormFieldVal.name: asiGetFormFieldVal
asiGetFormFieldVal.desc: Gets the value of a field on a form.

asiGetKeepList.name: asiGetKeepList

asiGetLogFileList.name: asiGetLogFileList
asiGetLogFileList.desc: Returns a list of the names of the log files.

asiGetMarchList.name: asiGetMarchList

asiGetNetlistDir.name: asiGetNetlistDir

asiGetOutputList.name: asiGetOutputList

asiGetPlotList.name: asiGetPlotList
asiGetPlotList.desc: Gets the list of signals that can be plotted for the current simulation session.

asiGetPsfDir.name: asiGetPsfDir
asiGetPsfDir.desc: Returns the name of the PSF directory.

asiGetSession.name: asiGetSession
asiGetSession.desc: Returns the session object given one of five possible identifiers.

asiGetSimName.name: asiGetSimName
asiGetSimName.desc: Gets the name of the simulator for a tool or session object.

asiGetTool.name: asiGetTool

asiGetTopCellView.name: asiGetTopCellView

asiSetSyncFlag.name: asiSetSyncFlag
asiSetSyncFlag.desc: This function makes the simulation run in a blocking mode. This implies that control does not come back till the simulation is over. This functionality is needed in the replay files in order to wait for a simulation to finish before proceeding. Call this function (asiSetSyncFlag(t)) just before launching a simulation. This function should only be used for testing capabilities. OCEAN should be used for scripting simulations.

asiTransientStore.name: asiTransientStore
asiTransientStore.desc: Copies the final transient operating points in processId.tr to the name you pass in fileName. This function assumes that your simulator writes the final transient operating points to netlistDir/raw/processId.tr.

asiMapNetName.name: asiMapNetName
asiMapNetName.desc: Maps the hierarchical schematic net name to the name in the netlist.

asiMapTerminalName.name: asiMapTerminalName

asiMapInstanceName.name: asiMapInstanceName
asiMapInstanceName.desc: Maps the hierarchical schematic instance name to the name in the netlist.

asiRegCallBackOnSimComp.name: asiRegCallBackOnSimComp
asiRegCallBackOnSimComp.desc: Registers the specified user-defined callback function to run after completion of a simulation. The callback function should accept two arguments, a session object and the simulation status.

asiUnRegCallBackOnSimComp.name: asiUnRegCallBackOnSimComp

asiRegCallBackOnSimCompForDist.name: asiRegCallBackOnSimCompForDist

drbBrowseFormCB.desc: Opens the Browse Project Hierarchy window.

msgHelp.name: msgHelp
msgHelp.desc: This function is used to access extended help for an error or a warning message. Currently, Distributed Processing (DP) is the only product that supports this feature.

addCheck.name: addCheck
addCheck.syntax:
addCheck(
t_name
[ ?sub t_sub ]
[ ?dev t_dev ]
[ ?devlist l_devlist ]
[ ?prim t_prim ]
[ ?mod t_mod ]
[ ?instparam t_instparam ]
[ ?modelparam t_modelparam ]
[ ?opparam t_opparam ]
[ ?parameter t_parameter ]
[ ?expression t_expression ]
[ ?min t_min ]
[ ?max t_max ]
[ ?regions t_regions ]
[ ?duration t_duration ]
[ ?message t_message ]
[ ?severity t_severity ]
[ ?analyses l_analyses ]
)
=> t_name / nil
addCheck.desc: Adds a new device check. Checks can be added to check a device parameter, a subcircuit parameter, a design variable or an expression. The scope of check is decided by the arguments ?sub, ?dev, ?mod, and ?prim. The ?min and ?max parameters can be used to set up the safe region if the parameter/expression being checked goes out of this region and a violation is reported.

evmOFDM.name: evmOFDM
evmOFDM.syntax:
evmOFDM(
o_waveform1
o_waveform2
e_sigStandard
n_tstart
e_modulationType
n_fftSize
n_PrefixLength
n_SymbolPeriod
[ ?packet n_packetLength ]
[ ?modifier e_modifier ]
[ ?skiplength n_skiplength ]
[ ?idx n_idx ]
[ ?getval g_getval ]
)
=> constellation o_waveform evm_value / nil
evmOFDM.desc: Processes the I and Q waveform outputs from the hb-envlp simulation run to calculate the Error Vector Magnitude (EVM) and plot the I versus Q scatterplot (constellation). EVM is a useful measurement to describe the overall signal amplitude and phase modulated signal quality. It is based on a statistical error distribution normalized from an ideal digital modulation. Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) is a modern high throughput modulation scheme widely used in wireless signals, such as 802.11a,g,n, where EVM measurement is useful . The EVM is calculated by detecting the I and Q signal levels corresponding to constellation points of each modulation type (can be BPSK, QPSK, 16QAM, and 64QAM) and calculating the difference between the signal level and the ideal signal level.

drplEvmBpsk.desc: Processes the I and Q waveform outputs from the transient simulation run to calculate the Error Vector Magnitude (EVM) and plot the I versus Q scatterplot. EVM is a useful measurement to describe the overall signal amplitude and phase modulated signal quality. It is based on a statistical error distribution normalized from an ideal digital modulation. Binary Phase Shift Keying (BPSK) is a typical modulation scheme where EVM is useful. The EVM is calculated by detecting the I and Q signal levels corresponding to the two possible I and Q symbol combinations, and calculating the difference between the signal level and the ideal signal level. Compared to other types of phase shift keying, such as QPSK, QAM16 and QAM64, BPSK has lowest bit error rate for the same signal to noise ratio.

sevChangeOutsOnSchematic.desc: Sets up for selection of selected output types from the schematic.

sevSaveOptions.name: sevSaveOptions
sevSaveOptions.desc: Displays the Save Options form that lets you select what voltages and currents should be automatically saved in the simulation.

sevDeleteSelectedAnas.name: sevDeleteSelectedAnas
sevDeleteSelectedAnas.desc: Deletes the analyses that are currently selected in the Analysis listbox.

sevNoAnaSelections.name: sevNoAnaSelections
sevNoAnaSelections.desc: Indicates whether any analyses are selected in the Analysis listbox.

sevActivateSelectedAnas.name: sevActivateSelectedAnas
sevActivateSelectedAnas.desc: Enables or disables the selected analyses.

sevDeleteSelectedVars.name: sevDeleteSelectedVars
sevDeleteSelectedVars.desc: Deletes any variables that are selected in the Variables listbox.

sevNoVarSelections.name: sevNoVarSelections
sevNoVarSelections.desc: Indicates whether any variables are selected in the Variables listbox.

sevFindSelectedVars.name: sevFindSelectedVars
sevFindSelectedVars.desc: Highlights the device on the schematic where the selected variable is used.

sevCopyCellViewVariables.name: sevCopyCellViewVariables
sevCopyCellViewVariables.desc: Copies the cell view variables and their values into the simulation environment.

sevCopyVariablesToCellView.name: sevCopyVariablesToCellView
sevCopyVariablesToCellView.desc: Copies the simulation session variables and their values into the cellview.

sevDeleteSelectedOuts.name: sevDeleteSelectedOuts
sevDeleteSelectedOuts.desc: Deletes the selected items from the outputs list box.

sevExportOutputsToTxt.name: sevExportOutputsToTxt
sevExportOutputsToTxt.desc: Exports the outputs specified in the Output listbox to a text file. This text file can be edited and imported back to ADE.

sevImportOutputsFromTxt.name: sevImportOutputsFromTxt
sevImportOutputsFromTxt.desc: Imports the outputs saved in a text file to the output list box in the main ADE window.

sevExportOutputsToCSV.name: sevExportOutputsToCSV
sevExportOutputsToCSV.desc: Exports the outputs specified in the ADE setup to the CSV file.

sevExportOutputsToFile.name: sevExportOutputsToFile
sevExportOutputsToFile.desc: Exports the output from the ADE setup to the text or CSV file, which is specified by the .cdsenv variable outputsImportExportVersion. If the value of outputsImportExportVersion variable is greater than 1.0, then the function generates the output to the CSV file, else it generates the output to the text file.

sevImportOutputsFromCSV.name: sevImportOutputsFromCSV
sevImportOutputsFromCSV.desc: Imports the outputs from the CSV file to the ADE setup.

sevImportOutputsFromFile.name: sevImportOutputsFromFile
sevImportOutputsFromFile.desc: Imports the output to the ADE setup from the text or CSV file, which is specified by the .cdsenv variable outputsImportExportVersion. If the value of outputsImportExportVersion variable is greater than 1.0, then the function imports the outputs from the CSV file, else it imports the outputs from the text file.

sevNoOutSelections.name: sevNoOutSelections
sevNoOutSelections.desc: Indicates whether any output is selected in the Outputs listbox.

sevRemovePlotWindow.name: sevRemovePlotWindow
sevRemovePlotWindow.desc: Removes the specified plot window from the list of plot windows owned by the given simulation environment session.

sevSetPropertyForSelectedOuts.name: sevSetPropertyForSelectedOuts
sevSetPropertyForSelectedOuts.syntax:
sevSetPropertyForSelectedOuts(
t_session 
t_property 
g_value
)
=> t / nil
sevSetPropertyForSelectedOuts.desc: Sets the property to the specified value on the selected outputs.

sevSimulator.name: sevSimulator
sevSimulator.desc: Displays the name of the simulator used in the session as a string.

sevRunEngine.name: sevRunEngine
sevRunEngine.desc: Runs a simulation from the simulation environment session.

sevStopEngine.name: sevStopEngine
sevStopEngine.desc: Stops the currently running simulation that is tied to the session.

sevIsContinuable.name: sevIsContinuable
sevIsContinuable.desc: Indicates whether the currently run simulation can be continued from its stopping point.

sevSetEngineOptions.name: sevSetEngineOptions
sevSetEngineOptions.desc: Displays the Engine Options form for the selected type for editing.

sevNetlistFile.name: sevNetlistFile
sevNetlistFile.desc: Creates the selected type of netlist file.

sevOpenEncap.name: sevOpenEncap
sevOpenEncap.desc: Opens the command type in window that lets you enter commands directly to the simulator.

sevNoOutputLog.name: sevNoOutputLog
sevNoOutputLog.desc: Indicates whether the simulation output log exists.

sevConvergence.name: sevConvergence
sevConvergence.desc: Displays the form for setting up the selected type of convergence aid.

sevNoResults.name: sevNoResults
sevNoResults.desc: Indicates whether the specified results exist.

sevNoPlottableOutputs.name: sevNoPlottableOutputs
sevNoPlottableOutputs.desc: Indicates whether there are any plottable outputs.

sevCircuitCond.name: sevCircuitCond
sevCircuitCond.desc: Displays the Circuit Conditions form that lets you set or display any special circuit conditions.

sevNoDesign.name: sevNoDesign
sevNoDesign.desc: Indicates whether a design is tied to the simulation environment.

sevSetSimDataDir.name: sevSetSimDataDir
sevSetSimDataDir.desc: Loads the results for the specified simulation environment session and results directory.

sevSaveResults.name: sevSaveResults
sevSaveResults.desc: Displays the Save Results form that lets you save the current results.

sevSelectResults.name: sevSelectResults
sevSelectResults.desc: Displays the Select Results form that lets you select and load a previously saved set of results.

sevDeleteResults.name: sevDeleteResults
sevDeleteResults.desc: Displays the Delete Results form that lets you delete a set of previously saved results.

sevEditPlottingOptions.name: sevEditPlottingOptions
sevEditPlottingOptions.desc: Displays the Setting Plotting Options form that lets you edit the plotting and printing options.

sevNoPlottableSignals.name: sevNoPlottableSignals
sevNoPlottableSignals.desc: Indicates whether there are any plottable outputs.

sevPlotSignals.name: sevPlotSignals
sevPlotSignals.syntax:
sevPlotSignals(
t_session
t_type
[ ?disableRedraw g_disableRedraw ]
)
=> t / nil
sevPlotSignals.desc: Plots the speacified type of signals that exist as outputs.

sevEvaluateAndPlotExpressions.name: sevEvaluateAndPlotExpressions
sevEvaluateAndPlotExpressions.desc: Evaluates and plots all the output expressions.

sevNoPlottableExpressions.name: sevNoPlottableExpressions
sevNoPlottableExpressions.desc: Indicates whether there are any plottable expressions.

sevPrintResults.name: sevPrintResults
sevPrintResults.desc: Displays the Print Results form that lets you print the selected type of simulation results.

sevRetrieveFromEffectiveCDF.name: sevRetrieveFromEffectiveCDF
sevRetrieveFromEffectiveCDF.desc: Retrieves data from the effective CDF. This function should be used before the sevAnnotateResults function.

sevAnnotateResults.name: sevAnnotateResults
sevAnnotateResults.desc: Annotates the selected results to the schematic window.

sevRegisterPcellsForAnnotation.name: sevRegisterPcellsForAnnotation
sevRegisterPcellsForAnnotation.desc: Returns a list of library and cell name pairs for the registered Pcells.

sevGetRegisteredPcellsForAnnotation.name: sevGetRegisteredPcellsForAnnotation
sevGetRegisteredPcellsForAnnotation.desc: Returns the list of library and cell name pairs of the registered Pcells to be used in the operating point annotation flow.

sevMonteCarloTool.name: sevMonteCarloTool
sevMonteCarloTool.desc: Opens the Analog Statistical Analysis tool.

sevOpenDRLBrowser.name: sevOpenDRLBrowser
sevOpenDRLBrowser.desc: Opens the Browse Project Hierarchy window.

sevIcon.name: sevIcon
sevIcon.desc: Displays the icon object corresponding to the specified name.

sevDeleteSelections.name: sevDeleteSelections
sevDeleteSelections.desc: Deletes the selected items in any of the simulation environment list boxes.

sevWhatsNew.name: sevWhatsNew
sevWhatsNew.desc: Opens the Whats New window for the simulation environment.

sevStartSession.name: sevStartSession
sevStartSession.syntax:
sevStartSession(
[ ?design g_design ]
[ ?lib g_lib ]
[ ?cell g_cell ]
[ ?view g_view ]
[ ?schematic g_schematic ]
)
=> t / nil
sevStartSession.desc: Starts the Virtuoso Analog Simulation Environment session tied to the specified design. It will try the design first, then lib/cell/view, and finally it will try the schematic. If none of these is specified, it will start a skeleton session that will not be able to do anything until a design has been tied to the session. The lib/cell/view arguments must be specified, otherwise they are ignored.

sevAboutTool.name: sevAboutTool
sevAboutTool.desc: Generates and displays the standard About DFII window for the tool with the tool name in the message.

sevEditModels.name: sevEditModels
sevEditModels.desc: Displays the Model Library Setup form that lets you edit the Spectre direct model libraries.

sevSetupStimuli.name: sevSetupStimuli
sevSetupStimuli.desc: Displays the Setup Analog Stimuli form that lets you specify the circuit stimuli.

sevSetupSimulationFiles.name: sevSetupSimulationFiles
sevSetupSimulationFiles.desc: Displays the Simulation Files Setup form that lets you specify the simulation files and paths for Spectre direct simulation.

sevNetlistAndRun.name: sevNetlistAndRun
sevNetlistAndRun.desc: Forces the circuit to create a netlist and then run the simulation.

sevRun.name: sevRun
sevRun.desc: Runs a simulation using the current netlist.

sevNetlistAndDebug.name: sevNetlistAndDebug
sevNetlistAndDebug.desc: Forces the circuit to netlist and runs the AHDL debugger.

sevDebug.name: sevDebug
sevDebug.desc: Runs the AHDL debugger using the current netlist.

sevLMGTool.name: sevLMGTool
sevLMGTool.desc: Opens the Transmission Line Modeler tool.

sevPKGTool.name: sevPKGTool
sevPKGTool.desc: Opens the RFIC Package Modeler tool.

sevKmodelTool.name: sevKmodelTool
sevKmodelTool.desc: Opens the RIFC Modeler for Cierto SPW tool.

sevPCMTool.name: sevPCMTool
sevPCMTool.desc: Opens the Spiral Inductor Modeler tool.

sevBPMTool.name: sevBPMTool
sevBPMTool.desc: Opens the Bond Pad Modeler tool.

sevActiveSelectedAna.name: sevActiveSelectedAna
sevActiveSelectedAna.desc: Returns the list of selected analyses that are currently enabled.

sevNonActiveSelectedAna.name: sevNonActiveSelectedAna
sevNonActiveSelectedAna.desc: Returns the list of selected analyses that are currently not enabled.

sevSession.name: sevSession
sevSession.desc: Displays the session ID of the simulation environment such as the ADE L window, the schematic window associated with ADE L, or a form launched from ADE L.

sevSetTopSaveDir.name: sevSetTopSaveDir
sevSetTopSaveDir.desc: This function sets the ADE L Save State directory for the simulation environment session.

sevTopSaveDir.name: sevTopSaveDir
sevTopSaveDir.desc: Displays the current ADE L Save State directory path.

sevDisplayViolations.name: sevDisplayViolations
sevDisplayViolations.desc: Displays the violations form. This function can be used only with an Analog Design Environment L session.

sevNoViolationsFound.name: sevNoViolationsFound
sevNoViolationsFound.desc: Determines if any violation file has been found in the results.

sevParasiticsDisplayed.name: sevParasiticsDisplayed
sevParasiticsDisplayed.desc: Determines whether the Show Parasitics menu will be disabled when the DC Operating Point results are available.

sevParasiticsNotDisplayed.name: sevParasiticsNotDisplayed
sevParasiticsNotDisplayed.desc: Determines if the Hide Parasitics menu will be disabled when the DC Operating Point results are available.

sevDevChecking.name: sevDevChecking
sevDevChecking.desc: Displays the Analog Design Environment Device Checking Setup form.

sevSetSolver.name: sevSetSolver
sevSetSolver.desc: Displays the Choose Solver form, which lets you select a solver.

sevSetConnectModules.name: sevSetConnectModules
sevSetConnectModules.desc: Displays the Connect Rules form that allows you to select built-in or user-defined connect rules.

sevInvokeSimvisionDebugger.name: sevInvokeSimvisionDebugger
sevInvokeSimvisionDebugger.desc: Displays the SimVision Debugger interface with GUI options during an AMS session.

sevNoLog.name: sevNoLog
sevNoLog.desc: Checks if the specified log file exists for the AMS interface.

sevViewNetlisterLog.name: sevViewNetlisterLog
sevViewNetlisterLog.desc: Displays the AMS netlister log file.

sevViewCompilerLog.name: sevViewCompilerLog
sevViewCompilerLog.desc: Displays the AMS simulation compiler log file. The log file can be either ncvlog.log or ncvhdl.log depending on the contents of the AMS design.

sevViewElabLog.name: sevViewElabLog
sevViewElabLog.desc: Displays the AMS simulation elaborator log file.

sevViewNcVerilogLog.name: sevViewNcVerilogLog
sevViewNcVerilogLog.desc: Displays the AMS simulation NcVerilog log file.

sevViewSimLog.name: sevViewSimLog
sevViewSimLog.desc: Displays the AMS simulator log file.

sevReturnVariablesWithEmptyValues.name: sevReturnVariablesWithEmptyValues
sevReturnVariablesWithEmptyValues.desc: Returns the set of variables in a session with empty values.

sevAddExpression.name: sevAddExpression
sevAddExpression.syntax:
sevAddExpression(
o_session
t_expressionname
t_expression
)
=> t / nil
sevAddExpression.desc: Takes the name and expression as a string and adds a corresponding output in ADE session.

sevGetExpressions.name: sevGetExpressions
sevGetExpressions.desc: Returns all the expressions in the specified ADE/ADEXL session.

sevDeleteSelectedSubckts.name: sevDeleteSelectedSubckts
sevDeleteSelectedSubckts.desc: Deletes the subcircuit instances selected in the Save By Subckt Instances pane of the simulation window.

sevDeleteSelectedOpPoints.name: sevDeleteSelectedOpPoints
sevDeleteSelectedOpPoints.desc: Deletes the operating point instances selected in the Save Operating Points pane of the simulation window.

cdfCreateBaseCellCDF.name: cdfCreateBaseCellCDF
cdfCreateBaseCellCDF.syntax:
cdfCreateBaseCellCDF(
g_cellID 
[ ?doneProc t_doneProc ]
[ ?formInitProc t_formInitProc ]
[ ?fieldWidth x_fieldWidth ]
[ ?fieldHeight x_fieldHeight ]
[ ?buttonFieldWidth x_buttonFieldWidth ]
[ ?promptWidth x_promptWidth ]
)
=> g_cdfDataID / nil
cdfCreateBaseCellCDF.desc: Creates a base-level CDF description for a cell. The CDF description is created with no parameters or simulation models.

cdfCreateBaseLibCDF.name: cdfCreateBaseLibCDF
cdfCreateBaseLibCDF.syntax:
cdfCreateBaseLibCDF( 
g_libID 
[ ?doneProc t_doneProc ]
[ ?formInitProc t_formInitProc ]
[ ?fieldWidth x_fieldWidth ]
[ ?fieldHeight x_fieldHeight ]
[ ?buttonFieldWidth x_buttonFieldWidth ]
[ ?promptWidth x_promptWidth ]
)
=> g_cdfDataID / nil
cdfCreateBaseLibCDF.desc: Creates the Base Library CDF that is applied to all the devices in the library. The CDF description is created with no parameters or simModels.

cdfCreateParam.name: cdfCreateParam
cdfCreateParam.syntax:
cdfCreateParam(
g_cdfDataId
[ ?name t_name ]
[ ?type t_type ]
[ ?defValue g_defValue ]
[ ?units t_units ]
[ ?parseAsNumber t_parseAsNumber ]
[ ?choices l_choices ]
[ ?prompt t_prompt ]
[ ?use t_use ]
[ ?display t_display ]
[ ?editable t_editable]
[ ?dontSave t_dontSave]
[ ?callback t_callback]
[ ?storeDefault t_storeDefault ]
[ ?parseAsCEL t_parseAsCEL ]
[ ?description t_description ]
)
=> g_cdfDataId / nil
cdfCreateParam.desc: Creates a parameter on the specified CDF database object with the specified attributes. The only attributes that are always required are the parameter's name and type. If this parameter description is not overriding an existing base-level parameter definition, you must also specify the default value.

cdfCreateUserCellCDF.name: cdfCreateUserCellCDF
cdfCreateUserCellCDF.syntax:
cdfCreateUserCellCDF(
g_cellId 
[ ?doneProc t_doneProc ]
[ ?formInitProc t_formInitProc ]
[ ?fieldWidth x_fieldWidth ]
[ ?fieldHeight x_fieldHeight ]
[ ?buttonFieldWidth x_buttonFieldWidth ]
[ ?promptWidth x_promptWidth ]
)
=> g_cdfDataId / nil
cdfCreateUserCellCDF.desc: Creates a user-level CDF description for a cell. The CDF description is created with no parameters or simulation models.

cdfCreateUserLibCDF.name: cdfCreateUserLibCDF
cdfCreateUserLibCDF.syntax:
cdfCreateUserLibCDF( 
g_libId 
[ ?doneProc t_doneProc ]
[ ?formInitProc t_formInitProc ]
[ ?fieldWidth x_fieldWidth ]
[ ?fieldHeight x_fieldHeight ]
[ ?buttonFieldWidth x_buttonFieldWidth ]
[ ?promptWidth x_promptWidth ]
) 
=> g_cdfDataId / nil
cdfCreateUserLibCDF.desc: Creates the user-level library CDF that is applied to all the devices in the library. The user-level CDF can override entries in the base-level CDF. Therefore, a combination of the base-level CDF and the user-level CDF becomes the effective CDF.

cdfGetBaseLibCDF.name: cdfGetBaseLibCDF
cdfGetBaseLibCDF.desc: Returns the base-level CDF description attached to a library. If one is not defined, it returns nil.

cdfGetUserLibCDF.name: cdfGetUserLibCDF
cdfGetUserLibCDF.desc: Returns the user-level CDF description attached to a library. If one is not defined, it returns nil.

cdfGetLibCDF.name: cdfGetLibCDF
cdfGetLibCDF.desc: Returns the effective CDF description attached to a library. If neither a base- nor user-level CDF description is defined, it returns nil. The resulting CDF description represents the overlay of the user-level CDF on the base-level CDF.

cdfGetBaseCellCDF.name: cdfGetBaseCellCDF
cdfGetBaseCellCDF.desc: Returns the base-level CDF description attached to a cell. If one is not defined, it returns nil.

cdfGetUserCellCDF.name: cdfGetUserCellCDF
cdfGetUserCellCDF.desc: Returns the user-level CDF description attached to a cell. If one is not defined, it returns nil.

cdfGetCellCDF.name: cdfGetCellCDF
cdfGetCellCDF.desc: Returns the effective CDF description attached to a cell. If neither a base- nor user-level CDF description is defined for the cell or its library, it returns nil. The resulting CDF description represents the overlay of the user-level cell CDF on the base-level cell CDF on the user-level library CDF on the base-level library CDF.

cdfGetInstCDF.name: cdfGetInstCDF
cdfGetInstCDF.desc: Returns the effective CDF description associated with an instance.

cdfSaveCDF.name: cdfSaveCDF
cdfSaveCDF.desc: Saves a CDF description to disk. The CDF description is then read in every time you open the cell of the library to which the description is attached. You can save only base-level CDF descriptions.

cdfDump.name: cdfDump
cdfDump.syntax:
cdfDump(
t_libName
t_fileName 
[ ?cellName t_cellName ]
[ ?level s_level ] 
[ ?edit g_edit ]
) 
=> t / nil
cdfDump.desc: Dumps the CDF description for the specified library and cell into the given file. If a cell is not specified, then only the library CDF description is dumped. The file is created in the current working directory or the directory specified with the file name. If g_edit is t, a text editor window is automatically opened on t_fileName. The default is no editor.

cdfDumpAll.name: cdfDumpAll
cdfDumpAll.syntax:
cdfDumpAll(
t_libName
t_fileName 
[ ?level s_level ] 
[ ?edit g_edit ]
) 
=> t / nil
cdfDumpAll.desc: Dumps the CDF description for the specified library and all its cells into the given file. You can also specify the level of the CDF description by using the ?level s_level argument. The specified file is created in the current working directory or the directory specified with the filename.

cdfDeleteCDF.name: cdfDeleteCDF
cdfDeleteCDF.desc: Deletes a CDF description, including all attached parameters.

cdfCopyCDF.name: cdfCopyCDF
cdfCopyCDF.syntax:
cdfCopyCDF(
g_cellId | g_libId
t_dataType
g_sourceCdfDataId
)
=> g_cdfDataId / nil
cdfCopyCDF.desc: Copies the CDF data of the specified type from specified source to a library or cell by creating a new CDF data ID.

cdfCopyParam.name: cdfCopyParam
cdfCopyParam.desc: Copies the specified parameter to the given CDF data object.

cdfFindParamByName.name: cdfFindParamByName
cdfFindParamByName.desc: Returns the parameter ID of the specified parameter name for the given CDF description, if it exists. If not, it returns nil.

cdfUpdateInstParam.name: cdfUpdateInstParam
cdfUpdateInstParam.desc: Stores the CDF parameters specified in the effective cell CDF of the instance master to the given instance. If a doneProc post-processing procedure is specified, the function runs this procedure to validate any updates to the instance. When the ID given is not for an instance or the instance master does not have CDF definition, it returns nil.

cdfRefreshCDF.name: cdfRefreshCDF
cdfRefreshCDF.desc: Updates the CDF structure in the memory for the specified library or cell Id with the contents stored on the hard disk. Returns nil if the CDF structures for the specified library and cell ID are not present in memory.

aedCopyCDF.name: aedCopyCDF
aedCopyCDF.desc: Opens the Copy Component CDF form.

aedDeleteCDF.name: aedDeleteCDF
aedDeleteCDF.desc: Opens the Delete Component CDF form.

cdfGetUnitScaleFactor.name: cdfGetUnitScaleFactor
cdfGetUnitScaleFactor.desc: Displays the current scale factor for the specified unit.

cdfSetUnitScaleFactor.name: cdfSetUnitScaleFactor
cdfSetUnitScaleFactor.desc: Sets the scale factor for the specified unit.

cdfEditScaleFactors.name: cdfEditScaleFactors
cdfEditScaleFactors.desc: Displays the Units Scaling Factors form which can be used to set scaling factors for displaying CDF parameters.

cdfEnableScaleFactorRetentionForZero.name: cdfEnableScaleFactorRetentionForZero
cdfEnableScaleFactorRetentionForZero.desc: Lets you retain the unit scale factor for a CDF parameter if its specified default value is 0 followed by the scale factor. This is possible only when the scale factor for a unit type is set to auto.

cdfDisableScaleFactorRetentionForZero.name: cdfDisableScaleFactorRetentionForZero
cdfDisableScaleFactorRetentionForZero.desc: Disables the unit scale factor retention for CDF parameters enabled using the cdfEnableScaleFactorRetentionForZero function.

cdfParseFloatString.name: cdfParseFloatString
cdfParseFloatString.desc: Uses the standard strtod (string to double) function to parse the input string. When the input string contains trailing non-numerical characters, the fragment of the string is compared against a supported set of scale factor designators.

cdfFormatFloatString.name: cdfFormatFloatString
cdfFormatFloatString.desc: This function formats the input string into a value representation, if possible. It formats the input string using the input scale factor, re-converts the value to a string, and then returns the formatted string value. If the input string cannot be converted, the input string is returned with no change to it.

cdfSyncInstParamValue.name: cdfSyncInstParamValue
cdfSyncInstParamValue.desc: This function generates all the CDF parameters for the first instance (d_instId1) and updates the second instance (d_instId2) with the same values. Both the instances must share the same cell.

cdfUpdateInstSingleParam.name: cdfUpdateInstSingleParam
cdfUpdateInstSingleParam.desc: Copies the specified parameter's effective value to the specified instance.

aedEditCDF.name: aedEditCDF
aedEditCDF.desc: Opens the Edit CDF form to the specified library, cell, and CDF type. The library and cell names must be strings referring to an existing library or cell, and the CDF type must be effective, base, or user.

cdfGetCustomViaCDF.name: cdfGetCustomViaCDF
cdfGetCustomViaCDF.desc: Returns the effective CDF description associated with a custom via or returns nil. When the custom via's cell or library has a base or user-level CDF defined, it returns the g_cdfDataId, otherwise returns nil.

cdfUpdateCustomViaParam.name: cdfUpdateCustomViaParam
cdfUpdateCustomViaParam.desc: Stores the parameters specified in the effective cell CDF of the custom via in the specified custom via instance. When the specified ID is not for a customVia instance or the instance master does not have a CDF definition, it returns nil.

profile.name: profile
profile.desc: Turns on global SKILL profiling for measuring time or memory.

profileSummary.name: profileSummary
profileSummary.syntax:
profileSummary( 
[ ?file t_filename ] 
[ ?sort s_sortKey ] 
[ ?filters g_filterSpec ] 
[ ?maxFns x_maxDisplayed ]
[ ?minSecs f_minSecs ] 
[ ?minBytes x_minBytes ]
[ ?children g_showChildren ] 
) 
=> t
profileSummary.desc: Prints a summary of profiling results, showing either the execution time or memory allocated to SKILL functions that were executed.

unprofile.name: unprofile
unprofile.desc: Turns off SKILL profiling but does not reset.

skDisableMessage.name: skDisableMessage
skDisableMessage.desc: Disables a SKILL Lint message from being reported inside a given function definition.

skDisableMessageBlock.name: skDisableMessageBlock
skDisableMessageBlock.desc: Disables one or a list of SKILL Lint messages from being reported by rules within the body of the function. You might want to turn off certain rules temporarily, and not globally, inside a particular block of code. SKILL Lint will recognize a call to this function if inserted inside the block of code being analyzed.

skEnableMessageBlock.name: skEnableMessageBlock
skEnableMessageBlock.desc: Re-enables reporting of one or more SKILL Lint messages that have been globally turned off within the body of this function only.

skIgnoreMessage.name: skIgnoreMessage
skIgnoreMessage.desc: Turns off the reporting of specified SKILL Lint messages. For a message to appear, both the message and its group have to be unignored.

sklint.name: sklint
sklint.syntax:
sklint(
[ ?file tl_inputFileName ]
[ ?context t_contextName ]
[ ?outputFile t_outputFileName ]
[ ?ignoreGroups l_ignoreGroups ]
[ ?globals l_globals ]
[ ?depends l_depends ]
[ ?rulesFile t_rulesFile ]
[ ?ignores l_ignoresMessageList ]
[ ?checkNlambda g_checkNlambda ]
[ ?noPrintLog g_noPrintLog ]
[ ?useGlobalIgnores g_useGlobalIgnores ]
[ ?useGlobalRulesFileList g_useGlobalRulesFileList ]
[ ?useDisableMessages g_useDisableMessages ]
[ ?checkCdsFuncs g_checkCdsFuncs ]
[ ?checkPvtFuncs g_checkPvtFuncs ]
[ ?checkPubFuncs g_checkPubFuncs ]
[ ?prefixes l_prefixList ]
[ ?checkCdsPrefixes g_checkCdsPrefixes ]
[ ?checkFuncPrefixes g_checkFuncPrefixes ]
[ ?tabulate g_tabulate ]
[ ?skPath t_skPath ]
[ ?codeVersion t_release ]
)
=> t / nil
sklint.desc: Checks a SKILL file or context and reports potential errors and ways to clean up your code.

skUnignoreMessage.name: skUnignoreMessage
skUnignoreMessage.desc: Turns on the reporting of specified SKILL Lint messages. For a message to appear, both the message and its group have to be unignored.

callInitProc.name: callInitProc
callInitProc.desc: Calls all the initialization functions associated with a context.

callUserAutoInitProc.name: callUserAutoInitProc
callUserAutoInitProc.desc: Calls the autoinit function for the given context name.

checkContextBit.name: checkContextBit
checkContextBit.desc: Checks and returns the context type of the specified context file.

defCapDepends.name: defCapDepends
defCapDepends.desc: Specifies which contexts depend on which other contexts.

defCapPrefixes.name: defCapPrefixes
defCapPrefixes.desc: Specifies which prefixes are acceptable for a context's global variables.

defInitProc.name: defInitProc
defInitProc.desc: Registers a function that the system calls immediately after autoloading a context.

isContextLoaded.name: isContextLoaded
isContextLoaded.desc: Returns t if a context file with the given base name has been loaded into the current session.

loadContext.name: loadContext
loadContext.syntax:
loadContext( 
t_contextFileName 
[ g_ignore64bitSubpath ]
) 
=> t / nil / error
loadContext.desc: Loads a context file into the current session.

loadTopContextForms.name: loadTopContextForms
loadTopContextForms.syntax:
loadTopContextForms( 
t_FileName 
[ ?debugMode g_debugMode ] 
[ ?writeProtect g_writeProtect ] 
[ ?writeProtectAll g_writeProtectAll ] 
[ ?lazyComp g_lazyComp ] 
[ ?printinfix g_printinfix ] 
[ ?integermode g_integermode ] 
[ ?mergemode g_mergemode ] 
[ ?readProtect g_readProtect ] 
) 
=> t / nil
loadTopContextForms.desc: Loads top-level SKILL or Scheme forms from a file. If the setContext mode is set, these forms are saved in a context. After the context is loaded, these forms are evaluated at the top-level, as if these were loaded from an .il or .ils file.

saveContext.name: saveContext
saveContext.desc: Saves the current state of the SKILL language interpreter as a binary file. This function must be used in conjunction with setContext.

setContext.name: setContext
setContext.desc: Allows contexts to be saved incrementally, creating micro contexts from a session's SKILL context.

setSaveContextVersion.name: setSaveContextVersion
setSaveContextVersion.desc: Resets the current saveContext version to x_newVers and returns the previous context version. If x_newVers has an unsupported value or the function is called between setContext and saveContext, it returns an error.

getCurSaveContextVersion.name: getCurSaveContextVersion
getCurSaveContextVersion.desc: Returns the current saveContext version (the version which the new context will have.) The possible return values are, 601 for compatible contexts and 602 for native contexts (for IC 6.1.6/CAT 33.00)

getNativeContextVersion.name: getNativeContextVersion
getNativeContextVersion.desc: Returns the native context version (for IC 6.1.6/CAT 33.00, the native context version is 602).

getCompatContextVersion.name: getCompatContextVersion
getCompatContextVersion.desc: Returns the compatible context version (for IC 6.1.6/CAT 33.00, the compatible context version is 601).

break.name: break
break.desc: Forces entry to the break handler if inserted directly into a SKILL function. The default break handler is the debugger.

breakpt.name: breakpt
breakpt.syntax:
breakpt( 
[ u_function 
[ break_condition ] ] 
)
where break_condition can be either
(break_tag 
g_condition 
) 
or 
(
(break_tag 
g_condition)... 
)
=> g_result
breakpt.desc: Sets breakpoints on one or more functions or function objects.

breakptMethod.name: breakptMethod
breakptMethod.syntax:
breakptMethod( 
[ S_name ]
[ l_specializer [ @before | @after | @around ] ]
[ break_condition ])
where break_condition can be either
(break_tag 
g_condition 
) 
or 
(
(break_tag 
g_condition)... 
)
=> t / nil
breakptMethod.desc: Sets breakpoint on the specified method's defmethod declaration.

count.name: count
count.desc: Counts the number of times a function has been called. This is an nlambda function. Returns the functions marked for counting.

debugQuit.name: debugQuit
debugQuit.desc: Exits one level of the SKILL debugger.

debugStatus.name: debugStatus
debugStatus.desc: Prints the functions and variables being traced, functions that have breakpoints set, functions being counted, and the line breakpoints statistics.

dump.name: dump
dump.desc: Prints the current value of all the local variables on the stack. SKILL++ variables are not displayed by this function. For SKILL++ use where to see the lexical bindings on the stack.

gcsummary.name: gcsummary
gcsummary.desc: Prints a summary of memory allocation and garbage collection statistics in the current SKILL run.

getAllLoadedFiles.name: getAllLoadedFiles
getAllLoadedFiles.desc: Returns a list of all files loaded since debug mode was turned on.

getCallingFunction.name: getCallingFunction
getCallingFunction.desc: Returns the name of the calling function or procedure at the specified level in the call stack.

getFunctions.name: getFunctions
getFunctions.desc: Returns functions defined in a file loaded after debug mode is turned on.

getGFbyClass.name: getGFbyClass
getGFbyClass.desc: Returns a list of generic functions specializing on a given class.

ilAddTopLevelErrorHandler.name: ilAddTopLevelErrorHandler
ilAddTopLevelErrorHandler.desc: Registers a new top-level error-handler. This error-handler is called after stacktrace, when an error occurs. If an error-handler already exists, the function displays a warning message.

ilDebugCountLevels.name: ilDebugCountLevels
ilDebugCountLevels.desc: Returns the number of top-level debug and error frames present in the SKILL stack if SKILL is in breakpoint or error top level. Otherwise, the function returns 1.

ilGetGFbyClass.name: ilGetGFbyClass
ilGetGFbyClass.desc: Returns a list of generic functions specializing on a given class.

ilGetIdeSessionWindow.name: ilGetIdeSessionWindow
ilGetIdeSessionWindow.desc: Returns the SKILL IDE session window ID. If g_force is set to a value other than nil, the function creates an IDE window and displays it on the screen.

ilGetTCovFiles.name: ilGetTCovFiles
ilGetTCovFiles.desc: Returns the list of files processed when you run an application in test coverage mode using the command line option -ilTCov <fileList>.

ilMergeTCovData.name: ilMergeTCovData
ilMergeTCovData.desc: Merges tCov files from several directories and stores them in a single directory.

ilRemoveMethod.name: ilRemoveMethod
ilRemoveMethod.syntax:
ilRemoveMethod( 
s_genFunction 
g_className 
[ g_method ]
) 
=> t / nil
ilRemoveMethod.desc: Removes a given method from a generic function.

ilRemoveTopLevelErrorHandler.name: ilRemoveTopLevelErrorHandler
ilRemoveTopLevelErrorHandler.desc: Unregisters the top-level error handler previously registered by the ilAddTopLevelErrorHandler function.

ilSlotBoundp.name: ilSlotBoundp
ilSlotBoundp.desc: Checks if a named slot is bound (has been assigned a value) to an instance.

ilToolBox.name: ilToolBox
ilToolBox.desc: Brings up the SKILL Development toolbox, which lets you debug SKILL programs using a form-based graphical user interface.

inNext.name: inNext
inNext.desc: Returns t if the function is called in the expression that is executed in the debugged code on the next() SKILL function.

inStepOut.name: inStepOut
inStepOut.desc: Returns t if the function is called in the stepout() SKILL function.

installDebugger.name: installDebugger
installDebugger.desc: Installs the SKILL debugger as the error handler so that the debugger is entered automatically upon error.

listAlias.name: listAlias
listAlias.desc: Prints a (property) list of all current aliases and associated function symbols, or the function symbol for which the given alias is defined.

listFunctions.name: listFunctions
listFunctions.desc: Returns all public function names that contain the given substring or match the given regular expression. If the second (optional) argument is specified as t (or a non-nil value), listFunctions looks at the SKILL virtual machine, rather than the cdsFinder database, and returns all isCallable Cadence public functions and user-defined SKILL functions that contain the given substring or match the given regular expression.

listVariables.name: listVariables
listVariables.desc: Returns all variable names that match the given substring or regular expression as part or all of their print name.

memoryAllocated.name: memoryAllocated
memoryAllocated.desc: Returns the amount of memory allocated by a process. The returned value is an approximation in megabytes and might not include the memory that has been allocated, but the amount that is unused.

next.name: next
next.desc: Allows execution to proceed until the next expression. This function only works if executed from within a break handler and if the code you want to step through was loaded under debugMode. See installDebugger.

pp.name: pp
pp.desc: Pretty prints the definition of a function. The function must not be read-protected. This is an nlambda function.

printFunctions.name: printFunctions
printFunctions.desc: Prints all function names that contain the given substring or match the given regular expression.

printObject.name: printObject
printObject.desc: Writes a description of an object to an output port.

printstruct.name: printstruct
printstruct.desc: Prints the contents of an association table or defstruct in a tabular format.

printVariables.name: printVariables
printVariables.desc: Prints all variable names that contain the given substring or match the given regular expression, along with their values.

removeMethod.name: removeMethod
removeMethod.syntax:
removeMethod( 
s_genFunction 
g_className 
[ g_role ]
) 
=> t / nil
removeMethod.desc: Removes a given method from a generic function.

resume.name: resume
resume.desc: Exits the interactive top-level loop started with the most recently invoked toplevel function and returns its argument to the caller of toplevel. Do not use this function programmatically; use it only as an interactive command.

skillDebugger.name: skillDebugger
skillDebugger.desc: Activates the SKILL Debugger. Usually invoked by a break or error handler.

skillDevStatus.name: skillDevStatus
skillDevStatus.desc: Returns the current status of the Cadence SKILL Development Environment license.

stacktrace.name: stacktrace
stacktrace.syntax:
stacktrace( 
[ g_unevaluated ] 
[ x_depth ] 
[ x_skip ] 
[ p_port ] 
) 
=> x_result
stacktrace.desc: Prints the functions on the stack and their arguments to the depth specified, or to the bottom of the stack if no depth is specified.

step.name: step
step.desc: Steps into functions and executes a given number of SKILL functions. This function only works if executed from within a break handler and if the code you want to step through was loaded under debugMode. See installDebugger.

stepend.name: stepend
stepend.desc: Allows execution to proceed to the end of the nth enclosing form and displays its result. stepend cannot proceed past the end of the current function. This function only works if executed from within a break handler and if the code you want to step through was loaded under debugMode. See installDebugger.

stepout.name: stepout
stepout.desc: Allows execution to proceed until the evaluator returns from the current function.

toplevel.name: toplevel
toplevel.desc: Starts an interactive top-level loop in either SKILL or SKILL++ mode.

tracef.name: tracef
tracef.desc: Turns on tracing of specified functions. Shows the functions called with their evaluated arguments and return values. This is an nlambda function.

tracelevlimit.name: tracelevlimit
tracelevlimit.desc: Limits the indentation level and hence the call depth while tracing functions, arrays, or variables.

tracelevunlimit.name: tracelevunlimit
tracelevunlimit.desc: Turns off limiting of the indentation level and hence the call depth while tracing functions, arrays, or variables.

tracep.name: tracep
tracep.desc: Turns on tracing of assignments to specified properties. This is an nlambda function.

tracev.name: tracev
tracev.desc: Turns on tracing of assignments to specified variables. This is an nlambda function.

unbreakpt.name: unbreakpt
unbreakpt.desc: Clears breakpoints. This is an nlambda function.

unbreakptMethod.name: unbreakptMethod
unbreakptMethod.desc: Removes breakpoints set on the specified method.

uncount.name: uncount
uncount.desc: Turns off counting and returns the current count results. This is an nlambda function.

uninstallDebugger.name: uninstallDebugger
uninstallDebugger.desc: Uninstalls the SKILL debugger as the error handler. Turns off debug mode.

untrace.name: untrace
untrace.desc: Turns tracing off for all functions specified that were traced using the tracef function. This is an nlambda function.

untracep.name: untracep
untracep.desc: Turns off tracing of the specified properties. This is an nlambda function.

untracev.name: untracev
untracev.desc: Turns off tracing for assignments to specified variables. This is an nlambda function.

unwatch.name: unwatch
unwatch.desc: Clears watchpoints set on the specified variables.

watch.name: watch
watch.desc: Sets watchpoints on the specified variables. If watch() is called without arguments, it returns the list of variables being watched. If no variables are being watched, it returns nil.

where.name: where
where.syntax:
where( 
[ g_unevaluated ] 
[ x_depth ] 
[ x_skip ] 
[ p_port ] 
) 
=> x_result
where.desc: Prints the functions on the stack and their arguments to the depth specified, or to the bottom of the stack, including the local variables and their bindings.

whereIs.name: whereIs
whereIs.desc: Prints the last file loaded in debug mode in which a function was defined, as well as the starting line number.

fndResetDb.name: fndResetDb
fndResetDb.desc: Resets a previously loaded Finder database.

startFinder.name: startFinder
startFinder.desc: Starts the SKILL API Finder utility. If the t_funcName argument is provided, the corresponding documentation of the function is displayed in the Finder. If a Finder window is already open, it will be updated or a new window will be displayed. The Finder window remains open, unless specifically closed, even after the parent window has been closed.

skTabulate.name: skTabulate
skTabulate.syntax:
skTabulate( 
?fileNames g_tabulatedFileNames
[ ?reportFile t_reportFile ] 
[ ?showFile g_showFile ] 
[ ?dontResolveSymLink g_dontResolveSymLink ] 
[ ?customerInfo l_customerInfo ] 
[ ?printFiltered g_printFiltered ] 
[ ?ext l_ext ] 
[ ?infoFile g_infoFile ] 
[ ?defnFile g_defnFile ] 
[ ?recurse g_recurse ] 
[ ?exclude g_exclude ] 
[ ?recurseExclude g_recurseExclude ] 
[ ?sendReport g_sendReport ] 
=> t
skTabulate.desc: Runs the SKILL Tabulator in batch mode.

skTabulateSKILL.name: skTabulateSKILL
skTabulateSKILL.desc: Brings up the SKILL Tabulator UI form.

ilgAddRecentFiles.name: ilgAddRecentFiles
ilgAddRecentFiles.desc: Adds the files listed in l_fileList to the SKILL IDE File menu.

ilgAppendText.name: ilgAppendText
ilgAppendText.desc: Inserts text into the SKILL IDE editor window at the current cursor location.

ilgCopy.name: ilgCopy
ilgCopy.desc: Copies the selected text into public text buffer. This function does not work on read-only files.

ilgCut.name: ilgCut
ilgCut.desc: Cuts and pastes the selected text into public text buffer. This function does not work on read-only files.

ilgFindIdent.name: ilgFindIdent
ilgFindIdent.syntax:
ilgFindIdent( 
x_column 
x_row 
[ ?tab w_tab ]
) 
=> l_coord / nil
ilgFindIdent.desc: Returns the nearest identifiers from a given opening parenthesis location '(' in the SKILL IDE editor tab.

ilgFindParenthesis.name: ilgFindParenthesis
ilgFindParenthesis.syntax:
ilgFindParenthesis( 
x_column 
x_row 
[ ?level S_level ]
[ ?direction S_direction ]
[ ?tab w_tab ]
) 
=> l_coord / nil
ilgFindParenthesis.desc: Returns the closest parenthesis in a file currently open in the SKILL IDE editor.

ilgFoldLine.name: ilgFoldLine
ilgFoldLine.desc: Folds a document block in SKILL IDE at (x_column x_row) where (x_column x_row) is the location of an opening parenthesis. If this function is called without arguments, the current cursor location is used for computing (x_column x_row).

ilgGetCursorLocation.name: ilgGetCursorLocation
ilgGetCursorLocation.desc: Returns the location of the cursor in the SKILL IDE editor window.

ilgGetEditLock.name: ilgGetEditLock
ilgGetEditLock.desc: Returns the read-only property for a SKILL IDE editor window.

ilgGetHighlight.name: ilgGetHighlight
ilgGetHighlight.desc: Returns the list of highlight IDs for the text highlighted in the SKILL IDE editor window.

ilgGetSelectedLocation.name: ilgGetSelectedLocation
ilgGetSelectedLocation.desc: Returns the location coordinates of the current selection in the SKILL IDE editor window.

ilgGetText.name: ilgGetText
ilgGetText.desc: Returns the text between l_location_begin and l_location_end. If these locations are not provided, the entire text in the SKILL IDE editor window is returned.

ilgInvokeIDE.name: ilgInvokeIDE
ilgInvokeIDE.desc: Displays the SKILL IDE main window.

ilgLastDir.name: ilgLastDir
ilgLastDir.desc: Returns the directory path of the file currently open in SKILL IDE.

ilgPaste.name: ilgPaste
ilgPaste.desc: Pastes the text from the clipboard/buffer to the cursor location in the SKILL IDE editor window. This function does not work on read-only files.

ilgPositionInComment.name: ilgPositionInComment
ilgPositionInComment.syntax:
ilgPositionInComment( 
x_column 
x_row 
[ ?tab w_tab ]
) 
=> t / nil
ilgPositionInComment.desc: Checks if the specified coordinates (x_column x_row) fall within a comments block in the SKILL IDE document.

ilgRegisterSelectionCB.name: ilgRegisterSelectionCB
ilgRegisterSelectionCB.desc: Registers a SKILL callback for SKILL IDE, which is called when some text is selected in the SKILL IDE editor window.

ilgResetErrorMarker.name: ilgResetErrorMarker
ilgResetErrorMarker.desc: Clears the error marker that was set by ilgSetErrorMarker() on line x_line in the SKILL IDE editor window.

ilgResetHighlight.name: ilgResetHighlight
ilgResetHighlight.desc: Resets a specified highlight in a SKILL IDE document between location l_location_begin and l_location_end.

ilgResetWarningMarker.name: ilgResetWarningMarker
ilgResetWarningMarker.desc: Clears the warning marker that was set by ilgSetWarningMarker() on line x_line in the SKILL IDE editor window.

ilgRunSKILLIDE.name: ilgRunSKILLIDE
ilgRunSKILLIDE.desc: Launches SKILL IDE and opens the files listed in lt_fileList.

ilgScrollToLocation.name: ilgScrollToLocation
ilgScrollToLocation.desc: Scrolls to the specified location in the specified SKILL IDE editor window or tab.

ilgSearchText.name: ilgSearchText
ilgSearchText.syntax:
ilgSearchText( 
t_text 
[ ?loc l_location ]
[ ?direction s_direction ]
[ w_tab ]
) 
=> l_location / nil
ilgSearchText.desc: Searches the specified text in a SKILL IDE document.

ilgSelectText.name: ilgSelectText
ilgSelectText.desc: Selects the text between location l_location_begin and l_location_end in the SKILL IDE editor window.

ilgSetColor.name: ilgSetColor
ilgSetColor.syntax:
ilgSetColor( 
t_text
t_value
[ x_alpha ]
)
=> t / nil
ilgSetColor.desc: Sets a custom color for the given SKILL IDE GUI control.

ilgSetCursorLocation.name: ilgSetCursorLocation
ilgSetCursorLocation.desc: Sets the cursor location in a SKILL IDE document.

ilgSetEditLock.name: ilgSetEditLock
ilgSetEditLock.desc: Changes the read-only property for a SKILL IDE editor window.

ilgSetErrorMarker.name: ilgSetErrorMarker
ilgSetErrorMarker.desc: Sets the error marker with the pop-up description t_description on line x_line of the SKILL IDE editor window.

ilgSetHighlight.name: ilgSetHighlight
ilgSetHighlight.syntax:
ilgSetHighlight( 
l_location_begin
l_location_end
t_color
[ ?fullWidth g_fullWidth ]
[ w_tab ]
) 
=> l_highlightID / nil
ilgSetHighlight.desc: Highlights the area within l_location_begin and l_location_end in the color specified by t_color.

ilgSetWarningMarker.name: ilgSetWarningMarker
ilgSetWarningMarker.desc: Sets the warning marker with pop-up description t_description on line x_line of the SKILL IDE editor window.

ilgUnfoldLine.name: ilgUnfoldLine
ilgUnfoldLine.desc: This function unfolds a document block in SKILL IDE at position (x_column x_row), if it was folded. Here (x_column x_row) is the location of an opening parenthesis. If this function is called without arguments, the current cursor location is used for computing (x_column x_row).

ilgUnregisterSelectionCB.name: ilgUnregisterSelectionCB
ilgUnregisterSelectionCB.desc: Unregisters a selection callback that was previously registered using ilgRegisterSelectionCB.

ipcActivateBatch.name: ipcActivateBatch
ipcActivateBatch.desc: Switches a child process to batch mode.

ipcActivateMessages.name: ipcActivateMessages
ipcActivateMessages.desc: Switches a child process into interactive mode. In interactive mode, output from the child is written to a log file and is passed on to the parent process.

ipcBatchProcess.name: ipcBatchProcess
ipcBatchProcess.desc: Invokes a process to execute batch commands. The child process in this case is a batch process that does not communicate with the parent process.

ipcBeginProcess.name: ipcBeginProcess
ipcBeginProcess.syntax:
ipcBeginProcess( 
t_command 
[ t_hostName ] 
[ tsu_dataHandler ] 
[ tsu_errHandler ] 
[ tsu_postFunc ] 
[ t_logFile ] 
) 
=> o_childId
ipcBeginProcess.desc: Invokes a process to execute a command or sequence of commands specified.

ipcCloseProcess.name: ipcCloseProcess
ipcCloseProcess.desc: Closes the input channel of the child process.

ipcContProcess.name: ipcContProcess
ipcContProcess.desc: Causes a suspended child process to resume executing. This is equivalent to sending a UNIX CONT signal.

ipcGetExitStatus.name: ipcGetExitStatus
ipcGetExitStatus.desc: Returns the exit value of the child process.

ipcGetPid.name: ipcGetPid
ipcGetPid.desc: Returns the runtime process identification number of the process executing this function.

ipcGetPriority.name: ipcGetPriority
ipcGetPriority.desc: Gets the current default priority. If a child process handle is given, ipcGetPriority returns the priority under which the relevant child process was invoked.

ipcIsActiveProcess.name: ipcIsActiveProcess
ipcIsActiveProcess.desc: Determines if a child process is active; that is, not stopped.

ipcIsAliveProcess.name: ipcIsAliveProcess
ipcIsAliveProcess.desc: Checks if a child process is still alive.

ipcKillAllProcesses.name: ipcKillAllProcesses
ipcKillAllProcesses.desc: Kills every process initiated by the parent through one of the ipcBeginProcess class of functions.

ipcKillProcess.name: ipcKillProcess
ipcKillProcess.desc: Kills the process identified by o_childId. This call results in a UNIX SIGKILL signal being sent to the child process.

ipcReadProcess.name: ipcReadProcess
ipcReadProcess.desc: Reads data from the child process stdout channel, allowing the developer to specify a time, in seconds, beyond which the read operation must not block. It only reads 4096 bytes for each call.

ipcSetPriority.name: ipcSetPriority
ipcSetPriority.desc: Sets the priority value for child processes. All processes spawned after this call run at the priority offset to x_priorityChange.

ipcSignalProcess.name: ipcSignalProcess
ipcSignalProcess.desc: Sends the specified POSIX signal to the specified UNIX/Linux child process.

ipcSkillProcess.name: ipcSkillProcess
ipcSkillProcess.syntax:
ipcSkillProcess( 
t_command 
[ t_hostName ] 
[ tsu_dataHandler ] 
[ tsu_errHandler ] 
[ tsu_postFunc ] 
[ t_logFile ] 
[ x_cmdDesc ] 
[ x_resDesc ] 
)
=> o_childId
ipcSkillProcess.desc: Invokes an operating system process capable of executing SKILL functions in the parent process and opens two additional channels to the child process that let the child send and receive the results of SKILL commands.

ipcSleep.name: ipcSleep
ipcSleep.desc: Causes the parent process to be delayed for the given number of seconds.

ipcSleepMilli.name: ipcSleepMilli
ipcSleepMilli.desc: Causes the parent process to be delayed for the given number of milliseconds. Use the otherwise identical ipcSleep function to specify the delay in seconds.

ipcSoftInterrupt.name: ipcSoftInterrupt
ipcSoftInterrupt.desc: Equivalent to executing the UNIX kill -2 command. If the child process is active, it is sent a soft interrupt. The child is responsible for catching the signal.

ipcStopProcess.name: ipcStopProcess
ipcStopProcess.desc: Causes the child process to suspend its execution. This is equivalent to sending a STOP signal through the UNIX kill command.

ipcWait.name: ipcWait
ipcWait.desc: Causes the parent process to suspend until the child terminates.

ipcWaitForProcess.name: ipcWaitForProcess
ipcWaitForProcess.desc: Causes the parent process to suspend until the child process is alive and ready for communication.

ipcWriteProcess.name: ipcWriteProcess
ipcWriteProcess.desc: Writes data to the stdin port of the child process.

phoIPCGetServerCheck.name: phoIPCGetServerCheck
phoIPCGetServerCheck.desc: Returns the name of the registered function that can be called to check if the server associated with the specified tool is operating correctly.

phoIPCRegisterServerCheck.name: phoIPCRegisterServerCheck
phoIPCRegisterServerCheck.desc: Registers a function that can be used to check if the server associated with the specified tool is operating correctly. The registered server check function is expected to have no arguments. If the function is not specified, or it has an argument, registration fails. If the function is registered, it checks that the IPC channel is open and connected to the child process. This function is intended to perform a quick check and is likely to be used inside a Pcell.

phoIPCServerCheck.name: phoIPCServerCheck
phoIPCServerCheck.desc: Calls the registered server check function for the specified tool and issues a warning in the CIW if the server is not running. In addition, when a valid cellview is specified, the function creates a label at the origin that displays the same message in the layout canvas.

phoIPCGetMessageProcessor.name: phoIPCGetMessageProcessor
phoIPCGetMessageProcessor.desc: Returns the name of the message processor associated with the specified tool.

phoIPCProcessMarkers.name: phoIPCProcessMarkers
phoIPCProcessMarkers.syntax:
phoIPCProcessMarkers(
d_cellviewID
l_markerList
s_displayToolName
)
=> t / nil
phoIPCProcessMarkers.desc: Specifies the default marker processor for the specified tool and generates markers in the Annotation Browser assistant, categorizing the markers based on the specified markerList.

phoIPCProcessPorts.name: phoIPCProcessPorts
phoIPCProcessPorts.syntax:
phoIPCProcessPorts(
d_cellviewID
l_opticalPortList
[ l_portMap ]
[ l_lppMap ]
)
=> t / nil
phoIPCProcessPorts.desc: Creates optical ports in the specified cellview using the specfied portList. This is the default optical port processor.

phoIPCProcessServerMessage.name: phoIPCProcessServerMessage
phoIPCProcessServerMessage.syntax:
phoIPCProcessServerMessage(
d_cellviewID
t_waveguideLayer
t_serverMessage
[ g_dropPorts ]
[ l_portMap ]
[ l_lppMap ]
)
phoIPCProcessServerMessage.desc: Issues messages from the IPC processor, which can further be used in Pcells to create geometries.

phoIPCProcessShapes.name: phoIPCProcessShapes
phoIPCProcessShapes.syntax:
phoIPCProcessShapes(
d_cellviewID
l_shapeList
l_portMap
[ l_lppMap ]
)
=> t / nil
phoIPCProcessShapes.desc: Uses shapeList to create shapes and electrical pins in the specified cellview. This is the default shape processor.

phoIPCRegisterMessageProcessor.name: phoIPCRegisterMessageProcessor
phoIPCRegisterMessageProcessor.desc: Registers the message processor corresponding to the specified tool. In addition, the function ensures that the message processor function is defined and has the correct number of arguments.

append.name: append
append.syntax:
append( 
l_list1 
l_list2 
) 
=> l_result 

append( 
o_table 
g_assoc 
) 
=> o_table 	

append( 
o_table1 
o_table2 
) 
=> o_newTable
append.desc: Creates a list containing the elements of l_list1 followed by the elements of l_list2 or returns the original association table including new entries.

append1.name: append1
append1.desc: Adds new arguments to the end of a list.

car.name: car
car.desc: Returns the first element of a list. car is nondestructive, meaning that it returns the first element of a list but does not modify the list that was its argument.

cdr.name: cdr
cdr.desc: Returns the tail of the list, that is, the list without its first element.

cons.name: cons
cons.desc: Adds an element to the beginning of a list. Thus the car of l_result is g_element and the cdr of l_result is l_list. l_list can be nil, in which case a new list containing the single element is created.

constar.name: constar
constar.desc: Adds elements to the beginning of a list.

copy.name: copy
copy.desc: Returns a copy of a list, that is, a list with all the top-level cells duplicated.

dtpr.name: dtpr
dtpr.desc: Checks whether an object is a non-empty list.

last.name: last
last.desc: Returns the last list cell in a list.

lconc.name: lconc
lconc.desc: Uses a tconc structure to efficiently splice a list to the end of another list.

length.name: length
length.desc: Determines the length of a list, array, association table, or string.

lindex.name: lindex
lindex.syntax:
lindex( 
l_list 
g_element 
[ ?all g_all ]
) 
=> x_result / l_result / nil
lindex.desc: Returns the index number of the given element in l_list.

list.name: list
list.desc: Creates a list with the given elements.

listp.name: listp
listp.desc: Checks whether the specified object is a list.

nconc.name: nconc
nconc.desc: Equivalent to a destructive append where the first argument is modified.

ncons.name: ncons
ncons.desc: Builds a list containing an element. This function is equivalent to cons( g_element nil ).

nth.name: nth
nth.desc: Returns an index-selected element of a list, assuming a zero-based index.

nthcdr.name: nthcdr
nthcdr.desc: Applies cdr to a list a given number of times.

nthelem.name: nthelem
nthelem.desc: Returns the indexed element of the list, assuming a one-based index.

pairp.name: pairp
pairp.desc: Checks if an object is a cons object, that is, a non-empty list. This function is equivalent to dtpr.

range.name: range
range.desc: Returns a list whose first element is n_num1 and whose tail is n_num2. This function is a prefix form of the : operator.

remd.name: remd
remd.desc: Removes all top-level elements equal to a SKILL object from a list. This is a destructive removal, which means that the original list itself is modified. Therefore, any other reference to that list will also see the changes.

remdq.name: remdq
remdq.desc: Removes all top-level elements that are identical to a SKILL object using eq from a list. This is a destructive removal, which means that the original list itself is modified. Therefore, any other reference to that list will also see the changes.

remove.name: remove
remove.syntax:
remove( 
g_x 
l_arg 
) 
=> l_result

remove( 
g_key 
o_table 
) 
=> g_value
remove.desc: Returns a copy of a list with all top-level elements equal to a SKILL object removed. Can also be used to remove an entry from an association table, in which case the removal is destructive, that is, any other reference to the table will also see the changes. remove uses equal for comparison. remove can also be used with an association table to identify and remove an entry corresponding to the key specified in the function.

removeListDuplicates.name: removeListDuplicates
removeListDuplicates.desc: Removes duplicate entries from a SKILL list and returns a new list with the duplicates removed.

remq.name: remq
remq.desc: Returns a copy of a list with all top-level elements that are identical to a SKILL object removed. Uses eq.

reverse.name: reverse
reverse.desc: Returns a copy of the given list with the elements in reverse order.

rplaca.name: rplaca
rplaca.desc: Replaces the first element of a list with an object. This function does not create a new list; it alters the input list, in the same way as setcar. This is a destructive operation, meaning that any other reference to the list will also see the change.

rplacd.name: rplacd
rplacd.desc: Replaces the tail of a list with the elements of a second list. This function does not create a new list; it alters the input list in the same way as setcdr. This is a destructive operation, meaning that any other reference to the list will also see the changes.

setcar.name: setcar
setcar.desc: Replaces the first element of a list with an object in the same way as rplaca. This is a destructive operation, meaning that any other reference to the list will also see the change.

setcdr.name: setcdr
setcdr.desc: Replaces the tail of a list with the elements of a second list in the same way as rplacd. This is a destructive operation, meaning that any other reference to the list will also see the change.

subst.name: subst
subst.desc: Substitutes one object for another object in a list.

tailp.name: tailp
tailp.desc: Returns arg1 if a list cell eq to arg1 is found by cdr down arg2 zero or more times. It returns nil otherwise. Because eq is being used for comparison l_arg1 must point to a tail list in l_arg2 for this predicate to return a non-nil value.

tconc.name: tconc
tconc.desc: Creates a list cell whose car points to a list of the elements being constructed and whose cdr points to the last list cell of the list being constructed.

xcons.name: xcons
xcons.desc: Adds an element to the beginning of a list. Equivalent to cons but the order of the arguments is reversed.

xCoord.name: xCoord
xCoord.desc: Returns the first element of a list. Does not modify the argument list.

yCoord.name: yCoord
yCoord.desc: Returns the tail of the list, that is, the list without its first element.

arrayp.name: arrayp
arrayp.desc: Checks if an object is an array.

arrayref.name: arrayref
arrayref.desc: Returns the element in a collection that is in an array or a table of the given index.

declare.name: declare
declare.desc: Creates an array with a specified number of elements. This is a syntax form. All elements of the array are initialized to unbound.

defprop.name: defprop
defprop.desc: Adds properties to symbols but none of its arguments are evaluated. This is a syntax form.

defstruct.name: defstruct
defstruct.desc: Creates a defstruct, a named structure that is a collection of one or more variables.

defstructp.name: defstructp
defstructp.desc: Checks if an object is an instance of a particular defstruct.

defvar.name: defvar
defvar.desc: Defines a variable and assign it a value.The variable defined follows the scoping rule.

makeVector.name: makeVector
makeVector.desc: Creates an array (vector) with the specified number of elements, and optionally initializes each entry.

setarray.name: setarray
setarray.syntax:
setarray( 
a_array 
x_index 
g_value 
) 
=> g_value

setarray( 
o_table 
g_key 
g_value 
) 
=> g_value
setarray.desc: Assigns the given value to the specified element of an array or to the specified key of a table. Normally this function is invoked implicitly using the array-subscription syntax, such as, x[i] = v.

tablep.name: tablep
tablep.desc: Checks if an object is an association table.

vector.name: vector
vector.desc: Returns a vector or array, filled with the arguments in the given order. The vector function is analogous to the list function.

vectorp.name: vectorp
vectorp.desc: Checks whether the specified object is a vector. The behavior of this SKILL function is the same as arrayp.

alphaNumCmp.name: alphaNumCmp
alphaNumCmp.desc: Compares two string or symbol names alphanumerically or numerically.

concat.name: concat
concat.desc: Concatenates strings, symbols, or integers into a single symbol.

copyDefstructDeep.name: copyDefstructDeep
copyDefstructDeep.desc: Performs a deep or recursive copy on defstructs with other defstructs as sub-elements, making copies of all the defstructs encountered.

get.name: get
get.desc: Returns the value of a property in a property list (including disembodied property list), association table, structure, database object, and a standard object (instance of a user-defined subclass of standardObject). get has no infix operator syntax.

getSG.name: getSG
getSG.desc: Evaluates and then retrieves the value of the specified attribute or property. It is a lambda implementation of getSGq().

getq.name: getq
getq.syntax:
getq( 
sl_id 
S_name 
) 
=> g_result / nil

sl_id->S_name 
=> g_result / nil
getq.desc: Returns the value of a property in a property list. Same as get except that the second argument is not evaluated. This is a syntax form.

getqq.name: getqq
getqq.syntax:
getqq( 
s_id 
S_name 
) 
=> g_result / nil

sl_id.S_name 
=> g_result / nil
getqq.desc: Returns the value of a property in a symbol's property list. Same as get except that neither argument is evaluated. This is a syntax form.

importSkillVar.name: importSkillVar
importSkillVar.desc: (SKILL++ mode) Tells the compiler that the given variable names should be treated as SKILL global variables in SKILL++ code.

integerp.name: integerp
integerp.desc: Checks if an object is an integer. This function is the same as fixp.

otherp.name: otherp
otherp.desc: Checks if an object is a user type object, such as an association table or a window.

plist.name: plist
plist.desc: Returns the property list associated with a symbol.

popf.name: popf
popf.desc: A pop that uses the setf function. It returns the value for g_place that is removed.

postArrayDec.name: postArrayDec
postArrayDec.desc: Takes an array or an associated table element with an index g_index, decrements its value by one, stores the new value back into the array, and returns the original value. This function is a prefix form of s--.

postArrayInc.name: postArrayInc
postArrayInc.desc: Takes an array or an associated table element with an index g_index, increments its value by one, stores the new value back into the array, and returns the original value. This function is a prefix form of s++.

postArraySet.name: postArraySet
postArraySet.desc: Takes an array or an associated table element with an index g_index, adds an n_modifier value to its original value, stores the new value back into the array, and returns the original value.

postdecrement.name: postdecrement
postdecrement.desc: Takes a variable, decrements its value by one, stores the new value back into the variable, and returns the original value. This function is a prefix form of s--. The name of the variable must be a symbol and the value must be a number.

postincrement.name: postincrement
postincrement.desc: Takes a variable, increments its value by one, stores the new value back into the variable, and returns the original value. This function is a prefix form of s++. The name of the variable must be a symbol and the value must be a number.

preArrayDec.name: preArrayDec
preArrayDec.desc: Takes an array or an associated table element with an index g_index, decrements its value by one, stores the new value back into the array, and returns the updated value. This function is a prefix form of --s.

preArrayInc.name: preArrayInc
preArrayInc.desc: Takes an array or an associated table element with an index g_index, increments its value by one, stores the new value back into the array, and returns the updated value. This function is a prefix form of ++s.

preArraySet.name: preArraySet
preArraySet.desc: Takes array or an associated table element with an index g_index, adds an n_modifier value to its original value, stores the new value back into the array, and returns the updated value.

predecrement.name: predecrement
predecrement.desc: Takes a variable, decrements its value by one, stores the new value back into the variable, and returns the new value. This function is a prefix form of --s. The name of the variable must be a symbol and the value must be a number.

preincrement.name: preincrement
preincrement.desc: Takes a variable, increments its value by one, stores the new value back into the variable, and returns the new value. This function is a prefix form of ++s. The name of the variable must be a symbol and the value must be a number.

pushf.name: pushf
pushf.desc: A push that uses the setf function. It modifies the contents of the original storage location.

putprop.name: putprop
putprop.desc: Adds properties to symbols or disembodied property lists.

putpropq.name: putpropq
putpropq.syntax:
putpropq( 
sl_id 
g_value 
S_name 
) 
=> g_value

sl_id->S_name = g_value 
=> g_value
putpropq.desc: Adds properties to symbols or disembodied property lists. Identical to putprop except that S_name is not evaluated. If the property already exists, the old value is replaced with a new one.

putpropqq.name: putpropqq
putpropqq.syntax:
putpropqq( 
s_id 
g_value 
S_name 
) 
=> g_value

s_id.S_name = g_value 
=> g_value
putpropqq.desc: Adds properties to symbols. Identical to putprop except that sl_id and S_name are not evaluated. If the property already exists, the old value is replaced with a new one.

quote.name: quote
quote.desc: Returns the name of the variable or the expression. This function is a prefix form of the ' operator. Quoting is used to prevent expressions from being evaluated.

remprop.name: remprop
remprop.desc: Removes a property from a property list and returns the property's former value.

rotatef.name: rotatef
rotatef.desc: Modifies the value of each place by rotating the values from one place to another in a cyclic order.

set.name: set
set.desc: Sets a variable to a new value. Similar to setq but the first argument for set is evaluated.

setf.name: setf
setf.syntax:
setf( 
g_place 
g_value 
) 
=> g_result

setf( 
g_place := g_value
=> g_result
