setf.desc: Assigns a new value to an existing storage location, destroying the value that was previously in that location. setf is the same as the assignment (:=) operator. This is a syntax form.

setguard.name: setguard
setguard.desc: Mainly enforces disciplined use of a symbol as a global variable by associating it with a guarding function that is either a symbol that identifies the name of the guarding function or a lambda form (just like the first argument to the apply function). If the guarding function is nil, the symbol is unguarded. The guarding function is called with two arguments whenever a new value is assigned to the symbol: the symbol and the value to be assigned to it. The result of the guarding function determines the setguard return value that gets assigned to the symbol.

setplist.name: setplist
setplist.desc: Sets the property list of an object to a new property list; the old property list attached to the object is lost.

setq.name: setq
setq.syntax:
setq( 
s_variableName 
g_newValueExp 
) 
=> g_result

setq( 
s_variableName = g_newValue 
) 
=> g_result
setq.desc: Sets a variable to a new value. setq is the same as the assignment (=) operator. This is a syntax form.

setSG.name: setSG
setSG.desc: Evaluates and then sets the value for the specified attribute or property. It is a lambda implementation of setSGq().

symbolp.name: symbolp
symbolp.desc: Checks if an object is a symbol.

symeval.name: symeval
symeval.desc: Returns the value of the named variable.

symstrp.name: symstrp
symstrp.desc: Checks if an object is either a symbol or a string.

charToInt.name: charToInt
charToInt.desc: Returns the ASCII code of the first character of the given symbol. In SKILL, a single character symbol can be used as a character value.

intToChar.name: intToChar
intToChar.desc: Returns the single-character symbol whose ASCII code is the given integer value.

listToVector.name: listToVector
listToVector.desc: Returns a vector (array) filled with the elements from the given list. A vector is represented by an array.

stringToFunction.name: stringToFunction
stringToFunction.desc: Wraps and converts a string of SKILL code into a parameterless SKILL function.

stringToSymbol.name: stringToSymbol
stringToSymbol.desc: Converts a string to a symbol of the same name.

stringToTime.name: stringToTime
stringToTime.desc: Given a date and time string, returns an integer time value representation. The time argument must be in the format as returned by the timeToString function, such as: June 28 16:57:06 2022.

symbolToString.name: symbolToString
symbolToString.desc: Converts a symbol to a string of the same name. This function is the same as get_pname.

tableToList.name: tableToList
tableToList.desc: Converts the contents of an association table to an association list. Use this function interactively to look at the contents of a table.

timeToString.name: timeToString
timeToString.desc: Takes an integer UNIX time value, returns a formatted string that the value denotes. The string is always in a form like: Dec 28 16:57:06 2021.

timeToTm.name: timeToTm
timeToTm.desc: Given an integer time value, returns a tm structure.

tmToTime.name: tmToTime
tmToTime.desc: Given a tm structure, returns the integer value of the time it represents.

vectorToList.name: vectorToList
vectorToList.desc: Returns a list containing the elements of an array.

blankstrp.name: blankstrp
blankstrp.desc: Checks if the given string is empty or has blank space characters only and returns true. If there are non-space characters blankstrp returns nil.

buildString.name: buildString
buildString.desc: Concatenates a list of strings with specified separation characters.

getchar.name: getchar
getchar.desc: Returns an indexed character of a string or the print name if the string is a symbol. Unlike the C library, the getc and getchar SKILL functions are totally unrelated.

index.name: index
index.desc: Returns a string consisting of the remainder of string1 beginning with the first occurrence of string2.

lowerCase.name: lowerCase
lowerCase.desc: Returns a string that is a copy of the given argument with uppercase alphabetic characters replaced by their lowercase equivalents.

lsprintf.name: lsprintf
lsprintf.desc: Returns a string according to the provided format. lsprintf is a lambda version of the sprintf function that can be used as an argument with apply or funcall.

nindex.name: nindex
nindex.desc: Finds the symbol or string, S_string2, in t_string1 and returns the character index, starting from one, of the first point at which the S_string2 matches part of t_string1.

outstringp.name: outstringp
outstringp.desc: Checks whether the specified value is an outstring port.

parseString.name: parseString
parseString.desc: Breaks a string into a list of substrings with break characters.

pcreCompile.name: pcreCompile
pcreCompile.desc: Compiles a regular expression string pattern (t_pattern) into an internal representation that you can use in a pcreExecute function call. The compilation method is PCRE/Perl-compatible. You can use a second (optional) argument to specify independent option bits for controlling pattern compilation. You can set and unset the PCRE_CASELESS, PCRE_MULTILINE, PCRE_DOTALL, and PCRE_EXTENDED independent option bits from within the pattern. The content of the options argument specifies the initial setting at the start of compilation. You can set the PCRE_ANCHORED option at matching time and at compile time.

pcreExecute.name: pcreExecute
pcreExecute.syntax:
pcreExecute( 
o_comPatObj 
S_subject 
[ x_options ] 
) 
=> t / nil
pcreExecute.desc: Matches the subject string or symbol (S_subject) against a previously compiled pattern set up by the last pcreCompile call (o_comPatObj). The matching algorithm is PCRE/Perl-compatible. You can use a third (optional) argument to specify independent option bits for controlling pattern matching. You can use this function in conjunction with pcreCompile to match several subject strings or symbols against a single pattern.

pcreGenCompileOptBits.name: pcreGenCompileOptBits
pcreGenCompileOptBits.syntax:
pcreGenCompileOptBits( 
[ ?caseLess  g_setCaseLessp ]
[ ?multiLine g_setMultiLinep ]
[ ?dotAll    g_setDotAllp ]
[ ?extended  g_setExtendedp ]
[ ?anchored  g_setAnchoredp ]
[ ?dollar_endonly g_setDollarEndonlyp ]
[ ?ungreedy  g_setUngreedyp ]
[ ?no_auto_capture g_setNoAutoCapturep ]
[ ?firstline g_setFirstlinep ]
) 
=> x_resultOptBits
pcreGenCompileOptBits.desc: Generates bitwise inclusive OR-bor()-of zero or more independent option bits that affect compilation so that you can specify them symbolically in the pcreCompile function. If you call pcreGenCompileOptBits with no arguments, the function returns a zero (options have their default settings).

pcreGenExecOptBits.name: pcreGenExecOptBits
pcreGenExecOptBits.syntax:
pcreGenExecOptBits( 
[ ?anchored g_setAnchoredp ]
[ ?notbol   g_setNotbolp ]
[ ?noteol   g_setNoteolp ]
[ ?notempty g_setNotemptyp ]
[ ?partial  g_setPartialp ]
)
=> x_resultOptBits
pcreGenExecOptBits.desc: Generates bitwise inclusive OR-bor()-of zero or more independent option bits that affect pattern matching so that you can specify them symbolically in the pcreExecute function. If you call pcreGenExecOptBits with no arguments, the function returns a zero (options have their default settings).

pcreGetRecursionLimit.name: pcreGetRecursionLimit
pcreGetRecursionLimit.desc: Returns the PCRE maximum recursion depth (stack depth) that is set by the pcreSetRecursionLimit() function. The default value is 10000000.

pcreListCompileOptBits.name: pcreListCompileOptBits
pcreListCompileOptBits.desc: Displays information about the options used with pcreGenCompileOptBits. See the description of pcreGenCompileOptBits for more information.

pcreListExecOptBits.name: pcreListExecOptBits
pcreListExecOptBits.desc: Displays information about the options used with pcreGenExecOptBits.

pcreMatchAssocList.name: pcreMatchAssocList
pcreMatchAssocList.syntax:
pcreMatchAssocList( 
g_pattern 
l_subjects 
[ x_compOptBits ] 
[ x_execOptBits ]
) 
=> l_results / nil / error message(s)
pcreMatchAssocList.desc: Matches the keys of an association list of subjects (strings or symbols) against a regular expression pattern (g_pattern) and returns an association list of those elements that match. The keys are the first elements of each key/value pair in the association list. You can use optional arguments to specify independent option bits for controlling pattern compiling and matching. The compiling and matching algorithms are PCRE/Perl-compatible.

pcreMatchList.name: pcreMatchList
pcreMatchList.syntax:
pcreMatchList( 
g_pattern 
l_subjects 
[ x_compOptBits ] 
[ x_execOptBits ]
) 
=> l_results / nil / error message(s)
pcreMatchList.desc: Matches a list of subjects (strings or symbols) against a regular expression pattern (g_pattern) and returns a list of those elements that match. You can use optional arguments to specify independent option bits for controlling pattern compiling and matching. The compiling and matching algorithms are PCRE/Perl-compatible.

pcreMatchp.name: pcreMatchp
pcreMatchp.syntax:
pcreMatchp( 
g_pattern 
S_subject 
[ x_compOptBits ] 
[ x_execOptBits ] 
) 
=> t / nil
pcreMatchp.desc: Checks to see whether the subject string or symbol (S_subject) matches the specified regular expression pattern (g_pattern). You can use optional arguments to specify independent option bits for controlling pattern compiling and matching. The compiling and matching algorithms are PCRE/Perl-compatible. For greater efficiency when matching a number of subjects against a single pattern, you should use pcreCompile and pcreExecute.

pcreObjectp.name: pcreObjectp
pcreObjectp.desc: Checks to see whether the given argument is a pcreObject or not.

pcrePrintLastMatchErr.name: pcrePrintLastMatchErr
pcrePrintLastMatchErr.desc: Prints the error message associated with the last failed matching operation (that is, when pcreExecute returns nil).

pcreReplace.name: pcreReplace
pcreReplace.syntax:
pcreReplace( 
o_comPatObj 
t_source 
t_replacement 
x_index 
[ x_options ] ) 
=> t_result / t_source
pcreReplace.desc: Replaces one or all occurrences of a previously-compiled regular expression in the given source string with the specified replacement string. The integer index indicates which of the matching substrings to replace. If the index is less than or equal to zero, the function applies the replacement string to all matching substrings. You can use an optional argument to specify independent option bits for controlling pattern matching. The matching algorithm is PCRE/Perl-compatible.

pcreSetRecursionLimit.name: pcreSetRecursionLimit
pcreSetRecursionLimit.desc: Sets the maximum recursion depth for SKILL/PCRE match algorithms. The maximum recursion depth needs to be set for systems that have a low stack depth, in order to prevent crashes while using SKILL PCRE functions.

pcreSubpatCount.name: pcreSubpatCount
pcreSubpatCount.desc: Counts the subpatterns in a PCRE pattern.

pcreSubstitute.name: pcreSubstitute
pcreSubstitute.desc: If o_pcreObject is not provided, pcreSubstitute copies the input string and substitutes all pattern tags in it using the corresponding matched strings from the last pcreExecute/pcreMatch* operation.

readstring.name: readstring
readstring.desc: Returns the first expression in a string. Subsequent expressions in the string are ignored. The expression is not processed in any way.

rexCompile.name: rexCompile
rexCompile.desc: Compiles a regular expression string pattern into an internal representation to be used by succeeding calls to rexExecute.

rexExecute.name: rexExecute
rexExecute.desc: Matches a string or symbol against the previously compiled pattern set up by the last rexCompile call.

rexMagic.name: rexMagic
rexMagic.desc: Turns on or off the special interpretation associated with the meta-characters in regular expressions.

rexMatchAssocList.name: rexMatchAssocList
rexMatchAssocList.desc: Returns a new association list created out of those elements of the given association list whose key matches a regular expression pattern. The supplied regular expression pattern overwrites the previously compiled pattern and is used for subsequent matching until the next new pattern is provided.

rexMatchList.name: rexMatchList
rexMatchList.desc: Creates a new list of those strings or symbols in the given list that match a regular expression pattern. The supplied regular expression pattern overwrites the previously compiled pattern and is used for subsequent matching until the next new pattern is provided.

rexMatchp.name: rexMatchp
rexMatchp.desc: Checks to see if a string or symbol matches a given regular expression pattern. The supplied regular expression pattern overwrites the previously compiled pattern and is used for subsequent matching until the next new pattern is provided.

rexReplace.name: rexReplace
rexReplace.desc: Returns a copy of the source string in which the specified substring instances that match the last compiled regular expression are replaced with the given string.

rexSubstitute.name: rexSubstitute
rexSubstitute.desc: Substitutes the pattern tags in the argument string with previously matched (sub)strings.

rindex.name: rindex
rindex.desc: Returns a string consisting of the remainder of string1 beginning with the last occurrence of string2.

sprintf.name: sprintf
sprintf.desc: Formats the output and assigns the resultant string to the variable given as the first argument.

strcat.name: strcat
strcat.desc: Takes input strings or symbols and concatenates them.

stringp.name: stringp
stringp.desc: Checks if an object is a string.

strlen.name: strlen
strlen.desc: Returns the number of characters in a string.

strncat.name: strncat
strncat.desc: Creates a new string by appending a maximum number of characters from t_string2 to t_string1.

strncmp.name: strncmp
strncmp.desc: Compares two argument strings alphabetically only up to a maximum number of characters.

strpbrk.name: strpbrk
strpbrk.desc: Returns a substring of the first occurence in t_str1 of any character from the string pointed to by t_str2

substring.name: substring
substring.syntax:
substring( 
S_string 
x_index 
[ x_length ] 
) 
=> t_result / nil
substring.desc: Creates a new substring from an input string, starting at an index point and continuing for a given length.

upperCase.name: upperCase
upperCase.desc: Returns a string that is a copy of the given argument with the lowercase alphabetic characters replaced by their uppercase equivalents.

atof.name: atof
atof.desc: Converts a string into a floating-point number. Returns nil if the given string does not denote a number.

atoi.name: atoi
atoi.desc: Converts a string into an integer. Returns nil if the given string does not denote an integer.

ceiling.name: ceiling
ceiling.desc: Returns the smallest integer not smaller than the given argument.

defMathConstants.name: defMathConstants
defMathConstants.desc: Associates a set of predefined math constants as properties of the given symbol.

difference.name: difference
difference.desc: Returns the result of subtracting one or more operands from the first operand. Prefix form of the - arithmetic operator.

evenp.name: evenp
evenp.desc: Checks if a number is an even integer.

expt.name: expt
expt.desc: Returns the result of raising a base number to a power. Prefix form of the ** exponentiation operator.

fix.name: fix
fix.desc: Returns the largest integer not larger than the given argument.

fixp.name: fixp
fixp.desc: Checks whether the specified object is an integer, that is, a fixed number.

fix2.name: fix2
fix2.desc: This function is a version of the fix function that works for rounding issue in floating-point calculations. The function returns the largest integer not larger than the given argument.

float.name: float
float.desc: Converts a number into its equivalent floating-point number.

floatp.name: floatp
floatp.desc: Checks whether the specified object is a floating-point number. Same as realp.

floor.name: floor
floor.desc: Returns the largest integer not larger than the given argument.

isInfinity.name: isInfinity
isInfinity.desc: Checks whether the given flownum argument represents infinity (positive or negative).

isNaN.name: isNaN
isNaN.desc: Checks whether the given flownum argument represents NaN (not-a-number). Else, it returns nil.

leftshift.name: leftshift
leftshift.desc: Returns the integer result of shifting a value a specified number of bits to the left. Prefix form of the << arithmetic operator. leftshift is logical (that is, vacated bits are 0-filled).

minus.name: minus
minus.desc: Returns the negative of a number. Prefix form of the - unary operator.

minusp.name: minusp
minusp.desc: Checks if a value is a negative number. Same as negativep.

modf.name: modf
modf.desc: Returns the floating-point remainder of the division of f_flonum1 by f_flonum2.

modulo.name: modulo
modulo.desc: Returns the remainder of dividing two integers. The remainder always has the sign of the divisor.

nearlyEqual.name: nearlyEqual
nearlyEqual.syntax:
nearlyEqual( 
n_val1 n_val2 
[ f_relTolerance [f_absTolerance] ] 
) 
=> t / nil
nearlyEqual.desc: Checks whether one value (n_val1) is approximately equal to another value (n_val2).

negativep.name: negativep
negativep.desc: Checks whether the specified value is a negative number. Same as minusp.

oddp.name: oddp
oddp.desc: Checks whether an object is an odd integer. oddp is a predicate function.

onep.name: onep
onep.desc: Checks whether the given object is equal to one. onep is a predicate function.

plus.name: plus
plus.desc: Returns the result of adding one or more operands to the first operand. Prefix form of the + arithmetic operator.

plusp.name: plusp
plusp.desc: Checks whether the given object is a positive number.

quotient.name: quotient
quotient.desc: Returns the result of dividing the first operand by one or more operands. Prefix form of the / arithmetic operator.

realp.name: realp
realp.desc: Checks whether the specified value is a real number. Same as floatp.

remainder.name: remainder
remainder.desc: Returns the remainder of dividing two integers. The remainder is either zero or has the sign of the dividend. Same as mod.

rightshift.name: rightshift
rightshift.desc: Returns the integer result of shifting a value a specified number of bits to the right. Prefix form of the >> arithmetic operator. rightshift is logical (that is, vacated bits are 0-filled).

round2.name: round2
round2.desc: This function is a version of the round function that rounds the result in floating-point calculations to its closest integer value.

sort.name: sort
sort.desc: Sorts a list according to the specified comparison function. By default, the sort function uses alphalessp, which defaults to an alphabetical sort when u_comparefn is nil. This function does not create a new list. It returns the altered input list. This is a destructive operation. The l_data list is modified in place and no new storage is allocated. Pointers previously pointing to l_data may not be pointing at the head of the sorted list.

sortcar.name: sortcar
sortcar.desc: Similar to sort except that only the car of each element in a list is used for comparison by the sort function. This function does not create a new list. It returns the altered input list.

times.name: times
times.desc: Returns the result of multiplying the first operand by one or more operands. Prefix form of the * arithmetic operator.

truncate.name: truncate
truncate.desc: Truncates a given number to an integer.

xdifference.name: xdifference
xdifference.desc: Returns the integer result of subtracting one or more operands from the first operand. xdifference is an integer-only arithmetic function while difference can handle integers and floating-point numbers. xdifference runs slightly faster than difference in integer arithmetic calculation.

xplus.name: xplus
xplus.desc: Returns the integer result of adding one or more operands to the first operand. xplus is an integer-only arithmetic function while plus can handle integers and floating-point numbers. xplus runs slightly faster than plus in integer arithmetic calculation.

xquotient.name: xquotient
xquotient.desc: Returns the integer result of dividing the first operand by one or more operands. xquotient is an integer-only arithmetic function while quotient can handle integers and floating-point numbers. xquotient runs slightly faster than quotient in integer arithmetic calculation.

xtimes.name: xtimes
xtimes.desc: Returns the integer result of multiplying the first operand by one or more operands. xtimes is an integer-only arithmetic function while times can handle integers and floating-point numbers. xtimes runs slightly faster than times in integer arithmetic calculation.

zerop.name: zerop
zerop.desc: Checks whether the specified object is equal to zero. zerop is a predicate function.

zxtd.name: zxtd
zxtd.desc: Zero-extends the number represented by the rightmost specified number of bits in the given integer.

band.name: band
band.desc: Returns the integer result of the Boolean AND operation on each parallel pair of bits in each operand. Prefix form of the & bitwise operator.

bitfield.name: bitfield
bitfield.desc: Returns the value of a specified set of bits of a specified integer. Prefix form of the <:> operator.

bitfield1.name: bitfield1
bitfield1.desc: Returns the value of a specified bit of a specified integer. Prefix form of the <> operator.

bnand.name: bnand
bnand.desc: Returns the integer result of the Boolean NAND operation on each parallel pair of bits in each operand. Prefix form of the ~& bitwise operator.

bnor.name: bnor
bnor.desc: Returns the integer result of the Boolean NOR operation on each parallel pair of bits in each operand. Prefix form of the ~| bitwise operator.

bnot.name: bnot
bnot.desc: Returns the integer result of the Boolean NOT operation on each parallel pair of bits in each operand. Prefix form of the ~ (one's complement) unary operator.

bor.name: bor
bor.desc: Returns the integer result of the Boolean OR operation on each parallel pair of bits in each operand. Prefix form of the | bitwise operator.

bxnor.name: bxnor
bxnor.desc: Returns the integer result of the Boolean XNOR operation on each parallel pair of bits in each operand. Prefix form of the ~^ bitwise operator.

bxor.name: bxor
bxor.desc: Returns the integer result of the Boolean XOR operation on each parallel pair of bits in each operand. Prefix form of the ^ bitwise operator.

setqbitfield.name: setqbitfield
setqbitfield.syntax:
setqbitfield( 
s_var 
x_val 
x_msb 
x_lsb 
) 
=> x_result
setqbitfield.desc: Sets a value into a set of bits in the bit field specified by the variable s_var, stores the new value back into the variable, and then returns the new value. Prefix form of the <:>= operator.

setqbitfield1.name: setqbitfield1
setqbitfield1.desc: Sets a value into a single bit in the bit field specified by the variable s_var, stores the new value back into the variable, and then returns the new value. Prefix form of the <>= operator.

atan2.name: atan2
atan2.desc: Computes the principal value of the arc tangent of n_y/n_x, using the signs of both arguments to determine the quadrant of the return value.

alphalessp.name: alphalessp
alphalessp.desc: Compares two string or symbol names alphabetically.

and.name: and
and.syntax:
and( 
g_arg1 
g_arg2 
[ g_arg3... ] 
) 
=> nil / g_val
and.desc: Evaluates from left to right its arguments to see if the result is nil. As soon as an argument evaluates to nil, and returns nil without evaluating the rest of the arguments. Otherwise, and evaluates the next argument. If all arguments except for the last evaluate to non-nil, and returns the value of the last argument as the result of the function call. Prefix form of the && binary operator.

compareTime.name: compareTime
compareTime.desc: Compares two string arguments, representing a clock-calendar time.

eq.name: eq
eq.desc: Checks addresses when testing for equality.

equal.name: equal
equal.desc: Checks contents of strings and lists when testing for equality.

eqv.name: eqv
eqv.desc: Tests for the equality between two strings or two numbers of the same type (for example, both numbers are integers). Except for numbers, eqv is like eq.

geqp.name: geqp
geqp.desc: This predicate function checks if the first argument is greater than or equal to the second argument. Prefix form of the >= operator.

greaterp.name: greaterp
greaterp.desc: This predicate function checks if the first argument is greater than the second argument. Prefix form of the > operator.

leqp.name: leqp
leqp.desc: This predicate function checks if the first argument is less than or equal to the second argument. Prefix form of the <= operator.

lessp.name: lessp
lessp.desc: This predicate function checks if the first argument is less than the second argument. Prefix form of the < operator.

neq.name: neq
neq.desc: Checks if two arguments are not identical using the eq function and returns t if they are not. That is, g_arg1 and g_arg2 are tested to see if they are at the same address in memory.

nequal.name: nequal
nequal.desc: Checks if two arguments are not logically equivalent using the equal function and returns t if they are not.

null.name: null
null.desc: Checks if an object is equal to nil.

numberp.name: numberp
numberp.desc: Checks if a data object is a number, that is, either an integer or floating-point number.

or.name: or
or.syntax:
or( 
g_arg1 
g_arg2 
[ g_arg3... ] 
) 
=> nil / g_val
or.desc: Evaluates from left to right its arguments to see if the result is non-nil. As soon as an argument evaluates to non-nil, or returns that value without evaluating the rest of the arguments. If all arguments except the last evaluate to nil, or returns the value of the last argument as the result of the function call. Prefix form of the || binary operator.

sxtd.name: sxtd
sxtd.desc: Sign-extends the number represented by the rightmost specified number of bits in the given integer.

caseq.name: caseq
caseq.syntax:
caseq( 
g_keyForm 
l_clause1 
[ l_clause2 ... ] 
) 
=> g_result / nil
caseq.desc: Works like the case() function, but uses eq() to find a matching clause instead of the equal() function. The keys used with caseq() should therefore not be strings or lists. In case you want to use a string value or a list, SKILL recommends using the case() function. See eq for details on the difference between the eq() and equal() functions.

catch.name: catch
catch.desc: Establishes a control transfer or a return point for the throw and err functions. The return point is identified with a s_tag. So, when a particular tag/exception is caught, catch evaluates g_form. If the forms execute normally (without error), the value of the last body form is returned from the catch. There can also be nested catch blocks and s_tag can be t (the value t  the catch function catch any condition thrown by throw).

decode.name: decode
decode.syntax:
decode( 
g_keyForm 
l_clause1 
[ l_clause2 ... ] 
) 
=> g_result / nil
decode.desc: Branches to one of the clauses depending on the value of the given expression. decode() evaluates g_keyForm and matches the resulting value sequentially against the clauses until it finds a match. Once a match is found it stops searching the clauses, evaluates the forms in the matching clause, and returns the resulting value.

do.name: do
do.syntax:
do( 
( 
( 
s_var1 
g_initExp1 
[ g_stepExp1 ] 
)
( 
s_var2 
g_initExp2 
[ g_stepExp2 ] 
) ... 
)
( 
g_terminationExp 
g_terminationExp1 ... 
)
            g_loopExp1 
            g_loopExp2 ... 
)
=> g_value
do.desc: Iteratively executes one or more expressions. Used in SKILL++ mode only.

exists.name: exists
exists.syntax:
exists( 
s_formalVar 
l_valueList 
g_predicateExpr 
)
=> g_result

exists( 
s_key 
o_table 
g_predicateExpr 
)
=> t / nil
exists.desc: Returns the first tail of l_valueList whose car satisfies a predicate expression. Also verifies whether an entry in an association table satisfies a predicate expression. This is a syntax form.

existss.name: existss
existss.syntax:
existss( 
s_formalVar 
l_valueList 
g_predicateExpr 
)
=> g_result

existss( 
s_key 
o_table 
g_predicateExpr 
)
=> t / nil
existss.desc: Returns the first tail of l_valueList whose car satisfies a predicate expression. Also verifies whether an entry in an association table satisfies a predicate expression. In the SKILL++ mode, this function always locally wraps the loop or iterator local variable (s_formalVar) in a let block while compiling the code. Local wrapping preserves the lexical scope of the loop variable. This function may work slower than its non-wrapped counterpart exists. This is a syntax form.

fors.name: fors
fors.syntax:
fors( 
s_loopVar
x_initialValue
x_finalValue
g_expr1
[ g_expr2 ... ]
)
=> t
fors.desc: Evaluates the sequence g_expr1, g_expr2 ... for each loop variable value, beginning with x_initialValue and ending with x_finalValue. In the SKILL++ mode, this function always locally wraps the loop or iterator local variable (s_loopVar) in a let() block while compiling the code. Local wrapping preserves the lexical scope of the loop variable. This function may work slower than its non-wrapped counterpart for. This is a syntax form.

forall.name: forall
forall.syntax:
forall(
s_formalVar
l_valueList
g_predicateExpr
)
=> t / nil
forall(
s_key
o_table
g_predicateExpr
)
=> t / nil
forall.desc: Checks if g_predicateExpr evaluates to non-nil for every element in l_valueList. This is a syntax form.

foralls.name: foralls
foralls.syntax:
foralls( 
s_formalVar
l_valueList
g_predicateExpr
)
=> t / nil
foralls(
s_key
o_table
g_predicateExpr
)
=> t / nil
foralls.desc: Checks if g_predicateExpr evaluates to non-nil for every element in l_valueList. In the SKILL++ mode, this function always locally wraps the loop or iterator local variable (s_formalVar) in a let block while compiling the code. Local wrapping preserves the lexical scope of the loop variable. This function may work slower than its non-wrapped counterpart forall. This is a syntax form.

foreachs.name: foreachs
foreachs.syntax:
foreachs( 
s_formalVar 
g_exprList 
g_expr1 
[ g_expr2 ... ] 
)
=> l_valueList / l_result

foreachs( 
( 
s_formalVar1... 
s_formalVarN 
) 
g_exprList1... 
g_exprListN 
g_expr1 
[ g_expr2 ... ] 
)
=> l_valueList / l_result

foreachs( 
s_formalVar 
g_exprTable 
g_expr1 
[ g_expr2 ... ] 
)
=> o_valueTable / l_result
foreachs.desc: Evaluates one or more expressions for each element of a list of values. In the SKILL++ mode, this function always locally wraps the loop or iterator local variable, s_formalVar,in a let block while compiling the code. Local wrapping preserves the lexical scope of the loop variable. This function may work slower than its non-wrapped counterpart foreach. This is a syntax form.

go.name: go
go.desc: Transfers control to the statement following the label argument. This is a syntax form.

map.name: map
map.desc: Applies the given function to successive sublists of the argument lists and returns the first argument list. All of the lists should have the same length. This function is not the same as the standard Scheme map function. To get the behavior of the standard Scheme map function, use mapcar instead. This function is usually used for its side effects, not its return value (see mapc).

mapc.name: mapc
mapc.desc: Applies a function to successive elements of the argument lists and returns the first argument list. All of the lists should have the same length. mapc returns l_arg1.

mapcan.name: mapcan
mapcan.desc: Applies a function to successive elements of the argument lists and returns the result of appending these intermediate results. All of the lists should have the same length.

mapcar.name: mapcar
mapcar.desc: Applies a function to successive elements of the argument lists and returns the list of the corresponding results.

mapcon.name: mapcon
mapcon.desc: Applies the function u_func to successive sublists of the lists and returns a concatenated list.

mapinto.name: mapinto
mapinto.desc: Applies g_function to the elements of l_sequences and destructively modifies the l_resultSequence. The first argument is a sequence that receives the results of the mapping. If l_resultSequence and the other argument sequences are not all of the same length, the mapping stops when the shortest of l_resultSequence or l_sequences is exhausted.

maplist.name: maplist
maplist.desc: Applies a function to successive sublists of the argument lists and returns a list of the corresponding results. All of the lists should have the same length.

not.name: not
not.desc: Same as the ! operator. Returns t if the object is nil, and returns nil otherwise.

regExitAfter.name: regExitAfter
regExitAfter.desc: Registers the action to be taken after the exit function has performed its bookkeeping tasks but before it returns control to the operating system.

regExitBefore.name: regExitBefore
regExitBefore.desc: Registers the action to be taken before the exit function is executed. If the function registered returns the ignoreExit symbol, the exit is aborted.

return.name: return
return.desc: Forces the enclosing prog to exit and returns the given value. The return statement has meaning only when used inside a prog statement.

setof.name: setof
setof.desc: Returns a new list containing only those elements in a list or the keys in an association table that satisfy an expression. This is a syntax form.

setofs.name: setofs
setofs.desc: Returns a new list containing only those elements in a list or the keys in an association table that satisfy an expression. In the SKILL++ mode, this function always locally wraps the loop or iterator local variable (s_formalVar) in a let block while compiling the code. Local wrapping preserves the lexical scope of the loop variable. This function may work slower than its non-wrapped counterpart setof. This is a syntax form.

throw.name: throw
throw.desc: Transfers the control back to the return point established in a catch block. The argument value is used as the value to be passed. The throw function should always be used inside catch(. . . g_form . . .).

compress.name: compress
compress.syntax:
compress( 
t_sourceFile 
t_destFile 
) 
=> t / error message
compress.desc: Reduces the size of a SKILL file, which must be SKILL source code, and places the output into another file.

display.name: display
display.desc: Writes a representation of an object to the given port.

drain.name: drain
drain.desc: Writes out all characters that are in the output buffer of a port.

edi.name: edi
edi.desc: Edits the named file, then includes the file into SKILL.

edit.name: edit
edit.desc: Edits a file, function, or variable. This function only works if you are in graphical mode. This is an nlambda function.

edl.name: edl
edl.desc: Edits the named file, then loads the file into SKILL.

encrypt.name: encrypt
encrypt.desc: Encrypts a SKILL file and places the output into another file.

expandMacroDeep.name: expandMacroDeep
expandMacroDeep.desc: This function recursively expands all macros specified in g_form.

fileLength.name: fileLength
fileLength.desc: Determines the number of bytes in a file.

fileSeek.name: fileSeek
fileSeek.syntax:
fileSeek( 
p_port 
x_offset 
x_whence 
) 
=> t / nil
fileSeek.desc: Sets the position for the next operation to be performed on the file opened on a port. The position is specified in bytes.

fileTell.name: fileTell
fileTell.desc: Returns the current offset in bytes for the file opened on a port.

fileTimeModified.name: fileTimeModified
fileTimeModified.desc: Gets the time a given file was last modified.

fprintf.name: fprintf
fprintf.desc: Writes formatted output to a port.

get_filename.name: get_filename
get_filename.desc: Returns the file name of a port.

getc.name: getc
getc.desc: Reads and returns a single character from an input port. Unlike the C library, the getc and getchar SKILL functions are totally unrelated.

getDirFiles.name: getDirFiles
getDirFiles.desc: Returns a list of the names of all files and directories, including . and .., in a directory.

getOutstring.name: getOutstring
getOutstring.desc: Retrieves the content of the outstring port (while it is open).

include.name: include
include.desc: Loads the file with name t_file in SKILL regardless of any errors in the file.

info.name: info
info.desc: Prints the formatted output to poport according to the specification.

inportp.name: inportp
inportp.desc: Checks if an object is an input port.

instring.name: instring
instring.desc: Opens a string for reading, just as infile would open a file.

isExecutable.name: isExecutable
isExecutable.desc: Checks if you have permission to execute a file or search a directory.

isFile.name: isFile
isFile.desc: Checks if a file exists and that it is not a directory.

isFileEncrypted.name: isFileEncrypted
isFileEncrypted.desc: Checks if a file exists and is encrypted.

isFileName.name: isFileName
isFileName.desc: Checks if a file or directory exists.

isLargeFile.name: isLargeFile
isLargeFile.desc: Checks if a file is a large file (with size greater than 2GB).

isLink.name: isLink
isLink.desc: Checks if a path exists and if it is a symbolic link.

isPortAtEOF.name: isPortAtEOF
isPortAtEOF.desc: Takes an input port and returns t if end-of-file (EOF) has previously been detected while reading the input port; it returns nil otherwise.

isReadable.name: isReadable
isReadable.desc: Checks if you have permission to read a file or list a directory. Uses the current SKILL path for relative paths. A path that is anchored to the current directory, for example, ./, ../, or ../../.., and so on, is not considered as a relative path.

isWritable.name: isWritable
isWritable.desc: Checks if you have permission to write to a file or update a directory. Uses the current SKILL path for relative paths. A path that is anchored to the current directory, for example, ./, ../, or ../../.., and so on, is not considered as a relative path.

lineread.name: lineread
lineread.desc: Parses the next line in the input port into a list that you can further manipulate. It is used by the interpreter's top level to read in all input and understands SKILL and SKILL++ syntax.

linereadstring.name: linereadstring
linereadstring.desc: Executes lineread on a string and returns the first form read in. Anything after the first form is ignored.

loadi.name: loadi
loadi.desc: Identical to load, except that loadi ignores errors encountered during the load, prints an error message, and then continues loading.

loadPort.name: loadPort
loadPort.syntax:
loadPort( 
p_port 
[?langMode g_langMode]
[?password g_password]
[?ignoreErrors g_ignoreErrors])
) 
=> t
loadPort.desc: Loads a SKILL file from p_port.

loadstring.name: loadstring
loadstring.desc: Opens a string for reading, then parses and executes expressions stored in the string, just as load does in loading a file.

makeTempFileName.name: makeTempFileName
makeTempFileName.desc: Appends a string suffix to the last component of a path template so that the resulting composite string does not duplicate any existing file name.

numOpenFiles.name: numOpenFiles
numOpenFiles.desc: Returns the number of files now open and the maximum number of files that a process can open. The numbers are returned as a two-element list.

openportp.name: openportp
openportp.desc: Checks if the given argument is a port object and it is open (for input or output), nil otherwise.

outportp.name: outportp
outportp.desc: Checks if an object is an output port.

outstring.name: outstring
outstring.desc: Takes no arguments and returns an opened output port for strings (or an outport). After a port is opened, it can be used with functions, such as fprintf, println, and close that write to an output port. You need to use the getOutstring function to retrieve the content of output port (while it is open).

portp.name: portp
portp.desc: Checks if an object is an input or output port.

pprint.name: pprint
pprint.desc: Identical to print except that it pretty prints the value whenever possible.

print.name: print
print.desc: Prints a SKILL object using the default format for the data type of the value.

printlev.name: printlev
printlev.syntax:
printlev( 
g_value 
x_level 
x_length 
[ p_outputPort ] 
) 
=> nil
printlev.desc: Prints a list with a limited number of elements and levels of nesting.

putc.name: putc
putc.desc: Puts the x_symbol to p_port (to complement getc function)

read.name: read
read.desc: Parses and returns the next expression from an input port.

readTable.name: readTable
readTable.desc: Reads and appends the contents of a file to an existing association table.

renameFile.name: renameFile
renameFile.desc: The renameFile() function changes the name of a file or directory.The S_old argument points to the pathname of the file or directory to be renamed. The S_new argument points to the new pathname of the file or directory. If the SKILL path is nil, renameFile() would search the current directory. Otherwise, the SKILL path would be searched first for S_old. A path that is anchored to the current directory, for example, ./, ../, or ../../.., and so on, is not considered as a relative path.

simplifyFilename.name: simplifyFilename
simplifyFilename.desc: Expands the name of a file to its full path.

simplifyFilenameUnique.name: simplifyFilenameUnique
simplifyFilenameUnique.desc: Returns the full path for the given t_path without links and a trailing slash / at the end of the result string. The function returns an error if the given t_path is incorrect.

truename.name: truename
truename.desc: Tries to find the specified file (t_string) and returns the full path to the file.

which.name: which
which.desc: Returns the absolute path of the given context file, or regular file or directory.

write.name: write
write.desc: Prints a SKILL object using the default format for the data type of the value.

writeTable.name: writeTable
writeTable.desc: Writes the contents of an association table to a file with one key/value pair per line.

arglist.name: arglist
arglist.desc: Returns the number and types of arguments expected for a function. Also checks if the specified function is a binary object,

assert.name: assert
assert.desc: Enables you to insert assertions into the SKILL code, either at the top-level or within a function. It evaluates the expression (g_expression) and returns nil if the expression value is non-nil. Otherwise, throws an error and returns the unevaluated expression.

atom.name: atom
atom.desc: Checks if an object is an atom.

bcdp.name: bcdp
bcdp.desc: Checks if an object is a binary primitive function.

booleanp.name: booleanp
booleanp.desc: Checks if an object is a boolean. Returns t if the object is t or nil. Returns nil otherwise.

boundp.name: boundp
boundp.desc: Checks if the variable named by a symbol is bound, that is, has been assigned a value. The single argument form of boundp only works in SKILL mode.

describe.name: describe
describe.desc: Prints information about the symbol s_symbol. If the symbol has a function definition, information on the argument list and other available details will be printed. If the symbol has a variable definition, information about its value and function will be printed. If the function is called without any arguments, the help message will be printed.

fdoc.name: fdoc
fdoc.desc: Returns the documentation string for the function bound to the symbol s_function. SKILL switch saveInlineDoc must be set to save and retrieve the doc string.

gc.name: gc
gc.desc: Forces a garbage collection. This function is also called by the system.

gensym.name: gensym
gensym.desc: Returns a new symbol based on the input argument.

getMuffleWarnings.name: getMuffleWarnings
getMuffleWarnings.desc: Returns a list of warnings that were called and suppressed by the preceding muffleWarnings command.

getSkillVersion.name: getSkillVersion
getSkillVersion.desc: Returns the major version if the argument is left blank; otherwise, returns the current subversion (or tarkit version) of SKILL that is running in the build

get_pname.name: get_pname
get_pname.desc: Returns the print name of a symbol as a string.

get_string.name: get_string
get_string.desc: Converts the argument to a string if it is a symbol. Otherwise it returns the string itself.

getVersion.name: getVersion
getVersion.desc: Returns the version number of the Cadence software you are currently using. If you specify the optional argument g_opt, as t (or a non-nil value), the subversion number of the Cadence software currently used is returned. By default, the full version number, including the hotfix version, of the Cadence software currently used is returned.

getWarn.name: getWarn
getWarn.desc: Returns the buffered warning if it has not already been printed.

help.name: help
help.desc: Retrieves and prints the cdsFinder documentation strings for the given function name (a symbol). If the given name is a string, it is interpreted as a regular expression, and the entire cdsFinder database is searched for functions whose name or documentation string contains or matches the given string. Help is an nlambda function.

inScheme.name: inScheme
inScheme.desc: Evaluates a form as top-level SKILL++ code, disregarding the surrounding evaluation context.

inSkill.name: inSkill
inSkill.desc: Evaluates a form as top-level SKILL code, disregarding the surrounding evaluation context.

isVarImported.name: isVarImported
isVarImported.desc: Checks if the specified variable was imported into SKILL++ or not.

makeSymbol.name: makeSymbol
makeSymbol.desc: Creates a symbol corresponding to the specified symbol or character string. You can optionally specify the namespace name (t_namespace) in which you want to create the symbol.

measureTime.name: measureTime
measureTime.desc: Measures the time needed to evaluate an expression and returns a list with performance data (n_utime, n_stime, n_clockTime, and x_pageFaults) for the executed expressions. This is a syntax form.

muffleWarnings.name: muffleWarnings
muffleWarnings.desc: Returns the result of the last expression evaluated. If the last expression evaluated calls the warn function (either SKILL warn() or C-level ilWarn*), the related message is not printed out.

needNCells.name: needNCells
needNCells.desc: Ensures that there is enough memory available for the specified number of SKILL objects (cells).

restoreFloat.name: restoreFloat
restoreFloat.desc: Restores a floating point number (f_number) from its serialized string (t_string) representation. t_string should be created by saveFloat().

saveFloat.name: saveFloat
saveFloat.desc: Serializes the given floating point number (f_number) to string (t_string).

schemeTopLevelEnv.name: schemeTopLevelEnv
schemeTopLevelEnv.desc: Returns the top level SKILL++ environment as an environment object.

setPrompts.name: setPrompts
setPrompts.desc: Sets the prompt text string for the CIW. The first prompt is used to indicate the topmost top-level. The second prompt is used whenever a nested top-level is entered.

sstatus.name: sstatus
sstatus.desc: Sets the internal system variable named to a given value. This is a syntax form.

status.name: status
status.desc: Returns the value of the internal system variable named. This nlambda function also works in SKILL++ mode.

theEnvironment.name: theEnvironment
theEnvironment.desc: (SKILL++ mode only) Returns the top level environment if called from a SKILL++ top-level. Returns the enclosing lexical environment if called within a SKILL++ function. Returns the associated environment if passed a SKILL++ function object. Otherwise returns nil.

unbindVar.name: unbindVar
unbindVar.desc: Resets a SKILL or Scheme variable so that its value becomes unbound.

addDefstructClass.name: addDefstructClass
addDefstructClass.desc: Creates a class for the defstruct.

alias.name: alias
alias.desc: Defines a symbol as an alias for a function. This is an nlambda function.

apply.name: apply
apply.desc: Applies the given function to the given argument list.

argc.name: argc
argc.desc: Returns the number of arguments passed to a SKILL script. Used to enhance the SKILL script environment. This function works only for scripting with SKILL standalone executable (skill).

argv.name: argv
argv.desc: Returns the arguments passed to a SKILL script. Used to enhance the SKILL script environment. This function works only for scripting with SKILL standalone executable (skill).

begin.name: begin
begin.syntax:
SKILL mode
begin( 
g_exp1 
[ g_exp2 ... 
g_expN ] 
) 
=> g_result
SKILL++ mode
begin( 
	def1 
	[ def2 ... 
		defN ] 
) 
=> g_result
begin.desc: In the SKILL mode, begin is a syntax form used to group a sequence of expressions. Evaluates expressions from left to right and returns the value of the last expression. Equivalent to progn. This expression type is used to sequence side effects such as input and output. Whereas, in the SKILL++ mode, begin is a syntax form used to group either a sequence of expressions or a sequence of definitions.

clearExitProcs.name: clearExitProcs
clearExitProcs.desc: Removes all registered exit procedures. When the optional argument g_tcovItem is set to t, it removes all exit procedures except those needed for the ilTCov reports.

declareLambda.name: declareLambda
declareLambda.desc: Tells the evaluator that certain (forward referenced) functions are of lambda type (as opposed to nlambda or macro).

declareNLambda.name: declareNLambda
declareNLambda.desc: Tells the evaluator that certain (forward referenced) functions are of nlambda type (as opposed to lambdas or macros).

declareSQNLambda.name: declareSQNLambda
declareSQNLambda.desc: Declares the given nlambda functions to be solely-quoting nlambdas.

defdynamic.name: defdynamic
defdynamic.desc: This syntax form sets the dynamic variable s_varName to g_value. In SKILL, this function works as a defvar. In Scheme, g_value is evaluated in the current lexical scope.

defglobalfun.name: defglobalfun
defglobalfun.desc: Defines a global function with the name and formal argument list you specify.

define.name: define
define.syntax:
define( 
s_var 
g_expression 
) 
=> s_var

define( 
( 
s_var 
[ s_formalVar1 ... ] 
) 
g_body ... 
) 
=> s_var
define.desc: (SKILL++ mode only) Is a syntax form used to provide a definition for a global or local variable. The define syntax form has two variations.

define_syntax.name: define_syntax
define_syntax.desc: Creates a syntax rule using the syntax_rule expander form.

defmacro.name: defmacro
defmacro.desc: Defines a macro which can take a list of formal arguments including @optional, @key, and @rest (instead of the more restrictive format as required by using mprocedure).

defsetf.name: defsetf
defsetf.desc: defsetf is a macro that allows you to specify an update function to use when setf() is called with a place using a given access function. It creates a macro with the prefix setf_ which is used by setf to update a value at the place given by s_accessFn().

defun.name: defun
defun.desc: Defines a function with the name and formal argument list you specify. This is a syntax form.

defUserInitProc.name: defUserInitProc
defUserInitProc.syntax:
defUserInitProc( 
t_contextName 
u_func 
[ autoInit ]
)
=> ( t_contextName s_procName )
defUserInitProc.desc: Registers a user-defined function that the system calls immediately after autoloading a context.

destructuringBind.name: destructuringBind
destructuringBind.desc: Enables you to bind value to variables in a list. The list of values is obtained by evaluating the l_expression. The destructuringBind macro then evaluates the g_body form.

dynamic.name: dynamic
dynamic.desc: This syntax form returns the value of the dynamic variable s_varName. If s_varName is not a dynamic variable, it returns an error.

dynamicLet.name: dynamicLet
dynamicLet.desc: Evaluates the init forms (g_init1, g_init2, ...) in the current lexical environment, and then binds the variables (s_var1, s_var2, ...) in parallel. The variables are bound as SKILL dynamic variables for the duration of the body forms.

error.name: error
error.desc: Prints error messages and calls err.

errset.name: errset
errset.desc: Encapsulates the execution of an expression in an environment safe from the error mechanism. This is a syntax form.

errsetstring.name: errsetstring
errsetstring.syntax:
errsetstring( 
t_string 
[ g_errprint ] 
[ s_langMode ] 
) 
=> l_value / nil
errsetstring.desc: Reads and evaluates an expression stored in a string. Same as evalstring except that it calls errset to catch any errors that might occur during the parsing and evaluation.

eval.name: eval
eval.desc: Evaluates an argument and returns its value. If an environment argument is given, g_expression is treated as SKILL++ code, and the expression is evaluated in the given (lexical) environment. Otherwise g_expression is treated as SKILL code.

evalstring.name: evalstring
evalstring.desc: Reads and evaluates an expression stored in a string.

expandMacro.name: expandMacro
expandMacro.desc: Expands one level of macro call for a form.

fboundp.name: fboundp
fboundp.desc: Returns the function binding, if defined, for a specified function name.

flet.name: flet
flet.desc: Enables you to define local functions with LET semantics.

funcall.name: funcall
funcall.desc: Applies the given function to the given arguments.

getd.name: getd
getd.desc: Returns the function binding for a function name.

getFnWriteProtect.name: getFnWriteProtect
getFnWriteProtect.desc: Checks if the given function is write-protected. The value is t if s_name is write-protected. Else, it is nil.

getFunType.name: getFunType
getFunType.desc: Returns a symbol denoting the function type for a given function object. Possible function types include lambda, nlambda, macro, syntax, or primop.

getVarWriteProtect.name: getVarWriteProtect
getVarWriteProtect.desc: (SKILL mode only) Checks if a variable is write-protected. Does not work in SKILL++ mode. In SKILL++ mode, use getFnWriteProtect instead.

globalProc.name: globalProc
globalProc.desc: Defines a global function using a formal argument list. The functions that you define using globalProc are defined within a lexical scope, but are globally accessible.

isCallable.name: isCallable
isCallable.desc: Checks if a function is defined or is autoloadable from a context.

isMacro.name: isMacro
isMacro.desc: Checks if the given symbol denotes a macro.

labels.name: labels
labels.desc: Enables you to define local functions with LET semantics.

lambda.name: lambda
lambda.desc: Defines a function without a name. This is a syntax form.

let.name: let
let.syntax:
SKILL mode
let( 
l_bindings 
g_expr1 ... 
) 
=> g_result 
SKILL++ mode
let( 
[ s_var ]
	(
		( s_var1 s_initExp1 )
		( s_var2 s_initExp2 )
	...
	)
body
)
=> g_result
let.desc: In the SKILL mode, this function provides a faster alternative to prog for binding local variables only. This is a syntax form. In the SKILL++ mode, this function declares a lexical scope. This includes a collection of local variables, as well as body expressions to be evaluated. This becomes a named let if the optional s_var is given.

letrec.name: letrec
letrec.syntax:
letrec(
	(
		( s_var1 s_initExp1 )
		( s_var2 s_initExp2 )
	... 
	)
body
) 
=> g_result
letrec.desc: (SKILL++ mode) A letrec expression can be used in SKILL++ mode only. All the bindings are in effect while their initial values are being computed, thus allowing mutually recursive definitions. Use letrec to declare recursive local functions.

letseq.name: letseq
letseq.syntax:
letseq(
	(
		( s_var1 initExp1 )
		( s_var2 initExp2 ) 
		...
	)
body
)
=> g_result
letseq.desc: A letseq expression can be used in both SKILL and SKILL++ modes. The bindings and evaluations are performed sequentially.

mprocedure.name: mprocedure
mprocedure.desc: Defines a macro with the given name that takes a single formal argument. This is a syntax form.

nlambda.name: nlambda
nlambda.desc: (SKILL mode only) Allows nlambda functions to be defined without having names. In all other respects, nlambda is identical to nprocedure. This is a syntax form that is not supported in SKILL++ mode.

nprocedure.name: nprocedure
nprocedure.desc: (SKILL mode only) Defines an nlambda function with a function name and a single formal argument. This is a syntax form that is not supported in SKILL++ mode.

procedure.name: procedure
procedure.desc: Defines a function using a formal argument list. The body of the procedure is a list of expressions to evaluate.

procedurep.name: procedurep
procedurep.desc: Checks if an object is a procedure, or function, object.

prog.name: prog
prog.syntax:
prog( 
l_localVariables 
[ 
[ s_label ] 
g_expr1 
] ... 
)
=> g_result / nil
prog.desc: Allows for local variable bindings and permits abrupt exits on control jumps. This is a syntax form.

prog1.name: prog1
prog1.desc: Evaluates expressions from left to right and returns the value of the first expression. This is a syntax form.

prog2.name: prog2
prog2.desc: Evaluates expressions from left to right and returns the value of the second expression. This is a syntax form.

progn.name: progn
progn.desc: Evaluates expressions from left to right and returns the value of the last expression. This is a syntax form.

putd.name: putd
putd.desc: Assigns a new function binding, which must be a function, a lambda expression, or nil, to a function name. If you just want to define a function, use procedure or defun.

setf_dynamic.name: setf_dynamic
setf_dynamic.desc: Evaluates g_value in the current lexical scope and updates the SKILL variable named s_name.

setFnWriteProtect.name: setFnWriteProtect
setFnWriteProtect.desc: Prevents a named function from being redefined.

setVarWriteProtect.name: setVarWriteProtect
setVarWriteProtect.desc: (SKILL mode only) Sets the write-protection on a variable to prevent its value from being updated. Does not work in SKILL++ mode.

unalias.name: unalias
unalias.desc: Undefines the aliases specified in an argument list and returns a list containing the aliases undefined by the call. This is nlambda function also works in SKILL++ mode.

unwindProtect.name: unwindProtect
unwindProtect.desc: Evaluates the g_protectedForm expression and then executes the SKILL g_cleanupForm expression. Even if the evaluation of g_protectedForm is interrupted or encounters an error, the g_cleanupForm expression is still executed. You can therefore use g_cleanupForm to close open file handles, reset variables, and restore the state to a known value.

warn.name: warn
warn.desc: Buffers a warning message with given arguments inserted using the same format specification as sprintf, printf, and fprintf.

cdsGetInstPath.name: cdsGetInstPath
cdsGetInstPath.desc: Returns the absolute path of the Cadence installation directory as a string. cdsGetInstPath is for the cds root hierarchy and is meant to be used by all Virtuoso and non-Virtuoso applications.

cdsGetToolsPath.name: cdsGetToolsPath
cdsGetToolsPath.desc: Returns the absolute path of the Cadence installation tools directory as a string after resolving the tools directory appropriately. This function is provided for multiple platform support mainly to simplify access to a common Cadence installation hierarchy for all Unix platforms.

cdsPlat.name: cdsPlat
cdsPlat.desc: Returns the platform for the Cadence software that is currently running. The possible values are: sun4v, sol86, hppa, ibmrs, wint, lnx86, or lni64.

changeWorkingDir.name: changeWorkingDir
changeWorkingDir.desc: Changes the working directory to the specified working directory.

cputime.name: cputime
cputime.desc: Returns the total amount of CPU time (user and system) used in units of 60ths of a second.

createDirHier.name: createDirHier
createDirHier.desc: Creates all directories specified in the given SKILL path that do not already exist

csh.name: csh
csh.desc: Starts the UNIX C-shell as a process to execute a command string.

deleteDir.name: deleteDir
deleteDir.desc: Deletes the specified directory. The directory name can be specified with either an absolute or relative path; the SKILL path is used in the latter case. A path that is anchored to the current directory, for example, ./, ../, or ../../.., and so on, is not considered as a relative path.

deleteFile.name: deleteFile
deleteFile.desc: Deletes a file. The file name can be specified with either an absolute or relative path; the SKILL path is used in the latter case. If a symbolic link is passed in as the argument, it is the link itself, not the file or directory referenced by the link, that gets removed. A path that is anchored to the current directory, for example, ./, ../, or ../../.., and so on, is not considered as a relative path.

exit.name: exit
exit.desc: Causes SKILL to exit with a given process status (defaults to 0), whether in interactive or batch mode.

getCurrentTime.name: getCurrentTime
getCurrentTime.desc: Returns a string representation of the current time.

getInstallPath.name: getInstallPath
getInstallPath.desc: Returns the absolute path of the Cadence DFII installation directory where the DFII products are installed on your system as a list of a single string.

getLogin.name: getLogin
getLogin.desc: Returns the login name of the current user as a string.

getPrompts.name: getPrompts
getPrompts.desc: Returns the current values of the first level and second level prompt text strings, respectively.

getShellEnvVar.name: getShellEnvVar
getShellEnvVar.desc: Returns the value of a UNIX environment variable, if it has been set. This function expands the environment variable name specified in the argument.

getSkillPath.name: getSkillPath
getSkillPath.desc: Returns the current SKILL path. The SKILL path is used in resolving relative paths for some SKILL functions.

getTempDir.name: getTempDir
getTempDir.desc: Returns the system temp directory as a string.

getWorkingDir.name: getWorkingDir
getWorkingDir.desc: Returns the current working directory as a string.

isDir.name: isDir
isDir.desc: Checks if a path exists and if it is a directory name.

prependInstallPath.name: prependInstallPath
prependInstallPath.desc: Prepends the Cadence DFII installation path to a file or directory and returns the resulting path as a string.

setShellEnvVar.name: setShellEnvVar
setShellEnvVar.desc: Sets or updates the value of the UNIX environment variable. This function expands the environment variable name specified in the argument.

setSkillPath.name: setSkillPath
setSkillPath.desc: Sets the internal SKILL path used by some file-related functions in resolving relative path names.

system.name: system
system.desc: Spawns a separate UNIX process to execute a command.

unsetShellEnvVar.name: unsetShellEnvVar
unsetShellEnvVar.desc: Removes an environment variable from the environment of the calling process. This function expands the environment variable name specified in the argument. If the environment variable (t_envVarName) does not exist in the current environment, the environment is left unchanged.

makeNamespace.name: makeNamespace
makeNamespace.desc: Creates a SKILL namespace with the given t_name. A namespace or its parts can be saved in a context and loaded with the context.

findNamespace.name: findNamespace
findNamespace.desc: Returns the namespace object with the specified name.

useNamespace.name: useNamespace
useNamespace.desc: Sets the given namespace for use and imports its symbols into the current namespace.

importSymbol.name: importSymbol
importSymbol.desc: Imports symbols into the given namespace. By default, this function imports into the IL (or default) namespace.

findSymbol.name: findSymbol
findSymbol.desc: Searches for a symbol that is specified as a string in the given namespace and returns its corresponding SKILL symbol.

addToExportList.name: addToExportList
addToExportList.desc: Adds the specified symbols to the namespace export list. This function does not throw any errors if a symbol is already exported. You can export any symbol from your namespace.

getSymbolNamespace.name: getSymbolNamespace
getSymbolNamespace.desc: Returns the namespace where the symbol is created.

removeFromExportList.name: removeFromExportList
removeFromExportList.desc: Removes symbols referenced in l_symbolList from the export list of its namespace. This function will not throw an error, if some of the symbols are not exported. If a symbol from l_symbolList was imported by useNamespace it will not removed by unuseNamespace.

addToNamespace.name: addToNamespace
addToNamespace.desc: Adds and imports the given list of symbol names to the export list of the namespace t_namespaceName.

shadow.name: shadow
shadow.desc: Adds symbols s_symbol to the shadow list of the default namespace. The symbols which are added to the shadow list are not overridden by import.

shadowImport.name: shadowImport
shadowImport.desc: Adds symbols to the namespace shadow list. By default, all warnings related to namespaces are suppressed in the shadowImport function.

removeShadowImport.name: removeShadowImport
removeShadowImport.desc: Removes the specified symbols from the namespace shadow list.

unimportSymbol.name: unimportSymbol
unimportSymbol.desc: Unimports symbols from the given namespace. By default, this function unimports from the IL (or default) namespace.

setf_arrayref.name: setf_arrayref
setf_arrayref.desc: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with arrayref.

setf_caaar.name: setf_caaar
setf_caaar.desc: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with caar.

setf_caadr.name: setf_caadr
setf_caadr.desc: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with caadr.

setf_caar.name: setf_caar
setf_caar.desc: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with caar.

setf_cadar.name: setf_cadar
setf_cadar.desc: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with cadar.

setf_caddr.name: setf_caddr
setf_caddr.desc: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with caddr.

setf_cadr.name: setf_cadr
setf_cadr.desc: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with cadr.

setf_car.name: setf_car
setf_car.desc: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with car.

setf_cdaar.name: setf_cdaar
setf_cdaar.desc: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with cdaar.

setf_cdadr.name: setf_cdadr
setf_cdadr.desc: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with cdadr.

setf_cdar.name: setf_cdar
setf_cdar.desc: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with cdar.

setf_cddar.name: setf_cddar
setf_cddar.desc: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with cddar.

setf_cdddr.name: setf_cdddr
setf_cdddr.desc: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with cdddr.

setf_cddr.name: setf_cddr
setf_cddr.desc: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with cddr.

setf_cdr.name: setf_cdr
setf_cdr.desc: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with cdr.

setf_get.name: setf_get
setf_get.desc: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with get.

setf_getSG.name: setf_getSG
setf_getSG.desc: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with getSG.

setf_getSGq.name: setf_getSGq
setf_getSGq.desc: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with getSGq.

setf_getShellEnvVar.name: setf_getShellEnvVar
setf_getShellEnvVar.desc: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with getShellEnvVar.

setf_getd.name: setf_getd
setf_getd.desc: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with getd.

setf_getq.name: setf_getq
setf_getq.desc: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with getq.

setf_getqq.name: setf_getqq
setf_getqq.desc: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with getqq.

setf_last.name: setf_last
setf_last.desc: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with last.

setf_leftEdge.name: setf_leftEdge
setf_leftEdge.desc: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with leftEdge.

setf_lowerLeft.name: setf_lowerLeft
setf_lowerLeft.desc: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with lowerLeft.

setf_nth.name: setf_nth
setf_nth.desc: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation to support setf(nth(...) ...) expressions. In the function, replace helper with nth.

setf_nthcdr.name: setf_nthcdr
setf_nthcdr.desc: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with nthedr.

setf_nthedr.name: setf_nthedr
setf_nthedr.desc: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with nthcdr.

setf_nthelem.name: setf_nthelem
setf_nthelem.desc: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with nthelem.

setf_rightEdge.name: setf_rightEdge
setf_rightEdge.desc: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with rightEdge.

setf_slotValue.name: setf_slotValue
setf_slotValue.desc: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with slotValue.

setf_topEdge.name: setf_topEdge
setf_topEdge.desc: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with topEdge.

setf_bottomEdge.name: setf_bottomEdge
setf_bottomEdge.desc: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with bottomEdge.

setf_upperRight.name: setf_upperRight
setf_upperRight.desc: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with upperRight.

setf_xCoord.name: setf_xCoord
setf_xCoord.desc: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with xCoord.

setf_yCoord.name: setf_yCoord
setf_yCoord.desc: Returns the result of the corresponding setf operation. In the function, replace helper with yCoord.

allocateInstance.name: allocateInstance
allocateInstance.desc: Creates and returns an empty instance of the specified class. All slots of the new instance are unbound.

changeClass.name: changeClass
changeClass.desc: Changes the class of the given instance (g_inst) to the specified class (g_className).

className.name: className
className.desc: Returns the class symbol denoting a class object.

classOf.name: classOf
classOf.desc: Returns the class object of which the given object is an instance.

classp.name: classp
classp.desc: Checks if the given object is an instance of the given class or is an instance of one of its subclasses.

defclass.name: defclass
defclass.desc: Creates a class object with class name and optional super class name (or names) and slot specifications. This is a macro form.

findClass.name: findClass
findClass.desc: Returns the class object associated with a symbol. The symbol is the symbolic name of the class object.

initializeInstance.name: initializeInstance
initializeInstance.syntax:
initializeInstance( 
g_instance 
[ u_?initArg1    value1 ]
[ u_?initArg2    value2 ] 
... 
)
=> t
initializeInstance.desc: Initializes  the newly created instance of a class. The initializeInstance is a generic function which is called by the makeInstance function. Methods can be defined for a particular class to allow complex initialization to be performed on the object.

isClass.name: isClass
isClass.desc: Checks if the given object is a class object.

makeInstance.name: makeInstance
makeInstance.syntax:
makeInstance( 
us_class 
[ u_?initArg1    value1 ]
[ u_?initArg2    value2 ] ... 
)
=> g_instance
makeInstance.desc: Creates an instance of a class, which can be given as a symbol or a class object.

printself.name: printself
printself.desc: A generic function which is called to print a stdObject instance. You can define your own methods to this generic function for specializing on a class to alter the default print representation of an instance of that class.

setSlotValue.name: setSlotValue
setSlotValue.desc: Sets the s_slotName slot of g_standardObject to g_value.

sharedInitialize.name: sharedInitialize
sharedInitialize.desc: This is a generic function, which is called when an instance is created, re-initialized, updated to conform to a redefined class, or updated to conform to a different class. It is called from the initializeInstance, updateInstanceForRedefinedClass, and updateInstanceForDifferentClass functions to initialize slots of the instance g_object using the corresponding initforms.

slotBoundp.name: slotBoundp
slotBoundp.desc: Checks if a named slot is bound to an instance or not.

slotUnbound.name: slotUnbound
slotUnbound.desc: This function is called when the slotValue function attempts to reference an unbound slot. It signals that the value of the slot s_slotName of g_object has not been set yet. In this case, slotValue returns the result of the method.

slotValue.name: slotValue
slotValue.desc: Returns the value contained in the slot slotName of the given standardObject.

ansiDefmethod.name: ansiDefmethod
ansiDefmethod.desc: A SKILL++ defmethod macro for supporting lexical scoping in callNextMethod. It creates a closure for a method.

callAs.name: callAs
callAs.syntax:
callAs( 
us_class 
s_genericFunction 
g_arg1 
[ g_arg2 ... ]
) 
=> g_value
callAs.desc: Calls a method specialized for some super class of the class of a given object directly, bypassing the usual method inheritance and overriding of a generic function.

callNextMethod.name: callNextMethod
callNextMethod.desc: Calls the next applicable method for a generic function from within the current method. Returns the value returned by the method it calls.

defgeneric.name: defgeneric
defgeneric.syntax:
defgeneric( 
s_functionName 
( s_arg1 
[ s_arg2 ... ] 
) 
[ g_exp ... ] 
) 
=> t
defgeneric.desc: Defines a generic function with an optional default method. This is a macro form. Be sure to leave a space after the function name.

defmethod.name: defmethod
defmethod.syntax:
defmethod( 
s_name 
( 
( s_arg1 
  s_class 
) 
s_arg2 ... 
)
g_exp1 ...
) 
=> t
defmethod.desc: Defines a method for a given generic function. This is a macro form. Be sure to leave a space after s_name.

getMethodSpecializers.name: getMethodSpecializers
getMethodSpecializers.desc: Returns the specializers of all methods currently associated with the given generic function, in a list of class names. The first element in the list is t if there is a default method.

isGeneric.name: isGeneric
isGeneric.desc: Checks if the specified symbol (function name) or funobj (function object) represents a generic SKILL++ function.

getApplicableMethods.name: getApplicableMethods
getApplicableMethods.desc: Returns a list of applicable methods (funObjects) for the specified generic function for a given set of arguments. The returned list contains methods in the calling order.

getMethodName.name: getMethodName
getMethodName.desc: Returns the method name for the given function object

getMethodRole.name: getMethodRole
getMethodRole.desc: Returns the method role for the given function object. U_funObject should be a valid generic function object.

getMethodSpec.name: getMethodSpec
getMethodSpec.desc: Returns the list of specializers for the given funobject.

getGFproxy.name: getGFproxy
getGFproxy.desc: Returns a proxy instance from the specified generic function object

nextMethodp.name: nextMethodp
nextMethodp.desc: Checks if there is a next applicable method for the current method's generic function. The current method is the method that is calling nextMethodp.

updateInstanceForDifferentClass.name: updateInstanceForDifferentClass
updateInstanceForDifferentClass.desc: A generic function, which is called from changeClass to update the specified instance (g_currentObj).

updateInstanceForRedefinedClass.name: updateInstanceForRedefinedClass
updateInstanceForRedefinedClass.syntax:
updateInstanceForRedefinedClass( 
g_obj 
l_addedSlots 
l_deletedSlots 
l_dplList 
) 
=> t
updateInstanceForRedefinedClass.desc: A generic function, which is called to update all instances of a class, when a class redefinition occurs.

ilArgMatchesSpecializer.name: ilArgMatchesSpecializer
ilArgMatchesSpecializer.syntax:
ilArgMatchesSpecializer( 
g_genericFunctionObj
g_specObj
g_argument
)
=> t / nil
ilArgMatchesSpecializer.desc: Determines whether a argument passed to the generic function at run time matches a particular specializer class, so that it then knows which method should be called.

ilEquivalentSpecializers.name: ilEquivalentSpecializers
ilEquivalentSpecializers.syntax:
ilEquivalentSpecializers( 
g_genericFunctionObj
g_specObj1
g_specObj2
)
=> t / nil
ilEquivalentSpecializers.desc: Defines a method to check if two specializers are equal. This is required during method redefinition.

ilGenerateSpecializer.name: ilGenerateSpecializer
ilGenerateSpecializer.desc: Returns a SKILL expression that makes an instance of the given specializer class and optionally set the slots. In the generated SKILL expression, l_argList can be used to initialize the slots.

ilSpecMoreSpecificp.name: ilSpecMoreSpecificp
ilSpecMoreSpecificp.syntax:
ilSpecMoreSpecificp( 
g_genericFunctionObj
s_spec1
s_spec2
s_specArg
)
=> t / nil
ilSpecMoreSpecificp.desc: Checks if spec1 is more specific than spec2. You need to define all required ilSpecMoreSpecificp methods for all existing custom specializers (so that the system can find a method to compare any pair of custom specializers).

subclassesOf.name: subclassesOf
subclassesOf.desc: Returns the ordered list of all (immediate) subclasses of u_classObject. Each element in the list is a class object.

subclassp.name: subclassp
subclassp.desc: Predicate function that checks if classObject1 is a subclass of classObject2.

superclassesOf.name: superclassesOf
superclassesOf.desc: Returns the ordered list of all super classes of u_classObject. Each element in the list is a class object.

addDependent.name: addDependent
addDependent.desc: Registers a dependent object for given object. SKILL checks if g_dependent already exists as a dependent of g_object (using the eqv operator), then g_dependent is not registered again and nil is returned.

getDependents.name: getDependents
getDependents.desc: Returns a list of dependents registered for the given SKILL object, which could be a class or a generic function

removeDependent.name: removeDependent
removeDependent.desc: Removes a dependent object from the given object.

updateDependent.name: updateDependent
updateDependent.syntax:
updateDependent(
u_class
g_dependent
s_notifType
u_classObj
)
=> t
updateDependent.desc: Updates the dependents of a SKILL object, which could be a class or a generic function, when the SKILL object is modified. The SKILL engine calls this method for each g_dependent at different times. For example, if g_dependent is a method, the SKILL engine calls updateDependent at the time of adding or removing the method; whereas, for dependent classes the SKILL engine calls the updateDependent method at the end of class creation.
